Cardinals Made 9 Roster Moves After Week 4; Here's What They Mean
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have made a slew of roster moves following their Week 4 loss to the New York Giants.
It's still early in the season, though Arizona's just 1-3 and are quickly falling out of the NFC West race. Some would say as expected, though games have been winnable for the Cardinals — they just haven't converted.
Breaking down every roster move and what it means:
Johnson was confirmed to miss the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a biceps injury on the team's final drive.
"I feel for him, obviously. ... It sucks for him first and foremost. Sucks obviously for the Arizona Cardinals, our offense, this team. But you know, [this is] NFL football. Here we are in October. Show goes on," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Monday.
Long suffered a knee injury in Week 4. It's not currently known if his injury is considered season-ending like Johnson's was.
What these mean: The Cardinals may be forced to play seventh-round pick Jayden Williams at left tackle this week against a Lions pass rush that ranks second in the NFL in terms of sacks. Arizona likes Williams , though losing Johnson for the season is massive. However, the Cardinals made another move today, which we'll get to here in a moment.
In terms of Long, he was acquired via trade and was utilized primarily as a blocking tight end. The Cardinals are still waiting on Tip Reiman to get healthy.
Quitoriano gets the call-up from the practice squad after spending training camp with the Cardinals. He was stashed away on the practice squad after final roster cuts and is familiar with what LaFleur and co. want to do offensively. Now, he gets his shot to land on the roster and serve as a depth piece behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins.
What this means : The Cardinals love to run 13 personnel, meaning a third tight end (Quitoriano now) will be utilized in the run game often. The good news? He's a capable blocker and there shouldn't be any hiccups in his integration to meaningful playing time. Quitoriano's now on a standard NFL deal, so he gets a pay raise and can skip waivers if eventually released due to being a vested veteran.
Wills, a former top-ten pick, didn't play at all in 2025 as he rehabbed a knee injury and was plucked off the Buffalo Bills' practice squad to help fill in for Johnson. Wills has nearly 60 starts under his belt and is just 27 years old.
Wills, per NFL rules, must be on the Cardinals' active roster for a minimum of three weeks since he came from another team's practice squad.
What this means: It's unknown if Wills will be game-ready to start in Week 5, though the Cardinals obviously believe in Wills enough to snatch him and have him on the active roster. Arizona may not have loved the idea of starting a seventh-round rookie at left tackle this early in the season. Whether Wills is prepared with less than a week's notice remains to be seen, though the Cardinals obviously wanted a veteran in the mix.
Yeboah was a tight end who spent time with the Cardinals this summer as a camp body but was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring. He reached a settlement with Arizona and was cut in August and now makes his way back to the desert.
What it means: With Quitoriano now on the active roster, Arizona restores their tight end depth on the practice squad. He'll serve only as an emergency player in case of injuries ahead of him, though similar to Quitoriano — he at least knows the offense.
Jamison was signed to the Cardinals' practice squad on Sept. 3 as Arizona dealt with some injuries in the secondary. Even in spite of losing Will Johnson, Jamison is released with Art Green now the only cornerback on the team's practice squad.
Lee was signed to Arizona's practice squad on Sept. 1. With injuries to both Johnson and Adams along the line, Lee's dismissal is surprising, though Arizona now opts for more exterior depth as opposed to interior play.
Bios on each from the team's press release:
"Deculus (6-5, 330) has appeared in 26 games (six starts) in his NFL career with the Chargers (2025) and Texans (2022-24). He played 13 games (five starts) with Los Angeles last season after being acquired in a trade from Houston. The 27-year old Deculus entered the league with the Texans as a sixth-round pick (205th overall) in the 2022 NFL Draft out of LSU and spent his first three seasons in the league with Houston. He spent the preseason with the Titans.
"Perry (6-0, 211) spent the preseason with Green Bay and has previously been on the practice squads of the Texans, Patriots and Packers in his NFL career. He entered the league with Miami in 2024 as an undrafted rookie free agent from TCU. While at TCU, Perry played five seasons and appeared in 52 games, collecting 233 tackles (166 solo), 15.5 tackles for loss, 2.0 sacks, three interceptions, 13 passes defensed, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery."
Deculus is a player who simply bolsters the team's depth at tackle while Perry arrives to a Cardinals team that has multiple safeties down, including Andrew Wingard, Dadrion Taylor-Demerson and Kitan Crawford.

title: Cardinals Sign Big-Name OT After Paris Johnson Jr. Injury
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals were initially thought to be counting on depth as a result of Paris Johnson Jr.'s season-ending bicep injury.
On Tuesday, they flipped the script.
The Cardinals, per reports, are signing Buffalo Bills offensive tackle Jedrick Wills Jr. to their active roster.
From NFL insider Mike Garafolo on X:
"The #AZCardinals are signing OT Jedrick Wills off the #Bills practice squad, sources tell me and @RapSheet. The 10th overall pick in 2020 heads to Arizona after the team lost LT Paris Johnson Jr. for the season."
The #AZCardinals are signing OT Jedrick Wills off the #Bills practice squad, sources tell me and @RapSheet . The 10th overall pick in 2020 heads to Arizona after the team lost LT Paris Johnson Jr. for the season. @SalSports reported Wills was signing elsewhere. AZ it is. pic.twitter.com/SvoKGl9tDg
Johnson was just placed on injured reserve today. The Cardinals are 1-3 entering Week 5.
Wills has played five total seasons in the NFL and is 27-years-old. He was initially drafted by the Cleveland Browns as the tenth overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. He played his first few seasons in Cleveland before not playing at all in 2025 due to rehabbing his knee injury, which was an MCL sprain:
“I injured a couple of ligaments, but usually when people like when they get fell on or something in their knee, they mess up all their ligaments and people can just go in and repair it and they get healthy," Wills said earlier this offseason after signing with the Chicago Bears before being released ahead of final roster cuts.
"I had minimal damage to my ligaments. It was more of an alignment issue from where I got fell on. So they had to actually – it wasn't my knee, they had to go into my femur and do what was called an osteotomy to kind of correct my alignment. So my knee is healthy.”
He previously met with the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions this offseason before signing with Chicago and eventually Buffalo.
Wills signed with the Bills' practice squad ahead of the 2026 regular season. Since the Cardinals signed him directly off another team's practice squad, Wills is guaranteed to be on the 53-man roster for three weeks at minimum per NFL rules.
Wills has played in 58 games with 57 starts under his belt at left tackle. He's played in just 17 games once in his NFL career but when healthy, he's shown that he belongs.
As for the Cardinals, Arizona has seventh-round pick Jayden Williams behind him at left tackle and Josh Fryar on the right side of the offensive line at tackle.
Wills is generally viewed as a strong pass-blocker but struggles in run-blocking.

title: All of a Sudden, Cardinals' Offensive Line Looks Drastically Different
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals ' offensive line will look drastically different in Week 5.
The injury bug continues to rattle Arizona, as the Cardinals are losing left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. to a bicep injury that will keep him out for the rest of the season while right guard Isaiah Adams isn't likely to play this week according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
The Cardinals, almost overnight, are down two starters along the offensive line.
Injuries derailed the Cardinals way before the season started. Second-round pick Chase Bisontis suffered a torn MCL during preseason play, and now backup Jon Gaines appears to be prepared for action if Adams can't go.
Gaines is a player the Cardinals internally like. He's had a few years to develop, has spot-started recently for Arizona and has versatility to play any of their three interior spots along the offensive line.
Meanwhile, at left tackle, training camp darling and seventh-round pick Jayden Williams is set to take over for Johnson.
"Really, really impressed with Jayden. I think I’ve said that in here if I haven’t, but he’s wise beyond his years. He played big-time college football, so we have a lot of confidence in him," LaFleur said yesterday.
The Cardinals are down two starters entering Week 5's contest against the Detroit Lions. Running back Jeremiyah Love is also dealing with an ankle injury, but that's another story.
Yet no matter how you slice it, things have changed for Arizona — quickly.
According to ESPN's metrics, the Cardinals' offensive line ranks 31st in pass-block win rate and 21st in run-block win rate. Losing two starters along a unit that needs continuity more than any other isn't exactly a step in the right direction.
It's not as if other starters are playing well, either.
Isaac Seumalo hasn't been the presence many hoped he'd be after signing in free agency. Hjalte Froholdt is strong in pass protection but has struggled in the run while Elijah Wilkinson is very much the liability he was thought to be in free agency.
Arizona's offensive line ranks in the bottom third of average yards before contact on rushing plays at a mere 1.0.
Now, the Cardinals approach Week 5 and a Lions team that ranks second in team sacks (15) with an even more depleted unit and questions around their ability to win in the trenches.
"Each week can be a little bit different in terms of who you’re trying to ‘protect’ a little bit more and who’s going to have a little bit more of a stressful down," LaFleur said when asked how a game-plan changes due to injuries along the OL.
"You try to move that stress around a little bit so that it’s not just 60-plus plays of stress for those said players. There are a lot of factors.”

title: Cardinals Double Down on Jacoby Brissett After 3-Interception Game
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are adamantly sticking with quarterback Jacoby Brissett ahead of their Week 5 matchup against the Detroit Lions.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur gave a one-word answer to a possible benching of Brissett after a 1-3 start to the season, and when asked what it would take for a possible quarterback change, LaFleur directed attention back to this week:
“I’m just focused on this week and trying to be as good as we can be. Again, we were 12 feet away from scoring 30 but we didn’t and we lost. We have to improve from it and work to be 1-0 this week," he said.
Fans in the desert are ready for a quarterback change, as Brissett's start to the regular season has been lackluster in terms of production. Last week's three-interception performance in New York didn't help, either.
“The first one, he was trying to give (WR) ‘Marv’ (Marvin Harrison Jr.) a chance. We got a little bit ‘edged’ there and he got his arm hit," LaFleur said.
"The second one — people are going to disagree with me on this one in terms of batted balls. If it’s an extreme issue throughout a course of 17 games or a couple of years, then yeah, I’d look at it. I’ve been with an MVP quarterback who had a lot of batted balls in 2015 in (Former NFL QB) Matt Ryan. We did not know why. Your only coaching tool for guys that are natural throwers is obviously the arm angle change and stuff like that. That’s like the no-crap statement.
"Then the other easy one (is) to tell the (offensive) line ‘Hey, we have to keep their arms down,’ but that’s kind of elementary coaching. There is something to be coached there at least. That one was almost kind of like — man, we started out so good and then all of a sudden, we weren’t playing good. It was kind of the catalyst to all of it right there.
"The third one — it’s fourth and goal at the four (yard line). It was the last play, and he had to get the ball out of his hands. Again, I think we can provide better clarity to make sure that we’re not even in that situation.”
Rookie Carson Beck and veteran Gardner Minshew are waiting in the wings, and if trends continue for the Cardinals, it feels more like a "when" and not "if" conversation surrounding changes at quarterback.

title: Cardinals Update Jeremiyah Love's New Injury
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is dealing with an ankle injury different from the one that kept him out for all of preseason action, according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
Love was spotted having his ankle worked on during the team's Week 4 loss to the New York Giants, a game where he wasn't featured on the team's final drive when Arizona's offense was marching down the field for a potential win before being stopped on the final play.
"It's a different one, and he's been dealing with it for a little bit, but it's just a management type thing. It's like [Love] tweaks it, and then he feels fine. So we're just trying to manage that. He's doing a good job with it too," LaFleur said.
Love finished with 63 rushing yards on 14 carries and later told reporters in the locker room the ankle injury wasn't bothering him.
"Not really bothering me, kinda just managing it," Love said (h/t The Arizona Republic ). "Cause we've got a long season; coaches don't want to overload me. So not necessarily bothering me to the point where I can't play, 'cause I can go out there and play regardless.
"Whether it's bothering me, I've gotta go out there and putting something on the line for the team to put us in the best position to have success. But it was alright."
Love was out-snapped by Tyler Allgeier 36-30 on Sunday. The Cardinals' running back was spotted going down with an injury the open portion of practice last week before returning.
Prior to that, Love had missed the team's final two preseason games but participated in every regular season matchup thus far.
This is certainly something to monitor as the Cardinals approach their Week 5 matchup against the Detroit Lions.
"It's frustrating because I'm the type of guy who is willing to do whatever I can to help the team have success," Love continued postgame (h/t AZCardinals.com ).
"I want to be out there regardless how I am feeling but my coaches care about me. They're not going to put you out there if you're not in a position to be yourself. It's frustrating for me personally, not even with the coaches, I'm really frustrated with myself because I just want to be good. I want to be 100 percent.
"I'm not where I want to be. I'm not able to go out there and (expletive) do spectacular plays every single time or stuff like that."

title: Cardinals Lose Paris Johnson Jr. to Season-Ending Injury: 4 Instant Reactions
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are set to lose starting left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. for the rest of the season after the former first-round pick tore his biceps in Week 4.
Johnson, set for surgery soon, exited on the final play from scrimmage against the New York Giants in their eventual loss , and the unsettling news was confirmed on Monday by Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur.
"I don't know exactly when it's [surgery] going to happen, but it's going to happen soon to obviously get the process going. I feel for him, obviously. ... It sucks for him first and foremost. Sucks obviously for the Arizona Cardinals, our offense, this team. But you know, [this is] NFL football. Here we are in October. Show goes on," LaFleur told reporters Monday.
Though Johnson wasn't voted a captain, Johnson was the undisputed leader in Arizona's offensive line room — and  this is a massive gut-punch for a Cardinals starting five that's already been tested with injuries in the interior.
Johnson, in his fourth year, now has landed on injured reserve in his last three seasons. Arizona's unit was already viewed as hit-or-miss, and one of their most tenured players on offense now is sidelined for the rest of 2026.
The Cardinals lost by far their best tackle and vocal leader upfront all in the same swing.
The late-round pick went from a potential roster cut to a fun training camp story in the blink of an eye this summer — and now Williams will be tasked with entering starting duties. The seventh-round tackle impressed in preseason duties and now has an opportunity to continue his progression.
"Really, really impressed with Jayden. I think I've said that in here if I haven't. But he's wise beyond his years. Obviously played big-time college football, so we got a lot of confidence in him," said LaFleur.
"Obviously, he's been doing some stuff in the 13 personnel game when we go to the two tight ends plus him, and he's not limited to just the run game. He can actually do some stuff — he was a tight end coming out. So not to be confused with a tight end in the NFL, but you guys know what I mean."
Williams has a golden opportunity to make a name for himself, and the Cardinals don't believe the moment is too big for him.
Losing your best tackle often spells doom for offenses, and with Elijah Wilkinson struggling at right tackle, the Cardinals may not believe they'll have much time to get passes off.
Jacoby Brissett's average time to throw of 2.6 seconds ranks bottom five in the NFL, pending Monday Night Football. His average intended air yards of 6.6 is bottom ten in the league as well.
Arizona's offense already doesn't push the ball deep downfield, but LaFleur didn't sound like the Cardinals will drastically change how they go about business.
"It's all 11, and then the variables of the defense you're going against. Do they have great edge guys? Do they have great interiors? Do they have a corner that plays [center]field? But all those kind of things," he said.
"So there's a lot of factors that go into it. Each week can be a little bit different in terms of who you're trying to 'protect' a little bit more, and who's going to have a little bit more of a stressful down. And you try to move that stress around a little bit so that it's not just 60+ plays of stress for those said players. So yeah, I mean, there's a lot of factors."
Unfortunately, with Johnson still needing a second contract, this season-ending injury really clouds up the big picture and his standing with the Cardinals.
Arizona picked up his fifth-year option, keeping the Ohio State product under contract through the 2027 season. However, Johnson became extension-eligible this past offseason and was hoping to get a long-term deal done with Arizona.
It's no secret Johnson was looking for top dollar, though two prior season-ending knee injuries and now a biceps issue will cause some serious questions to rise in future contract negotiations.
Johnson will either have to bet on himself returning and reaching a high level of play or take a massive discount compared to what he was likely asking for.

title: Cardinals' Andrew Wingard Gets Major Relief With Injury News
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals safety Andrew Wingard was carted from the sideline to the locker room in Week 4's battle against the New York Giants with no immediate diagnosis on his knee injury after the game from head coach Mike LaFleur .
However, news just hit for Wingard and his injury — and it's encouraging.
From NFL insider Jeremy Fowler:
"Cardinals safety Andrew Wingard suffered a bone bruise in his knee Sunday in New York but the ligaments are intact, per @rapsheet and me. Timeline for return uncertain but relative good news for Arizona," he wrote on X.
Cardinals safety Andrew Wingard suffered a bone bruise in his knee Sunday in New York but the ligaments are intact, per @rapsheet and me. Timeline for return uncertain but relative good news for Arizona.
Wingard was hurt in the first quarter after he and Malik Nabers landed awkwardly on a contested catch.
Wingard sure seems set to miss some time, though avoiding a season-ending injury is a best-case scenario for both player and team.
The Cardinals were forced to trot out Wydett Williams Jr. in his spot, and the rookie undoubtedly struggled by allowing massive gains through the air in coverage. Perhaps more time next to Budda Baker will help, though Arizona undoubtedly needs a better showing from Williams.
With Kitan Crawford on injured reserve and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson still missing time after being hurt in preseason, the Cardinals' depth at safety is ultra thin at the moment. Arizona also lost cornerback Will Johnson for the year earlier in the season, so the entire secondary has been hit with injuries.
Wingard, a free agent signing this offseason, earned starting duties almost immediately upon arrival from the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Wingard was part of a special turnaround in Jacksonville, and before the season, he said he saw the makings of something similar in the desert.
"I've loved every second of it since I've stepped in this building and in this locker room. I haven't seen a single ego. There's no divas. It's like all these guys are such good guys and good people, and that was one of our things in Jacksonville that got us over the top," he said .
"We just had dudes that cared about each other and were good people and go to work every day and grind. So I've seen nothing but great things from all these guys since I stepped in the building and they've welcomed me in, and it's felt great."
Prior to exiting with his injury, Wingard tallied 23 total tackles, one pass defensed, one interception and one forced fumble.

title: Cardinals Defend Decision to Sit Jeremiyah Love in Final Moments
full_text:
ARIZONA — With the game on the line, the Arizona Cardinals ' heftiest offseason investment was nowhere to be found.
The Cardinals' 36-24 loss to the New York Giants came down to the wire, with Jacoby Brissett and the team's offense being stonewalled near the goal line in the final moments of Week 4 action at MetLife Stadium.
The Cardinals, down 30-24, had first-and-goal at the Giants' four-yard line with 22 seconds left and one timeout. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love — previously rushing for 63 yards on 14 carries (4.5 YPC) — was on the sidelines as Arizona opted for veteran running back Tyler Allgeier, who was on the field while Brissett threw three consecutive incompletions before a game-sealing pick-six.
There've been several talks of the town, but Love's absence on the biggest string of plays dominated social media following the game. Perhaps rightly so, as one of the Cardinals' more dynamic players was sidelined in crunch time.
This is what LaFleur had to say postgame:
"Well, we're just in our two-minute situation right there, so in our pass emphasis, it's obviously Tyler (Allgeier) being kind of that 'third-down back,' if you will. So they're heating us up pretty good. From that standpoint, it's more his role. Jeremiyah can obviously be out there and do it, but you want to segment, I guess you could say, a little bit. It wasn't like we were going to be using our back in the pass game, if you will. So it's more of a protection emphasis."
Arizona's first play was a play-action pass that fell incomplete to Michael Wilson. LaFleur says the Cardinals' second play was initially a run before it was checked to a pass, which also fell incomplete to  Wilson.
"Yeah, the second-down one was a run play. We just had a run alert with it because they went all out. So we could have ran it, but literally they would have gone all out, so it would have been a situation where you'd be praying that it worked, not just running it to run it," LaFleur said.
"That was the thought process on the second down. Again, you thought they probably would all out it, so we had the kind of the out route to Mike (wide receiver Michael Wilson) there that we feel good about."
A third-down incompletion to Trey McBride was followed by Brissett's third interception of the day, which was returned for a touchdown as time expired.
Arizona's performance in the red zone had been an underlying narrative around the Cardinals to start the season, as the offense has settled for field goals too much for their liking as opposed to punching it in for six.
Most believe Love's ability as a pass-catcher would have been beneficial to have on Arizona's final drive, as he's a better route-runner than Allgeier and could get open easier if the Giants indeed were wanting to send pressure like they were.
The rookie running back was spotted getting his ankle worked on during the game. It's noteworthy Love missed multiple weeks of the preseason with a high ankle sprain while he went down during the open portion of practice last week.
"I’ll have to see. I haven't talked to him yet in terms of that, but I know that they just kept saying he'll be up. So, we'll look at it a little bit more tomorrow, obviously," LaFleur said.

title: 3 Advanced Stats Reveal the Real Story of Cardinals' Week 4 Loss
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals suffered another frustrating loss in Week 4, falling to the New York Giants 36-24 at MetLife Stadium. After taking control early (14-3 lead), Arizona struggled to sustain its momentum and was held to just seven points in the second half.
"There is no script for this one," head coach Mike LaFleur said postgame.
"No loss is fun, all three losses that we've had over the last three weeks have been different. This one is going to sting."
Here are a few stats that stand out.
The New York Giants blitzed the Arizona Cardinals 53.8% of the time in Week 4. This was the highest blitz rate by a Giants defense since the start of the last season, per Next Gen Stats.
Against the blitz, Jacoby Brissett completed 6-of-18 passes for 55 yards. Overall, Brissett was pressured on more than half of his dropbacks Sunday (52.4%).
"They were heating us up pretty good," LaFleur said. "I'm going to put it on me in terms of having the right play design to get these guys open where we can play pitch and catch a little bit easier."
Arizona has struggled to limit explosive pass plays this season. Unfortunately, things did not improve against the Giants, as the Cardinals allowed five receptions of 20+ yards.
Malik Nabers, who was selected two picks after Marvin Harrison Jr. in the 2024 NFL Draft, was responsible for three of the five explosive pass plays (39,28,25).
Through four games, the Cardinals have allowed 14 passes of at least 20+ yards.
"We want explosives, and we want to limit explosives," coach LaFleur said postgame. "I got to look at the tape and see where some of the breakdowns occurred. We'll get it fixed and get it fixed fast."
The Cardinals' ground game was rolling early. After the first quarter, Arizona's running backs produced 81 yards on nine carries (9.0 YPC). To counter the rushing attack, the Giants decided to stack the box. Per Next Gen Stats, New York loaded the box with 8+ defenders 46.2% of the time. This was the third-highest stacked box percentage in Week 4 (Pending MNF).
"They just started loading it up. You could tell they had to talk about just playing a little bit harder," Mike LaFleur told J.P. Shadrick and A.Q. Shipley on the Cardinals Locker Room Show. "They loaded up, and when they do that, we obviously got to take advantage of it. And we just didn't."
Coach LaFleur believes there were "opportunities in the pass game" because there were so many defenders in the box.
"Obviously, I have to do a better job of putting these guys in positions to be successful to be able to attack that pressure in man (coverage) that they were giving us."

title: Cardinals Report Card: Grading Every Position After Week 4 Loss
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 1-3 after a frustrating loss in Week 4.
It was another matchup where the Cardinals had an opportunity to win in crunch time before falling flat.
Let's grade every position group A-F using C as an average:
We'll start with the good: Brissett tossed two touchdown passes and his trio of interceptions — to varying extents — weren't all on him. He was able to march the Cardinals down the field and put them in position to win the game.
With that said, the Cardinals didn't win the game, and Brissett's 55.2 passer rating was the worst he's had in years. Granted he's not exactly afforded time thanks to his offensive line, but Brissett's performance today wasn't anywhere close to a passing grade.
The Cardinals aren't making a quarterback change for Week 5, but if Brissett doesn't turn the tide quickly, it could be coming sooner rather than later.
The only thing holding this group back was not winning, which could have been the case had Arizona opted to hand the ball off on any of their four final plays when they were near the goal line.
The Cardinals' running back duo of Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier performed about as good as you could have asked, rushing for 105 yards on 22 carries (4.7 YPC) and a touchdown. Arizona got off to a 14-3 lead and for some reason abandoned the run until later in action.
When they did lean on the ground, both rushers performed extremely well. This will be one of the bigger regrets when Mike LaFleur reflects back on the game.
The Cardinals' array of pass-catchers by no means had a bad day. Marvin Harrison Jr. found the end zone for the first time this season while Arizona also had a surprise score from TE2 Elijah Higgins. Michael Wilson finished with 95 yards on seven receptions, too.
Yet none of the Cardinals' pass-catchers were able to make a play when the game was on the line, failing to either come down with tough receptions or create separation in any of Arizona's last four targeted passers (Harrison and Trey McBride were respectively open but that's a topic for another article).
McBride was limited to a mere checkdown option for Brissett (31 yards on seven catches). Harrison went quiet after his touchdown reception and Wilson had his number called twice in the final moments. The unit performed mostly well — they just couldn't find a way at the end.
Arizona's rushing attack looked pleasant early thanks to the holes paved by the Cardinals' offensive line. Yet that momentum went away, quickly, and the Cardinals were forced to deal with a heavy pass approach the rest of the way.
As a result, Brissett was blitzed on nearly 54% of his dropbacks with a pressure rate of 38.5%. Brissett was only officially sacked twice, but his 2.52 average seconds to throw time was among the fastest in the NFL this week.
As we established in our studs and duds , the right side of the offensive line particularly is a problem with Isaiah Adams and Elijah Wilkinson. Brissett wasn't running for his life every single play, though you would have liked to see much more from Arizona's unit.
A weak spot of the Cardinals' defense was one of their strong points today. Arizona allowed a mere 3.1 yards per carry with no touchdowns to the Giants on the ground with four tackles for a loss. New York's rushing attack was overall average.
In their pass rush, they tallied four quarterback hits and two sacks with Walter Nolen III coming alive along with a surprising sack from Darius Robinson. In the run, Roy Lopez was all over the place with six tackles.
A good step in the right direction.
It was really encouraging to see Josh Sweat make a splash on Sunday, reaching his first sack with multiple pressures while Zaven Collins — mostly known for the run — also brought Jameis Winston down today. We've been harping on this group all season to take a step up and help Arizona get to the quarterback, and that happened (at least to better extents) today.
The only thing stopping this grade from being a D grade is Mack Wilson Sr. forcing a fumble in the second half. Wilson was picked on in coverage, allowing two touchdowns through the air. Jack Gibbens, meanwhile, led the Cardinals in tackles with eight.
It was an overall mixed bag from this position, though the overall success allowed to the Giants' passing attack overshadows anything good that happened with the group.
Garrett Williams was all over the place and looked much healthier than he did last week. Denzel Burke came away with an interception. Without Will Johnson, expectations have to be tempered with this group. They did benefit from an improved pass rush, though Arizona's inability to limit Malik Nabers to any extent (6-112-1) dragged their overall performance down.
Budda Baker's performance really is carrying a ton of weight here, as the star defender undoubtedly had his best outing of 2026 with an interception and a pair of impressive pass breakups.
Fellow starter Andrew Wingard exited due to injury and was replaced by rookie Wydett Williams, who allowed several big plays in the passing game and even had a penalty (block in the back) on Baker's interception return. It was a very forgettable performance from Williams, which balances out Baker's strong performance.

title: Falcons Waive Former UGA RB, Sign Former Patriots Draft Pick as Replacement
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are coming off back-to-back weeks of imposing their will on opposing defenses with their running game. Atlanta has the No. 2 rushing offense in the league, powered by Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr.
There hasn't been a lot of room for a third running back through the first four games of the year, but that hasn't stopped them from trying to improve the room with changes.
On Monday, the team announced they had placed popular undrafted free agent running back Cash Jones on waivers and signed former Jam Miller as a replacement.
Miller was selected by the New England Patriots in the seventh round of April's NFL Draft. He rushed 25 times for 92 yards in the preseason for the Patriots, but he didn't make their 53-man roster out of camp.
Miller was a key contributor for the Alabama Crimson Tide across a four-year career. His best season was 2024 when he had 668 yards rushing and seven touchdowns. He also added 16 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown.
Jones was considered to have an outside shot at making the Falcons' 53-man roster out of training camp. He was used at running back, wide receiver and on special teams after signing with the Falcons as an undrafted free agent out of Georgia in the spring.
He shined in the Falcon's preseason win over the Indianapolis Colts with seven carries for 41 yards, and he added four catches for 62 yards and a touchdown.
His versatility made him a possibility to make the team. However, the Falcons surprised everyone by keeping just two running backs on the active roster and releasing both Jones and Tyler Goodson. They both re-signed with the team as practice squad players, but Goodson was poached by the Cowboys and signed to their roster.
There's a strong possibility that Jones' time in Atlanta isn't done, and he could rejoin the practice squad in the near future. However, for now, the Falcons are still carrying just three running backs on the team.
The timing of the move is a little ironic for the former SEC stars, as the No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs travel to Tuscaloosa on Saturday night to take on the No. 6 Alabama Crimson Tide.
The Falcons will take on the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football. It will be their third-straight nationally televised game, and they're hoping to make it a third-straight win.

title: Homecoming or Breakout Party? Inside Falcons LB Harold Perkins Jr.'s Big Night
full_text:
Monday Night Football was a happy homecoming for Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Harold Perkins Jr.
It came at the expense of a sad “Domecoming” for the New Orleans Saints (1-3), as Atlanta (2-2) thrashed the NFC South arch rival 45-24 to spoil the 20th anniversary of the Caesars Superdome reopening after Hurricane Katrina .
“It was a surreal feeling,” said the New Orleans-born Perkins. “I was just trying to do my part and not let my teammates down. I was taking it all in.”
Perkins finished the primetime game tied with cornerback CJ Henderson for a team-high and career-high 10 tackles on the night. He notched his first career sack by getting half credit with safety Xavier Watts as they brought down Saints quarterback Tyler Shough in the backfield. Perkins added a quarterback hit.
Harold Perkins Jr. was everywhere last night, posting 7 tackles, 1 sack, 1 PBU, and 3 stops pic.twitter.com/0Oz3Ykh997
The highly versatile six-round NFL Draft pick out of LSU was also active in pass coverage, breaking up a pass.
“I thought Perk was outstanding,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said of the 6-foot-1, 223-pounder. “Really excited for Perk coming home. I thought he was really good.”
Perkins was just 11 months old when Hurricane Katrina tragically destroyed the city of New Orleans in August 2005. It forced his family to uproot and move to the greater Houston area, settling in Cypress, Texas, where he became a football star at Cypress High School.
Twenty-one years after disaster struck, a “beaucoup” number of Perkins family members watched him play his fourth career NFL game, and first in the Superdome. The Falcons linebacker said that around 30 family members, including his grandmother, were in the building to watch his standout performance.
Some were draped in Falcons gear, while some stayed loyal to their Saints fandom.
“It means a lot, just coming out there, coming back home,” Perkins, 22, said. “Not even just playing the Saints – be able to just be around my family, and they get to see me ball.”
With Perkins leading the way, Atlanta’s defense beleaguered the Saints all night.
New Orleans was held to 320 total yards: 270 passing and 50 rushing.
Shough was sacked twice, but spent the entirety of the game getting chased out of the pocket by the Falcons.
“We were out our top,” Perkins said. That means the Falcons unit was rabid and fierce.
“We played like some savages,” he added.
Per ESPN, Atlanta ranks eighth among the 32 NFL teams in total defense after Monday’s game.
Led by defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich , the Falcons have the league’s top run defense, as was evident in New Orleans.
“Credit our defense as a whole, our coaches for setting us up and putting us in the right positions to win,” Perkins said. “We just went out there and executed.”
The Falcons have a short, six-day turnaround before their next game.
They will finish their three-game primetime run at home against the Baltimore Ravens (3-1) on the Oct. 11 edition of Sunday Night Football.
Baltimore’s two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson has an outside chance of playing after spraining his left ankle in the second quarter of the Ravens’ Week 4 win against the Tennessee Titans. Jackson was in a protective walking boot and may miss extra games.
Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will likely start against Atlanta if Jackson isn’t good to go.
Falcons-Ravens is set for an 8:20 p.m. kickoff from Mercedes-Benz Stadium. NBC will televise the game.

title: Falcons Power Rankings: The National Media Can't Agree on Atlanta
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons dominated in a prime-time road game for the second week in a row , launching themselves from worst to first in the eyes of many in the national media. Yet, somehow, national power rankings still don't agree on the Falcons. Some list them in the top 15, while others rank them among the seven worst teams in the NFL.
The Falcons' next game can settle some of this debate.
Atlanta’s upcoming opponent, the Baltimore Ravens , are ranked as high as the No. 4 team in the NFL by some publications. The Falcons could see a serious rise next week if their offensive exploits continue on Sunday night.
The divisional beatdown elevated the Falcons in the NFL’s weekly power rankings across several platforms. Falcons OnSI pulled the results from those sites and put them all in one place for fans. Take a look below to see where the Falcons land compared with their division rivals.
After the Falcons dropped to No. 31 just two weeks ago, SI now lists them in the top 24 after their “ruination” of the Saints. It seems Conor Orr is starting to buy some of the hype, and he joked that we should all have prayer candles for Michael Penix Jr.'s continued health.
Elsewhere in the South, SI ranks the Panthers No. 14 (up nine spots), the Saints No. 25 (down five spots), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (idle).
Pete Prisco has more faith in the Falcons, lifting them into the league's top 20. He believes their season has turned around with Michael Penix Jr., and that is probably understating it -- Atlanta scored just 16 points in its first two games before putting up 35 against Green Bay and 45 against New Orleans.
Elsewhere in the South, CBS ranks the Panthers No. 18 (up eight spots), the Saints No. 23 (down five spots), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (down one spot).
Nick Shook is bullish on the Falcons after their consecutive weeks of domination. After having them as low as No. 31 after Week 2, he has Atlanta all the way up to No. 15 after Monday night. He said there should be “cautious” optimism about this team, but the next three weeks will determine how real this team could be – they have home games against Baltimore, Chicago, and San Francisco.
Elsewhere in the South, NFL.com ranks the Panthers No. 14 (up eight spots), the Saints No. 20 (down four spots), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (down 1 spot).
Despite describing the Falcons as “worst to first,” ESPN ranks them oddly low in its power rankings. Atlanta is somehow slotted behind the 0-4 Texans, the Packers (whom they just demolished in Week 3), and the Saints (whom they just demolished in Week 4).
Marc Raimondi highlighted the instant offensive turnaround since swapping Cooper Rush for Michael Penix Jr., but somehow that isn't enough to put them ahead of the teams they just embarrassed on national television? Strange.
Elsewhere in the South, ESPN ranks the Panthers No. 18 (up four spots), the Saints No. 21 (down three spots), and the Buccaneers No. 30 (idle).

title: Atlanta Falcons May Catch a Break With Baltimore Ravens Star Questionable
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons could be facing the Baltimore Ravens without Lamar Jackson when the two teams meet on Sunday Night Football.
Jackson is dealing with a sprained ankle that gives him only an outside chance of playing against Atlanta, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport .
Jackson could potentially miss multiple games depending on how his rehabilitation progresses, although the injury is not considered long-term and is not expected to require surgery.
The potential absence would be a significant blow to Baltimore. Jackson has been one of the NFL’s most productive quarterbacks this season, throwing for 967 yards with six touchdowns and one interception while completing 66.3 percent of his passes. He has also added 144 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground.
Jackson was playing well before suffering the injury Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. He completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns while adding 20 rushing yards in the first half as Baltimore built a 24 to 7 lead.
The injury occurred on a sack late in the first half, and Jackson did not return after halftime. He was seen leaving the stadium in a protective walking boot, adding to the concern surrounding his availability for Sunday’s matchup with Atlanta.
With Jackson sidelined, Tyler Huntley took over at quarterback to begin the second half. Huntley completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards and added 16 rushing yards on four carries. Although Baltimore was unable to score in the second half, the Ravens held on for a 24 to 18 victory.
Huntley’s performance could prove important if Jackson is unable to recover in time for Sunday. He is familiar with Baltimore’s offense and has previous starting experience with the Ravens, giving the team an experienced option behind Jackson.
Still, replacing Jackson would be a major challenge. His ability to make plays as both a passer and runner forces defenses to account for him on every snap. His mobility also creates opportunities for Baltimore’s rushing attack and play-action passing game.
Making it even more difficult for Hundley, the Falcons have the NFL's No. 1-ranked rushing defense . If they can focus on Derrick Henry without the threat of Jackson running, it will be hard to move the ball on the ground against Atlanta.
The Falcons will have to prepare as if Jackson could play until Baltimore makes an official decision. However, if he is ruled out, Atlanta would instead face Huntley and a Ravens offense that already gained experience playing without Jackson this season.
Jackson’s status will remain one of the biggest storylines throughout the week as Baltimore monitors his recovery.

title: Former Jaguars Top 10 Pick Finally Seeing His Work Pay Off with Atlanta Falcons
full_text:
C.J. Henderson has spent the past few seasons trying to find the consistency that made him a top-10 pick in the NFL Draft. On Monday night, he showed the Atlanta Falcons why they believed he could provide it.
With A.J. Terrell on injured reserve, Henderson has stepped into a starting role at cornerback. Rather than simply filling a void, he delivered one of his most productive performances in recent memory during Atlanta’s dominant win over the New Orleans Saints.
Henderson led the Falcons with 10 total tackles while adding a pass deflection and forcing a fumble that he also recovered.
It was the type of performance defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich envisioned when discussing Henderson earlier in the week.
“CJ is a tremendous luxury. In my opinion, he’s a one (cornerback). He’s a guy that would start on a lot of teams,” Ulbrich said.
Ulbrich also believes Henderson gives Atlanta security at cornerback while Terrell is sidelined and was excited to see him “show this league exactly who he is now.”
Henderson did just that against New Orleans.
His strip of Saints running back Kendre Miller created the only turnover in the game when the Falcons needed it most, up 7-0 early. Henderson looked ready for the moment and said as much.
“I had confidence. I’ve been working on my craft, you know, and letting my work come to life,” Henderson said.
That opportunity became even more important once Terrell went on injured reserve. Atlanta suddenly needed Henderson to take on a larger role in the secondary, and the former No. 9 overall pick responded.
“I’m out there attacking the ball, making plays,” Henderson said. “I feel like I can help this team.”
Henderson’s road to Atlanta has not been straightforward. Jacksonville selected him ninth overall in 2020 with the expectation that he could become a cornerstone of its secondary. Injuries and inconsistent play limited his time with the Jaguars, however, and Jacksonville eventually traded him to Carolina during the 2021 season.
Henderson spent three years with the Panthers as a part-time starter, and spent 2024 on the Texans' and Steelers' practice squads without making an appearance.
Atlanta provided a new opportunity for Henderson last season, and he's elevated his game in 2026.
The Falcons secondary played with confidence throughout Monday night’s victory, and Henderson credited preparation and trust for the unit’s performance.
“Just by doing our job, trusting our keys, trusting our training,” Henderson said. “That’s what we harp on during the week.”
Henderson acknowledged there are still plays the secondary needs to clean up, but his performance provided Atlanta with an encouraging development while Terrell remains unavailable.
10 tackles, a forced fumble and recovery, and a pass breakup made Henderson one of the Falcons’ most productive defenders Monday night.
Now, the challenge is turning that performance into consistency.
“I feel good,” Henderson said. “When you have a lot of confidence coming in, I mean, I’m still in there. We’ve got to finish on it.”
For Henderson, Monday night was an opportunity to show that the work he has continued to put in is translating when his number is called.
For the Falcons, it may have shown they have more depth at cornerback than they realized.

title: Falcons RB Bijan Robinson Making History in Prime Time
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson continues to prove that the bigger the stage, the better he plays.
Robinson delivered another dominant primetime performance Monday night against the New Orleans Saints, rushing for 145 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries in Atlanta’s 45-24 victory. The performance continued an incredible stretch for Robinson, who performs best when the lights are brightest.
The numbers go beyond that streak. Since the 1970 NFL/AFL merger, Robinson currently owns the highest scrimmage yards per game average in primetime history, with 145.4 yards per game across his first 11 primetime appearances.
At this point, it is becoming more than a trend.
Robinson has established himself as one of the NFL’s most dangerous players when the lights are brightest, and Monday night provided another reminder of why.
The Falcons wasted no time getting him involved. On Atlanta’s third play from scrimmage, Robinson broke loose for a 59-yard touchdown that immediately quieted the Superdome crowd.
BIJAN ROBINSON. TO. THE. HOUSE. ESPN | ANF pic.twitter.com/MwZu66Ji8p
Robinson credited his offensive line for creating the opportunity.
“They made the hole right there on that backside, and I just took it,” Robinson said.
Once he found open space, Robinson had one goal.
“I was just like, ‘Can’t get caught.’”
The explosive run set the tone for a Falcons offense that scored 45 points and has now put up 80 points over its last two games. Robinson has been at the center of that offensive turnaround, but he was quick to give credit to everyone around him.
The @AtlantaFalcons are the only team in NFL history to have a 2-game span with: 80+ points 800+ total yards 8+ rushing TDs no more than 1 turnover no more than 1 sack allowed pic.twitter.com/C70yfZYCFs
“It’s fun to see just the O line and just how they bring so much energy to this offense,” Robinson said. “Without those guys, we don’t have what we have.”
Robinson also credited offensive coordinator Tommy Rees for having them ready.
“It’s all in the preparation, and we saw that look,” Robinson said.
That preparation allowed Atlanta to establish the run early while also opening opportunities for quarterback Michael Penix Jr. Robinson believes Penix’s ability to threaten defenses through the air has made the entire offense more dangerous.
“He helps out with the run game,” Robinson said. “You can’t just stack the box because you have to respect that he can get the ball anywhere on the field.”
The combination has made Robinson increasingly difficult to contain, particularly in primetime.
Still, Robinson is not interested in letting the recent success create complacency.
“This is a great win, but you gotta keep on getting better. Gotta keep on getting better,” Robinson said.
That mindset may be just as important as his production.
Robinson understands the attention surrounding the Falcons will continue to grow if they keep winning, but he wants the team focused.
“As a leader of the team, I try to make sure that the guys don’t get complacent,” Robinson said. “We’re always just trying to stay alive, stay humble, and stay focused on the task at hand.”
For now, though, there is no denying what Robinson has become.
When the lights come on, the Falcons keep handing him the football.
And Robinson keeps delivering.

title: 5 Biggest Winners From the Falcons’ Dominant Win Over the Saints
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons delivered one of their most complete performances of the season Monday night, dominating the New Orleans Saints 45-24 in a statement victory at the Caesars Superdome.
Atlanta controlled the game from the opening whistle, combining a dominant rushing attack with timely passing plays and a defensive front that made life difficult for Saints quarterback Tyler Shough. With the Falcons clicking on both sides of the football, several players stood out in a game that quickly turned into a rout.
Here are the biggest winners from Atlanta's Monday night victory.
What more can be said about Bijan Robinson in primetime?
I asked him why he performs so well in primetime games: "Every game to me is a prime-time game," he said. "They're all the same to me in terms of mentality."
Robinson continued his remarkable run under the bright lights, finishing with 19 carries for 145 yards and two touchdowns. He consistently found running lanes and broke through the Saints' defense, helping Atlanta establish control early.
Brian Robinson Jr. provided an excellent complement as his backup. Robinson Jr. finished with 14 carries for 62 yards and three touchdowns, giving the Falcons a powerful one-two punch in the backfield.
The duo helped Atlanta tie a franchise record with five rushing touchdowns in a single game. The Falcons previously did so against the San Diego Chargers on Oct. 21, 1973, and the Carolina Panthers on Nov. 23, 2008.
For Atlanta, the rushing attack was simply overwhelming.
With A.J. Terrell unavailable, C.J. Henderson was asked to step into a larger role at cornerback.
Henderson forced a fumble, played strong coverage throughout the night, and finished with a team-leading 10 tackles. He stayed around the football and gave the Falcons exactly what they needed from him.
Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich previously said Henderson gives Atlanta security at cornerback and said he was excited to see him "show this league exactly who he is now."
Henderson certainly made his case Monday night.
The Falcons defensive front made Tyler Shough uncomfortable for most of the evening.
Cameron Thomas, Brandon Dorlus, Gervon Dexter, and Maason Smith combined for 11 quarterback hits, consistently collapsing the pocket and preventing Shough from getting comfortable. The pressure helped Atlanta's secondary and forced New Orleans into difficult situations throughout the game.
The defensive line delivered a complete performance, helping set the tone for the Falcons' defensive dominance.
Jahan Dotson only caught two passes Monday night, but both were significant.
His biggest contribution came on a 31-yard touchdown reception that extended Atlanta's lead and pushed the game further out of reach. It was Dotson's first touchdown as a Falcon, giving him an early signature moment with his new team.
Atlanta did not need Dotson to produce a massive statistical performance, but when he got opportunities, he made them count.
Michael Penix Jr. played complementary football and gave the Falcons exactly what they needed from their quarterback.
Penix completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards and a touchdown without throwing an interception. He looked comfortable operating the offense and consistently delivered when Atlanta needed a big play. He connected with Drake London, Jahan Dotson, and Kyle Pitts for key gains throughout the night while taking only one sack.
There were a few throws Penix would probably like to have back, but overall, it was another encouraging performance.
More importantly, his connection with London continues to develop.
Through two games, London has 290 receiving yards, up from just 80 yards over his previous 22 games. The chemistry between Penix and London is becoming increasingly difficult for opposing defenses to handle.
On Monday night, Penix looked confident, controlled, and in command as Atlanta cruised to its 45-24 victory.

title: 5 Takeaways From the Falcons’ Statement Win Over the Saints
full_text:
NEW ORLEANS – The Atlanta Falcons crashed the Saints' 20th-anniversary 'Domecoming' party Monday night, smothering New Orleans 45-24.
Here are some takeaways from the Falcons’ dominant win over the Saints.
Anyone who plays the Falcons should know Bijan Robinson, especially when the lights are brightest. The Falcons’ running back came into this game averaging 145.4 yards from scrimmage in prime time, the most in the NFL since 1970.
The Saints clearly missed that assignment, and Robinson nearly matched that historic average in the first half alone. The star running back went untouched on his first touch of the game, carried the ball 59 yards for a score, and finished the half with 108 total yards and a pair of touchdowns.
Robinson finished with 145 yards on the ground, adding another five through the air. His Week 4 totals marked the fourth straight Monday game with 125+ rushing yards, tying him with Eric Dickerson and Emmitt Smith for the longest such streak in NFL history.
As for the Falcons, they moved to 10-1 on Monday Night Football since 2015, and are 2-0 in prime-time games this season.
Since Michael Penix Jr. returned from injury, Tommy Rees’ unit has been completely unrecognizable – for reference, they scored just 16 combined points and had two of the NFL’s five worst EPA/play performances of the season (-0.41 in Week 1 and -0.51 in Week 2).
With Penix, this offense has found an elite gear.
Their 45 points are their most in any regular-season game since 2016, and this performance comes one week after the offense pummeled the Packers for 35 points and 498 total yards last Thursday. This also marked the franchise’s best two-week stretch since 2016.
According to ESPN’s Marc Raimondi, the Falcons’ offense scored more points in the first half (24) than in any half of any game over the last five seasons. They came out of the locker room and kept rolling, finishing with touchdown drives on all three of their second-half possessions.
They finished with 13 plays of 10 yards or more, with Bijan Robinson (145 yards) and Brian Robinson Jr. (62 yards) combining for 207 rushing yards (the second straight week of surpassing the 200-yard mark) and tying the franchise record with five rushing touchdowns. It was the first time since 1973 that two Falcons players each recorded multiple rushing touchdowns in the same game.
Penix showed full control of the offense on Monday, making several clutch throws and unlocking his skill players' potential by pushing the ball downfield.
He finished 15-of-20 for 223 yards and a touchdown, while Drake London had his way with Saints defensive back Kool-Aid McKinstry, including this 37-yard reception in the first half en route to five catches for 96 yards for the night.
Drake London vs Kool-Aid McKinstry pic.twitter.com/NEjaLzNYIF
Jahan Dotson and Kyle Pitts Sr. also got involved for the first time this season, notching long gains of 31 and 28 yards. Dotson’s fourth-quarter reception was his first touchdown as a Falcon and effectively slammed the door on any hope of a Saints comeback.
Seven different players caught a pass Monday, and what a difference a quarterback can make.
Kevin Stefanski would attempt a pair of aggressive conversions in the first half against the Saints.
Their first fourth-down attempt came at the Atlanta 36-yard line, or the equivalent of a 53-yard field goal. With the offense needing seven yards for a first down, the decision initially drew some skepticism. Ultimately, Michael Penix Jr. couldn't get the snap off, and the Falcons took the five-yard delay of game before punting.
Perhaps it was just Stefanski trying to be aggressive and set the tone early in a heated rivalry game, but it could also signal he isn't confident in kicker Nick Folk's leg from that distance.
The NFL’s most accurate kicker over the last three seasons (just three total misses in that span), Folk matched that total over the Falcons’ first two weeks – he missed kicks of 45 and 54 yards against the Steelers and a kick of 53 yards against the Panthers.
The second attempt came at the Saints’ 8-yard line on 4th-and-4. A Penix pass fell incomplete, but Kool-Aid McKinstry was flagged for defensive holding. The Falcons would score on the next play.
With the Falcons leading by seven and having the chance to snatch early momentum, this attempt made much more sense. The aggressive move paid off.
Folk would also connect on a 29-yard field goal later in the first half.
Tyler Shough was the NFL’s third-leading passer coming into this game, and the Saints were scoring 27 points per game, but the Falcons’ defense came ready to shut down this potent offense.
The Saints’ young quarterback was harassed all game, including this sack that pushed the Saints out of field-goal range to close the first half.
SACKED! @xavierwatts6 x @HP113k ESPN | ANF pic.twitter.com/CkAwF1xsPi
Atlanta’s front four punished the New Orleans offensive line, holding the rushing attack to just 15 yards on the ground (50 for the game) and just 10:42 total time of possession in the first half. Shough was sacked only twice, but he rarely had time to drop back without a Falcons defender pushing him off his spot.
The Falcons also forced a Kendre Miller fumble, marking the first time this season that Atlanta has won the turnover battle.
Harold Perkins Jr. was outstanding again for this defense, recording his first sack of the season, tallying a career-high eight tackles, and also playing strong pass coverage . Other standouts included C.J. Henderson (who led the Falcons in tackles (10), forced/recovered a fumble, and defended a pass), Xavier Watts, Samson Ebukam, and the entire front four.
The Falcons did struggle a bit more in the second half, surrendering points on both of their first two defensive possessions that spanned 11:33 of the clock. They would later rally and force a turnover on downs on their third possession, all but cementing the Falcons’ win.
The evening wasn't all sunshine for the Falcons, as both the offense and defense lost a key contributor.
On offense, left tackle Jake Matthews suffered a groin injury, while edge rusher Za’Darius Smith left the game with a concussion/neck injury. Neither returned to action.
Matthews, playing in his 200th career game as a Falcon, is the NFL’s active leader in consecutive games played (199). The iron man was replaced by Michael Jerrell at left tackle, and his health will be pivotal as the team heads into a shortened week. The Falcons have not played a game without him lining up since Sep 14, 2014, ironically, also after Atlanta played New Orleans.
Smith leads the Falcons in sacks (2.5) and ranks third in pressures (11). Losing him for an extended period would be a tough blow, given the depth concerns at edge after the losses of James Pearce Jr. (until Week 9) and Jalon Walker (for the season).
The Falcons won't have much time to recover. Atlanta now faces a shortened week before returning home, making the status of both Matthews and Smith particularly important.

title: Falcons Lose Pair of Crucial Players On Monday Night Football
full_text:
NEW ORLEANS -- The Atlanta Falcons could be without two key players after sustaining injuries during the first quarter of Monday night's game with the New Orleans Saints.
Edge rusher Za'Darius Smith left the game after the opening defensive possession, while left tackle Jake Mathews was lost later in the quarter.
The training staff initially brought out the cart to take Smith off the field, but he left the field under his own power. Smith went back to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion and neck injury.
Smith was later ruled out, and would not return to Monday night's game.
He leads the team in sacks (2.5) and is third in quarterback pressures (11). Losing Smith would be a major blow to the Falcons' front seven, especially given their edge depth concerns. The Falcons are already without James Pearce Jr. (until Week 9) and Jalon Walker (for the season), so any additional losses here would be difficult to overcome.
On offense, Matthews would be another brutal loss. Monday marked his 200th career start in a Falcons uniform, making him just the fourth player in franchise history to reach that milestone. In that span, the durable left tackle has missed just one game. He holds the NFL's longest active streak for games started (199).
It was announced that he suffered a groin injury, and he is questionable to return. In Matthews' place, Michael Jerrell lined up at left tackle.
This article will be updated as more information becomes available.

title: Falcons Reunion With Former LB Won’t Happen Against Saints, Injury Report
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons (1-2) will not face one of their defensive anchors from the previous three seasons when they face the New Orleans Saints (1-2) tonight .
Saints linebacker Kaden Elliss has been ruled out for the Week 4 NFC South rivalry game against his former team with a calf injury, a designation announced last Friday, Oct. 2, three days before the matchup.
Elliss spent the 2023 through 2025 seasons in Atlanta, accruing 380 tackles during his time there. He led the team in tackles during the 2024 and 2025 seasons.
This March, Elliss left the Falcons to rejoin the Saints, who drafted him in the seventh round out of Idaho in 2019. He inked a three-year, $33 million deal to return to New Orleans.
Elliss was a major part of the Saints’ plan to contain Falcons running back Bijan Robinson , who entered Week 4 leading the NFL with 467 scrimmage yards and fresh off a NFC Offensive Player of the Week performance in Atlanta’s 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers .
Elliss’s inside knowledge of the Falcons and anchoring presence in the middle of the Saints’ defense would have been key against arguably the best running back in the NFL.
New Orleans will now likely look to reserve inside linebackers Danny Stutsman and Isaiah Stalbird to help fill in for Elliss’ absence.
Elliss isn't the only player for the Saints who will be missing on Monday night. New Orleans also ruled out edge rushers Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings.  Granderson has 11 tackles and a sack on the season, and Jennings has added seven tackles and a forced fumble.
Fellow linebacker Pete Werner is also listed as questionable for the game with a shoulder injury. Facing Robinson and the Falcons' running game down one linebacker is a daunting challenge on its own, but missing Elliss and Werner could cause big problems for the Saints defense.
The Falcons have linebacker troubles of their own, with Divine Deablo listed as questionable with a hamstring, which could open the door for rookie Harold Perkins Jr. to see more snaps. Perkins has seen time in passing situations, and with his speed, he could be an excellent answer to Saints quarterback Tyler Shough's ability to scramble.
All-time, Atlanta holds a 58-56 head-to-head record in 114 games dating back to the 1967 season.
Falcons versus Saints will kick off at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time from Caesars Superdome on ESPN.
The game will honor 20 years of the Saints’ “Domecoming” when they returned to the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.

title: The Ravens Need A More Potent Pass Rush, Starting This Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens continue to strive to become a drastically better defense than they were a year ago.
The need to get more pressure on the quarterback. Physically impacting the QB more than they have in years remains an area of aspiration and perspiration, but is still lacking production. It’s something that may come naturally with $30M edge signing Trey Hendrickson and $20M defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuikke getting to play meaningful reps together – injuries have precluded that to this point – and perhaps it’s just a matter of time.
But it’s something that must emerge as they face better quarterbacks with more regularity, with a dynamic Falcons offense awaiting them in Atlanta Sunday night. Rookie head coach Jesse Minter is already being somewhat defensive and defiant about what’s transpired thus far . The reality of what’s to come is probably somewhere between the picture he paints and where the team ranks in key pass rush metrics.
The Ravens were not able to get hands on young and vulnerable QB Cam Ward nearly as much as expected on Sunday, though he did often resort to chucking the ball out of bounds.
“They were very protection conscious, I would say,” Minter said of the Titans. “If you go back and watch all the third downs, they are in split-back [formations], chipping both edges. When you rush four against seven, it is going to look like what it looks like, so I thought the guys rushed pretty well overall.
“We can be a little bit more coordinated, and then I thought four or five times where we had opportunities to sack the quarterback, we are either leaving our feet too early or not taking that extra step. So again, I think our defensive line — especially some of the interior guys that we missed a lot during camp — working toward that, and I expect us to have really good days rushing the passer going forward."
The Ravens have a 4.9% sack rate for the season, which is 23rd in the NFL. It was 4.6% last season. So, no one is going to be pumped about that . Pressure is more important, and there has been an uptick there. Baltimore has a 35.1% pressure rate this season, 19th in the NFL; it was at 31.7% last season.
Madubuike is their best interior rusher and it’s not close, and he’s only played two games in over a year. He’s still knocking rust off but can take games over week after week at the top of his powers. Hendrickson was probably more impacted by the finger injury than the team let on, we’ll see how quickly he can return from the procedure he had last week, but his resume is legit.
Hendrickson is generating a 17.5% pressure rate, which is bigtime and far superior than anything we’ve seen in this locker room for a long time. One sack on 80 pass-rush reps isn’t ideal, but the best should be to come (though he will suffer against the run). He also leads the team with 10 hurries.
Tavius Robinson, the chief beneficiary opposite Hendrickson when he is going, leads Baltimore with two sacks and six QB hits. He has a motor and sets the edge the way the Ravens demand. What has been lacking is hybrid defender Kyle Hamilton impacting the QB as much as many expected; Minter barely blitzed last week, so not much opportunity there, and Hamilton has just three pressures on 25 pass rushes this season.
Getting more pressure on Michael Penix Jr. will be vital on Sunday. He is still feeling his way back from a third ACL repair and has a tendency to throw off his back foot some and deliver some turnover worthy throws when under duress. Given that the Falcons are the best run stopping team in the NFL, and the most dominant team running the ball, the Ravens are going to need some turnovers.

title: Zay Flowers Is Doing Things No Ravens WR Has Done Before. Here's Why:
full_text:
Let’s take a moment to celebrate what an audacious and stupendous start Ravens receiver Zay Flowers is having to his season – more explosive than any in franchise history – before we allow for the fact that things are about to change.
Flowers has been as impactful as any skill player in the NFL, he has been a total menace to defenses in the three games he has played while hampered with a hamstring injury, and we must also recognize that he only played one half in Week 1, missed Week 2, was on a tight pitch count Week 3 and then lost starting quarterback Lamar Jackson at halftime of Week 4 and the Ravens took the air out of the ball.
It makes what Flowers, signed to a long-term deal before the season , is doing all the more outlandish. But, with Jackson almost certain to miss a week or two (at least) with an ankle injury and the Ravens’ offensive line/blockers beset by injuries , and the run game going backwards and the schedule ramping up, and Flowers the only cog showing up regularly downfield, his pace is about to diminish.
Maintaining his level of explosion over a full season even with Jackson would be pretty remarkable, and the Ravens are going to have to get more creative with him out in space and in the run game and doing things behind the line of scrimmage with back-up QB Snoop Huntley unable to push the ball downfield like Jackson . Rookie coordinator Declan Doyle has done his best work totally unlocking Flowers and making him a threat in every quadrant of the field in ways like never before., and his usage in the slot has been particularly impactful.
“In our offense, he is going to line up at five different positions,” head coach Jesse Minter said Monday. “So, you can have a game plan for him when he is the outside receiver to maybe take him away, or maybe when he is the slot receiver, but then he is ending up as No. 3 a lot.
“He is ending up on linebackers in zone coverages. He is ending up out of the backfield a few times as we have seen this year. So, I think that is just a credit to Zay to be able to do all that and sort of understand the concepts that he can move around to different spots, and then to Declan, obviously, moving him around.”
Here’s how he’s done it, and where Flowers ranks among the top receivers in the NFL a month into the season (and, again, he’s only truly completed two contests thus far):
Flowers is second in the NFL, averaging 19.6 yards per reception. He is fourth in the NFL at 117.3 yards per game. He is fifth in Yards After the Catch (165) and would be tops had he not missed so much time and been limited to just 56 routes run this far (less than half of teammate Rashod Bateman, for instance, and well off the volume of other top 10 NFL receivers.
Flowers is third in the NFL catching 78% of his passes for a first down or touchdown and he is in truly rarified air in some of the advanced stats that speak to the downfield impact he is making:
Yards Per Route Run: 6.29 – 1st in NFL (1.41 is NFL avg).
Jaxson Smith-Njigba (SEA) is second among qualified receivers at 4.15, a massive chasm
Yards Per Target: 16.00 – 1st in NFL
Tyquan Thornton (KC) is second at 14.1 yards per target, again, well off this pace
The fact Flowers has twice as many receiving yards as any Raven , and everyone knows where the ball is going if it’s going more than eight yards downfield, and starting receiver Ja’Kobi Lane has barely played due to injury, and no one can intervene, is pretty special.
The most significant change in Flowers’s usage is something we told you was coming in the spring: he is a real dervish when he has a two-way go from the slot and he’s always done his best work in the middle of the field and being deployed more often from the slot plays even more into it.
Flowers has been in the slot 60% of the time this season; it was 37% last season. This has meant everything.
He has 14 catches on 16 targets for 282 yards (20.1/rec!) and a touchdown in the slot this season.
Doyle has also put him motion more than ever (27%, not a huge difference from 23% a year ago) and has already put Flowers in the backfield for four snaps this season; he was positioned there just twice all of last season. Everything about this offense is going to be stripped down without Jackson for however long they are without him, but Flowers is already doing things Ravens receivers simply have not done.
