title: Three Key Changes Coming To Ravens Offense With Lamar Jackson Likely Out
full_text:
The Ravens will be preparing as if they do not have MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson the next two weeks. Trust us.
If it turns out that he plays against the Browns in Week 6, great, but as we explained on Monday, when a player of this import leaves a game and does not return and then gets an MRI on his ankle and he is asked to do as much as Jackson does, and we are still in early October, and the team has Super Bowl ambition, that superstar is going to spend at least a week on the sidelines . And the Ravens have already shown the propensity to take the long-view with Ronnie Stanley and Zay Flowers and Trey Hendrickson this season.
So, alas, even more change is coming to an offense that has seen Stanley, the star left tackle, and Flowers, maybe the best receiver in the NFL right now, in and out of games with injuries and that will start yet another new offensive line deployment Sunday night in Atlanta with more injuries taking hold. And it  would be very wise to get real and leave rookie guard Vega Ioane as the starting center . Enough fluctuation is already being dictated by injury.
And this means veteran back-up Snoop Huntley, who stabilized the 2025 season after Jackson went down, will be called into action, offering some of the athletic traits that Jackson employs, but not nearly to the same degree.
“He might not be a ‘win-because of’ quarterback, but he's certainly a ‘win-with quarterback,’” longtime former top GM Marty Hurney told me on “The Daily Flock Show” Tuesday. “He has proven that. And I like Tyler Huntley. I have a lot of confidence in him. So, you know, if I was inside that building, I would just be saying, ‘Listen, you know, when Lamar's ready, he's ready, but let's not push him.’
“‘Let's take our time. We have a great option that we know can win for us, and let's just be smart about this. Because we're 3-1, we're going to be in this thing the whole way and let's just be judicious and make sure that Lamar doesn't come back too quick.”
Huntley, of course, is not close to Jackson and almost no one in the history of this game is. His absence will require significant recalibrations, and here are three key changes rookie Declan Doyle will make against a tough Atlanta team Sunday night, with the Ravens also dealing with the loss of premier blocking tight end Durham Smythe for the season:
Jackson is leading the NFL with 10.1 yards per attempt; Huntley is below six yards per attempt in his career. That ain’t changing with a makeshift OL up front and at a time when the run game is suffering and falling behind the stick chasing low-percentage attempts doesn’t make much sense.
Huntley is far more adept spraying the ball around in the screen game and expect to see more of a reliance on YAC (Flowers is the only regular pass catcher getting any so far this season, with Derrick Henry, not seen much in the pass game, second on the team in yards after the catch, somehow).
The Ravens OL strength is on the perimeter and the passing game and running game must lean into that , and the ball is not going to be carrying nearly as much downfield. The Falcons are likely to blitz more than Baltimore has seen given its going to be QB 2 and a OL-in-progress, and sharp screens and finding the hots out quicky will be everything. Also, to that end …
The Falcons are going to attack as we noted and while beating them with 50-yard throws downfield might not be in the cards with Huntley, finding some chunk yards with playmakers like Flowers out of the backfield in the ground game on the boundary makes too much sense to ignore. Atlanta is allowing just 2.7 yards/rush, ridiculously effective (no one else is below 3.2/carry), and this will require some creative workarounds to reach the desired volume in the run game against a defense that is showing out like this.
Rashod Bateman and Devontez Walker catching balls behind the line of scrimmage or getting end arounds is something else we might see. Atlanta’s 72% success rate against the run is obscene but Baltimore much show conviction with it.
No one thinks about him as a pass catcher and he’s barely seen the field on third down in his career – even at his peak prime – unless it was a short-yardage situation. But more targets for him are in order. If the Falcons blitz as much as we suspect, that naturally calls for Justice Hill in the backfield, but they need Henry to bleed the clock and shorten the game and try to grind that defensive front down.
Perhaps we see more pony packages with both backs on the field; they have been sporadic-at-best in the past (former offensive coordinator Todd Monken used them in six games during his two years in charge), as Doyle has yet to attempt it. Henry has caught all seven of his targets for 44 yards this season; he had 15 catches for 150 yards all of last season and 13 for 193 in 2024.
The pace of usage in the pass game is already trending up and the way the Falcons play will likely lend itself to more targets.

title: Ravens Lose Premier Blocking TE Durham Smythe For Season As Injuries Mount
full_text:
Ravens blocking tight end Durham Smythe, who had taken on a very significant hybrid role in this offense, will not play again this season with an Achilles tear according to reports.
That always appeared to be the case Sunday, when he suffered the injury against the Titans, and while head coach Jesse Minter would not commit to specifics when he met the media Monday, NFL Network is reporting that an MRI confirmed what seemed likely when he initially went down. Smythe was handling essential duties at the line scrimmage, functioning as the primary blocking tight end, while also serving as a fullback in the ground game and was also split out as a wide receiver on occasion. He was doing many of the “Joker” responsibilities that matter so much in an offense that was inspired by longtime NFL coach Sean Payton (as Payton explained to us this offseason ).
With Baltimore’s offensive line under siege from injuries and ineffectiveness and the ground game going backward in recent weeks for top back Derrick Henry, the injury comes at a terrible time. Smythe was particularly impactful in the backfield running the ball out of the gun (the Ravens have been more effective there than under center), and he is also the only player on the offense who had past experience with rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, playing for him in Chicago last season.
The Ravens expect MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson to miss at least a week or two with an ankle injury, meaning back-up Snoop Huntley takes over at a time when personnel issues are becoming more acute. Starting receiver Ja’Kobi Lane remains on Injured Reserve and Minter did not sound overly optimistic about fellow rookie Adam Randall, a running back who could also handle some “Joker” duties being activated off IR to face the surging Falcons Sunday.
Smythe was one of the few free-agent additions the Ravens made anywhere on offense – resources were poured into the defense – and the team will have to lean on veteran blocker Nick Vannett, who is on the practice squad, while rookie ends Matthew Hibner (whose blocking is better than expected) and Josh Cuevas will have even more asked of them.
It comes as the Ravens are juggling the offensive line, with injuries to centers and guards becoming acute, and the team wise to leave rookie guard Vega Ioane at center and figure things out from there.
“I think Durham has done a great job with our offense and coming over really with Dec,” Minter said on Monday. “Having the knowledge and being a problem solver on the field, being a guy that can line up in a bunch of different spots within the blocking schemes and the pass schemes, his value has certainly been good.
"Again, we have a deep room there. We have a bunch of guys, and it may be an opportunity for somebody else. Again, it is going to be our job as a coaching staff and the position coach and the coordinator to make sure we are doing the things that those guys can do. “
Smythe was a vital contributor in a Week 1 win, and in Week 2 Doyle didn’t lean on him nearly as much with an 11-point lead, saying he was interested in the development of his young tight ends, as Baltimore ended up blowing that game to New Orleans despite being a heavy favorite.
With the Ravens unable to generate more than 3.2/carry on running back runs the past two weeks with their interior OL under siege, this is a major weapon for Doyle wiped away. The Ravens have an Rushing Expected Points Added of +0.80 with Smythe on the field and -4.8 without. They have a Throwing EPA of 29.98 with him on the field (helping leaky protection) and 19.44 without.
The Falcons lead the NFL allowing a paltry 2.7 yards/carry. Smythe, 31, signed a one-year, $3M deal with the Ravens. this offseason.

title: Unsung Heroes From The Ravens’ Week 4 Win Over Titans
full_text:
In Week 4, the Baltimore Ravens came out on top in a home regular-season game for the first time in over 10 months on Sunday, when they held on to secure a 24-18 victory over the still-winless Tennessee Titans . They were one of just two AFC North teams to emerge victorious this past week, putting them in a tie atop the division standings with the upstart Cleveland Browns.
In a game where they were heavily favored to win, the Ravens built up a three-score lead before a rash of injuries caused them to play much more conservatively in the second half. Even though the Titans showed a lot of fight and were able to move the ball at times and get stops, the Ravens made more when it counted and are now 3-1 as a result.
The Ravens were able to secure the victory thanks to some underrated yet impactful performances from a handful of well-known starters and some of their less-heralded players making plays on both sides of the ball.
With his close friend and the face of the franchise, Lamar Jackson, sidelined after sustaining an ankle injury that might not have kept him out of a more competitive game, the former Pro Bowl reserve stepped up and finished the game in his place. The Ravens were up 24-7 at halftime, so Huntley just needed to help the offense chew up the clock and take care of the ball. They achieved both goals under his stewardship for the final two quarters as he went 8-of-9 for 63 passing yards and a passer rating of 95.8 and ran twice for 18 yards before taking a couple of kneeldowns.
"I think 'Snoop' as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs and be able to make plays on third down," head coach Jesse Minter said "[I] thought he did a nice job on a couple of the keepers yesterday in getting yards. And so, he just gives you that ability to kind of make plays with his feet. He has kind of got a really cool, good mentality to be that guy."
After primarily playing special teams last week in his 2026 debut following a faster-than-expected recovery from the torn ACL that ended his promising rookie season, the second-year pro saw more action on defense in this game. Even though he still played a limited role in response to some of the Titans' 12 personnel packages, he still made his presence felt and made some impactful plays. His lone tackle came on a solo late in the third quarter, where he perfectly read and blew up a screen to Pro Bowl running back Tony Pollard for no gain.
LOVED seeing Teddye Buchanan make this play. Teddye was having a great rookie year prior to his injury and it's good to see him healthy again. pic.twitter.com/nzzlbeGJse
Buchanan helped force a third straight three-and-out in the fourth quarter when he went unblocked on a blitz call with an unabated path to what should've been his first career full sack after recording a half as a rookie, but he completely whiffed on the attempt. Nonetheless, the pressure forced Cam Ward to move off his spot, and he wound up throwing an incomplete pass after defensive tackle Nnamdi nearly got a sack but forced a deep incompletion instead. He played just 11 snaps on defense and finished as the Ravens' fifth-highest-graded defender according to Pro Football Focus , with an overall grade of 66.6.
"I think as Teddye has come back and proven to be now capable of playing some more snaps, that we will certainly try to find ways to get use out of both him and Trenton [Simpson]," Minter said.
The sixth-year veteran came up clutch for both quarterbacks in this game by reeling in both of his targets for 46 receiving yards, the second-highest total on the team. He got open for a Jackson on a second-and-long scramble drill in the second quarter and picked up 28 yards on a catch-and-run and in the second quarter.
#Gophers Rashod Bateman with the catch for a 28 yard play for the Ravens #pROWGophers #GophersinthePros 📺NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube pic.twitter.com/CmJOzAJ50n
On what should've been the Ravens' fifth scoring drive of the game in the fourth quarter, he connected with Huntley on an 18-yard gain on third down to extend the possession that would eventually stall out and end with a missed Tyler Loop field goal from 40 yards out. Bateman finished as the Ravens' fifth-highest-graded offensive player with an overall PFF grade of 72.

title: Lamar Jackson Unlikely To Play Ravens Primetime Matchup vs. Falcons With Minor Ankle Sprain
full_text:
When the Baltimore Ravens take the field at Mercedes-Benz Stadium for their first nationally televised night game in Week 5 against the suddenly surging Atlanta Falcons, it's likely that they will be doing so without franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson .
The two-time league MVP had his ankle rolled up while getting sacked on the second-to-last play of the first half in the team's Week 4 home win over the Tennessee Titans . Although he remained in uniform and on the sideline for most of the second half, he did not re-enter the game at any point before heading back into the locker room in the final minutes of the 24-18 victory.
According to a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapopor t, the testing that Jackson, who's been off to a sizzling start to the season, revealed that he suffered an ankle sprain of minor severity, but now only gives him an "outside chance" to be available for Sunday Night Football.
#Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is dealing with a sprained ankle that gives him only an outside chance to play Sunday against the #Falcons , sources say. Jackson could end up missing multiple games based on how rehab goes, but the injury is not considered long-term or surgical. pic.twitter.com/pIKU5IfA3J
"Jackson could end up missing multiple games based on how rehab goes, but the injury is not considered long-term or surgical," Rapoport wrote.
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter didn't divulge any specific diagnosis or details about the nature of his star signal caller's injury when addressing the media immediately after the team's win this past Sunday or in his weekly Monday presser the following day. However, the report echoes sentiments he expressed in both sessions.
"I don't know the chances yet. We're still gathering a lot of information and the imaging and things like that," Minter said. "He's just dealing with a little bit of an ankle [injury] and we'll see where that shakes out. Full trust and confidence in him that when it's ready to roll that we'll roll and go from there...I really don't think it's going to be crazy long-term, but we'll see what happens."
Jackson is off to another MVP pace to start this season through three and a half games. He has thrown for 967 passing yards, six touchdowns to one interception, completed 70.8% of his passes and produced a passer rating of 119.6. Jackson also leads the league with 10.1 yards gained per attempt, 10.9 adjusted yards gained per attempt and 14.2 yards gained per completion. As a runner, mostly on scrambles, he has picked up 144 rushing yards on 19 carries for nine first downs and a touchdown.
If Jackson can't suit up against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday next week, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley has proved in the past, as recently as last year, that he is capable of leading them to big wins against formidable opponents.
Two of the Ravens' most impressive wins from the 2025 season came with the seventh-year veteran at the helm, starting in place of the three-time First Team All-Pro selection. Both were must-win games, coincidentally, against NFC opponents, with the first being in Week 8 at home in a 30-16 triumph over the Chicago Bears and the second was in Week 17 on the road and resulted in a 41-24 victory over the Green Bay Packers.
While both instances also featured heavy doses of star running back Derrick Henry, Huntley made plays with his arm and legs in each as well. He had five or fewer incompletions and threw for a touchdown in both and ran eight times for 50-plus yards as well.
In the first six years of his career, Huntley has compiled a record of 7-9 as a spot starter, the bulk of which has come with the Ravens, who he originally signed as an undrafted free agent out of Utah in 2020.
The seventh start of his career just so happened to be for Baltimore and came against Atlanta in Week 16, and he led the team to a 17-9 victory. His development as a passer and all-around player at the position has come a long way since then, so they still shouldn't be counted out heading into this primetime Battle of the Birds either way.
"You just look at what [Huntley] has done over the last few years, and [where he has] been in games like that, been in must-win situations and got the job done," Minter said Monday. "He has played well. The guys believe in him, and I think that is as important as anything. The guys have a lot of confidence in him to be able to go out there and do it."

title: Ravens Must Prioritize Pass Protection, Live With Struggling Run Game For Now
full_text:
The NFL is a league of tradeoffs and constant adjustments.
No other sport demands more from a physical standpoint and injuries are a weekly factor and personnel problem-solving is never-ending. The best front offices find a way to prioritize the overarching principles that foster winning to thrive under roster duress and understand risk/reward. They know when to tempt the football gods and when to back off of certain goals in order to live to fight another day.
Nowhere is this juggling act more critical than when the quarterback position becomes involved, and for a franchise that boasts one as uniquely historic as Lamar Jackson, striking the right balance and being willing to accept certain inefficiencies and problems in other areas in order to prioritize the health of the QB is paramount. The Ravens find themselves at one of these forks in road, again, in Week 5.
Jackson, who somehow doesn’t have a real contract beyond this season in a way that peers like Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen always do, being asked to play behind an experimental offensive line, needs to feel a certain way about his ability to explode and escape and be the best athlete on the field in order to operate at a genius level. Dealing with an ankle injury that kept him out of the second half of Sunday’s 24-18 win and required an MRI on Monday, is immediately problematic.
And given Baltimore’s current issues with the run game , and sorting out that offensive line, and finding dependable downfield weapons outside of Zay Flowers (playing out of his mind right now), it would not be surprising to see the Ravens be cautious with this situation so early in the season. They have already played the long game in handling early-season injuries to Flowers and left tackle Ronnie Stanley and top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson, and I suspect they do the same with Jackson this week.
This organization is also going to reinforce, throughout the coaching rooms and in game-planning sessions and with the decisions about how personnel is deployed on game day, that protecting Jackson and finding ways to keep the pass game humming, even at the expense of sagging efficiencies on the ground, is a new way of life as they sort through the litany of injuries on offense.
As odd as it seems for running back Derrick Henry to be this bogged down at or behind the line of scrimmage after tearing up the league his first two seasons in Baltimore, protecting the A Gap from penetrating linemen and linebackers is Job No. 1 ; allowing rookie coordinator Declan Doyle’s scheme to exploit defenses for explosive plays has become a primary hallmark, The Ravens may have to live with an inability to run the ball between the tackles at all in order to maintain a modicum of pass protection required to keep Jackson and Flowers dominating when they do get to play together.
The Ravens are not used to being a below-average team moving the ball on the ground with running backs, but that’s where they are. And it may be where they are stuck as ever-shifting five-man units figure things out at the line of scrimmage and with potent blocking tight end Durham Smythe now injured, too.
Here’s where the Ravens stand entering Week 5 in running back production:
2026                    2024-25
Yds/Carry :                   4.2 (11th)             5.4 (1st)
Yds B4 Contact :         1.17 (17th)          1.86 (2nd)
3rd Down Conv :         25% (24th)          61% (4th)
The problem is truly acute trying to advance the ball up the gut. There is nowhere for Henry to go. Here’s how the last three weeks of RB runs up the middle compared to Henry’s first two seasons here:
2026                2024-25
Yds/Carry :                   5.1 (4th)               3.4 (18th)
Yds B4 Contact: 1.52 (10th)           0.85 (22nd)
As this OL has fluctuated at center and guard, the under-center rushing game has dried up  (50 rushes from RBs for just 180 yards the last three weeks at 3.6/carry). But shotgun runs have continued to provide some burst and opportunities to the perimeter, running behind the tackles , and pitch plays to Henry offered some relief against the Titans, and leaning into more of that makes sense.
Using some of the under-center stuff as a play-action decoy, absolutely. But the Ravens can’t be slaves to some of their preseason aspirational goals, evolution is everything, and there are many, many ways to get multiple with run looks. There are no easy solutions, however, when an offensive line is negating the possibility of pushing the ball downfield . And back-up Snoop Huntley is nothing close to Jackson.

title: Ravens Penalty Problems Only Getting Worse
full_text:
Penalties are becoming a plague for the Ravens.
It tends to come with the territory sometimes with new coaching staffs, as much as they don’t want to hear it and don’t want it correlated to them. It’s a fact. It's a problem in Baltimore
When there is sweeping change in this league, especially after a coach manages to stay here roughly 20 years prior (like John Harbaugh), there are going to be hiccups and missteps and issues the following September. But now it’s October and the Ravens injury situation continues to deepen , making the margins between winning and losing even tighter, even against winless teams like Tennessee, and racking up 13 penalties for 130 yards at home, without the crowd being an excuse, is no way to go through an NFL season.
For the Ravens' offense, where things are decidedly new from a schematic and language and philosophical standpoint, and the pre-snap ambitions have changed and cadence has been introduced and tempo is shifting and more motion is in use, the degree of difficulty gets jacked up even higher. And when you add new starting offensive lines every week and linemen are out of position and going through three centers in four games, the propensity for disaster is even higher .
And so here rookie head coach Jesse Minter finds himself, exactly where he did not want to be , among the NFL leaders in far too many penalty categories and having to preach focus and discipline to a largely-veteran team, and, let’s keep it real, already sending some messages to rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle through his remarks after Sunday’s win over the Titans about all those pre-snap devices he fancies so much and the role they seem to be playing for an offense that can’t stop derailing due to penalties.
“It sort of goes back to the comment about who you have and what they’re good at,” Minter said at his Monday press conference. “And whether it’s young guys who haven’t been in it as much, all that stuff you’re always looking at and always trying to find that perfect balance … So you want to use motion and shifts and cadences as a weapon … but we need to find that really good balance.”
With Lamar Jackson dealing with an ankle injury and more backups being thrust into starting roles with injuries taking hold throughout the offensive line, and 20 percent of this roster invested in rookies, there may be some explanations for the confusion and struggles. But this is the NFL, they get to pick their players, and it’s a $365M payroll that shouldn’t be undermining itself from week to week.
The Ravens are leading the league in a way no one wants to lead the league. Their 39 total penalties are third-most in the NFL, and their 24 offensive penalties are tied for the most in the NFL and the teams they are clustered with (Chargers and Packers) are two of the most disappointing offenses in the league.
Here are some other ugly truths that are driving Minter crazy:
12 Opposing 1st Downs From Penalties: 2nd most
-6.60 Offensive Penalty Expected Points Added: 30th
Scaling things back can help on offense. Getting some solidified personnel on the offensive line couldn’t hurt. But this trend continues to go in the wrong direction, and the schedule is ramping up into the middle of the season.

title: 14 Winners and 3 Losers From Ravens' Resilient Home Win Over Titans
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens established their first win streak in Week 4 of the 2026 regular season on Sunday by holding on in a 24-18 triumph over the Tennessee Titans.
They came into this game favored to come out on top by 10-plus points and were well on their way to covering that spread before they had several starters go down and not return with injuries. While they weren't able to maintain their double-digit halftime lead by the end, they made enough key plays in all three phases of the game to snap their four-game home losing skid.
Here are several Ravens players and coaches who stepped up and showed out, and others who made some costly mistakes from coaching and execution standpoints.
While the future Hall of Famer didn't go off against his former team in their first meeting since they opted to move on from him after the 2023 season, he still plowed his way into the end zone at least once for the fourth week in a row, and he got the win in the end. Henry led the Ravens with 73 rushing yards on 23 carries, caught a pair of passes for six receiving yards, and helped grind out a time-consuming drive in the fourth quarter.
The fourth-year pro continued the impressive start to his breakout season with another highly impactful outing. He led the team in total tackles with nine, had a pass breakup and recorded his first career interception on the Titans' second play from scrimmage, which set up the Ravens' offense for a short first scoring drive.
The Ravens' franchise signal caller was having one hell of a first half before he suffered an ankle injury while taking an ill-advised sack on the team's penultimate play. Jackson was carved up the Titans' defense through the air, going 15-of-20 for 222 passing yards and two touchdowns, with a passer rating of 144.2 and picked up 20 yards on two carries. His passing yardage total in two quarters matched Titans quarterback Cam Ward's total from all four quarters.
The second-year pro stepped up in a big way with four-time Pro Bowl veteran edge rusher Trey Hendrickson out after undergoing finger surgery. He led the Ravens with three quarterback hits and was generating consistent pressure on Ward, including the near-sack that led to Simpson's interception. His six pressures and a 32% pass rush win rate were both the highest marks on the team as well.
The two-time Pro Bowler continued on his track to becoming a First or Second Team All Pro selection with another highly productive outing. Before Jackson went out with an injury, he was on pace for another career day with over 100 receiving yards in the first half for the second time this year. He finished with team highs in targets (10), receptions (8) and receiving yards (118) and scored his second touchdown of the season.
TOUCHDOWN @ZayFlowers !!!!! TUNE IN ON @NFLonCBS and @paramountplus . pic.twitter.com/2NaRTSKXJT
Playing in his first home game since he suffered what ended up being a season-ending neck injury last year, the two-time Pro Bowler had a massive impact as a pass rusher and run defender. He led Ravens defensive linemen with four total tackles, including three solos, one of which was a key stop to complete a goal-line stand and turn the ball over on downs. His two quarterback hits were the second-most on the team, as were his five pressures and 19.2% pass rush win rate.
Nnamdi Madubuike got quick penetration on the Ravens' 4th-down goal-line stop, then held off the Titans blocker with one arm while making the tackle with the other. Awesome work by the whole D-line on this play and great to see Nnamdi back playing at a high level. pic.twitter.com/vqaq5cQZMj
The three-time Pro Bowler recorded five receptions for just 27 receiving yards, but he picked up some key drive-extending first downs, scored his first touchdown of the season and reached 500 career receptions by the end of the game.
5️⃣ 0️⃣ 0️⃣ pic.twitter.com/bHtpAy6d60
The undrafted rookie made the most of the first defensive snaps of his career by coming up clutch with a huge sack late in the fourth quarter to set up a third and long with two minutes left in the game.
The first-round rookie made his first career start at center despite being a natural guard and passed the test with flying colors. Going up against one of the best interior defensive linemen in the league, Jeffrey Simmons, he was part of the collective effort that limited the four-time Pro Bowler to just one pressure on 32 pass-rush snaps, according to Next Gen Stats.
The three-time All Pro was his usually highly impactful and consistently disruptive self once again, making plays on the ball and ball carriers alike. He recorded the second-most total tackles with seven, including a team-high six solos, broke up a pass and forced a key fumble on a punch-out just before halftime.
Safety @kyledhamilton_ forces the fumble!! Tune in on @NFLonCBS and @paramountplus . pic.twitter.com/qdlmWvtdvZ
While the second-year specialist didn't end on a high note by missing a 40-yarder way wide left, it shouldn't overshadow the fact that he scored what ended up being their last points of the game by drilling a 64-yarder as time expired in the first half. In doing so, he not only set a new career high, but it also marked the second-longest field goal in franchise history and set a record for the longest made at their home stadium.
TYLER LOOP 64-YARD FIELD GOAL!!! Tune in on @NFLonCBS and @ParamountPlus . pic.twitter.com/7OK4uup6fN
The second-year pro had his best game of the season to date, in which he tackled exceptionally well in space and with authority, both on defense and on special teams. He tied Hamilton for the most solo tackles on the team with six and was in the right place at the right time to recover a fumble and an onside kick attempt.
The rookie punter was a field-flipping weapon once again, helping the Ravens win the battle for field possession by pinning the Titans' offense back in their own 20-yard line on four of his six punts, including a long of 56 yards.
The first-year play-caller was in his bag once again throughout this game with his play designs and sequencing, even after Jackson went down, but the first half was truly another masterclass. He did a great job scheming up ways for Flowers and several other weapons to get open, and they still nearly posted 400 yards of total offense.
Declan Doyle shows Wildcat with Derrick Henry, motions Lamar Jackson back under center, quick snaps, and Mark Andrews breaks wiiiiide open for a touchdown. Diabolical work by Doyle. 😈 pic.twitter.com/Iej7ENL5fr
In addition to Jackson, the Ravens had three other starters and prominent role players leave the game with injuries and didn't return. The other three included four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Marlon Humphrey (calf), offensive guard Andrew Vorhees (foot), who was making his first start of the season, and veteran blocking tight end Durham Smythe (Achilles). While Jackson was spotted leaving the stadium wearing a protective boot on his left foot, he was the only one of the banged-up bunch whom head coach Jesse Minter sounded the most optimistic about, even saying that they considered having him re-enter the game in the second half before ultimately deciding not to risk further injury.
The Ravens continued to be one of the most penalized teams in the league on Sunday when they hit the double-digit accepted-flag threshold for the second time this year, recording season highs in both penalties (13) and penalty yardage (131). They've been their own worst enemy on offense, especially with pre-snap procedural penalties that set them back before they can get started and committing unnecessary holds or drifting downfield that negate big gains on runs, scrambles and screens.
The 10th-year veteran saw his most extensive playing time of the season to date after Humphrey went out with a calf injury in the first half and was targeted early and often by Ward in the passing game. He gave up a handful of 10-plus-yard completions for first downs and was called for a…

title: Ravens Reveal Concerning Status on Lamar Jackson After Week 4 Injury
full_text:
The Ravens are preparing this week as if quarterback, Lamar Jackson might not be able to face the Falcons, with head coach Jesse Minter still speaking in very cryptic terms about the superstar’s ankle injury, while it also sounds like rookie guard Vega Ioane has a strong chance to stay at center for at least another week.
Minter, a rookie coach still having to sort through a lot of personnel issues, would be wise not to further complicate his job by letting Ioane continue to rep at center no matter who his quarterback is. Jackson, who did not play in the second half as reserve Snoop Huntley took over, got an MRI on his ankle Monday. The two-time MVP is a unique talent who generally needs to feel very good about his ability to burst and escape and it has not been uncommon for him to miss time for these types of injuries.
The Ravens have taken the long-view approach to potentially nagging injuries to left tackle Ronnie Stanley, top receiver Zay Flowers and top edge rusher Trey Hendrickson already this season, and Minter’s tone seemed to connote that possibility in his Monday press conference. Minter wouldn’t commit to any timetable for Jackson and said the team was still “gathering a lot of information” from his MRI.
“We’ll see where that shakes out,” Minter said, adding, “I really don’t think it’s going to be crazy long-term, but we’ll see what happens.”
Minter did not offer an update on blocking tight end Durham Smythe (Achilles), who has proven to be a vital cog in all aspects of the offense at the line of scrimmage, or corner Marlon Humphrey (calf) and guard Andrew Vorhees (foot), who also left the 24-18 win over the Titans and did not return.
No matter what the Ravens decide at center – again, moving Ioane will open them up to significant criticism given how suspect A-gap pass protection was prior to this rookie taking over – they are potentially going to have to shuffle starting guards, again, with Vorhees in doubt and youngster Emery Jones Jr. stepping up Sunday. Ioane basically shutdown Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, arguably the most disruptive interior defender in the NFL the last two seasons, on the pass rush and had no significant issues snapping the ball.
“I thought it was really impressive for him to play that position … to have one full week to prepare to play those elite defensive tackles they have, and to play the way he did,” Minter said. Outside of a “couple of snap infractions,” he’d like to have back, Minter didn’t offer much of a critique (nor should he).
Minter did not explicitly commit to a starter for Week 5, and intimated the team is continuing to look at options to bolster offensive line personnel after adding two journeymen to the practice squad last week.
“He’s proven he’s definitely one of our best interior linemen, if not our best interior lineman,” Minter said, “and wherever he plays we’ll feel really good about.”
Minter also reiterated a message from post-game Sunday, that the limited scope of the offense in the second half after Jackson was injured was more about the rain and playing conditions and continued injuries the team was dealing with and not an indication of what it believes Huntley is capable of. Of course, the profile of the passing game – and in particular the ability to connect with Zay Flowers all over the field - will not be the same with Huntley.
The back-up is far more conservative pushing the ball downfield , and is not nearly as explosive as Jackson keeping the ball and running, though he is plenty mobile. Jackson is leading the NFL at 10.1 yards/attempt this season, while Huntley is at 5.9/attempt for his career.
“He’s been in must-win situations and got the job done,” Minter said of Huntley. “He’s played well, the guys believe in him, and that’s as important as anything.”

title: Buffalo Bills Named Logical Trade Suitor For Future Hall of Fame Edge Rusher
full_text:
Buffalo Bills edge rusher Greg Rousseau has been electric through four games of the 2026 season.
Rousseau is off to a red-hot start after notching six sacks so far and he is well on his way to a career-best season that shows the Bills made the right call in extending him last offseason.
However, the Bills could use more pass-rush juice, as they have 10 sacks in total and only 2.5 of those have come from edge rushers not named Greg Rousseau.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox listed Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack as a potential trade candidate , and he believes the Bills could come calling if he's on the block.
"The Chargers won't be eager to move Mack as long as they believe they can rebound," Knox said. "If they believe their season is lost, however, they could save $8 million in cap space by moving him."
"Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, San Francisco 49ers," Knox added.
Off to an 0-4 start, history is against the Chargers rebounding and making the playoffs, as the 1992 San Diego Chargers are the only team in league history to accomplish that feat.
Mack has already flirted with retirement before , and chances are his odds of hanging up his cleats will increase with another NFL season under his belt.
Knowing that, the Chargers would be silly not to consider trading Mack and getting something for him before he departs Los Angeles for nothing in 2027.
The Bills don't have a dire situation at edge rusher, but that may change if Rousseau can't keep up what we have to believe is an unsustainable pace.
Maybe Bradley Chubb, Michael Hoecht and T.J. Parker can pick up the slack if Rousseau falls off, but we can't say they will be able to for sure.
Mack is long in the tooth but he's still got plenty of gas left in the tank. Through four games this season, Mack has posted three sacks, which would rank second on the Bills. Last season, the future Hall of Famer had 5.5 in just 12 games.
Putting Mack opposite Rousseau would give the Bills one of the more potent edge rusher duos in the NFL and would also put Buffalo in better position to compete for a Super Bowl.
In terms of cost, Mack shouldn't be too expensive with the entire league knowing he may only be a half-year rental because of the fact that he could very well retire in 2027.
Knowing that, it may only cost a fourth-round pick to acquire him, or maybe a third in a deal that features a pick swap. The Bills have their third- and fourth-round picks the next two years, so that's a price general manager Brandon Beane can afford.

title: Bills Well Behind Rest of NFL in Critical Offensive Stat That Was Costly vs. Patriots
full_text:
Despite their current record, the Buffalo Bills have had several miscues over the course of the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season.
And, while some observers overlooked those mishaps in September, maybe they shouldn’t have: everything hasn’t been hunky-dory.
Plays that nearly cost the Bills on the road in Week 1 against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium, as well as at home in Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers at Highmark Stadium, caught up to first-year head coach Joe Brady’s squad this past Sunday against the New England Patriots in Orchard Park, resulting in a critical loss in the AFC East.
Even if some fans may not want to admit to the fact, it was a game that had massive playoff implications written all over it for Buffalo in spite of the calendar only reading October . . . and the players let it slip through their fingertips, which is awfully similar to last fall when the team fell short to New England at home in primetime on NBC ’s Sunday Night Football in Week 5.
The parallels between the two contests and subsequent results are uncanny.
However, instead of entering this October’s game against the Patriots on a four-game winning streak that included outscoring their opponents by a total count of 133-90, this time around the Bills were heading into the matchup on a three-game run after outscoring their opponents 101-78 through the month of September.
And, although it might not seem like much to some, the National Football League is a game of inches, so going from an average margin of victory of 10.8 points in 2025 prior to the first Patriots’ matchup down to an average of 7.7 points per contest in 2026 is undeniably notable.
With Jim Leonhard’s young defensive unit still adjusting to a new scheme on the other side of the operation, the room for error is seemingly smaller this year for quarterback Josh Allen and his teammates this season, and that proved to be the case once again on Sunday against New England.
This time, though, the “smoke detectors” that Brady had been referring to since the preseason finally sounded the alarms over the weekend, and it’s something that needs to be fixed in a hurry.
One such area that appears to be in need of some serious change?
The team’s two-point conversion efficiency, which wound up costing Buffalo late in the fourth quarter following a go-ahead, 34-yard touchdown pass from Allen to third-year wide receiver Keon Coleman with 4:27 remaining in the game.
After the trip across the goal line, Buffalo led 26-21 and chose to try a two-point attempt in order to make it a seven-point affair, which could’ve made things a bit more difficult for the Patriots on the other side.
The result, though, was an incomplete pass from Allen to wide receiver Joshua Palmer, which really had no chance of completion at all. And, what’s even more frustrating is the fact that film review shows Buffalo’s gunslinger missed tight end Dalton Kincaid on the play, who was wide open right in front of his quarterback’s eyes after the playmaker initially stayed in to block.
Instead of the simple toss for a completion to Kincaid, however, Allen chose to try and fit a ball in between two defenders in the back of the end zone to Palmer, and  . . .  it was a bit of a frustrating head-scratcher for fans, to say the least.
“You study what you expect to get from the defense, kind of what their two-point situations (have previously) presented defensively, (and) you hope to put together a play that you feel is going to be successful against that,” Bills’ offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr. said Monday at One Bills Drive .
“There’s also times where, as a coaching staff, you’re studying the two-point plays that are being run around the league and see if they fit with your personnel. But, obviously, we’ve got to do a better job there.”
With that said, should it have really been that much of a surprise to anyone invested in the critical moment that Buffalo failed to convert?
Although Carmichael Jr. is in his first season as offensive coordinator in Western New York in conjunction with first-year head coach Joe Brady, when looking at the recent stats from the Bills, maybe the failure shouldn’t have been much of a shocker to anyone at all, even in spite of the addition of Brady’s new offensive counterpart.
Although all 32 teams in the NFL collectively had the lowest two-point conversion success rate in the last 15 years heading into the 2025 season at just 41%, Buffalo was well below that rate last year.
According to the TeamRankings’ database , the Bills were just 28th in the league one season ago when it came to successful two-point conversions at a rate of just 22.22%, which was down from a success rate of 75% in 2023 and 50% in 2024.
Furthermore, what’s even more concerning?
Well, since Buffalo has now failed on both of its two-point attempts so far this season after Sunday’s screwup against New England , the team’s now just 2-of-11 on two-point tries since September 2025, and one of those successful tries occurred when former backup quarterback Mitchell Trubisky was in the game against the New York Jets in Week 18 last season.
Needless to say, the Bills are trending in a terrible direction when it comes to the backpocket play, and it’s not something to take lightly.
Who knows when the team might need to convert in such a critical moment later on this year?
It might even happen in the playoffs . . . if Buffalo can reach that point of the season.
And, although it’s unclear exactly what needs to happen in order to correct the issue moving forward, utilizing players like the previously mentioned Coleman, as well as Kincaid, who were both drafted in part due to their supposed red-zone skills, might be a good start.
Using Allen’s trusty legs and overwhelming brute strength would be helpful, too.
For some reason, seemingly none of those players have been utilized as much as they should be in that area of the field throughout their careers, though, at least not when it pertains to the two-point attempts, anyway.
With that in mind, something’s got to give. Points are precious in the NFL, and Buffalo simply can’t continue its struggles in this area going forward.

title: None of Brandon Beane's Last Three First-Round Draft Picks Helped Bills vs. Patriots
full_text:
It may be time to face a serious conversation about general manager Brandon Beane's first-round draft results since 2022.
The Buffalo Bills suffered a 29-26 divisional home loss to the New England Patriots in Week 4, and none of the team's three most-recent first-round draft picks were there to step up in key situations.
In fact, one of those picks hasn't even been in the building since 2024. The Bills cut bait on 2022 first-round cornerback Kaiir Elam following his awful performance in the 2024 AFC Championship Game loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
As for Buffalo's 2023 and 2025 first-round selections, both tight end Dalton Kincaid and cornerback Maxwell Hairston were on the field for what was a deflating October 4 loss.
Let's take a closer look at each of Beane's last three first-round picks below. Remember, the Bills traded out of Round 1 in both 2024 and 2026.
The Bills traded up two spots to draft Elam in 2022, but sixth-round rookie Christian Benford quickly eclipsed the first-rounder on the depth chart, and he never recovered.
Buried on the bench, and highly ineffective when forced to fill in as an injury replacement, Elam played his way off the roster. His dud in the 2024 AFC Championship Game proved to be the final straw. Buffalo dealt him to the Dallas Cowboys at the start of the 2025 league year.
Elam has since been cut by the Cowboys , Kansas City Chiefs, Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers. He's currently on the Chargers' practice squad.
The Bills traded up two spots to keep Kincaid away from the Cowboys, landing a legitimate offensive weapon who is still waiting to reach his full potential.
It was lack of consistent availability that plagued Kincaid over the past two seasons. Now, that he's healthy , there's no excuse for not working him heavily into the pass offense's game plan.
We wrote about offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael's ambitious plans for Kincaid this season. Furthermore, everyone from Josh Allen to Joe Brady to general manager Brandon Beane has mentioned how much more dangerous Buffalo's offense is when the tight end is on the field.
Over the first two wins, Kincaid totaled 12 receptions for a combined 225 yards. In the Week 4 loss, the Bills targeted Kincaid only twice.
"Anytime Dalton comes away with two targets and one of them being in the last drive of the game, obviously, I didn't do a good enough job," said first-year head coach Joe Brady, who doubles as the offensive play caller.
Hairston suffered a knee injury that upended his rookie training camp experience and kept him on Injured Reserve for the first 1.5 months of the 2025 regular season. Then, a Week 18 ankle injury sidelined the cornerback for the playoffs.
As a returning player with three prior starts, Hairston backed into the starting CB2 role to begin the 2026 campaign. The fast, but undersized Hairston was torched by Drake Maye and Romeo Doubs during the 29-26 loss to New England.
Additionally, his effort on Hunter Henry's 3rd-and-10 conversion was questionable at best.
“No, I think that's clear [the effort was not acceptable] and I think he would tell you that. And again, the thing that I love about Max is the pride. He cares, he wants it, he will address it," said defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. "I'm sure he's as pissed as anybody in the organization on how that looked and the way it went about."
It would not be surprising to see second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun play over Hairston when Christian Benford returns from injury.

title: Buffalo Bills Sign Cornerback After Offensive Lineman Gets Poached
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are saying goodbye to one player and saying hello to another.
The Bills announced on Tuesday that they are signing cornerback A.J. Woods to the practice squad . In addition to that, Buffalo is reportedly losing one of its practice squad players.
According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , the Arizona Cardinals are signing offensive lineman Jedrick Wills off the Bills' practice squad.
Arizona's decision to poach Wills off Buffalo's practice squad is a result of the team losing left tackle Paris Johnson for the rest of the season due to a torn biceps injury. Wills will now join the Cardinals' 53-man roster to provide some depth.
A former No. 10 overall pick of the Cleveland Browns in 2020, Wills has not lived up to his draft billing. He signed with the Chicago Bears in the offseason and competed for their left tackle job before failing to make the 53-man roster.
After getting cut, the Bills signed him to the practice squad , but he did not get in any games for Buffalo over the first four. He has not played in a game since 2024 after missing all of last season because of knee surgery.
A.J. Woods played his college ball at Pitt and totaled 105 tackles, four interceptions, seven tackles for loss, two sacks and 25 passes defensed over five seasons.
The 5-foot-11, 195-pound cornerback went undrafted out of Pitt in 2024 and signed with the Washington Commanders following the draft.
Woods didn't last long in Washington and has since spent time on the practice squads of the Philadelphia Eagles and Denver Broncos, but he has never played a regular season snap.
He was most recently with the Atlanta Falcons in the offseason before getting cut loose on cutdown day. Buffalo is the first team he has signed with since getting cut by the Falcons.
Woods played in two preseason games with the Falcons this year and posted a Pro Football Focus coverage grade of 52.7. He gave up three receptions on three targets for 16 yards, good enough for a passer rating of 88.9. Woods played snaps at both slot cornerback and safety in those contests.
With the addition of Woods, the Bills now have three cornerbacks on their practice squad, along with Anthony Kendall and Kani Walker.
Buffalo also has Christian Benford, Dee Alford, Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun on the 53-man roster, but Benford has been dealing with a toe injury that kept him out in Week 4.

title: Bills NFL Power Rankings Week 5: Ugly Stretch Sends Buffalo Sliding
full_text:
Entering Week 4, the Buffalo Bills were undefeated and were sitting atop many NFL power rankings . Now entering Week 5, that’s no longer the case.
Buffalo is coming off its first loss of the season, falling 29-26 at home against the New England Patriots. While their sloppy win the week before over the Los Angeles Chargers gave them a gritty win, their ugly loss to the Patriots was far more concerning.
They’re now on the heels of back-to-back poor performances, which has them falling down just about every NFL power ranking. That said, let’s take a look at some of the major outlets to see where the Bills land.
“Jim Leonhard with the coordinator quote of the week. It’s hard to communicate at home because of the crowd noise. But, ‘if we complain about that, we are assholes’.”
Dee Alford attempted to say the noise inside Highmark Stadium made it difficult for the defense to communicate, which led to an elite quote from Jim Leonhard. He didn’t call Alford out directly , but he made it clear that he doesn’t believe noise should ever be an excuse, especially since most teams see this as an advantage that impacts the offense.
“They're still scoring at the highest clip in the league. But the early season success is now contextualized by beating two winless teams, including a Week 3 struggle against the Chargers, prior to Sunday's wake-up loss to the Patriots − winners of two in a row at Buffalo. Now it's up to the Bills to stabilize away from Western New York, given they'll only play at home once over the next six weeks.”
Davis brings up an excellent point. The Bills had three home games in a row, but will now go on a two-game road trip before their bye week. They will have just one game at home in Week 8 before going back on the road for two games. That’s a lot of travel for a team struggling to find consistency.
“The Bills opened the season with 77 points and 855 yards in two weeks. Quarterback Josh Allen looked unstoppable against Houston and Detroit, two teams with Super Bowl aspirations. Now the Texans and Lions are a combined 2-6, and the Bills are coming back down to earth. Coach Joe Brady's offense has been held to 25 points per game over the past two weeks and turned the ball over seven times,” Nick Suss wrote.
Suss still believes the Bills can contend in the AFC, which is absolutely true. The season is a marathon, not a sprint, so there’s time to turn things around. That said, losing to a division rival is never a good thing.
“Losing to the Patriots at home is not a good look for this team. They could have taken a real hold on the division, but let it get away as they face a tough one this week with the Rams.”
Facing the Rams coming off a loss might not be the worst thing since it could prevent the Bills from entering the game with too much confidence. That said, they could have truly buried the Patriots with a win, but fell short. That’s why they’re sliding down so many power rankings.

title: Buffalo Bills Might Have Drake Maye Problem Moving Forward
full_text:
While the Buffalo Bills certainly have plenty of problems within their own team to worry about at this point in time, the current leader in the AFC East through four weeks of the 2026 season appears to have another bugaboo on its hands: New England Patriots’ third-year quarterback Drake Maye.
Although he struggled during the first three weeks of his “junior” campaign through the month of September earlier this fall, Maye quickly reminded everyone on Sunday afternoon at Highmark Stadium why he was considered by many outside observers to be the odds-on favorite to win the league’s Most Valuable Player award this past winter.
The former No. 3 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft was dominant for a majority of the divisional contest against Buffalo, and—at least for Sunday—he undoubtedly looked like the better, more confident of the two quarterbacks, which is concerning, to say the least.
Yes, Allen is a former MVP in his own right, but Maye might not be far behind him if his play continues like he displayed against the Bills in Orchard Park this past weekend.
Entering the contest, the one-time North Carolina Tarheels’ star had just a 1-to-7 ratio in terms of his touchdown-to-turnover rate this year, which ranked dead last amongst NFL gunslingers.
But, then something clicked against Jim Leonhard’s defense this weekend, and Maye went on to complete just a shade under 60% of his attempts for a season-high 269 passing yards and three passing touchdowns to go along with just one interception. He also added a season-high 54 yards rushing on eight carries for an annoyingly impressive average of 6.75 yards per attempt.
Needless to say, it was a stellar performance from Maye, and it’s something that he’s seemingly done quite regularly against the Bills, regardless of their defensive coordinator or scheme.
Excluding Week 18 against the Bills in the 2024-2025 season finale where he sat for most of the outing at Gillette Stadium as a rookie, Maye accounted for 247.9 total yards per game (229.6 YPG passing, 28.3 YPG) and four total touchdowns to just two interceptions the last two seasons against Sean McDermott-led defenses.
And, adding in Sunday’s performance against Leonhard’s new 3-4 scheme , Maye’s stats look even better, especially considering he surpassed his previous career-highs against Buffalo in passing touchdowns and rushing yards, while falling just five yards short of setting a new career-high in total passing yards—specifically against the Bills—for the game.
In totality, Maye’s four complete contests against Buffalo following Sunday’s solid showing in Western New York read as follows: 80-of-126 passing for 958 passing yards and a 63.5 completion percentage, 139 rushing yards on 21 attempts for an average of 6.6 yards per carry, seven total touchdowns (five passing, two rushing), and just three interceptions.
Furthermore, when extrapolating that data, if New England’s young 24-year-old franchise leader only played Buffalo’s defense for a 17-game stretch, then his season totals would reach around 4,072 passing yards, 591 rushing yards, and a total touchdown-to-interception ratio of 30:13.
For fans in and around Foxborough, Massachusetts, those stats are encouraging.
However, for Bills Mafia members . . . Maye’s inexplicable ability to pick apart the defense whenever he’s lined up against Buffalo is a bit disheartening.
And, given that Josh Allen has looked incredibly rough over the past two games, it certainly gives pause to the notion that the Bills can unseat the Patriots atop the AFC East after last year’s unexpected run to the Super Bowl by New England.
Now that Maye and Co. are right back in the thick of the divisional race, things could definitely get interesting heading into the months of October, November, and December.
Buffalo and first-year head coach Joe Brady had their shot to quietly keep the Patriots down entering Week 5, but now the Bills' rival has new life . . . and for good reason.

title: Jim Leonhard Indirectly Calls Out Dee Alford for Bills' Crowd Noise Comment
full_text:
Sorry, Dee Alford. Jim Leonhard isn't buying it.
Following the Buffalo Bills' three-point home loss to the New England Patriots, Alford mentioned the crowd noise factor while addressing reporters in a locker room media scrum.
"Sometimes, the game can be loud and super loud to the point where we not able to get the play that fast [when] we need it," said Alford, suggesting the home crowd presents a challenge when it's roaring.
Whether or not noise was a factor, the Bills allowed struggling quarterback Drake Maye to pass for 269 yards and three touchdowns in the October 4 matinee. The Bills' secondary was beaten by a no-name Patriots' receiving corps in multiple key spots throughout the 29-26 loss.
"We got to hurry and line up, and sometime we don't be able to get the play. But that's not an excuse. That's just something we got to continue to grow and get better with as a secondary as far as communication," said Alford.
Unfortunately, Alford wasn't the only Bills' defensive back who made questionable postgame comments after the Week 4 setback. Safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson couldn't stop himself from trash talking the victors.
Leonhard, who played 10 seasons in the NFL after going undrafted out of Wisconsin, knows plenty about functioning in loud environments.
"It's always harder to communicate at home than it is on the road. If we complain about that, we are [expletive]. We have to turn that into the biggest advantage we have. As hard as it is for us, it's significantly harder for an offense," said Leonhard on Monday afternoon in Orchard Park .
Having spent multiple seasons playing for the Bills and the New York Jets, the former safety has a lot of experience with passionate fan bases.
"We have to make it an advantage for us: We can't use that as a crutch. It is what it is," said Leonhard. "Every team, not every team, most teams, the good teams, that's an issue [for them] when you play a home game. I'm excited we got this fan base."
While Buffalo's new Highmark Stadium contains more than 10,000 fewer seats than its predecessor, it is said to make for an even louder environment due to the building's apparent ability to trap noise.
Ultimately, the Bills are fortunate to consistently host a raucous crowd hellbent on making line miserable for opposing offenses.
Now, Alford has to learn to deal with it.

title: Three CB Additions Bills Must Pursue After Secondary Melts Down vs. Patriots
full_text:
The most concerning part of the Buffalo Bills ' three-point loss to the New England Patriots was the defensive secondary.
The unit allowed Drake Maye, who had thrown only one touchdown against six interceptions coming in, to torch the Bills for 269 yards and three touchdowns in what could be a devastating defeat in the long run .
Without top cornerback Christian Benford due to a toe injury , youngsters Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun had their problems against a receiving corps that still lacked prized free agent acquisition A.J. Brown, who was out with a high ankle sprain.
With this latest concerning outing, the time to press the red panic button may be now, so here are three cornerbacks that general manager Brandon Beane needs to consider adding if the Bills are to shore up their secondary issues sooner rather than later.
Four weeks into the season, Robertson is looking like one of the biggest steals of the 2026 NFL offseason. He leads the league with seven passes defensed and is on pace for about 110 tackles, which would be 17 more than Cooper DeJean, last year's tackles leader among cornerbacks.
The seventh-year man out of Louisiana Tech was signed to a two-year, $15.02 million contract in the offseason, and his 84.6 Pro Football Focus grade is third-best among NFL corners .
Robertson's performance has been no fluke, as he's gone against Dallas' dynamic receiver duo and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the reigning Offensive Player of the Year, in the first quarter of the season.
With quarterbacks Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota injured , Washington is in a position to continue racking up losses, and if it happens, Robertson could be a top trade target if he keeps up his play.
In addition to Buffalo's struggles at outside cornerback, slot corner Dee Alford suffered an ankle injury in the third quarter on Sunday, ruining what was a good start for him .
Alford caught a break just before halftime when a Maye pass to Romeo Doubs bounced out of the receiver's hands for Alford's first pick as a Bill. But at the end of the day, Buffalo lost and, to make matters worse, he commented on how the noise at the new Highmark Stadium was hard to overcome.
"It's always harder to communicate [on defense] at home than it is on the road," defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said in response to Alford's comment. "If we complain about that, we are [explicit]."
If Alford gets in the doghouse or gets hurt further, Buffalo could turn to Williams, one of the more underrated slot guys in the game, who is in the last season of his rookie contract. His presence could let Leonhard experiment further with his defensive personnel.
Tre'Davious White is not just a nostalgia pick , though the current Bills coaching staff may not agree with that sentiment because he has not been signed yet.
The now-31-year-old was able to play at a high level in 2025 after dealing with numerous injuries throughout the early 2020s. The nine-year-veteran led the Bills with 10 passes defensed and also recorded 40 tackles and an interception.
White is more experienced than any defensive back currently on the Bills' roster, and on a unit that lacks veteran leadership outside of C.J. Gardner-Johnson and Bradley Chubb, White would be welcomed in that area also.
It's still early in the 2026 season, but time is running out to right the ship in the secondary with a schedule that appears to be tougher than expected coming up soon.

title: Bills 2027 NFL Mock Draft Ushers in New Era For Secondary
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills made some huge changes on the defensive side of the ball this offseason. After nine seasons with Sean McDermott as their head coach, the Bills decided to move on . McDermott, in addition to his head coaching duties, was also the architect of Buffalo's defense.
With him out, the Bills turned to Joe Brady as head coach and Brady hired Jim Leonhard as the new defensive coordinator . Leonhard employs a multiple-front defense, although their base scheme is more of a 3-4. That change itself was huge and while they're primarily utilizing many of the same players, there are a few new faces.
One of those additions is C.J. Gardner-Johnson , who had a huge game in Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers. His performance is a reminder of how much a strong secondary can help a defense, which is one reason Cody Williams of FanSided has Buffalo adding a new safety in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
Williams believes the Bills have an offense that can be unstoppable, but says their defense lets them down too often. He believes adding Notre Dame's Tae Johnson could usher in a much-needed new era , while praising Johnson for his ability to play in coverage as well as against the run.
"I'm a broken record when it comes to the Bills, but my goodness does this back seven on defense need to be shored up to help Josh Allen and a near-unstoppable offense not be let down in big moments. Safety play has waned in Buffalo in recent year, and Tae Johnson is the type of player who can come in and be the new era for the Bills. He has great ball skills but also a quality ability to crash down and defend the run well, just as we've seen from successful safeties in Buffalo in the past," Williams wrote.
Johnson had a breakout campaign in 2025 for Notre Dame, recording 48 tackles, four interceptions, and three pass defenses.
The good news for Buffalo is that the cupboard isn't bare at safety. In addition to Gardner-Johnson, they've seen Cole Bishop develop into a quality starter. Gardner-Johnson is a free agent in the offseason, but has seemed thrilled with the staff thus far. Adding Johnson would solidify the group, while giving Leonhard plenty of options for attacking the opposing offense.

title: Dee Alford Gives Lame Excuse for Bills' Poor Home-Field Defensive Performance
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills really ran former All-Pro nickel cornerback Taron Johnson out of town in favor of this guy?
Signing mid-tier free agent Dee Alford always seemed a little strange, and it made less sense that the Bills gave him more than $5 million per year (per Spotrac) while trading the handsomely-paid Johnson away to the Las Vegas Raiders for a late-round draft pick.
Although Johnson's production had dropped off in recent years, he was a proven starter with the ability to effectively cover receivers and lay the lumber against the run. Meanwhile, Alford, albeit younger, showed himself to be a less physical part-time starter for the Atlanta Falcons.
While Johnson appears to fit nicely with the Raiders , Alford, outside of a lucky interception against the New England Patriots, has been less than impressive. The slot cornerback is allowing a career-worst 9.2 yards per target through four games against opposing receivers.
The effort from @Raiders CB Taron Johnson to chase down Kenneth Walker III and save a touchdown. pic.twitter.com/5pAFzMptn7
Now, he's indirectly complaining that the Bills' fans are too loud.
Following the October 4 home loss to New England, Alford claimed the Bills' defense experienced difficulty in its pre-snap communication due to the intense Highmark Stadium crowd noise.
Buffalo allowed the Patriots to score a season-high 29 points while quarterback Drake Maye passed for 269 yards and three touchdowns.
While the fans are attempting to affect the opposing offense, and potentially force a false start or delay of game penalty, Alford suggested that the home-field advantage may not been an advantage after all.
"Sometimes, the game can be loud and super loud to the point where we not able to get the play that fast [when] we need it," said Alford.
The process should become easier as the Bills' new defense gains experience working together, but it obviously provided enough of a challenge on Sunday for Alford to mention it.
"We got to hurry and line up and sometime we don't be able to get the play. But that's not an excuse. That's just something we got to continue to grow and get better with as a secondary as far as communication," said Alford.
As for adjusting and communicating through the crowd noise, Alford expects to address it through practice.
"There's a lot of things we do at practice as well. We train loud music, loud speakers," said Alford. "Just to try to show a scenario like what happened in the game, and we've been getting better with it, every week."
Alford wasn't the only Bills' player to make questionable comments in the wake of the Week 4 home loss. Starting safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson made waves by insulting Patriots' wide receiver Efton Chism.

title: Overreaction? Panthers Saved Their Season With Primetime Win Over Lions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers season is alive and well after a primetime win over the Detroit Lions . Carolina beats Detroit 32-26 as Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan show out with their connection and elite-level plays.
This is the Panthers' first Sunday Night Football win in almost 11 years, with their last coming on October 25th, 2015, with a home victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. That team went on to play in the Super Bowl.
This isn't to say that Bryce Young and Co. are making a Super Bowl run, but winning on primetime still matters and can catapult a team toward a successful season.
With the win, the Panthers sit at first place in the NFC South, having a 2-2 record and a win over the Atanta Falcons, who just demolished the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football.
Obviously, Carolina's win was huge for morale, overall momentum, and the standings. What if the Panthers lost though?
Despite obliterating the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2, Carolina would be tied for the second-worst record in the NFC South. The Falcons took care of business against the New Orleans Saints on Monday night, improving to 2-2 and looking elite on offense since Michael Penix Jr. came back.
Had Carolina lost, that would've been 0-2 at home, with two of its next three games on the road against teams that made the playoffs last season, the Eagles and the Packers.
Maybe the rest of the division struggles just as much as Carolina could, but thats why the win on Sunday night was so important, Carolina stays above the rest of the queue for another week, and can't make any mistakes this weekend with the bye.
No one expected the Buccaneers to be this bad for four weeks, so that gives Carolina some room, but even so, if Carolina lost, they'd be only one game above Tampa Bay. It's a world of difference for the rest-of-the-year outlook.
So no, it's not an overreaction. The NFC South will likely remain a tight race through the rest of the season, so the week-to-week outlook can fluctuate throughout the year.
Carolina's next four weeks are as follows.
Sunday, 10/18, 1:00 PM ET, at Philadelphia Eagles
Sunday, 10/25, 1:00 PM ET, vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Thursday, 10/29, 8:15 PM ET, at Green Bay Packers
Sunday, 11/8, 1:00 PM ET, vs. Denver Broncos
2-2 in that four-week stretch is a must. If Carolina can somehow go 3-1, then there's something real going on in Charlotte.
Obviously, the Tampa game is a must-win for division purposes, but there's even a chance that the Bucs' are still winless by that point. Losing to a potential 0-6 Tampa Bay team would be as demoralizing a loss as any loss in the NFL.

title: Panthers Survived the Injuries. Now the Help Could Be Coming
full_text:
I'm almost afraid to look at the Panthers' injury report anymore. Seriously, has there been a week when somebody hasn't gone down? We're only four games into the season, and it already feels like I've spent half of it talking about injuries.
Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve. Xavier Legette is there now, too. Jalen Coker missed the Detroit game, Damien Lewis was out, and Carolina was already playing without Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton. Then Monroe Freeling got hurt Sunday night because, of course, he did.
That's a big reason I picked Detroit. At some point, I figured Carolina was going to run out of guys, and all of these injuries were finally going to catch up with them. Instead, the Panthers beat the Lions 32-26 with a bunch of guys playing roles I don't think anybody expected them to be playing four games into the season.
Now, for the first time in a while, Carolina might actually be getting some people back. The Panthers made several roster moves Tuesday and have two open spots on the 53-man roster. Dave Canales said Trevor Etienne should be ready to practice after the bye , while Moton and Wharton are getting closer but still need medical clearance.
I don't know exactly when all three will be back, and I'm not going to pretend they're all walking through the door the minute the bye ends. After spending the last few weeks wondering who's going down next, though, I'll take this kind of injury news.
I've been wondering about this for the last couple of weeks, and Detroit might've been the best example yet. Both starting cornerbacks were on injured reserve. Lewis was out, Legette was out, Coker was out, and Moton still wasn't available. I'm probably forgetting somebody at this point.
Corey Bullock stepped in for Lewis and, outside of a rough start, did a pretty good job. Will Lee III is playing a much bigger role at cornerback than I thought he would this early. It feels like every week somebody else is getting thrown into the lineup and basically being told, "You're up."
And somehow, it keeps working. Carolina is 2-2 and just beat Detroit with a lineup that looks a whole lot different from what we thought it would when the season started. I don't know how much longer you can keep doing that, though, and I'd rather not find out.
Moton is probably the biggest one for me. Carolina has been trying to hold this offensive line together without him, and now Freeling is banged up, too. If Moton can get cleared after the bye, that would be a pretty big deal for an offensive line that's had to keep moving pieces around.
I'd like to see Wharton back, too, and the same goes for Etienne. I don't know how much Etienne changes the offense with Chuba Hubbard playing the way he is, but give me another healthy player at this point, and I'll worry about where he fits later. None of these guys has to come back and save Carolina because, at 2-2, the Panthers have already shown they can survive without them.
I just don't want to keep finding out how many injuries this team can take before it finally becomes too much.
I hated this Week 5 bye when the schedule came out. I remember looking at it and complaining about four games before the bye. That's it? Carolina has to play the rest of the season after getting its only break in early October?
Yeah, I'm not complaining anymore. If you've seen the injury report, you know why. Carolina needs this week about as badly as a team can need a bye after only four games, and now there's at least a chance the Panthers come out of it healthier than they went into it.
The funny part is they've actually played pretty well while all of this has been going on. Carolina is 2-2, went to Atlanta and won 34-3, and then beat Detroit on Sunday Night Football with guys missing everywhere. That's what has me curious about what happens next.
I still don't know exactly what this Panthers team is. I've changed my mind about them about three times already, and we're only four games into the season. But they've already shown me they can survive without a lot of these guys.
I'd like to see what they can do with them.
