title: Panthers Could Go Edge Rusher Shopping During Bye Week
full_text:
The defending NFC South champion Carolina Panthers and the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs are the first teams this season to get some time off this season. Dave Canales’s club evened its win-loss record on Sunday night, outlasting the Detroit Lions, 32-26.
Quarterback Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and pair of scores. Both touchdown tosses went to wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan, who finished the evening with 14 catches for 192 yards. Carolina’s offense rolled up 445 total yards and averaged 6.2 yards per play.
While the Panthers’ defense managed to keep Lions’ running back Jahmyr Gibbs under wraps—15 attempts for 46 yards and one YD—quarterback Jared Goff hit on 32 of his 32 throws for 412 yards and one score. Despite gaining 452 total yards, Carolina managed to limit Detroit to two offensive touchdowns and four field goals.
Nevertheless, coordinator Ejiro Evero’s unit managed only one sack in the team’s six-point victory. Hence, this little piece of information according to Next Gen Stats .
“Jared Goff was pressured on 34 percent of his dropbacks, but every Panthers pressure loomed large. With no pressure (66 percent of his dropbacks), Goff completed 25-of-35 passes for 348 yards, a touchdown and a 112.6 rating. Under pressure, Goff was 7-of-17 for 64 yards and a 52.1 rating. Patrick Jones II led the Panthers with five QB pressures.”
The Panthers have been looking for a consistent pass rush for too many seasons. In four games in 2026, Canales’s club has come up with only eight sacks. Of course, there are mitigating circumstances as edge rusher Nic Scourton, a second-round pick in 2025 who tied for the team lead with five sacks this past season, was lost for the year during training camp with a knee injury.
One of Dan Morgan’s prized offseason additions was edge rusher Jaelan Phillips. He’s second on the team with a pair of sacks and is tied for the team lead with four quarterback hits. A real positive has been second-year pro Princely Umanmielen, who also has four QB hits and leads the club with three sacks. He’s currently Pro Football Focus’ No. 10 edge rusher when it comes to pass rush efficiency.
GOFF BROUGHT DOWN BY PRINCELY UMANMIELEN #NFL #Lions #OnePride #Panthers #KeepPounding #DETvsCAR pic.twitter.com/pruNsNpVTX
A year ago, the third-round pick from Ole Miss played in 17 total games (including the playoff loss to the Rams) and managed only 1.5 QB traps. And don’t discount Jones’s performance on Sunday night. The 2025 offseason addition from the Minnesota Vikings played in only four games this past season due to injury.
Despite a few positives, the Panthers could certainly use some more help here. Veterans such as Joey Bosa , Haason Reddick, and Leonard Floyd remain unsigned. A year ago with the Buffalo Bills, the oft-injured Bosa played and started 15 regular-season games—his highest total since 2021 while he was with the Chargers—and finished with five sacks and five forced fumbles. He also started both of the Bills’ playoff games.
There are other options as well. Nonetheless, Morgan may want to kick the tires on a couple of these veteran defenders. The Panthers next take the field in Week 6 against the Eagles at Philadelphia.

title: Bryce Young's MVP Chances Just Doubled — Is 2% on Kalshi Actually Too Low?
full_text:
Two percent. That's what Kalshi is giving Bryce Young right now to win NFL MVP, and before Sunday night's 32-26 win over Detroit, he was sitting at less than 1%.
Is 2% a lot? No. But I'm not sure I would've given him much of a chance either before the season started, so maybe I shouldn't complain too much. Still, after what I've watched through four games, I think 2% might be a little low.
I feel like I have to say that every time I write something positive about Young. It's only four games, there's a lot of football left, and nobody is handing out the MVP award in October.
Now that we've gotten that out of the way, can we talk about how good he's been?
Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. That came after 291 yards against Cleveland, 287 yards and three touchdowns against Atlanta, and 361 yards with three touchdowns in Week 1 against Chicago.
That's 1,268 yards and nine touchdown passes through four games. I also don't think there's been a game yet where I've walked away thinking Young was the reason Carolina lost, and I couldn't always say that before.
This is probably where I've been a little unfair to Young. After Chicago, I wanted to see him do it again because the Panthers lost. He did against Atlanta, but then I wanted to see what happened the next week.
He played well against Cleveland, and somehow I was still sitting here waiting for more. Then he goes out on Sunday Night Football against Detroit and throws for 329 yards without turning the ball over.
What exactly am I waiting for?
I'm not saying Young is going to win MVP, and I'm not even saying I'd put him in my top three right now. But I'm done treating every good game like we need another one before it counts.
He's played well for a month. I think we can say that now.
This is where I have to slow down a little. Carolina is 2-2, and I don't care how many yards Young throws for, I have a hard time believing an MVP is coming from a team that finishes 8-9 or 9-8.
If he's really going to make this interesting, the Panthers are going to have to win a lot more games. That's why Philadelphia after the bye has my attention.
Would I expect Young to go into Philadelphia, throw for 300 yards and beat the Eagles? I don't know. A month ago, I probably would've said no without thinking much about it.
I'm not doing that anymore.
If Young goes into Philadelphia and plays well again, especially if Carolina wins, that 2% is going to start looking pretty small.
When the MVP chants started Sunday night, my first reaction was basically, come on, we're four games into the season. I still think it's early. Way too early.
But Panthers fans haven't had much to get excited about at quarterback in a long time, and now they've got one throwing for more than 300 yards on Sunday Night Football while beating Detroit. Let them have some fun with it.
Kalshi says Young has a 2% chance to win MVP. I'm not putting money on it, and I'm definitely not predicting he's going to win it.
But less than 1% before Detroit and 2% after?
Maybe ask me again after Philadelphia.

title: Grading Every Position Group in Panthers' Stunning Upset of Lions on SNF
full_text:
Week 4 has come and gone , and the Carolina Panthers might just be the biggest story of the weekend, specifically QB Bryce Young and WR Tetairoa McMillan. Carolina beats the Detroit Lions in an offensive battle , winning 32-26 and improving to 2-2 entering the bye week.
While the win was exciting and brought a ton of momentum to the franchise, it wasn't a perfect performance all around.
Some position groups excelled, while others presented opportunities for the Lions to mount a comeback and win. Below are the grades for each of Carolina's position groups in the Panthers' victory over Detroit.
If there was one negative to point out, it was that Young threw 6 consecutive incompletions at one point in the second half. Other than that, it was perfection. Young was poised, used subtle movements to evade pressure in the pocket and find his targets, and showed what elite ball placement and anticipation look like from a QB.
Chuba Hubbard was outstanding, scoring the first touchdown of the game and his longest touchdown run of the season thus far. The 15-yard score was just the start. Hubbard finished with 20 carries for 122 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
Averaging 6.1 yards per carry, Hubbard found gaps, broke loose for chunk plays, and tough yards through tacklers for 7-yard gains. AJ Dillion got five carries and rushed for 2 yards, which is essentially nothing, so the grade bumps down just a tad bit since the RB2 produced 7 total yards.
The best performance of Tetairoa McMillan's young career, and it's not close. 14 catches, 192 receiving yards, and 2 touchdowns. The stats are one thing, but McMillan's greatness came at crucial moments, especially the viral 3rd-and-14 right-sideline catch in the fourth quarter.
John Metchie III made some nice catches in the middle of the field, as did Brycen Tremayne and TE Darren Waller. All three pass catchers averaged 12+ yards per reception, meaning they made highly effective plays in the game.
This grade could be even higher, given that the line deals with major injuries, but a B- is fair. What made Young's performance that was so special was that he produced that well while constantly under pressure. Pressure came early and often from Aidan Hutchinson, but who doesn't he get home against? That's one of the best pass rushers in football.
The good grade especially stems from the run blocking; as mentioned before, Hubbard averaged 6.1 yards per carry on 20 attempts, and the Panthers will gladly take that 10 out of 10 times.
Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs didn't take over the game, didn't gash the Panthers with any huge explosives, so thats a win in itself. Gibbs rushed for just 46 yards and 1 touchdown, holding a top two running back in the league to under 50 yards rushing is great.
Carolina could've been better in the pass rush; Jared Goff was sacked only once for a 6-yard loss.  Goff often had time to find his open receivers downfield and finished the night throwing for over 400 yards. Goff isn't very mobile, so if pressure did come then he'd likely go down or at least throw more incompletions.
Devin Lloyd's return was much needed, as he posted 9 tackles, 1 TFL, and 1 QB hit. Stopping the run is arguably what Lloyd is best at, and he got to Gibbs multiple times to prevent huge plays. Bobby Okereke was just solid, posting 7 tackles and not making no back-breaking mistakes.
Neither linebacker got burned on any play or made a critical mistake; it was just a solid effort all around.
Losing both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson looks like a huge problem . Akayleb Evans was targeted 15 times and surrendered 12 catches for over 200 yards and 1 touchdown. That can't happen again if Carolina wants to keep winning. As for Will Lee III, he wasn't a detriment to the team like Evans was, but he wasn't spectacular either.

title: Panthers vs. Lions Made One Thing Very Clear for Carolina's Bye Week
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are riding high after their first Sunday Night Football win in 11 years, beating the Detroit Lions 32-26 and improving to 2-2 heading into the bye week. Carolina controlled most of this game, despite the final score only being only a six-point difference.
QB Bryce Young and WR Tetairoa McMillan were the game's two main takeaways, each making a statement with elite performances. Young threw for over 300 yards for the third time in four games and remains the league leader in passing yards .
McMillan posted the best game of his young NFL career , totaling 14 catches, 192 receiving yards, and 2 touchdowns. The offense was masterful in every facet, yet theres one takeaway from the game that is arguably more important than any of the success on that side of the ball.
The most impressive part of Carolina's Week 4 win is the fact that its defense didn't allow the Lions to score 45 points. Starting corners Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson were both placed on IR entering Sunday night, leaving the Panthers thin and inexperienced in that room.
Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans are the starting corners moving forward, with Horn and Jackson out. Lee is Carolina's fourth-round pick from the 2026 NFL Draft, and Evans is in his fifth season in the NFL, with essentially one full season's experience in Carolina.
Detroit's offense targeted Evans heavily on Sunday night. Targeted 15 times (32% of passes beyond the line of scrimmage), Evans surrendered 12 catches, for 202 receiving yards, and 1 touchdown.
It became so clear that Lions' QB Jared Goff was targeting Evans that it was hard not to feel sympathy for him. That said, Carolina plays more really good offenses and receivers down the stretch of the season.
If the production, or lack thereof, displayed by Evans is what the Panthers are getting for the rest of the year, then theres no other option than to find another cornerback. The only question is which CB Carolina could target.
Many veteran corners could serve the Panthers and provide the stability they need at the back end of the defense.
Our Zach Roberts highlighted 8 corner options across the league , including those on Carolina's practice squad, as viable candidates.
Some of those corners were older options like Marshon Lattimore or Tre'Davious White, and talented players who may need a change of scenery like Deonte Banks. One other corner could be available, and would be an instant upgrade.
Packers corner Keisean Nixon is a prime trade candidate. His contract is up next spring, so Green Bay could look to move off him and get some sort of compensation back rather than letting him walk for nothing.
Over four weeks, Nixon has posted 16 solo tackles, 1 interception, 3 passes defended, and 0.5 sacks.

title: Bryce Young Contract Extension: How Much Could Panthers’ QB Earn After Hot Start?
full_text:
He has made steady progress every year since being drafted first overall in the 2023 NFL draft. Carolina Panthers’ starting quarterback Bryce Young had a forgettable rookie season in which the team finished 2-15. Enter new head coach Dave Canales, who sat down the 2021 Heisman Trophy winner after a miserable two-game start in 2024. Young would wind up starting the final 10 games that year and there was certainly some improvement.
Bryce Young vs. Rams in 1080p (Wild Card, 2025) #KeepPounding pic.twitter.com/wcc1T25GUZ
The Panthers got off to a 1-3 start this past season, but once again Young made strides. He started all but one game in 2025 and he finished the year with career highs in completion percentage (65.6), passing yards (3,011) and touchdown tosses (23).
Although he struggled in the first half of games and consistency was an issue from week to week, the Panthers wound up winning the NFC South for the first time since 2015 and the franchise reached the playoffs for the first time since 2017. In the playoff loss to the Rams, he threw a first-quarter interception then settled down and played well albeit in a 34-31 setback.
However, 2026 has been a much different story for the four-year pro. Joseph Person of The Athletic had this to say following Carolina’s 32-26 Sunday night win over the visiting Detroit Lions.
Panthers QB Bryce Young Week 4 Highlights vs. Lions 29/41 329 PASS YDS 2 TD 0 INT Panthers win 32-26 pic.twitter.com/YTUv4em1HE
“Young secured the first primetime win of his career and took another step toward securing the bag in the process. Young entered his fourth season without an extension because the Panthers wanted to see more consistency from the No. 1 pick from 2023. He has delivered, with Sunday just the latest stellar performance in a breakthrough season.”
After four weeks of play, Young leads the NFL with 1,268 passing yards. In his first three seasons, a total of 47 games (including playoffs), he threw for at least 300 yards only three times. He’s reached that mark twice in four outings this season.
Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan were dealing 🃏🏈 Young started 12-of-13 for 141 yards and a touchdown, while McMillan piled up 110 yards and a score on six catches. #Panthers #NFL pic.twitter.com/WKzgw0phdR
“Young carved up the NFL’s worst passing defense,” added Person, regarding the win over the Lions, “completing his first 11 passes on his way to a 329-yard passing night with two touchdowns. He became the first QB in team history with 250 passing yards and at least one touchdown pass in each of the first four games of a season.”
Unless there’s a major falloff the remainder of 2026, a new deal appears inevitable for the 25-year-old signal-caller. The team picked up the fifth-year option in April, which means he's under contract until 2027. It’s hard to speculate what those numbers could actually look like at this time, but one NFL analyst appears convinced that Young is going to get paid after his fast start this season.
"Bryce [Young], you have earned a MASSIVE deal! He's going to break the bank." @BMac_SportsTalk after the Panthers' win over the Lions #scoreboard pic.twitter.com/R4qqVmctSw
Could president of football operations/general manager Dan Morgan and executive vice president of football operations Brandt Tilis get a deal done sooner than later? It’s been a very encouraging start by Young, who has made consistent improvement since that forgettable rookie year in 2023.

title: Panthers’ 2026 Start Speaks Volumes About Franchise’s Recent History
full_text:
The improving Carolina Panthers have once again gotten into a habit which became somewhat predictable in 2025 and would not necessarily be considered a positive. A year ago, the team finished 8-9 and won its first division title since 2015. From Weeks 7-17, Dave Canales’s club alternated wins and losses over a 10-game stretch.
This season, the Panthers bounced back from an opening day from a 59-37 home loss to the Chicago Bears to rout the Atlanta Falcons, 34-3, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. A week later, Carolina fell to the Browns at Cleveland, 21-18, but followed that up with Sunday night’s 32-26 victory over the visiting Detroit Lions.
T-MAC ARE YOU SERIOUS! @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uIhOgbACgr
Hence, Canales’s team owns a 2-2 record after four games, the same as the suddenly-resurgent Falcons. That’s not exactly an earth-shattering start to a season…unless you’re the Carolina Panthers.
Yes, that is correct. You have to go back five years to find the last time this team avoided owning a losing record after four games. That season, under head coach Matt Rhule, the Panthers won their first three games before dropping 12 of their final 14 contests.
The past two seasons under Canales, Carolina lost three of its first four games. In fact, the 2024 Panthers actually got off to 1-7 start before prevailing in four of their final nine outings. Four weeks into ‘24, the team had been outscored a combined 129-73 in their four outings. This past season, the club’s scoring differential was minus-20 (75-95) after four contests.
Thanks to quarterback Bryce Young and the league’s top-ranked passing attack in terms of yards per game, the Panthers have already put 121 points on the board—the fourth-most in the league. Of course, they have also given up 109 points—tied for the sixth-most in the NFL.
All told, Canales’s squad ranks fourth in the NFL in total yards per game. The team has scored at least 32 points in three of their four games. That’s a figure Carolina failed to reach in any game in 2025. Including playoffs, the Panthers scored 30-plus point in five of their 28 total outings this past season.
Yes, a 2-2 record certainly sounds like mediocrity. In this case, it’s a very encouraging start for a franchise that could indeed finish the season with a winning record for the first time since 2017.

title: Panthers Surge to Unforeseen Heights in NFL Power Rankings After Thriller
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are coming off a huge and somewhat stunning win . Facing the favored Detroit Lions despite being at home, the Panthers weathered a storm of injuries once again, but this time they came out victorious.
Where does that leave them in NFL Power Rankings? Moving up to unprecedented heights, in some cases.
No matter where you get your NFL Power Rankings from, the Panthers are on the rise. They are among the teams with the biggest jump in the NFL.
On Bleacher Report , the Panthers surged from 21st to 15th in the NFL, a new high. Gary Davenport wrote, "Much like the division they play in, the Carolina Panthers aren't an easy team to get a bead on four weeks into the season."
Davenport said the Panthers are among the best offensive teams in the NFL, and Bryce Young is playing like a top-10 quarterback. Defensively, though, the Panthers have been "erratic," to say the least.
"This is the team that surrendered 59 points to the Chicago Bears at home back in Week 1. The Lions actually out-gained the Panthers in a shootout that included almost 900 yards of offense," he wrote, adding that for now, though, Carolina appears to be the NFC South frontrunner.
Over at ESPN , the Panthers rose from 22nd to 18th in the NFL. " First-year playcaller Brad Idzik and much-maligned QB Bryce Young are steering the ship for the top aerial attack by averaging 301.3 yards per game," Mike Kaye pointed out.
Even CBS Sports' Pete Prisco had to give the Panthers major props, and that is a sentence that has virtually never been uttered before. He moved them from 26th to 18th, making Carolina the single biggest mover in the power rankings.
Doubling down on rare praise, Prisco wrote, "Bryce Young is earning himself a big payday. He was outstanding in the victory over the Lions Sunday night."
It's even better on FOX Sports . Ralph Vacchiano moved them from 16th to 12th after the inspiring victory over the Lions. "In the worst division in football, they should start to pull away from the pack very soon," he wrote.
All across the board, NFL media members are beginning to praise the Panthers. Despite immense injuries that would have absolutely sunk lesser teams against the Lions on Sunday night, Carolina is moving on up.

title: Panthers' Week 5 Bye Looked Terrible. Now It Looks Like a Gift
full_text:
I hated the Panthers' Week 5 bye when I first saw the schedule. Four games and you're already taking your only week off? I didn't understand that at all.
My first thought was what happens in November or December, when everybody is beat up and Carolina has been playing every week for two months. That's when I wanted the bye, not four games into the season.
Well, have you seen this injury report lately?
The Panthers are 2-2 after beating Detroit 32-26 on Sunday Night Football, and I'm not sure they could've made it much longer without a break. It feels like every week somebody else is going down, and Sunday night wasn't any different.
Maybe I was looking at the early bye all wrong.
I'm not even sure where to start with the injuries. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve. Xavier Legette joined them before the Detroit game, while Jalen Coker and Damien Lewis couldn't play Sunday night.
Then more guys got banged up against Detroit, because apparently Carolina hadn't lost enough players already. We're four games into the season, and the Panthers are already asking guys further down the depth chart to play some pretty important snaps.
Do I still wish the bye came later in the season? Probably. Ask me again in December after Carolina has played 10 straight games, and there's a good chance I'll be complaining about it.
But that's a December problem.
Right now, the Panthers need this week. Some of these guys need time to get healthy, and the guys who have been filling in probably wouldn't mind a few days off, either.
Dave Canales tried to find the positives in the early bye when the schedule came out, and I'll admit I didn't think much of it at the time. He said four games would give Carolina a " quick snapsho t" of what was actually working, what wasn't, and what the Panthers might need to change.
That's pretty much exactly where they are now.
Canales has four games to look at, and I think we know a lot more about this team than we did a month ago. The offense looks better than I expected, the running game finally showed up against Detroit, and there are still plenty of things defensively that need to be figured out.
Canales also mentioned something else back then that looks even more important now. He said the early bye could give an injured player another week to get back before Carolina gets into what he called the "meat and potatoes of the season."
Have you seen this injury report?
Yeah, that extra week doesn't sound too bad anymore.
This is another thing I didn't really expect.
When the schedule came out, I looked at what Carolina had waiting after the bye and thought, great. Go to Philadelphia, come home for Tampa Bay, and then turn around four days later and go to Green Bay.
Philadelphia and Green Bay still bother me. I'm not going to pretend either of those games suddenly looks easy because Carolina beat Detroit. But Tampa Bay is 0-4, and I'm definitely looking at that game differently now.
I'm also looking at Carolina differently.
That's probably the part I wasn't considering when I hated this schedule in May. I was looking at who the Panthers had to play without knowing what this Panthers team was going to look like.
Now I've seen them beat Atlanta 34-3. I've watched them lose a game in Cleveland that I still think they should've won. And now they just beat Detroit on Sunday Night Football with half the roster seemingly on the injury report.
Am I picking them to go into Philadelphia and Green Bay and win both games? I'm not there yet. But I'm also not looking at those games and automatically writing down losses anymore.
I still don't know how I'm going to feel about this bye later in the season. Playing 13 straight games is a lot, and if Carolina is fighting for something in December with a beat-up roster, I'm probably going to remember that they used their bye in early October.
I'll complain about it then.
For now, give me the week off.
Carolina is 2-2, coming off its biggest win of the season and finally starting to show me what this team might be. Canales gets some time to look at the first four games, and more importantly, some of these injured guys get another week before the Panthers have to go to Philadelphia.
I thought the Week 5 bye was terrible when the schedule came out.
I'm starting to think the Panthers got lucky.

title: Lane Johnson Retirement Leaves Bears' Darnell Wright as NFL's Best Right Tackle
full_text:
Five-time All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson was a surprising healthy scratch from the Philadelphia Eagles' gameday roster last Sunday, and now we know why. In a social media post on Tuesday, Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL after nearly 14 seasons . A spot in the Pro Football Hall of Fame doubtlessly awaits this NFL legend, but his retirement leaves one burning question unanswered: who is now the best right tackle in the NFL?
There are surprisingly few players with a legitimate claim to the right tackle throne, especially since the Penei Sewell moved to left tackle in Detroit this offseason. The Chargers' Joe Alt has been excellent since he was selected fifth overall in the 2024 NFL draft, but injuries continue to bedevil him. Both he and Ladd McConkey suffered injuries against the Seahawks in Week 4 and may miss some time.
There are plenty of solid, ascending right tackles, such as Amarius Mims and Armand Membou, and reliable veterans like Brian O'Neill. But when looking across the changed landscape of right tackles in the NFL, only one name appears as the undisputed king: the Chicago Bears' Darnell Wright.
The last calendar year has been a life-changing time for Wright. At the conclusion of the 2025 NFL season, Wright earned his first All-Pro honors, finishing second only to Penei Sewell, who took first-team honors. He later appeared in ESPN's best offensive tackles list at No. 6, the highest ranking of any right tackle. Then, at the start of training camp, Wright signed a record-setting contract extension with the Bears .
If anyone expected Wright to rest on his laurels in 2026, he's only proven them wrong. Through four weeks, Wright has earned an elite 97.1 impact grade from Pro Football Network , making him the highest graded offensive lineman in the NFL. The next best players in PFN's ranking are both two-time All-Pros: guard Quinn Meinerz (88.8) and left tackle Garrett Bolles (88.4).
Wright is an absolute road grader in the run game, earning a 94.1 run protection grade from PFN, also the best mark in the league. His 86.0 pass protection grade comes in second only behind Bolles' 88.1 grade. He's not been called for a single penalty yet and he's only allowed four pressures in 163 passing snaps, according to Pro Football Focus .
There's a long way yet to go in the season, but Wright feels like a top candidate to win the Protector of the Year award just one year after Joe Thuney was the inaugural winner .
The Bears selected Wright with the No. 10 pick in the 2023 NFL draft, and he's arguably been GM Ryan Poles' best draft selection yet. Many Bears fans bemoaned the missed opportunity to draft defensive tackle Jalen Carter, but Wright's career arc through three-plus seasons should put any such complaints to bed. He started off strong even as a rookie and has only gotten better, missing just two out of 55 games.
Now, with Lane Johnson retired and a Protector of the Year award firmly within sight, there can be no denying the truth. Darnell Wright is the best right tackle in the NFL, perhaps even the best player at either tackle position, and I don't think he'll be relinquishing his title any time soon.

title: 2 Big-Swing Bears Trade Targets on the Edge That Ryan Poles Must Pursue
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' defense has turned out to be a major surprise through the first month of the 2026 NFL season.
Head coach Ben Johnson and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen have thrived on the "no-name defense" overperforming through the first four games.
At some point, general manager Ryan Poles and rest of the team's brain trust will have to embrace some big names, though. After Marcus Davenport's release and subsequent retirement on Monday, a name could be useful along the edge beyond just another depth piece. There's inexperience and past medical histories to worry about.
While the natural reaction is to eye a reunion with Khalil Mack, given his Los Angeles Chargers' 0-4 hole and the prior familiarity with Allen, Poles isn't going for a 35-year-old with no long-term future in the Windy City beyond a rental.
He could go for these two under-30 stars who are on teams that are going nowhere fast instead, though:
ESPN's Adam Schefter has already floated Arizona Cardinals EDGE Josh Sweat as a potential deadline name to watch. Sweat has seven tackles, two quarterback hits, and a sack through a 1-3 start for Arizona.
The Cardinals' only win was against the aforementioned 0-4 Chargers and though they've improved over the past two games, they've held multiple 20-point deficits in NFC West divisional games. Arizona should be a seller by November 10.
Sweat has no guaranteed money beyond the 2026 season, so Poles could essentially have him on a "prove-it" arrangement. Of course, with Chicago's current defensive ends, there could be chances to prove it on a massive stage.
Dayo Odeyingbo is showing no signs of residual damage from his Achilles tear, but the chances of another major injury are higher because of it. Austin Booker is playing well in his rookie season, but there's always the chance deep waters pose problems when the stakes raise in January.
Sweat's run defense leaves a bit to be desired, but he'd be a strong fit opposite Montez Sweat -- who, no, is not his brother -- assuming Allen's complex playbook doesn't cause any friction.
Miami Dolphins defensive end Chop Robinson bulked up to 265 pounds in the offseason, making him a stronger edge-setting option. He hasn't become elite overnight, but the third-year EDGE is improving.
Allen doesn't use wide-9 techniques like Jeff Hafley that open up unique lanes for Robinson to attack. It'd take an adjustment for Robinson, since he's played in some havoc-heavy schemes like Hafley's and Manny Diaz's at Penn State.
With that said, Anthony Weaver's concepts were closer schematically to Allen's, which focus on cohesion with the interior defensive linemen to close the gaps. Robinson played under Weaver for two seasons.
Robinson is more of a long-term play. The upside of Robinson and Odeyingbo on passing downs is tantalizing. At 23, he's a moldable piece that could grow within the Bears organization for years to come.
We'll see how desperate Miami gets. The Dolphins have no need to lock many pieces down and have unclean books from dead money already.
Perhaps Poles could strike gold with Robinson if Miami looks to move their valuable assets for future-focused returns.

title: Ben Johnson Mic'd Up Video Shows Chicago Bears Coach's Hilarious Tendencies
full_text:
We always love a good mic'd up video, so you know we especially love one featuring Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson.
Johnson was given the mic'd up treatment for the Week 4 game against the New York Jets. It was cool to hear what Johnson said while on the sideline, but we also noticed he really, really enjoys clicking his pen.
In the video below, you can see Johnson repeatedly clicking it starting at the 13-second mark. At that rate, Johnson might be replacing his pen on a weekly basis. The good news is Johnson makes quite a bit of money to be able to afford it.
Another tendency we heard from Johnson was him saying "knock it, hit it, gash it" to himself. That is, of course, about the run game, which flourished against Gang Green thanks to Kyle Monangai .
We'd venture to guess the two times Johnson said "knock it, hit it, gash it" weren't the first times he has said that.
Enjoy Ben Johnson on the mic 🎤 @ChicagoBears @insidethenfl Week 4 Mic'd Up on X pic.twitter.com/Ga1fAOR8pw
Ben Johnson is all of us. After all, who doesn't love clicking their pen? It's a time-honored tradition, but while it's enjoyable for the person clicking the pen, it's also extremely annoying for the people who have to listen to it.
Thankfully for those around Johnson, there's enough noise in the stadium that Bears personnel likely doesn't hear him doing it.
After the game, you could see the love Johnson has for Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, who he coached with in Detroit. Glenn served as the Detroit Lions' defensive coordinator while Johnson was Detroit's offensive play-caller.
"Good job," Johnson said to Glenn. "I love you,man."
Johnson also offered some words of encouragement to Glenn, who has had a rough tenure in New York over a season-plus, as evidenced by his 4-17 overall record.
"You guys are close," Johnson said. "You guys are close. You're right there... Keep going."
It's true the Jets have been more competitive this season, but you wouldn't have known that in Week 4, as the Bears dominated the Jets in all three phases of the game.
While Chicago only scored 23 points, it should have had a lot more but the Bears were just 2-for-7 in the red zone , something they must clean up.
On defense, the domination was fully clear. The Bears held the Jets to just 157 yards of total offense, and 58 of those came on one play, which was Geno Smith's 58-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Williams that victimized Tyrique Stevenson.
With that impressive showing, the Bears have now posted three straight impressive performances on defense, and as you heard in the mic'd up video, Johnson is definitely loving it.
If the Bears can put it all together the rest of the way, a Super Bowl could be in their future.

title: Matt LaFleur Doesn't View Bears-Packers Like Ben Johnson Does
full_text:
Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur isn't playing up the rivalry aspect of his team's historical NFC North rivalry with the Chicago Bears. Not like Ben Johnson has over the past year, anyway.
LaFleur shared an unpopular answer with his fanbase on why he isn't taking a similar approach to Johnson when asked by the media.
“Because this game is about players and so we’ll keep it about the players. I’m not the one out there they’re playing … don’t get me wrong. I love the rivalry. It’s awesome. It’s great. It’s intense," LaFleur said .
"You can feel it on gameday. You can feel it throughout the course of the week and also the significance, I mean, they’re the defending North champions. So what a great opportunity, great challenge for us in our home stadium to play against the defending champs.”
Johnson has had a much different approach about the game. After the Bears came back to win down 18 at halftime against the Packers in the NFC Wild Card game this past January, he swore about how he wanted to beat Green Bay. He furthered that sentiment at the NFL Draft Combine in February.
It's understandable why there is such a drastic difference between how LaFleur and Johnson view this game.
The Packers may be the least convincing 2-2 team in the league. Owning one-score wins over the one-win New York Jets and winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Green Bay has hardly put a scare into the NFC North this season.
Atlanta Falcons running back tandem Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. ran over the injury-riddled defense to the tune of 244 rushing yards during the Packers' infamous 35-14 Thursday Night Football loss .
In Week 1, Carson Wentz took over the Minnesota Vikings' offense in the first quarter and game-managed a gem alongside a running back room that hardly carried the load themselves. Minnesota's defense put the offense in good spots to score by forcing mistakes from Jordan Love and Co., while the Packers gave up four touchdowns in the Vikings' four red-zone trips.
It's clear that EDGE Micah Parsons is missed. Parsons has no clear timetable to return just yet, putting the 2026 season in dangerous territory for the Pack.
Pretty much nothing is going right for Green Bay. LaFleur doesn't need to provide anymore ammo after losing to Chicago in two high-stakes matchups last December and January to squander the division away and get sent home from the playoffs.
On the flip side, life is sweet for Johnson.
His Bears quarterbacks, all three of them through four games, and both of his running backs, D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, are contributing to the No. 1 offense in the league through four games. Dennis Allen's "no-name defense" is thriving despite the absences of slot corner Kyler Gordon and defensive tackle Shemar Turner, among others.
Johnson owns the upper hand in this rivalry, and may just own the upper hand on a division-wide scale despite Chicago's Week 2 loss to Minnesota . In year two, he already has a true contender on his hands.
Don't be surprised to see Johnson embrace the rivalry, while LaFleur continues to downplay the sky falling around him.
Good thing LaFleur and GM Brian Gutekunst were extended this past offseason, because being lame ducks with the chance to start 2-3 after a third straight loss to the Bears would be catastrophic for their careers.

title: Two Bears Earn Early NFL All-Rookie Honors, And One Surprising Honorable Mention
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have started the 2026 NFL season on a roll, going 3-1 in the first quarter of the season despite Caleb Williams' hamstring injury sidelining him for the last two games. There's plenty of credit for this hot start to go around, including contributions from key rookies. Two in particular are already making a name for themselves in the NFL world, earning a spot in The Athletic's early All-Rookie team .
Dane Brugler, writing for The Athletic , assembled this list of standout rookies through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season, and he slotted Dillon Thieneman in as a first-team All-Rookie safety, while Malik Muhammad made the cut as the second-team All-Rookie nickel cornerback. Justifying his selection of Thieneman, Brugler wrote, "Thieneman leads all rookie defensive backs in tackles (30) and has paced Chicago in tackles in each of its first four games. His end-zone interception of Anday Dalton in Week 3 felt like a momentum-changing play."
As for Muhammad, Brugler writes, "Despite playing almost exclusively outside in college, most of his snaps have come in the nickel this season — he's allowing just 44.4% completions when targeted."
The 2026 NFL draft was the first draft for Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles in which his first-round pick was not in the Top 10, and that of course made his job more difficult. Fans and analysts will say it's easy to hit on prospects with such a high pick, but it's not so easy when you're picking in the 20's. But the early returns from Poles' fifth rookie class are evidence that he might just be a really good drafter.
The Bears added Dillon Thieneman with the No. 25 pick in the draft, and it was considered the biggest Round 1 heist of the draft . Some early struggles in training camp foreshadowed a bumpy rookie season, but Thieneman already looks like a savvy veteran. He's allowed just a 22.7 passer rating when targeted, according to Pro Football Focus , which means opposing quarterbacks would have more success if they had simply thrown the ball at their own feet.
What's more, Thieneman has earned a 91.7 impact grade from Pro Football Network , the second-highest score for any safety in the NFL, trailing only two-time All-Pro Talanoa Hufanga.
Meanwhile, Muhammad made Bears franchise history after Week 2 , becoming the first Bears rookie to record an interception and a sack in his first two games. As Brugler noted, he's been playing in the slot position despite almost no experience there in college, and he's not only surviving but thriving. His 41.9 passer rating allowed when targeted is the fifth-best mark for all cornerbacks according to Pro Football Focus .
The inclusion of Muhammad and Thieneman in Brugler's All-Rookie Team list probably doesn't surprise any Bears fans, but one of Brugler's Honorable Mentions may. Sam Roush earned a shoutout as an Honorable Mention among rookie tight ends. Brugler did not provide any context for any of his Honorable Mentions, but I don't entirely disagree.
For one thing, the list of rookie tight ends who have caught even one pass yet is short. For another, Roush has shown flashes of a quality tight end. He shone in the Bears' preseason joint practice with the Tennessee Titans , and he went on to make a beautiful 19-yard reception in their preseason finale. However, his abysmal Week 2 performance against the Minnesota Vikings soured many Bears fans against him.
Whatever fans think of him, however, it doesn't seem like the coaches are giving up on Roush. He's still earning targets in games, including a critical fourth-down conversion in the Bears' Week 3 upset win over the Philadelphia Eagles . Bears fans may still be unhappy with him, but it's far too soon to eulogize Roush's career, and Brugler may be on to something by including him as an Honorable Mention.

title: Kyler Gordon's Bears Return Set to Disrupt Malik Muhammad, Tyrique Stevenson
full_text:
Whenever Kyler Gordon returns to the Chicago Bears, the rest of the secondary will have to acquiesce. The 26-year-old is within his practice window to return to the team after a stint on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list.
Gordon's return could come this Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, though Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons is more likely. As Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said this week, it all comes down to Gordon being sustainably healthy enough to suit up.
Gordon's return is coming at a good time. Chicago's offense has held up well without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, and the defense has relied on backs like Cam Lewis and rookie Malik Muhammad to handle the slot responsibilities.
That's put an undue burden on Tyrique Stevenson on the outside. Stevenson has allowed a 143.8 passer rating and PFF grades him as a 44.4 in coverage.
Gordon's eventual presence is going to shift those responsibilities.
Muhammad was an outside corner at the University of Texas. The former Longhorns allowed just two passes of over 30 yards during his time in Austin, with opposing quarterbacks owning a measly 60% completion rate during his senior season.
Muhammad belongs on the boundary. He was drafted to help a cornerback room that was seen as depleted because it lost Nahshon Wright in free agency . Muhammad is the gamble that either solves this problem with a fourth-round pick or highlights the need for more outside help by the trade deadline or next offseason. The early returns are positive, but there's still plenty of season left to find that out.
The position is only that dire because Stevenson has been a glaring issue in coverage. Ben Johnson has benched him temporarily, but he played against the New York Jets in a 23-12 win at Soldier Field because of the banged-up nature of the secondary.
Gordon's integration back into the lineup may be the beginning of the end of Stevenson's time on the Bears. Given that this is a contract year, the lack of faith in Stevenson, which has already been evident in a Week 3 benching, doesn't speak to this relationship extending beyond his rookie contract.
Stevenson came to Chicago with high hopes and delivered on them early, but his best days were under Eric Washington and Jon Hoke. Stevenson may not be a good fit for Allen's system, but he still has plenty of value in this league.
The sooner Gordon returns, the sooner the Bears and Stevenson can accept the reality that unless injuries necessitate a need and a transformation takes place, this partnership peaked years ago and isn't headed for a renewal.

title: Chicago Bears Week 4 Rookie Report: Who's Rising and Falling After Week 4 Win?
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have received major contributions from a few members of the rookie class through the first quarter of the season. However, not everyone in the class has thrived so far.
Unlike last season, their biggest contributors have come on the defensive side of the ball. Their offensive additions have made a minimal impact.
It's still early to make an accurate assessment of how their careers will go with only four games in the books. We have a pretty good idea where their respective rookie seasons are going at this point, though.
Dillon Thieneman squarely belongs in the Defensive Rookie of the Year conversation right now. He's had at least six tackles in every game, and Sunday's win over the Jets marked the first game in which he didn't have a pass deflection (the fact that the defense was only on the field for 32 plays and the Jets called only 15 passes surely played a role there).
You could make a strong case that he's been Chicago's best defensive player thus far , and that's saying a lot when his running mate, Coby Bryant, has been on IR since the start of training camp. Thieneman has had an awful lot on his plate, and he's thrived anyway.
Logan Jones really might not see the field this season. Aside from a terrible performance against Minnesota in Week 2, Garrett Bradbury has held his own at center.
The veteran would have to lose the job for Jones to crack the lineup. The odds of that happening don't seem high after he's stacked solid performances against the Eagles and Jets. Fans will lament this selection at the end of the season, but he's a shoo-in to take over the starting job next offseason, with Bradbury only playing out a one-year deal.
Speaking of draft picks that Bears fans lament, Ben Johnson doesn't seem ready to give up on the Sam Roush experiment anytime soon. The rookie tight end was on the field for 23 plays against the Jets. Unfortunately, he just can't seem to get out of his own way.
Sure, Roush got into the stat sheet with an 8-yard grab against the Jets. However, that 8-yard grab was a screen pass that could've been an explosive play if he waited for the convoy of blockers he ran around. He really might've reached the end zone from 30 yards out if the blockers did their job downfield.
Ben Johnson is really trying to make the Ben Roush "secret weapon" thing a reality 😂 pic.twitter.com/988l8Xqrn1
Is he potentially being overanalyzed because of a rough showing against the Vikings? Sure. Any other player would get the same treatment if they got tackled short of the first-down line after running around their blockers on a screen play, though.
Zavion Thomas saw a career-high 9 offensive snaps against New York. Why is his stock down? Because Ben Johnson isn't scheming passes his way. He didn't have a single target against a team that is severely lacking speed at cornerback.
Notably, Thomas has also been somewhat disappointing in the return game after showing a lot of promise there in the preseason finale against Tennessee . He gained only 70 yards off 4 kick return attempts against the Jets. An average of 17.5 yards per return won't cut it for someone who was drafted in the third round largely for the impact he'd bring to the return game.
Their decision not to use Thomas on punt returns is also a conundrum, especially considering Kalif Raymond's impact on offense thus far. Has he shown ball security issues there in practice? Or do they just like what they've seen from the veteran there?
Malik Muhammad II has been a revelation. The fourth-round pick has already settled in as a key defensive starter, and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has already said that he might be their best cover man. He's earned that praise, too.
Muhammad has allowed only 8 catches on 18 targets and has given up a passer rating of 41.9% when targeted. The 22-year-old is coming off another rock-solid performance against the Jets, and he helped the team hold Garrett Wilson to only three grabs for 27 yards . Muhammad might not be a household name yet, but he certainly seems well on his way.
On the bright side, we don't have to keep using Keyshaun Elliott's Arizona unis. They FINALLY snapped a picture of him. However, that picture was taken on the sideline.
He's only played on special teams thus far, and is still waiting to see his first action on the defensive side of the ball. Unfortunately for him (and fortunately for everyone else), with the starting linebackers settling in nicely after a rough start to the season, he'll probably have to keep waiting. It always seemed like a redshirt year for Elliott after he missed virtually all of training camp.
The Bears' defense only played 32 defensive snaps against the New York Jets. The fact that Jordan van den Berg played seven of them shows they've seen enough from him to give him a spot in the rotation. It's not like anyone on the defensive side of the ball was gassed at any point and he needed to come in to relieve them.
However, JVDB still played the second-fewest snaps among all nine active defensive linemen, behind only special teams ace Daniel Hardy, who has only seen seven snaps on defense this season. The rookie defensive tackle's role could expand as the season progresses, but he'll have to make the most of the limited opportunities he receives. He hasn't done so thus far.

title: Why No-Name Chicago Bears Defense Can't Be Too Proud of Surge Just Yet
full_text:
The Bears shouldn't get too carried away with this "no-name" defensive surge coach Ben Johnson raved about following Sunday's 23-12 win over the New York Jets .
Sure, the defense has shown improvement since the opener when they allowed 37 points to Carolina but benefited from a tremendous offensive explosion. There's no doubt about this. When a team goes three weeks and allows 28 total points in today's NFL, it's a defensive triumph.
In fact, the Bears on defense are fifth in defensive EPA, their passer rating against is third best in the NFL as well as No. 1 over the past three games, and they have even risen to 13th in rushing defense after struggling at this mightily in recent years .
If you look at the NFL statistics for the first "quarter" of the season, the Bears are where a team wants to be at No. 1 on offense and No. 3 on defense.
However, those numbers are more reflective of a team playing tremendous complementary football than they are of the defensive side achieving elite all-around status the way their offense has. There is one underlying flaw they have and it can be exploited greatly in a few coming games, although not necessarily this week at Green Bay.
The Bears have the best offensive mind and a top 5 defensive mind. Bears rank #1 in total offense averaging 429 YPG. Bears rank #3 in total defense allowing just 282.3 YPG Shoutout Ben Johnson and Dennis Allen.🔥 pic.twitter.com/F4zLqxArrh
What has happened is the offense's ball control — No. 1 in the league at 36:35 per game — has helped kept the Bears defense off the field. The Bears also lead the NFL in total plays (74.5 per game). The defense has taken it away enough to get the offense opportunities to hold the ball and score but the defense has also done a great deal right on its own to stop teams.
There is nothing wrong with any of this, but if they are to be taken seriously as a Super Bowl contender they need to stop the run better.
It's low-hanging fruit for some team to grab against the Bears. A ball-control team, especially a running team with power backs like Atlanta or like Seattle or even New England, can commit to the run and keep it away from the Bears offense as they burn a run defense that gives up too many yards on early downs.
Bears defense is supposed to be bad, yet the Jets offense struggled wayyyyy more against them then they did Detroit
The Bears defense still gives up too many yards on average, anyway. They're tied for 24th in yards allowed per play (5.9) and running game weakness is the big part of this. So are the occasional chunk pass plays allowed, like the  touchdown Tyrique Stevenson gave up on Sunday.
Their rushing defense is in the top half of the league and they've had only the second-fewest rushes attempted against them. Yet, they still give up 4.9 yards per run and that ranks 29th in the NFL. It's exactly where they finished last year and a tenth of a yard better per rush.
They give up too many yards before contact to backs as they're moved off the line of scrimmage.
Bears Defense 2026 (4 games) 🔸 Opp pts/gm  16.3 (4th) 🔸 Opp yds/gm  282.3 (3rd) 2025 (17 games) 🔸 Opp pts/gm  24.3 (23rd) 🔸 Opp yds/gm  363.7 (29th) pic.twitter.com/qhjfsPzLtz
What has allowed them to flourish is their offense putting up points and possessing the ball, while forcing other teams to abandon the run in order to keep up. It's why there are so few rushing attempts against them and why they are so high in rushing defense while giving up so many yards per rush.
The offense is carrying them even though the defense has made strides in areas like the pass rush, where they are tied for eighth in sacks per game, and 14th in ESPN's team pass rush win rate.
If you want to look at a really telling analytic, they are last in the NFL in run-stop win rate (24%).
A defensive approach emphasizing being stout against the run but failing to actually do it can cause a rapid collapse. A team riding on its own offense's ball control coattails and also its own defensive rush-and-cover improvement can have problems when the opponent does commit to the run and also can play a little defense.
The Bears are at the forefront of a trend of sorts. "The run game is back en vogue throughout the NFL," @ProFootballTalk says. "The best offenses are unpredictable, and they keep the defense on their heels." Florio calls it "incredible" to go 2-0 without Caleb Williams. pic.twitter.com/qS8M21pLYZ
Bijan Robinson is coming or, rather, they're going to him.
The Atlanta Falcons mauled the Packers and the Saints in their last two games using power running and play-action passing.  It's exactly the way to stop Ben Johnson's team. In other words, give him a taste of his own medicine.
59 yards on the third play from scrimmage. Bijan Robinson, everyone 🤩 @ATLvsNO on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bUgQ5t7g0S
Last week was said the be a "trap" Bears game between strong opponents and after Monday Night Football. The real trap looks now like Atlanta for the Bears, after facing the rival Packers and before consecutive games against Super Bowl teams New England and Seattle.
After the Bears beat the Jets, linebacker Devin Bush said it was "...one of the easiest NFL games I've ever played in. I'm not sore at all."
After seeing his offense hold the ball all day, Bush even said, "I got bored a couple times" when he was on the sidelines all that time.
Considering the Falcons ran for over 200 yards in each of their past two games while pummeling the Packers and Saints, no one on the Bears' defense is likely to be yawning in Week 6.
Brian Robinson matches Bijan's second TD of the day pic.twitter.com/5vTzoy9qyG

title: Bears Reunite with Veteran Wide Receiver After Marcus Davenport Release
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are making more roster moves ahead of their Week 5 showdown with the Green Bay Packers. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Bears are signing veteran receiver and training camp standout Scotty Miller to the practice squad. Miller showcased good chemistry with the second- and third-string players in training camp, and in three preseason games he hauled in seven receptions for 65 yards.
Miller seemed like a good bet to make the Bears' final 53-man roster, but he missed the cut. Now, the Bears are bringing him back to the practice squad after a series of roster moves on Monday opened up a spot for him.
One of the Bears' more surprising additions this offseason was the signing of Marcus Davenport halfway through training camp. By that point in the offseason, it seemed like the starting defensive line was just about set, and Davenport would provide only marginal help at best. Indeed, he didn't even practice with the Bears in August as he continued his own ramp-up program.
In the end, Davenport missed the cut for the final 53-man roster and was signed to the Bears' practice squad . On Saturday, the Bears finally called him up to the active roster ahead of their dominant Week 4 victory over the New York Jets . He recorded just one assisted tackle in his first game as a Bear, a game which ended up being his only game as a Bear and his final NFL appearance.
In a series of roster moves on Monday, the Bears cut ties with Marcus Davenport , a move that he had apparently requested after the game. Later that day, we learned that Davenport was retiring from the NFL altogether. If that is truly the last we see of Davenport in the NFL, at least he got to go out with a win.
Miller grew up less than an hour away from Halas Hall, in Barrington Illinois. Even if he's not on the active roster, it has to be pretty cool to be on the Bears' practice squad. He's a dependable veteran and, as aforementioned, he showed some good chemistry with the backups in training camp. In his career, he's caught 99 passes for 1,216 yards and six touchdowns. Maybe reception No. 100 will come as a member of the Bears.
Of course, the hope is that the Bears never need to bother calling him up to the active roster, but if Miller does have to step in as the WR5 or WR6 for a game, he can more than handle his own. He also brings special teams experience to the table, to boot.

title: Everything That Went Wrong For Chicago Bears in Week 4 Win Over New York Jets
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are riding high after a Week 4 win over the New York Jets and a 3-1 start overall.
The Bears are playing well on offense despite not having Caleb Williams, who is still recovering from his hamstring injury that is going to keep him out another week .
What's more impressive is how well the Bears have played on defense over the last three games. That side of the ball was Chicago's biggest concern going into the season.
While the Bears dominated the Jets on Sunday, they did not play a perfect game and there were some issues throughout. Here's what went wrong for Chicago in Week 4.
The Bears won handily, no doubt, but they should have absolutely blown the doors off the Jets.
The only reason the score wasn't more lopsided was because the Bears struggled mightily in the red zone , converting on just two of seven attempts throughout the game.
For reference, scoring at a 28.5% clip would rank dead last in the NFL if that was Chicago's season-long success rate, according to TeamRankings.com .
Through four games, the Bears are scoring touchdowns on just 42.11% of their red-zone trips, the third-worst in the league.
The Bears coughed up the football twice to the Jets, with D'Andre Swift losing a fumble and Tyson Bagent throwing an interception. Swift's fumble actually got him benched , but we don't think that decision will carry into next game.
Chicago nearly had a third turnover on another pick from Bagent, but it was negated because of a penalty.
The Bears are now tied for the ninth-most giveaways in the NFL with six. That's something Chicago needs to clean up moving forward.
The Bears' defense was phenomenal for a third straight game and there is every reason in the world to be excited about this unit. But that doesn't mean everyone played well.
The Jets threw for just 119 yards in the contest, but Tyrique Stevenson was responsible for 96 of those yards , which he surrendered on five receptions on seven targets, per PFF.
Stevenson was also guilty of allowing the Jets' only semblance of a showing of life on offense during the game when he permitted Isaiah Williams' 58-yard touchdown catch.
The bad news is, Stevenson still isn't good. The good news is, the Bears may not have to depend on him for much longer. With Kyler Gordon coming back soon , the Bears can deploy him in the slot and move Malik Muhammad to the boundary.
Even before Gordon's return, the Bears were moving away from the fourth-year cornerback by putting Muhammad on the outside and Cam Lewis in the slot in Week 3. Unfortunately, Lewis wasn't able to play in Week 4 due to injury , but we'd expect him back in the slot if he plays in Week 5. Gordon might be back as soon as this week, also, after he practiced in full last week.
While Monangai was running all over the Jets to the tune of 146 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries, he suffered a thumb injury late in the contest.
Head coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is day-to-day and is "going to be OK," according to ESPN's Courtney Cronin , but his status obviously bears monitoring, especially with the struggles Swift has seen of late.

title: Zac Taylor Drops Latest Bengals Star Injury Update As Dolphins Practices Begin
full_text:
The Bengals are back to practice this afternoon in anticipation of Sunday's road battle against the Miami Dolphins.
Names like Ja'Marr Chase (concussion), Tee Higgins (groin), Bryan Cook (ankle), and more are trying to recover in time to get on the field this week.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor updated their statuses on Wednesday before the latest practice session.
Taylor noted that Chase is still in the concussion protocol, while Higgins is going to be limited at practice today. Kyle Dugger (quad) and Cook will not practice today, but Taylor didn't close the door on them practicing Thursday.
B.J. Hill (Achilles) is slated to return to practice today.
"They'll be out today," Taylor said about Cook and Dugger before touching on Thursday chances they practice. "We'll see. Probably Dugger is less likely, and we'll see where Bryan's at."
Cincinnati is 2-2 in the 2026 season after consecutive losses in recent weeks. They were down to just two wide receivers on Sunday, but could get Colbie Young back this week and may be able to have Higgins on the field as well.
"Yeah, we'll just keep working through the week. I think initially, when he did it, I would have thought it was going to be longer term than it was, but he's done a really good job rehabbing and trying to put himself in a position to get back sooner rather than later. I'm not ready to declare when that will be, though," Taylor said about Young.
WLWT's Charlie Clifford reported the team brought no one in for a tryout or workout on Tuesday during the off day.
"We just have to make it work. No one wants to hear any reason why that wouldn't work," Taylor said Sunday about playing without Chase and Higgins. "We got an unbelievable coaching staff that can problem-solve. The players understand it. I mean, you got a guy like Mitch (Tinsley), who just showed back up, and he's playing a lot of snaps for us. He and Dohnte (Meyers) are the last two receivers we have left, and they're out there making plays. And all four of our tight ends that are out there are doing exactly what we need them to do to put us in position. No one wants to hear it, but I am proud of the team for how they fought. There was a lot that went into that game. We're really disappointed that we lost.
"We're not that kind of team this year that's going to take consolation in the losses, but I am allowed to see the silver lining, and this team has a lot of fight. If I get this team for 14 more weeks or 13 more weeks, whatever it is — I'm signing up for that all day, because we're going to have a great year. It's just disappointing that we didn't get this one."
Cincinnati has three practices this week for these names to test their injuries and try to play.

title: Joe Burrow Dials Into His Top NBA Player Comparison as 2026 Season Rolls on
full_text:
Joe Burrow appeared on the Gronk & Jules Podcast recently and dove into a few fun topics, including what NBA player he'd compare himself to.
Burrow is an accurate sharpshooter on the field and picked a similar type of player on the court.
He went with NBA star Klay Thompson, who's won a few world titles in his career with the Golden State Warriors.
"I was like a poor man's Klay Thompson, like I can really shoot it. I can defend," Burrow told Julian Edelman on the FOX Sports podcast.
Cincinnati is getting ready for its latest battle in the AFC against Miami. They are in the morass of 2-2 teams and currently sit last in the AFC North
The team likely needs to win this weekend or history says this season's Super Bowl hopes are nearly over. According to RotoWire , no 2-3 team in the last decade has ever reached a Super Bowl.
"We're not where we want to be yet," Burrow said to Edelman when the Bengals were 2-0 at the time. "I'm going to always push us to be perfect, but to be sitting where we are, how the games have played out, we're really happy with it. Obviously, it's a long season. You know, the first two weeks have so many eyes on them, so much pressure on it, just because of how anticipated the entire country is, just go watch football.
"Those are probably two of the least meaningful games in the season. A lot of teams go 2-0 and don't do anything the rest of the year. I think a team a couple years ago went 2-0 and ended up 3-14. So doesn't really matter what happens the first two weeks. Just what happens the next week."
Burrow has played well enough to win, but not quite to his MVP-level standards. He'll try to post a complete, winning performance this weekend, with no turnovers.

title: T.J. Houshmandzadeh Calls Out Key Bengals’ Position Group After Jaguars Loss
full_text:
Former Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver T.J. Houshmandzadeh sees a major issue that opponents are exploiting through the first five weeks of the season.
After Cincinnati's tough loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Houshmandzadeh pointed directly to the left side of the Bengals' offensive line. Joe Burrow played well at times but threw two costly interceptions and continued to face pressure.
Houshmandzadeh believes teams have found a clear formula for making life difficult for Burrow and the Bengals' offensive line.
"To beat the Bengals, it seems as if you attack the left side of the offensive line," Houshmandzadeh said. "The left side of the offensive line, bro, we gotta be better, man. Like, we gotta be better. We can't just be letting [guys] come and smack Joe."
For Cincinnati, that's a concerning assessment, especially with Burrow at the center of everything the Bengals hope to accomplish this season. If opposing defenses believe they can consistently pressure the Bengals by attacking one side of the offensive line, Cincinnati will have to address it quickly.
Houshmandzadeh also indicated that defending tight ends on the other side of the ball could be another recurring problem.
"Every tight end just gets off on us," Houshmandzadeh said. "We cannot stop a tight end."
Despite those concerns, the former Bengals star isn't sounding the alarm about Cincinnati's season just yet.
"It's tough, man. I'm kind of disappointed, to be honest with you," Houshmandzadeh said. "Defense had one off game. Not yesterday. Last week, one off game. They played well yesterday."
He also noted Burrow's two interceptions, calling them "two costly plays" that hurt Cincinnati despite an otherwise strong performance. The Bengals now turn their attention to the Miami Dolphins before their Week 6 bye week.
Houshmandzadeh called Miami a potential "get right team," but was also quick to point out that nothing is guaranteed in the NFL.
"This is the National Football League. Anybody can beat you," Houshmandzadeh said.
That makes getting things corrected up front even more important. Baltimore awaits Cincinnati following the bye, and protecting Burrow will only become more important as the Bengals move deeper into their schedule. For Houshmandzadeh, Cincinnati has to prevent opposing defenses from turning the left side of its offensive line into an obvious point of attack.

title: Latest Head Coaching Hot Seat List Throws Zac Taylor in a Complicated Category
full_text:
Every game in the NFL season matters. That's why the Cincinnati Bengals, coming off their second straight loss in the 2026 season, have some folks on edge.
The 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars this past Sunday moved the Bengals to 2-2 on the young season. While the sky may not be falling, the chances that it will soon start raining meatballs are growing higher.
A season that ends with the Bengals missing out on the postseason for a fourth straight season may all but seal the fate of head coach Zac Taylor. On Monday, Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr revealed his latest head coaching hot seat list, and Coach Taylor landed on the list in a very interesting spot.
Orr broke down the hot seat list in tiers. For Coach Taylor, he is in tier 3, which is also known as the tier of "Established names battling staleness, time and circumstance." The Bengals head coach is listed at number five on the hot seat ranking.
"The Bengals exiting a loss to the Jaguars having almost completely reverted to the 2025 version of themselves officially took the polish off what was a promising Zac Taylor offseason," wrote Orr . " Taylor is under contract through the 2027 season, making this the offseason where he would either sign a Band-Aid, LaFleur-style extension or separate from the Bengals for good. Taylor will always be under the microscope given the ticking clock on Burrow’s prime. With teams like the Bills making similar pivots in the offseason to turn away from successful, established head coaches, and a likely surge in interested candidates, the Taylor conversation will likely become a weekly fixture if the Bengals remain mired in mediocrity. "
After the loss on Sunday, Taylor's overall record as the head coach of the Bengals sits at 54-65. Taylor has taken this franchise to heights not seen in decades; however, just like Orr pointed out, things are growing stale.
Some of the chatter this summer was about this being a so-called now or never year for the team. A date against the lowly Miami Dolphins awaits them this Sunday. It's weird to call a game against an opponent who is 0-4 a must-win, but Coach Taylor can't afford any slip-ups against lower caliber teams.

title: Joe Burrow Faced Something the Bengals Haven't Seen Since 2024 in Loss to Jaguars
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals dropped their second straight game of the season in brutal fashion on Sunday. The 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars will be drilled into everyone's mind until the team takes the field this Sunday against the Miami Dolphins.
There are plenty of reasons as to why the Bengals found themselves on the losing end. One of the biggest reasons is that the offensive line was not prepared for the looks the Jaguars' defense was giving them.
Actually, one stat proves that the Jaguars were bringing more than the Bengals have seen since a Week 11 game against the Los Angeles Chargers in 2024.
According to Next Gen Stats , Joe Burrow was pressured 20 times on Sunday, which was 34.5% of his dropbacks.
The Bengals quarterback was definitely feeling the pressure. Burrow threw two interceptions, the last one being the backbreaker that stalled a potential game-winning drive.
The Jaguars had just two sacks with all those pressures, but the pressures still played an important role in the their win over the Bengals.
The Bengals have a lot to clean up before they take on the Dolphins. Quarterback pressure was an issue on Sunday, and it was an issue two weeks ago when the Pittsburgh Steelers secured a win over the Bengals after a fumble recovery on a Burrow sack.
This is not the same offensive line the Bengals have had in previous seasons. The team has allowed just nine sacks this season, the 15th most in the league. Things have certainly changed up front, but the pressure from the Jaguars' defense may be the secret sauce in beating the Bengals.
Facing that many pressures in one game is bound to lead to more mistakes from a quarterback. Burrow is still one of the more elite players in the game, but just like watching Jared Goff on Sunday Night Football, Burrow's not the kind of quarterback to evade pressure.
The pressure is coming. Can the Bengals craft a game plan that will lead Burrow and this offense to more success? They better, because the weeks are starting to fly by.

title: Potential Blockbuster Bengals Trade Makes Even More Sense After Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins Injuries
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have a loaded offense with one of the best wide receiver duos in the league. Tee Higgins is one of the best, if not the best, No. 2 wide receiver in the league. He'd be the No. 1 wide receiver on a large chunk of teams in the league. Ja'Marr Chase is one of the best wide receivers in football right now, but both of them suffered injuries on Sunday.
Higgins is dealing with a groin injury and Chase is in concussion protocol.
Pair that with the fact that the Bengals have one of the worst wide receiver No. 3 situations in the NFL, and there's a clear need at the position in Cincinnati.
There are a few options that the Bengals could look at this season, and one of them sticks out above the rest: Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.
Harrison is the perfect trade target for the Bengals to make a move for. He is one of the more disrespected players in the league right now because he's underperformed relative to the expectations that were placed on him to begin his career. Still, Harrison is an uber talented wide receiver with the potential to develop into one of the better No. 2 wide receivers in the league if he's placed in the right system.
The Bengals could be the perfect system, especially with Higgins as a nearly identical receiver to Harrison. This would give the young pass catcher the perfect player to learn from and grow under. Plus, being added to an offense with so much talent would take some pressure off Harrison.
Harrison has good hands and good route running skills. He's been an elite jump ball player, but those skills haven't translated to the NFL as much as scouts would have anticipated. Still, he's incredibly young and incredibly talented. If the asking price in a trade for Harrison isn't that high, the Bengals should take a chance on him.
Harrison was not only a top prospect entering the 2024 NFL Draft, but he was considered a safe bet to become a high-end NFL player.
"Harrison comes from impressive NFL bloodlines and possesses similarities that made his father, Pro Football Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison, special. Harrison can run but isn’t a burner. What makes him tough to handle is his consistent play speed paired with quality salesmanship in his routes. He’s able to uncover no matter where he’s aligned or which part of the field his assignment takes him to, and he is capable of finishing catches in a crowd," Lance Zierlein wrote on NFL.com. "Harrison can be sudden while working possession routes, and he’s well qualified to beat any opponent with his ball skills if the battle heads deep. Harrison is a touchdown champ with a variety of ways to excel, and that characteristic figures to follow him into the pros. He has the traits and tools to win in all three phases of the route and on all three levels of the field. He’s a pedigree prospect and a Day 1 starter with high-end production expected."
If the Bengals can get Harrison for a reasonable price, they should add him. Not only because of injuries to Higgins and Chase, but for what he could mean to this offense when the wide receiver room is fully healthy.

title: Bengals Making Double History with Uniform Combo in Miami Along with Adding a Rare Twist
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals announced months ago they would being doing another “Open in Orange” game to kick off the 2026 season against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The Bengals lost their inaugural “Open in Orange” game in 2024, falling 16-10 to a New England Patriots team that would go 3-13 the rest of the way.
The Bengals wore orange pants with their orange jerseys that day, a combination never since repeated.
Last year’s Open in Orange game for the Week 2 home opener saw the team go with white pants under the orange jerseys. And though the team won the game 31-27 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, the team lost the services of quarterback Joe Burrow to a toe injury that required surgery.
The team is running back the exact same uniform combination from that game, wearing orange jerseys, white pants with orange stripes and orange socks.
The Bengals have never lost while wearing that combination, though the sample size is small. The only other time they wore it was also against the Jaguars in 2021, a 24-21 win on Thursday night football.
Full combination aside, the Bengals have had great success in the orange jerseys, going 28-11-1 (.713 winning percentage) since unveiling them in 2004.
They are 147-166-3 (.472) in all other jerseys during that span.
