title: Bengals Veteran Playmaker Deemed Team's Top Trade Candidate Early in 2026 Season
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have a chance to compete for the Super Bowl this season, despite an ugly loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers last week. The Bengals have one of the most talented rosters in the league right now.
Cincinnati's offense is the heartbeat of the team, as it's always been since Joe Burrow joined the team. But the defense is carrying its weight this season, too, which is why this roster is so dangerous. Still, they could look to make moves over the coming weeks. In fact, there's already growing speculation following one of their veteran players.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox recently listed Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki as the most tradable player on the roster at the current moment. If the Bengals look to make a move, this could be the one.
"Tight end Mike Gesicki has proven that he can be a difference-making piece of the Cincinnati Bengals' offense. However, he hasn't filled that role consistently," Knox wrote. "In Week 1, for example, he caught five passes for 78 yards and a touchdown. However, he had just three catches between Weeks 2 and 3 and finished 2025 with 307 yards.
"Gesicki should be viewed as a viable trade chip by the Bengals. He's talented, but he's also 30 and will likely be a cap casualty in 2027. The Bengals can save $8 million in 2027 cap space by releasing or trading Gesicki in the spring. They also have multiple other options at tight end in Drew Sample, Eric All Jr., Jack Endries, and Tanner Hudson."
Gesicki is the top tight end on the Bengals' offense, but they have plenty of serviceable depth behind him. They could use players like Drew Sample, Jack Endries, and Erick All Jr. to fill the gaps on offense if Gesicki is to be moved.
Gesicki could generate some trade interest, too. He's a very reliable option who has proven that he has what it takes to win. He's able to work in line and out wide in the Bengals' offense. There are a few teams who could be desperate for a tight end this year.
It's unlikely at the moment, but the Bengals could look to make a move that brings in draft capital but keeps the team ultra-competitive in the AFC. Gesicki is a key piece of the Bengals' offense, and he's one of their top red zone targets. All offseason, they looked to bring in talent to build a competitive team. It wouldn't make much sense to trade from their talented roster this early in the season.
Especially given how many other pass catchers are injured on the roster right now.

title: 3 Free Agent Wide Receivers Bengals Could Add to Help Position Depth During 2026 Season

They likely need to make another free-agent addition this week for the back end of the group to be stable enough for another full game of punishment on Sunday. Outside of Tyreek Hill , the really impactful options are thin on the market right now, but Cincinnati just needs another body to get through this stretch. None of the injuries to the four hurt players right now are expected to be very long term.
Let's dive into three candidates.

The 6-2, 215-pound pass catcher earned 70.7 and 73 Pro Football Focus grades in 2024 and 2023. He was very injured last season and only played 102 snaps.
Brown has a 13.4 yards-per-catch career average and could help take some burden off of Dohnte Meyers' plate in the coming weeks.
The former Bills standout has sputtered in his career of late, playing in six games last season.
He had just a 61.2 PFF grade on 263 snaps, but has averaged 15.9 yards per catch and has 30 career touchdowns at 27 years old.

He's been consistently average, never grading above 70.1 or below 58.4 on PFF across a full season. The 31-year-old should be able to pick up the Bengals offense quickly and fill in for spot snaps across the next few weeks.

title: Cincinnati Bengals Young Receivers Shine at Right Time
full_text:
It felt like the Cincinnati Bengals' Week 3 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers was going to be the one that stung the most in the early portion of the season. That was until a 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday became official.
The Bengals' offense could not capitalize when it mattered most, coming just one yard shy on a 4th and 10 that would have extended the game. It also doesn't help that the offense was without Ja'Marr Chase and had a banged-up Tee Higgins down the stretch.
Key players on the Bengals' offense may have been missing, but the team may have discovered that they are a lot deeper at wide receiver than they ever realized.
First-year receiver Dohnte Meyers and second-year receiver Mitchell Tinsley definitely won over some fans, even in defeat.
Meyers had a monster game, hauling in seven receptions for 82 yards, which would be career highs in both categories.
Tinsley came into Sunday's game having only eight career receptions. He left Sunday's game with a single-game career high in receptions (3) and receiving yards (49).
With Chase and Higgins' availability being unknown at the moment, the Bengals are going to have to turn to Meyers and Tinsley.
This offense is going to look a lot different if both of quarterback Joe Burrow's top targets are out for a significant time. However, fans can take solace in the chemistry that already seems to be built between Burrow and his young receivers.
There's going to be a lot of talk about the Bengals' wide receiver room this week. But the running back room is going to face its own kind of scrutiny.
The Bengals rushed for just 23 yards on Sunday. Even if Higgins and Chase were healthy the entire game, that isn't a recipe for success.
Now, the Bengals enter a game with the Dolphins that one could really say is "must win". The team is also entering said game with so much uncertainty on the offensive side of the ball. The Bengals' offense wasn't supposed to be the issue this season. Yet, it seems they have hit a crossroads.

title: Predicting Where Browns QB Dillon Gabriel Ends Up By the End of the Season
full_text:
For the Cleveland Browns, the quarterback position has stayed level for the first four weeks of the season, as Deshaun Watson has led the team to a 3-1 record. Shedeur Sanders remains the backup, while rookie Taylen Green sits behind him.
Yesterday, the Browns designated second-year QB Dillon Gabriel to return to practice after he suffered a back injury in the final preseason game vs. the Patriots. Gabriel now has a 21-day practice window, during which Cleveland can activate him at any time.
Cleveland will most likely slide Gabriel into the QB3 spot behind Watson and Sanders, but if they don't activate him in those 21 days, he will either be cut or remain in the IR spot for the whole season.
Gabriel was the 94th overall pick in the 2025 Draft; many Browns fans questioned the pick at the time given when he was taken and the plan for him. In Gabriel’s defense, he started 10 games last year, playing solid football for a backup. His completion percentage being below 60% and yards per attempt at just 5.1 put him among the lowest in the league.
So what should the plan be for a player like Gabriel? We know he can be a solid backup at any place, but his ceiling as a player seems limited; his future will most likely be on another team.
We have unfortunately see n countless starting quarterbacks go down with injury in just the first four weeks of the NFL season (Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart, Sam Darnold, Caleb Williams, and Kyler Murray, to name a few), so there will always be a market for a backup in the modern NFL.
If Cleveland was able to get any draft compensation for Gabriel, I think they will take it; we have already seen the Vikings trade away former first-rounder JJ McCarthy for just a fifth-rounder. The Atlanta Falcons were the favorite pick for Gabriel to land, as they are coached by former Browns coach Kevin Stefanski and have kept their lefties (Penix & Tagovailoa) as their starter and backup.
The Falcons would be the most reasonable team for Gabriel, but other teams that do not have an established guy at backup could make a move for him. That includes teams like the Jets, Buccaneers, Jaguars, or Dolphins, who have either rookies or players with no experience starting in their backup position.
The future of Dillon Gabriel does not look to be in Cleveland, and the decision of keeping him or not may come sooner rather than later.

title: Browns Have 2 Under-the-Radar Trade Targets Who Could Transform Their Defensive Line
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are a good football team. There's no questioning that.
Through the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season, the Browns sit with an overall record of 3-1, placing them first in the AFC North.
But even with such success, there are improvements to be made, especially if the team wants to realistically make a run by the time the playoffs roll around.
With defensive tackle Mason Graham injured, young superstar Jared Verse still attempting to get his feet underneath himself and the rest of the line being relatively unknown in the long-term reliability department, making a move to land one more big man up front should be on the Browns' radar.
Here are two rushers the front office should target who can help boost the Browns' defensive unit:
A fifth-overall selection in the 2022 NFL Draft, Kayvon Thibodeaux's development path hasn't quite panned out the way the New York Giants had hoped it would.
While he isn't a bad player, not by any means, he hasn't replicated the success he found back in 2023, when he recorded a career-high 11.5 sacks. Since then, though, he has totaled just eight across the last three seasons.
And just last offseason, the team added a young, high-upside piece to the defensive line by taking edge rusher Abdul Carter with the No. 3 overall selection.
With the Giants continuing to struggle to find wins, all while the defense continues to get younger, moving Thibodeaux could be a good way for the team to land some extra draft capital and maybe a mid-level contributor.
When the Browns traded Za'Darius Smith back in 2024, they landed a fifth- and sixth-round pick. When the Steelers recently traded defensive back Joey Porter Jr., they received a sixth- and second-round pick.
That makes the market easier to understand for the Browns.
If they send New York a 2027 third-round pick and a 2027 fourth-round pick, which they have three of as of now , they could get the deal done. Not only does this give the Giants more opportunities to continue the youth movement this offseason, but it also lands them something for a player who will likely seek a new contract with a different team at the end of the season.
The only issue Cleveland will run into when discussing a move for Thibodeaux is the Giants' lack of starting potential at the position with Brian Burns out for the season.
So, to make this happen, the Browns will have to bring something convincing to the table, or toss in one of Sam Williams or Derek Barnett .
Back in the 2018 NFL Draft, Payne went 13th overall.
And since then, he has been quietly one of the league's best defensive tackles.
Across the last nine seasons, he has totaled 440 tackles, 37 sacks, 65 tackles for a loss, 84 quarterback hits and seven forced fumbles. Routinely forcing his way into the backfield, Payne is still a highly sought-after 29-year-old.
With the Washington Commanders at the bottom of the NFC East, holding a 1-3 record, changes are going to be made as the team prepares to retool at the deadline and into the offseason. Payne, who is an unrestricted free agent in 2027, is likely on the chopping block and looking for a long-term extension with a new squad.
Pairing Payne with second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham could be a perfect opportunity for the Browns, especially if they can give him an extension this offseason with Deshaun Watson's contract relatively off the books.
Payne could also slide into the No. 1 spot if Graham's injury is more long-term than the team initially thought. Fortunately, that isn't something you'd have to worry about with Payne, as he has only missed three games across the last nine years.
So, what about landing him ? What would that cost?
Again, the market is somewhat all over the place, but with what the Steelers got in return for Porter Jr., a player like Payne would warrant something similar.
If the Browns threw a 2027 fourth-rounder and a 2028 second-rounder the way of the Commanders, there should be no reason for them to pass on the offer.
The Browns should be buyers as the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline approaches, and if Payne ends up on an offer sheet, they should be willing to spend a bit to land him.

title: Browns Need To Get Their Ground Game Going and Here’s How They Can Do It
full_text:
Over the course of the regular seasons’ first four games, a lot of things have been going right for the Cleveland Browns .
The ground game is not one of them.
So far, the Browns are 23rd in the league in rushing yards (93.8) and rushing yards per carry (3.7), but even those numbers feel a little misleading, as they’re aided by Deshaun Watson’s rushing totals.
If we focus only on running backs, the Browns are averaging just 59.8 rushing yards per game and 3.5 yards per carry.
Second-year back Quinshon Judkins has been struggling the most, as he’s gained just 177 yards on 59 carries for a 3.0-yard-per-carry average.
Luckily, he managed to score his first rushing touchdown of the season last Thursday night, right after Jaleel McLaughlin scored on a 28-yard scamper for Cleveland’s very first rushing touchdown of the season.
So, what can the Browns do to improve their ground game mess? Here are some options:
This looks to be the course of action for the moment in Cleveland. Judkins was a highly touted prospect coming out of Ohio State, who the Browns picked up in the second round last year.
Judkins had a few promising games last year, including his first -- and only -- 100-rushing yard effort against the Vikings, as well as a three touchdown performance against the Dolphins and a two-score outing against the Raiders.
Nonetheless, when looking at the big picture, Judkins’ issues were evident since last season. He finished his rookie year averaging 59.1 yards per game and 3.6 yards per carry, so his current struggles -- 44.3 rushing yards per game -- shouldn’t be all that shocking.
If Judkins is on the verge of breaking out, he better do it soon, because Cleveland won’t be able to mask some of the other deficiencies on offense much longer without a run game.
Fellow second-year back Dylan Sampson was supposed to be featured prominently for the Browns , but a knee injury in Week 1 landed him on the IR and he won’t be eligible to come back before Week 6.
That has opened the door for Raheem Sanders and McLaughlin to get some work, but the yield has been all that great, either. Sanders has carried the ball just six times for 31 yards, while McLaughlin has rushed the ball just twice for 31 yards, too, including last week’s score.
The sample size is minimum, but at least Sanders and McLaughlin are doing a little bit more on limited opportunities in the run game. Judkins should remain the featured back, but look for Sanders and McLaughlin to get a little more involved going forward.
Usually, a common hesitation when rotating backs has to do with reluctance to trust a back in the game when his pass protection isn’t all that solid.
That’s why signing a veteran street free agent or trading for another team’s back could lead to a better redistribution of carries, even if that player hasn’t been with the team at all.
Options aren’t precisely plentiful, though. Fan favorite Nick Chubb could’ve made sense, but he made his retirement official a few weeks back . Joe Mixon recently worked out for Seattle but won’t be signed for now. Former Brown Kareem Hunt is also a free agent waiting for a call. Other names that stand out include Antonio Gibson, Dameon Pierce and Miles Sanders, but neither really looks like a plug-n’-play solution.
As for the trade market, the Giants could have a couple of interesting targets in Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary, while the Bears could also look to move Roschon Johnson after Kyle Monangai’s recent breakout game. Tennessee’s Tony Pollard has also been mentioned as a potential trade target, as well.
Maybe Cleveland will look outside the organization for some help in the backfield, but don’t count on it happening too soon. The Browns’ probably want to see Sampson in action before they pull the trigger on any roster additions.
Meanwhile, Judkins, Sanders and McLaughlin will have to do better, because relying on Watson to keep the chains moving on the ground doesn’t seem like a great idea.

title: Jets Have Plenty of Talent, But Browns Can Exploit These Key Weaknesses
full_text:
While it may be easy to look at the Cleveland Browns' week five matchup and call it an "easy win", the New York Jets are a lot tougher than most people think.
Compared to last season, New York has really tied some strings together, including defensively where they finally got an interception .
Despite the increase in production, here are some issues the Browns can attack this week in hopes of winning their fourth straight game.
So far this season, Quinshon Judkins has been quiet through the first four games.
After week four, Judkins is only averaging three yards per carry. Through 59 attempts, he has only 177 yards and one touchdown.
Luckily for the Browns, this game may be perfect to get the second-year man out of Ohio State going.
Quinshon Judkins — 2026 Season (Rush + Rec) 177 Rush Yds | 1 Rush TD 96 Rec Yds | 0 Rec TD Total: 273 Total Yds, 1 Total TDs Pace: 1,160 Total Yds | 4 Total TDs #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/qhFyfVD65h
The Jets' defense has been pretty tough this year. While they rank sixth in passing defense, the rushing defense has been quite the opposite, ranking 25th.
For numbers, the Jets, on average, allow only 193.3 passing yards per game. On the other hand, they allow 123.5 rushing yards each week.
The Browns must use this week as a jump-start game for Judkins. After this week, the Browns will face a Baltimore Ravens rushing defense that ranks in the top 10.
Through four games, the Browns have a total of 12 sacks. This is tied for fifth-best in the league with the Las Vegas Raiders.
For the Jets, they are tied for the third most sacks allowed in the league with 12.
While Cleveland will be without their sack leader, Mason Graham , the unit still managed to bring down Aaron Rodgers five times without the former fifth overall pick.
If the Browns can send pressure early and dominate on defense, they should have an easier path to that 4-1 start.
While we very well could end up seeing another scoreless first quarter, the Browns have to try and strike first.
MetLife Stadium is a tough environment to play in. Similar to Browns fans, Jets fans are always loud and loyal to their team, no matter how good or bad the play is.
This is why it will be crucial to run the ball, control the clock, score first, and then get a quick three-and-out on defense.
If the Browns can do these few things, they will set themselves up nicely for a chance at another win in 2026.

title: Browns Make Major Move With Dillon Gabriel Ahead of Week 5
full_text:
Browns second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel has been taken off injured reserve and will return to practice.
Gabriel, who spent a portion of last season as the Browns' starting quarterback, will now fight his way through the depth chart in hopes of earning the backup quarterback role.
Gabriel won the starting job last season, beating out Shedeur Sanders.
In 10 games, Gabriel threw for 937 yards, 10 touchdowns, and two interceptions. Gabriel is now the fourth quarterback on the Browns' 53-man roster, joining Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders , and Taylen Green.
The concept of keeping four quarterbacks isn't a new one for the Browns. Along with Sanders and Gabriel, the Browns signed Joe Flacco and Kenny Pickett to the initial 53-man roster last season. Pickett was then traded in August before the season opener.
Sitting at 3-1, the Browns will now have another body to rely on in case of injury or poor play.
#Browns roster moves: Eligible to return to practice: DT Kalia Davis (designated for return) QB Dillon Gabriel (previously designated for return on Aug. 30) Signed to practice squad: WR James Proche II DT Chris Williams Released from practice squad: RB Eric Gray P Wes Pahl…
In addition to activating Dillon Gabriel, the Browns made a series of roster moves on Tuesday.
Former San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Kalia Davis has been activated off the injury reserve. The fourth-year man out of UCF signed with Cleveland in March on a one-year deal after three seasons in San Francisco.
The addition of Kalia Davis will provide the Browns with much-needed depth after losing Mason Graham to injury. Davis has 41 tackles in 33 games in the NFL.
The Browns have signed veteran wide receiver James Proche to the practice squad after completing a workout on Tuesday.
James Proche is someone that many Browns fans should be familiar with. The special teams star played two seasons in Cleveland before signing with the Tennessee Titans, where he spent last season.
The move comes as a response to the injury to Tylan Wallace , who went down in the matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night.
The Browns also signed defensive tackle Chris Williams to the practice squad.
Chris Williams is now in his fifth season in the NFL. The Wagner College product originally signed with the Indianapolis Colts as an undrafted free agent in 2020. The addition of Williams adds another layer of protection with the injuries on the defensive line mounting up.
Williams has 43 tackles in 44 career games in the NFL.
In corresponding moves, the Browns released running back Eric Gray, punter Wes Pahl, and offensive tackle Xavier Truss from the practice squad.

title: The Unspoken Reason the Browns Are Sitting at 3-1 Right Now
full_text:
Over the 2026 offseason, the Cleveland Browns made a couple of big moves.
From firing their head coach, to trading away one of if not the best players in franchise history, to arguably winning the 2026 NFL Draft, the Browns were busy during the time off.
Now that we are into the season, one man has been flying under the radar in regard to the credit given for the team's hot start.
On January 28th, 2026, Todd Monken was named the Browns' new head coach.
In his first NFL head-coaching gig, he has led the Browns on and off the field to a 3-1 start while overcoming some incredible feats.
Here are some ways coach Monken has changed the Browns.
The Browns are the only team in NFL history to have: fewer TDs fewer made FGs fewer rushing yards fewer net passing yards more turnovers more penalties ...than their opponents through 4 games of a season and yet still have a winning record.
No matter of what has happened in the first four games, Monken has kept his guys energized and active in the game.
In years past, former head coach Kevin Stefanski had many times when it was clear to see the team giving up on him.
So far this season, the Browns faced tough defensive drives from the Panthers, where Carolina took the lead late in the game. The Browns didn't quit though, and came back to win.
In the most recent game against the Steelers, Cleveland scored 21 of their 27 points in the second quarter. In the second half, an old Browns team would've quit by the end of the third quarter after scoring zero points and constantly getting stopped.
Before coming back to Cleveland, Monken spent a few years in Baltimore as the Ravens' offensive coordinator.
After leaving the Browns' AFC North rival, some players like Tylan Wallace decided to also leave the team and follow "Coach Monk" to Cleveland.
Over the months since coach Monken took over the job, many players have commented on how different the vibe in the locker room is with Monken compared to Stefanski last season.
While the Browns did put a lot of work into the offense this offseason, there is ultimately one fact that stands out.
The Browns only scored 20 or more points in six games last season.
So far in 2026, the Browns have not only scored over 20 in three out of four games, but the team average for points per game currently sits at 20.3
Diving deeper, there is one final factor that has been the biggest win of Monken's tenure so far.
2026 is the final contract year for Deshaun Watson as a Cleveland Brown.
Coming into the season, many fans and analysts argued Watson would not last more than two games, and could potentially even be traded from the team.
Despite a bad showing in week one, Watson not only looks his best he has ever looked since the trade back in 2022, but he has led the Browns on three straight game-winning drives.
With Monken leading the charge, Watson and the Browns can continue to win games.

title: 5 winners, 3 losers from Browns First Four Games of 2026
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have hit the quarter pole in the 2026 season and after the first four games, they find themselves in first place.
The Browns have gotten contributions from all sides of the ball and have won by playing complementary football. The surprise start to the season has given the Browns plenty of wins; however, the team is not without disappointments as well.
Watson entered the season with his career on the line. If things did not go well to start, he would have gotten buried in the depth chart, leaving his NFL career to die. He looked horrible out of the gate in Jacksonville, but then turned his play around. It has not always looked like what the Browns expected when they traded for him, but he has made astounding plays in the fourth quarters of games and has led the team to three straight game-winning drives.
The Browns running attack has been stagnant. There have been little holes to run through, and when there are, Judkins has been slow to get to them. He is coming off a season-ending injury to his leg, so he might need more reps to get his timing back, but Judkins has not looked like the promising rookie he was last season. The offense will need to add the running dimension to their offense to continue any success.
Coming into the season much was said about the lack of depth on the defensive line. In the preseason games, they were bullied and teams were getting big chunk plays. Through the quarter mark of the season, the defensive line, led by Mason Graham, has been in the backfield and rushing opposing quarterbacks. Graham went down, but the production did not.
The defensive line continued to harass the quarterback and the Browns, slowing down offenses. They are proving that they have plenty of depth by having the “next man up” mentality.
Jeudy came into the season looking to lead the position group while the young players adjusted to the league. He quickly got passed up as a top option by the young receivers and Harold Fannin Jr. becoming go-to targets. Jeudy made a couple of nice plays on the last drive in their last game, which may springboarded him going in the next quarter of the season.
Much was ado about Boston in training camp with his big frame and sticky hands. Boston has used his size to make big plays for the offense and has become Watson’s number one option. He has not looked like a rookie and his play-making abilities are looking like they will help the Browns for years to come.
Every single kick has gone through the uprights and Szmyt has become a reliable kicker. When the offense has stalled Szmyt  put points on the board with his leg. Time and time again, he easily hit the kicks, heavily contributing to the 3-1 start. They will need his leg going forward to win games as they will play a lot of one-score games.
The Browns have had more laundry on the field than a college student coming home for winter break. The presnap penalties have ruined drives before they even had a chance to start. There have been false starts, illegal formations, holding, and everything in between.
The Browns had the Pittsburgh Steelers backed up on the one-yard line, when they promptly jumped offsides, giving the Steelers breathing room. They are winning in spite of the penalties, but those mistakes will eventually come to bite them against tougher teams.
After two seasons of losing and a tumultuous offseason, the fans' frustration was boiling over. After the first game, it looked like it would be another long season and a lot of scouting for college quarterbacks. But then the Browns quickly turned it around the fans were energetic, positive, and feeding the team in their primetime win. The patience paid off in the first quarter of the season and the fans have something to cheer for in the next quarter.
They have gotten contributions across the board and the Browns will need production from a lot of different positions to continue their success.

title: 4 Reasons Why the Browns Should Avoid Trading Shedeur Sanders
full_text:
Ever since Deshaun Watson began impressing many people as the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback, some have begun calling for Cleveland to dish out their young quarterback.
If you ask me, it would not be a smart decision to deal Shedeur Sanders at this moment.
Here are four reasons why:
The Browns drafted Sanders with the 144th overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
In his first offseason with the team, Sanders was not given a fair chance to even get reps with the starters under former head coach Kevin Stefanski.
Taking that into consideration, Sanders finished the 2025 season as the Browns' starting quarterback, in which he threw for over 1400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. He was also named a Pro Bowl selection.
As of now Sanders has a lot of talent, but it is raw. Some say sitting behind Deshaun Watson is ruining his career, but I believe he is getting valuable experience watching Watson succeed while still getting reps in practice.
After this season, Watson's contract will expire, and he will become a free agent. Whether Cleveland decides to re-sign him or not, he is currently 31 years old and not getting any younger.
Let's say the Browns end up dealing Sanders. What will they do after Watson is done? Would it not be nice to immediately insert a guy who has been in the Todd Monken system, sitting and learning from the sideline this whole time?
Also, It has been shown through film that he has the potential to end up as the next Sam Darnold or Mac Jones. Each of those guys was written off by their former teams when all they needed was a change of scenery and a new offensive system.
If the Browns get rid of Sanders, especially knowing Cleveland's luck, it almost feels guaranteed that it will come back to bite them in the future.
Source: #Browns are not looking to trade QB Shedeur Sanders. They really like how Sanders has developed under Todd Monken this year and want to keep developing him. “There is absolutely nothing cooking there” I was told. pic.twitter.com/qQ1dCErjXq
The last time the Browns made it through an entire season with the same starting quarterback each week was back when Baker Mayfield led the Browns to a playoff win in the 2020 season.
Since then, a combination of bad QB play, injuries, and contracts has pretty much led the Browns to go into each season knowing they will need more than one guy.
Once again, it makes much more sense to plug in a guy who knows the system, has sat and watched, and really is a leader on the team over a veteran free agent in the case Watson can't play.
Week three of the 2018 season featured one of the most memorable Browns moments in recent history.
With the first pick in the 2018 NFL Draft, the Browns selected Baker Mayfield. In that week three matchup on Thursday Night Football at home against the Jets, Mayfield made his debut.
From that moment on, the feeling he brought to Browns fans was one they hadn't felt in a very long time. Hope.
Since he was traded in 2022, Cleveland hasn't had a guy who had that same swagger, gave the fans the same feeling, and overall brought everyone together. No disrespect to Joe Flacco, but he came in as a veteran and wasn't with the team for very long.
Any moment Shedeur Sanders steps on the field, the feeling of excitement roams through the air regardless of whether the Browns are in Cleveland or not.
If the Browns trade him away, it will be the second time within 10 years that a beloved quarterback gets dealt.

title: Denzel Boston's Case for 2026 Offensive Rookie of the Year is Rock Solid and Here's Why
full_text:
As we make our way past the first quarter of the NFL regular season, a number of rookies have wasted no time in making big time plays on both sides of the ball.
Among them stands Cleveland Browns’ wide receiver Denzel Boston, a second round pick out of Washington who’s quickly become the team’s top receiving threat.
Here are six reasons why Boston could become Cleveland's first ever Offensive Rookie of the Year:
First off, Boston has been really good . The former Husky started showing off his impressive skills during the offseason, and that translated well into the summer during training camp and preseason. Once the regular season kicked off, Boston confirmed what everybody in Berea already knew -- he’s incredibly hard to guard.
So far, Boston has caught 13 balls for 284 yards with two scores, averaging 71.0 yards per game and hasn’t fumbled the football once. All this while not just playing alongside one of the league’s most uncertain quarterback situations, but also helping Deshaun Watson find his groove as the team’s starter and becoming a steadying influence for the team’s offense.
After four games as his quarterback, Watson understands that when he throws the ball in Boston’s direction -- something he’s done 22 times already -- good things happen for Cleveland .
Boston is currently ranking third in targets within the Browns’ offense, one behind tight end Harold Fannin Jr. and six behind team leader and fellow rookie wideout KC Concepcion. Yet, Boston leads the team handily in receiving yards with 284, compared to Fannin’s 153 and Concepcion’s 144. In other words, nobody is stretching the field for Cleveland better than Boston.
Among all rookie wideouts, Boston is already a big deal , too. He’s ranked first or tied for first in receiving yards, receiving touchdowns, and yards per reception (minimum two receptions), while ranking third in targets and catches.
And among all wideouts in the NFL, rookies and veterans, Boston is second in yards per reception (21.8) and 10th in receiving yards.
Should he keep up his current pace, Boston would end the season with 1,207 receiving yards and nine touchdowns. In terms of yards, that’s mostly in line with what the team’s last two Pro Bowl wideouts produced -- Jerry Jeudy had 1,229 yards in 2024 while Amari Cooper had 1,250 in 2023. However, Boston’s nine projected scores would equal the nine touchdowns combined from Jeudy (four) and Cooper (five) over those two years combined.
It’s no secret that we’ve been living in a passing league for quite some time. Yet, wide receivers have had to wait to get their dues when it comes to this award. Only 12 wideouts have been named Offensive Rookie of the Year since the award was inaugurated in 1967, with half of them being recognized since 2003 including three in the last five years. For the second time ever in the awards history, Boston would make it back-to-back for the position, after Tetairoa McMillan took it home last year.
Boston currently has the second shortest betting line to take home the OROY award with +400 to +750 odds, so it's clear he's getting noticed.
So far, 35 running backs have taken this award through its first 49 years, so it’s always a good bet, Yet, the draft’s top rookies have been or are currently injured, and no rookie has rushed for more than one score yet in the season, so it's fair to say there hasn’t been a real attention grabber so far in the run game.
Plus, the last running back to win OROY honors was eight years ago -- Saquon Barkley in 2018. From an award standpoint, their time might have passed.
Ten quarterbacks were drafted in the 2026 NFL Draft, including Fernando Mendoza No. 1 by the Raiders, None of them have started a game.
As a matter of fact, the Bucs’ undrafted Jalon Daniels is the only rookie quarterback to start a game so far in the season. QBs have won half of these awards over the past decade, including two out of the last three, but there are no obvious candidates at this position so far in 2026.
Along with Offensive Player of the Year, this is the only major individual honor that the Browns as a team have never won, notwithstanding the legendary Jim Brown taking AP’s inaugural Rookie of the Year award in 1957, before it got split into an offensive side and a defensive side.
Boston is Cleveland’s best bet since, at least, Baker Mayfield’s 2018 rookie campaign. It’s still early in the year, but Boston is doing his part while the rest of the league might be lining up to help him achieve it.

title: Would a Khalil Mack Trade Make Sense for the Browns?
full_text:
Khalil Mack, a former NFL Defensive Player of the Year, may soon be on the move.
The Cleveland Browns, sitting at 3-1 and tied atop the AFC North, could be a logical landing spot.
The Los Angeles Chargers, where Mack currently plays, have started the season with an unexpected 0-4 record after losing to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4. On Sunday, Oct. 4, ESPN’s Adam Schefter identified Mack as a player who could draw trade interest if the Chargers’ struggles continue:
After two trades last week, here are more names to monitor ahead of next month’s #NFL trade deadline. pic.twitter.com/i9XdEC0oPQ
Khalil Mack, 35, was on that list because of the Chargers' abysmal start to the season. While Mack is not the player he was when he won the NFL Defensive Player of the Year award in 2016, Mack still offers strong production with 3 sacks and 14 total tackles already this season.
Mack could be an attractive addition for teams with winning records looking to bolster their defensive front.
Cleveland’s 3-1 start could encourage the Browns to invest in their defensive line for a potential playoff push. Mack would strengthen an already productive Browns pass rush, which has recorded 11 sacks through four games, tied for eighth in the NFL. The Browns also lost their starting defensive end , Alex Wright, to a ruptured Achilles during training camp.
ESPN sources: The Browns are placing starting DE Alex Wright on season-ending injured reserve with a ruptured Achilles, and they now will sign former first-round pick DE Derek Barnett. Wright was carted off the practice field Thursday after getting hurt during a one-on-one drill… pic.twitter.com/RDBRDFeAj9
The Los Angeles Chargers could view a trade as a chance to acquire draft capital for a veteran playing on an expiring contract. The Browns have plenty of draft capital, currently holding 11 selections in the 2027 NFL Draft. Three of those selections are in the fourth round, and two are in the fifth.
Mack’s experience on multiple defensive fronts could also make him a fit for Cleveland’s scheme. Mack would return to a true defensive end role opposite Jared Verse for the Browns, similar to his time with the Raiders.
Browns defensive line coach Jacques Cesaire has emphasized attacking, penetrating, and disrupting offenses, which plays to Mack’s strengths.
Based on Mack’s $8 million base salary , a trade immediately after Week 4 would leave Cleveland responsible for approximately $6.2 million, assuming no salary adjustment. The Chargers would retain the cap charges for his $10 million signing bonus and roughly $1.8 million in base salary already earned.
Cleveland could accommodate that remaining salary within its approximately $14.2 million in available cap space.
While the Chargers' true asking price for Mack is unknown, Mack’s age and expiring contract could limit the return, although his production could create competition among interested teams. Given his track record , Browns general manager Andrew Berry is unlikely to overpay for a short-term rental.
A package of 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks is one possible framework, though whether that would satisfy Los Angeles remains uncertain. With Mack’s contract expiring after the season, Cleveland would be paying for a short-term boost to its pass rush.

title: Jake Ferguson's Silly Fine Rescinded After Cowboys TE Brings Receipts to Appeal
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson won't be coughing up five figures worth of fine money to the NFL after all.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the $13,611 fine the NFL handed out to Ferguson last week over a touchdown celebration has been rescinded by the appeals officers that are appointed jointly by the NFL and NFLPA.
The NFL believed Ferguson's celebration during the Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders was him "shotgunning a beer" and called it "an offensive demonstration that could be construed as being in poor taste."
Even if Ferguson had been imitating shotgunning a beer, fining him for it was extremely hypocritical because Bud Light is the NFL's biggest sponsor.
In order to get the fine rescinded, Ferguson appealed and told the officers that "it was his Gatorade celebration that he previously had done on multiple occasions in practice, as the team had documented on social media," Schefter revealed.
Ferguson wasn't the only player around the NFL to get fined for what the league believed was a beer-shotgunning celebration.
San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and Indianapolis Colts guard Matt Goncalves were also fined for the same reason.
Juszczyk's fine has since been rescinded "because his celebration was simulating drinking a juice box, not a beer," which makes sense because his nickname is literally "Juice."
Juszczyk also apparently called the league out for being hypocritical considering its partnership with Bud Light.
"Mr. Juszczyk finally stated that the fine is hypocritical with the amount of Bud Light sponsorships surrounding the NFL," the appeals officers said.
Goncalves hilariously said he was actually imitating drinking "an ice cold Coca-Cola," so maybe he'll get his taken back, too. As of this writing, his has not been rescinded.
Ferguson has 12 catches for 83 yards and three touchdowns over four games this season. Not exactly gaudy yardage production, but it's not surprising with the tight end having to compete for targets with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
We thought Ferguson would regress with touchdowns after scoring eight in 2025, but he's on pace to pass that.
Where Ferguson has struggled is with blocking, which was especially noticeable last week against the Houston Texans.
Ferguson either needs to improve on that front or the Cowboys have to stop putting him in situations where he needs to block, which will limit his snaps.

title: Jerry Jones Isn't as Concerned About DaRon Bland as Cowboys Need To Be
full_text:
The Joey Porter Jr. trade was huge for the Dallas Cowboys, but that does not mean they have solved their problems at cornerback.
On the other side, the Cowboys have a struggling DaRon Bland , which is, of course, nothing new because Bland has not been adequate for two-plus seasons now.
When asked about Bland on Wednesday on 105.3 The Fan, Jerry Jones said that while he understands why fans are concerned about Bland, the Cowboys owner admitted he isn't as concerned as they are.
“I understand how our fans could be concerned. But I’m not as concerned as you might think," Jones said of Bland.
Jones also said that Bland "has a chance to get better" with the addition of Joey Porter Jr., which is certainly true because teams are going to be inclined to pick on Bland more instead of going after Dallas' No. 1 cornerback.
That did not yield good results in Week 4 . Bland gave up 104 yards and a touchdown on seven targets thrown his way, with the Texans completing five of those passes and Bland finishing with a 71.4% completion rate and a 153.3 passer rating allowed, according to Pro Football Focus , which is just .5 shy of a perfect mark.
We hoped getting over injury issues would help Bland play better, but that has not been the case through four games.
Bland is giving up a completion rate of 65% and a passer rating of 129.2 when targeted overall, and he has allowed 160 yards and three touchdowns.
It's pretty clear the Cowboys aren't ready to give up on Bland yet, but they can't allow this to go on for much longer.
The best solution is to deploy Cobie Durant there when he returns from injury. Durant was the Cowboys' best cornerback through a game-plus, and he was that throughout the offseason, also.
That won't be an immediate solution, though, as Durant is still hurt and isn't likely to play this week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
It's also worth noting that Dallas might need Durant to play in the slot with Caleb Downs having to play more snaps at safety because of injuries to Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke.
Thompson and Locke are both on injured reserve . Locke has to miss at least two more games, with the Week 5 game included in that count, and Thompson will be out at least three more.
In the meantime, the Cowboys should be giving Ameer Speed and Shavon Revel more snaps instead of having Bland play all of them. If nothing else, at least make him earn it.
Whatever the Cowboys decide to do, they can't keep doing the same thing with Bland on the boundary if his play does not improve. This defense simply can't afford it.

title: DeMeco Ryans Exposes Dallas Cowboys' Failure To Address Fatal Flaw
full_text:
In each of the past two weeks, the Dallas Cowboys have had a field goal blocked. First, it was the Baltimore Ravens , who blocked a 59-yard attempt by Brandon Aubrey while playing in Rio.
In Week 4, it was the Houston Texans who blocked one of Aubrey’s attempts, this one from 65 yards, and Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans said they identified where to attack the Cowboys by watching the film.
While appearing on the team’s YouTube show, Ryans said they noticed a consistent breakdown, which let them know where they had an advantage.
“During the film study you definitely saw a breakdown in the protection. You’ve seen it consistently. That’s how you study film,” Ryans said during the show . “You look for those weaknesses, how you can exploit a team. We saw a weakness there in the C and D gap area.”
Of course finding the weakness is just part of the equation. As Ryans stated, the next step is seeing whether or not the opponent addressed the flaw. For the Cowboys, that wasn’t the case.
“We were able to show that kick from the Baltimore game, how they were able to block it, and we’re gonna design a plan similar to that to see if they fixed it. That’s what all teams do. If you see a breakdown, see if they fixed it the next week.”
As we all saw on Sunday, the Cowboys either didn’t notice the flaw while doing their film study, or simply failed to fix it. Not only did that lead to one blocked field goal, but Houston came within inches of blocking the final extra point, which would have made it a three-point game and might have led to overtime.
Whether it was a lack of identifying the problem or a shortcoming in addressing it, this is a terrible look for special teams coach Nick Sorensen, who has to feel his seat heating up.
In addition to the blocked kicks, Sorensen’s unit has been plagued with mistakes. Aubrey kicked the ball out of bounds twice during the loss to Baltimore, giving the Ravens a favorable starting position from the 40-yard line.
There was also the fateful kickoff with seven seconds remaining. Dallas could have kicked the ball short, and forced time off the clock, but elected not to. Instead, Aubrey booted it out of the back of the end zone and no time was taken off the clock. That allowed the Ravens enough time to get one play in, and call a timeout with one second remaining to steal the win.
Entering Week 5, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the Cowboys will be focused on their protection on special teams, but it’s clear that the special teams struggles go well beyond that flaw. To save his job, Sorensen needs to be much better at identifying and shoring up those issues.

title: Dallas Cowboys Deemed Potential Suitor For Reunion Trade With Edge Rusher
full_text:
If there's one thing that's very clear with the Dallas Cowboys so far in 2026, it's that their defense is not good.
One area specifically that has lacked is the pass-rush , where Dallas is getting some pressure but not enough sacks.
How bad is the pass-rush, you ask? Well, the Cowboys have four sacks and two of them came last week. Most teams wouldn't be all that satisfied with two sacks, but for the Cowboys, that showing amounted to a monumental breakthrough.
With four sacks in four games — only 1.5 of those have come from edge rushers, by the way — the Cowboys are tied for the second-fewest in the NFL, so it goes without saying more help is needed.
In an article naming possible trade candidates ahead of the deadline, the Cowboys were dubbed a potential suitor for Jadeveon Clowney by Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox .
"The Texans could still get back in the playoff mix, but they could be prompted to send Clowney to a contender for a strong return — which they should be able to get," Knox said.
The Houston Texans are off to an 0-4 start, which puts their playoff hopes in a precarious spot, to say the least.
Only one team in NFL history has ever overcome an 0-4 start (the 1992 San Diego Chargers), so Houston is seriously up against it. Should their fortunes not turn around, the Texans could decide unloading Clowney, who is on a one-year deal, is the play.
On paper, trading for Clowney absolutely makes sense considering the Cowboys have a dire need at EDGE.
Clowney has 1.5 sacks in two games this season and he was productive for Dallas last season with 8.5 over 13 contests.
Granted, three of those came in a meaningless Week 18 game, but 5.5 in 12 contests is still very good and the Cowboys would gladly take that kind of production.
The problem with this idea is the Cowboys might not deem the former No. 1 overall pick as a fit in Christian Parker's defense .
After Stephen Jones said the Cowboys "absolutely" wanted Clowney back last December, nothing materialized in the offseason and he ultimately wasn't re-signed.
In February, Jones noted that the Cowboys were looking for guys who fit Parker's system, so we're led to believe Dallas didn't think Clowney fit the bill or else they would have re-signed him.
"We're going to work through Christian [Parker]," Jones said back in February when asked about re-signing Clowney. "A lot of it will happen this coming week in terms of the type of player [we want]. We're going to continue to have those talks, then we'll make final decisions on who we think will be productive in this particular system."
Clowney, who expressed how much he enjoyed being in Dallas, later pushed back on the idea that he isn't a fit in any particular system.
"Ain't no scheme I can't play in, 3-4 to 4-3, to whatever down scheme that you had. I think I've proved that I can play in them all, and not just play in them, but also dominate in them schemes and do my job at a high level," Clowney said.
Scheme fit will no doubt be a factor in who the Cowboys try to bring in, but if all else fails and Clowney is the best option Dallas has to improve the edge rushers room, they should trade for him and figure out a way to make it work.

title: 3 Dallas Cowboys With Most to Prove Entering Week 5
full_text:
A win in Week 4 against the Houston Texans moved the Dallas Cowboys to 2-2 on the season. It also set them up for a huge swing, since they have the opportunity to pick up a second win on Thursday Night Football.
Dallas will enter as favorites against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who won't have Baker Mayfield under center. With Mayfield injured , the Bucs will turn to undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels, who is making just his second career start.
This could be a "get-right" game for the Cowboys, provided they don't overlook their opponent. It could also be a chance for the following three players to improve their stock as they enter Week 5 with something to prove.
Joey Porter Jr.'s performance on Sunday was a huge boost to the secondary, but also a reminder of how bad DaRon Bland has struggled over the past two seasons. Bland continues to surrender receptions at an alarming rate, finishing with a 48.2 PFF grade this weekend .
Bland signed a massive extension ahead of the 2025 season, with the Cowboys expecting him to return to the form they saw in 2023 when he had nine interceptions. That hasn't happened and there's a chance he could be running out of opportunities in Dallas. That's a lot of pressure to be feeling as he enters the Week 5 matchup with the Bucs.
Don't get me wrong, Caleb Downs has been great for the most part as a rookie. He has 27 tackles, one sack, and one pass breakup in the first four games of the year. That said, he's coming off a rough outing, which resulted in him landing in the Cowboys' bottom five for PFF grades in Week 4 .
He allowed five receptions on five targets for 54 yards against the Texans, which was a letdown. It's also not his norm. That said, Downs will surely enter this game with the desire to prove the Houston game was a fluke.
Jake Ferguson made one huge play for the Cowboys, hauling in a seven-yard pass on fourth-and-four during the final drive. Had Ferguson not come up with that play, there's a good chance Dallas loses the game. He deserves praise for that play, but overall, Ferguson didn't have a great outing.
He had a total of three receptions for 11 yards and was a liability in run blocking . He's been taking a lot of heat for his performance this season, not only for the blocking but for his career-low average of 6.9 yards per reception. Throw in his costly fumble in Week 3 and it's hard to think of any player with more to prove in Week 5 than Ferguson.

title: Cowboys vs. Buccaneers: 3 Keys to Victory in Week 5
full_text:
For the second time in a row, the Dallas Cowboys will square off with a winless franchise. They defeated the Houston Texans in Week 4 , dropping them to 0-4. Now, they have a quick turnaround as they take on the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football.
The Cowboys boast one of the most explosive offenses in the NFL, entering the week second in the league with 122 points scored. Their defense is still questionable , with 112 points surrendered through four games.
Dallas has the stage set for success, with the Bucs going into this game without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield as well as star safety Antoine Winfield Jr. That doesn't mean this is going to be an easy win, but the Cowboys can secure a victory if they focus on these three keys to victory.
Through four games, the Bucs have been one of the best teams against the run, surrendering just 3.2 yards per attempt. Vita Vea is a major reason for that as the 347-pounder is capable of clogging up lanes. He's also known for making plays in the backfield. In 116 career games, Vea has 48 tackles for loss and 35 sacks. He can ruin an offensive game plan and the Cowboys need to keep him out of their backfield to prevent that from happening.
The good news for Dallas is that they're hopeful to have Tyler Smith back in action . He missed four games following thumb surgery, but could be back on Thursday. If so, he will join Cooper Beebe and Tyler Booker to form one of the more dominant interior lines, which is exactly what they need against the Bucs.
Undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels made his debut against the Green Bay Packers in Week 4 and it was a rough outing for the Kansas product. Daniels had 148 yards passing with one touchdown and two picks, while being sacked three times.
His performance might give Dallas plenty of confidence, but they can't go out there and expect Daniels to make it easy. He may be a rookie, but he's in the NFL for a reason. The last thing the Cowboys need is to allow him to get comfortable. That means Donovan Ezeiruaku and Rashan Gary need to be at their best and get some pressure on the young signal-caller, which should force him into some mistakes.
There isn't a receiver in the league playing better than CeeDee Lamb right now . He's coming off a dominant performance, which saw him rack up 189 yards and a touchdown on 17 receptions. In four games, he has 37 catches for 498 yards and four touchdowns.
Oftentimes, teams overthink things and try to get everyone involved when it's clear that one player is in the zone. That's the case with Lamb right now and while George Pickens and Jake Ferguson will end up with targets, the offense needs to continue to be focused on Lamb. Dak Prescott has to keep feeding the hot hand and force the ball into Lamb's hands until someone actually stops him.

title: Joey Porter Jr. Ready to Take Next Step Dallas Cowboys' Defense Desperately Needs
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys sure could use more snaps out of cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in his second game with the team.
Porter made his 2026 and Cowboys debut on Sunday in the 34-30 win over the Houston Texans and, according to Next Gen Stats , played 24 of a possible 54 snaps for Dallas.
The former Pittsburgh Steelers second-round pick was extremely effective in those snaps and with the Cowboys' secondary banged up and struggling the way it has been all season, it goes without saying more Porter is needed.
Well, Porter was asked about possibly playing more snaps in the Week 5 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and he said he's all for it as long as the Cowboys are.
“I feel comfortable about that, but it’s all really up to the coaches and what they have for me. I just got here not too long ago, so I’m still trying to learn everything and get the grasp of how things are run here. So it’s really up to them," Porter said, per Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com .
Porter brings up another valid subject when talking about an increase in his snaps.
Not only has he not had much practice and playing time this year, which could impact his conditioning, he's also trying to learn a new defense on the fly, which only makes his acclimation tougher. And, this week adds another challenge with it being a short week.
That said, if Porter feels comfortable enough to take on more, the Cowboys are almost certainly going to give it to him because, again, they desperately need him on the field.
Porter immediately showed why defensive coordinator Christian Parker calls him a "boundary eraser."
Over his 24 snaps, Porter spent 19 of them in coverage. And, in those 19 coverage snaps, he was only targeted once and didn't allow a completion. Porter lined up against Nico Collins for five snaps and zero targets came his way on those.
The only problem was Porter's presence made the Texans more inclined to pick on DaRon Bland , who was as bad as he has been for two years running now.
That's something Dallas needs to figure, and the likely solution will be to play Cobie Durant over Bland, assuming the Cowboys don't deploy Durant in the slot with Caleb Downs needed more at the safety spot due to injuries to P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson.
On the bright side, the Cowboys had two boundary cornerback spots to worry about before Porter's arrival. Now, they only have one and that's about all this struggling defense can ask for.

title: Dallas Cowboys' Week 5 Injury Report Sheds Light On Team Health In Short Week
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys came up clutch in Week 4's 34-30 win over the Houston Texans to move to 2-2.
It was a game that Dallas needed to have after the collapse in Brazil against the Baltimore Ravens. The Cowboys simply couldn't afford to fall to 1-3.
Now headed into a Thursday Night Football matchup at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Cowboys will be looking to move above .500 and start building a winning streak, but a short week also means a lengthy injury report, especially after such an intense game with the Texans.
Fortunately, there's no new concerns for fans to be stressed about.
There were no changes to the team's Tuesday injury report when it comes to names or current designation.
Here's the full injury report:
Cobie Durant, CB - DNP (hamstring) DeMarvion Overshown, LB - DNP (hamstring) Drew Shelton, OT - DNP (hamstring) Tyler Smith, OL - Limited (thumb)** Alijah Clark, S - Full (ankle) Tyler Goodson, RB - Full (ankle) Malik Hooker, S - Full (forearm) James Houston, OLB - Full (shoulder) CeeDee Lamb, WR - Full (thigh) Joey Porter Jr., CB - Full (ankle) ** - designated to return and in the 21-day window to return to practice
A lengthy injury report with multiple notable names certainly caught the attention of Dallas fans on Monday after the team's walkthrough. It's never fun to see CeeDee Lamb listed or new Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who made his Dallas debut against the Texans after arriving from the Pittsburg Steelers last week.
But in reality, Dallas is getting healthier after some major injury issues during the first four weeks.
The health of Cowboys offensive guard Tyler Smith is one of the biggest pieces of positive injury news for Dallas headed into Week 5. He missed the first four games of the year after undergoing thumb surgery prior to the start of the season.
The Cowboys could look to bring him back against Tampa Bay or elect to sit him out for one more game before the team heads into Week 6 on extra rest. The latter might be the best option but it remains to be seen which direction Dallas will go.
The Cowboys and Buccaneers will kick off from AT&T Stadium on Thursday at 7:15 p.m. CT.

title: Everything That Went Wrong For Dallas Cowboys in Week 4 Win Over Houston Texans
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys managed to barely escape Reliant Stadium with a win over the Houston Texans on Sunday — and barely is certainly the right word.
The Cowboys had to mount a two-minute drive to re-take the lead late, and then a last-second Hail Mary from the Texans was literal inches away from being completed , which would have been especially devastating after the heartbreaking Week 3 loss.
While the Cowboys will certainly take the win, there's a lot to clean up. Here's everything that went wrong for Dallas in their Week 4 victory over Houston.
Javonte Williams scored three times , but other than that there was nothing to write home about for the Cowboys' rushing attack.
Williams averaged just 3.3 yards per carry (and we're rounding up), and he's now averaging just 3.7 yards per carry this season.
Compare that to last season, when Williams averaged 4.8 yards per carry. Through four games, the Cowboys rank 25th in yards per game after ranking ninth last season.
Hopefully things will improve when Tyler Smith gets back , which could be as soon as this week. However, expecting one man to rectify poor blocking upfront might be expecting too much.
The Cowboys' coverage was a roller coaster in Week 4.
Things started off really bad in the first quarter, settled down over the next two, and then got bad again in the fourth quarter, which allowed Houston to re-take the lead late.
DaRon Bland was especially bad while the Texans picked him on relentlessly. He faced seven targets and allowed five catches for 104 yards and a touchdown, according to Pro Football Focus . Caleb Downs, Malik Hooker and Reddy Steward struggled in coverage, also.
Ultimately, C.J. Stroud finished 347 passing yards and found pay dirt twice.
It was great to see Joey Porter Jr. do his job and shut down one side of the field for Dallas, but there's still another side that needs to be tended to. Hopefully one of Shavon Revel, Cobie Durant or Ameer Speed can solve that issue moving forward because it doesn't look like Bland has what it takes.
The Cowboys had a tough time sustaining drives against the Texans, with Dallas converting on just 5-of-14 third downs.
According to TeamRankings.com , that conversion rate (35.7%) would rank 20th in the NFL if it were the Cowboys' season-long rate. This showing was an outlier for Dallas, though, with the Cowboys ranking fourth (51.02%) in third-down rate in 2026.
The Cowboys had yet another field goal blocked in Week 4, and Brandon Aubrey missed a field goal, also, but those weren't the only special teams issues the Cowboys had.
Texans returner Jaylin Noel ripped off a 53-yard return that gave Houston great field position, and the Texans went on to capitalize with a touchdown.
We don't know how the Cowboys will fix these issues, but we do know they need to figure it out.
Dak Prescott was lucky to get out of Reliant Stadium in one piece.
The Cowboys signal-caller was hit a whopping 12 times by Texans defenders throughout the contest. Luckily, all he left with was a bandaged hand after getting stepped on .
Granted, the Texans have some ridiculously talented pass-rushers, but the Cowboys need to do a better job protecting Dak because, without him, this season would be cooked.

title: Dallas Cowboys-Josh Sweat Trade Is Too Perfect For Jerry Jones To Pass Up
full_text:
Jerry Jones made it clear that he intended to fix the Dallas Cowboys defense this year and he's been putting in the work. Not only did the Cowboys add a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker this offseason, but they went into the year with six new starters.
When the regular season began, Jones said he wasn't done making moves and he proved as much by trading for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Porter had an impressive debut for the Cowboys in Week 4, but the defense still surrendered 30 points. Their offense did enough to get the win, but it's clear their defense still needs help.
They could continue to look for reinforcements, with Stephen Jones hinting recently that they're still open for business . If that's true, they could find a game-changer in Josh Sweat, who was recently mentioned by Adam Schefter as a trade candidate. While appearing on The Pat McAfee Show, Schefter said Sweat being on the block has been a rumor "for a while," and added that continued losses could lead to Arizona making a move.
"Josh Sweat, like, that's been going on with him for a while now. The idea that he could be dealt and, you know, if Arizona loses some games here, maybe they could get an attractive enough pick that they would be willing to deal him. A big-time pass rusher who had 12 sacks last year," Schefter said.
One of the positives in trading for Sweat, beyond the fact that he had 12 sacks in 2025, is the fact that he wouldn't be a one-year rental. Dallas has made moves for players such as Porter and George Pickens lately, and they've come over in need of a new deal.
That's not the case for Sweat as he signed a four-year, $76 million contract with the Cardinals in 2025. There is a potential out in his contract ahead of the 2027 season, but the Cowboys can keep him around through the 2028 campaign if they wished.
Another plus is Sweat's ties to Parker. In 2024, Parker was the passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach for the Philadelphia Eagles, and Sweat was one of their top pass-rushers.
He recorded eight sacks that season, before signing with Arizona in 2025. That means Parker already knows he fits the system he runs, and has seen Sweat find success in that scheme. That's why this trade feels too perfect for Jones to ignore.

title: One Advanced Metric Reveals Silver Lining to Broncos’ 2-2 Start
full_text:
Four games into the 2026 NFL season, the Denver Broncos sit at 2-2 , with slow starts in each game and a pathetic total of just 13 first-half points.
It's clear the Broncos have a lot of work to do to become a top contender.
However, it's worth noting the Broncos have played four teams that have all shown why they rank among the favorites for a deep playoff run, if not a trip to the Super Bowl. The Broncos' 2-2 start isn't something to dismiss outright, because they've found ways to beat two top teams, and in the other two games, they've had their chances.
As the advanced metric DVOA shows , the Broncos have faced the NFL's toughest schedule in the first four weeks. No other team has faced the gauntlet that Denver has.
Four weeks into the season, DVOA now accounts for opponent adjustments to the tune of 40%. The Broncos sit 14th overall in DVOA at 0.6%, ranked 15th in offense at -2.2%, 14th in defense at -0.7%, and 15th in special teams at 2.1%. Remember that DVOA is better for defense when it's negative.
But what about Denver's opponents thus far? As it turns out, the Broncos have already faced the top three teams in DVOA. In order of ranking, they are the San Francisco 49ers, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Kansas City Chiefs.
The 49ers rank first overall at 54.8%, first in offense at 44.6%, fifth in defense at -13.5 %, and 22nd in special teams at -3.4%.
The Jaguars rank second overall at 40.1%, fourth in offense at 21%, third in defense at 19.4%, and 18th in special teams at -0.2%.
The Chiefs rank third overall at 25.6%, fifth in offense at 20%, 10th in defense at -5%, and 16th in special teams at 0.6%.
While special teams isn't a strength for these three teams, they have top offenses and defenses — all three offenses in the top five and two defenses in the top five plus one in the top 10.
Add to this that the Los Angeles Rams rank seventh overall in DVOA at 18%, seventh in offense at 13.6%, fourth in defense at -18.9%, and 32nd in special teams at -14.5%. That means that every team the Broncos have faced is in the top 10 in overall DVOA, offensive DVOA, and defensive DVOA, with three in the top four in each category.
The Broncos have areas to improve, but the fact is, they've faced four teams that all have a legitimate case for the Super Bowl.
The question now is what happens with the Broncos in the next four games?
Denver will face the Seattle Seahawks on a short week in Week 6 on Thursday Night Football and the Chiefs again in Week 8. The Seahawks rank sixth overall in DVOA and have the top defensive DVOA.
In other words, while the schedule won't be as tough as it was the first four weeks, the Broncos still have to face two tough opponents in their next four. And they can't take the likes of the Los Angeles Chargers (this week's opponent) and the Arizona Cardinals lightly, even though they rank lower in DVOA. The Cardinals rank 19th overall, while the Chargers rank 31st.
Again, if there's a silver lining to the first four weeks, it's that the Broncos faced four tough teams and still found a way to win two of those games, both at home.
The Broncos would certainly like to get more than two wins in the next four games to secure a chance at the playoffs. But to do so, they need to win at least one of these two games against the Seahawks or Chiefs, while taking care of business versus the Chargers and Cardinals, both of which are on the road.
