title: Three Things That Mattered in Chiefs' 30-27 Win Over Raiders
full_text:
For the fourth week in a row, the Kansas City Chiefs secured a victory to open the 2026 season. For the third week in a row, it was far from the prettiest of triumphs.
Still, the only thing that matters in the NFL is whether you won or lost. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes, head coach Andy Reid and company ensured a positive outcome against the Las Vegas Raiders, finishing with 30 points to the host team's 27. Several developments stood out, both good and bad , which creates an interesting dynamic as Kansas City heads into the bye week.
With that in mind, here are three of the top things that mattered from Sunday's game.
When the Chiefs first signed Kenneth Walker to a hefty multi-year contract during the offseason, some (including this writer) believed the team would have to give him a heck of a workload in order for him to be worth it. Now that the dust has settled on the running back market and four games have been played, it's safe to say the reigning Super Bowl MVP has lived up to the hype and then some.
Walker delivered yet another classic performance on Sunday afternoon and evening, toting the ball 22 times for 177 yards (eight yards per carry) and a pair of touchdowns. A whopping 152 of those yards and both scores arrived in the second half. Ahead of Monday Night Football , he's currently leading the sport in yards and yards per attempt while also holding a staggering lead on missed tackles forced with 43 (Detroit Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs is second with 28).
The prized free agent pickup joined Jim Brown and O.J. Simpson as the only players ever with two or more 170-plus-yard rushing performances in the first four games of a season. He's elusive, explosive, consistent and is a perfect fit given the tweaks made by the coaching staff .
Right when everyone thought Walker couldn't endear himself to his teammates and fans enough, he found a way to do just that in Week 4.
Yes, Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins attempted 52 passes. He was bound to rack up some volume. Not only that, but Las Vegas mustered only 2.8 yards per carry on the ground. On the other hand, allowing a 38-year-old to pick apart your defense to the tune of 365 yards and a pair of touchdowns and letting the home team hold the ball for 35:42 of game time is iffy at best. Twenty-seven points later, it was a somewhat alarming showing for the Chiefs' defense again.
According to RBSDM , Cousins averaged 0.25 EPA per play overall and the Raiders owned a 61% success rate on early-down passes. The Chiefs' linebackers got absolutely picked apart by the home club's tight ends, Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer. Removing Week 1's throttling of the Denver Broncos , Kansas City's defense is now 20th in EPA/play and 17th in success rate surrendered. It isn't like the Raiders, Miami Dolphins or Indianapolis Colts are unstoppable on offense.
Coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's defense got to Cousins for hits plenty of times and ranked 14th in pressure rate ( via TruMedia ), although coming away with no sacks for another week is concerning. It isn't time to panic given the youth and sample size this group is dealing with, but we're firmly in wait-and-see mode here.
With left tackle Josh Simmons nursing a back injury and left guard Kingsley Suamataia benched , the Chiefs were already behind the proverbial eight-ball as a passing offense. Once wide receiver Rashee Rice left the game in the first quarter with a hamstring injury , things got even worse. Luckily for them, Tyquan Thornton rose to the occasion and had the best game of his career, but the outing ended prematurely due to a gruesome ankle injury of his own in the final frame.
Losing someone with 11 catches, 219 yards and a pair of touchdowns in four games is far from the end of the world, to be fair, but it's the timing and nature of Thornton's impact that make this loss significant.
The former second-round NFL Draft selection is a chunk-play savant, averaging 23.1 yards per reception in 2025 and 19.9 at the time of his injury. In Weeks 1-4, 53.3% of the plays directed to him went for a first down or touchdown. KC tried him four times on third down on Sunday, with two being immensely successful.
Thornton's rapport with Mahomes seems to be second to only tight end Travis Kelce, and his ability to routinely outplay the bar set for him (+18.4% catch rate over expected this year) adds electricity to an aerial attack that needs it.
No one knows at this moment when or whether Thornton, who suffered a dislocation, will return in 2026. Perhaps the replacement solution is giving rookie Cyrus Allen more playing time or reuniting with old friend Tyreek Hill , but something's got to give so Kansas City doesn't regress in a major way — especially while Simmons is still on the shelf.

title: Tyquan Thornton’s Injury May Make Tyreek Hill Reunion With Chiefs Inevitable
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs topped the Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 yesterday, they lost a budding star in the process. Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who was in the midst of a career-high 111-yard, two-touchdown performance, suffered a gruesome injury late in the fourth quarter that will presumably knock him out for the rest of the campaign.
Concerns about the wide receiving corps had already risen after WR1 Rashee Rice exited the contest on the second drive with a hamstring strain. Now, Andy Reid's squad might be short two of its top three wideouts when it returns from the bye in Week 6. All of these factors combined make a Tyreek Hill reunion in Kansas City impossible to ignore. Unsurprisingly, more reports linking Hill and his former team have surfaced since the final whistle sounded last night.
ESPN insider Adam Schefter revealed this morning that Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, is looking to negotiate a contract for the 32-year-old speedster. A deal could reportedly be signed in the "next few days," which is a pretty significant development in the situation.
Developing: Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus said he plans to begin negotiating a deal for his veteran wide receiver with multiple teams today. One of those teams is the Chiefs, who have maintained contact with Hill. “I would anticipate Tyreek  potentially signing with a team… pic.twitter.com/RBn7ju28Ku
Hill is coming off a horrific injury of his own, as he dislocated his knee and tore multiple ligaments four games into the year with the Miami Dolphins in 2025. He spent the offseason recovering and is nearing full health — whatever that might entail — entering his 11th year in the pros.
"Cheetah" spent six years in Kansas City and reeled in 6,630 yards and 56 touchdowns with the franchise during his tenure. He helped the team win Super Bowl LIV against the 49ers and was Patrick Mahomes' favorite downfield target until he was traded to Miami in the 2022 offseason. It's no coincidence that all the smoke connecting Hill to the Chiefs has re-emerged with the wide receiver room's status looking grim. ESPN's Nate Taylor wrote in an article yesterday that Hill was targeting a November return — The Athletic's Michael Silver echoed that same sentiment — but Schefter's latest report suggests a signing might be more imminent than initially believed. There's also a world where Hill signs with the Chiefs soon but spends multiple weeks ramping back up to game speed.
I expect the Chiefs to have strong interest in a Tyreek Hill reunion when the free agent receiver is healthy enough to play. He's believed to be targeting a November return. Players I talked to in the locker room (Mahomes, Kelce, Chris Jones & others) are all for it. @TheAthletic
Even if Rice does not miss any time, general manager Brett Veach has to act sooner rather than later to add another target to the passing attack. It's upsetting that it had to come at the expense of a player who was developing into a fan favorite, but the Chiefs no longer have to create an open roster space for Hill if they place Thornton on season-ending IR.
The important caveat to note is that we don't know what Hill will look like in game action. He is aging rapidly and dealing with an injury that many thought could end his career at the time. The Chiefs can't realistically expect him to return to his elite form right away.
Regardless, a Chiefs reunion with Hill was already likely before yesterday's string of injuries. Now, it simply seems inevitable before it becomes official sometime this week.

title: Biggest Winners and Losers From Chiefs' Win Over the Las Vegas Raiders
full_text:
The biggest Raiders-Chiefs game in quite some time lived up to the billing. Six lead changes, several big-play swings, and a finish that required every bit of Kansas City's blood pressure to rise.
In the end, the Chiefs defeated a longtime division rival on their home turf to move to 4-0 and took sole possession of first place not just in the AFC West, but in the entire AFC.
It wasn’t perfect, and it was tense, but it was a win, and the Chiefs head into their bye week unbeaten. Here is a full breakdown of the biggest winners and losers from Sunday afternoon in Las Vegas.
What else is there to say at this point? Kenneth Walker leads the NFL in rushing with 537 yards through four games, 116 more than the next closest back. Sunday was perhaps his best performance yet, and the biggest splash came at the perfect time.
On a first-and-10 in the fourth quarter, he found an opening immediately and took it 76 yards to swing the game wide open, setting up Tyquan Thornton's second touchdown of the afternoon and giving the Chiefs a lead they would not relinquish.
His fourth-quarter production didn't stop there, though. He added two more touchdowns in the fourth quarter, one from two yards out and one from 22, to put the game away. Even without the long run, Walker still topped 100 yards. He finished with 177 yards on 22 carries, and the Chiefs do not win this game without him, once again.
The Chiefs did not record a sack for the third straight week, which remains a legitimate concern. But 18 pressures, according to PFF, and 10 quarterback hits on Kirk Cousins was progress, and nobody showed up bigger along the defensive line than defensive end George Karlaftis.
He accounted for six of those hits, and none was bigger than the last one. On the Chiefs' final defensive snap, his hit on Cousins caused an errant throw that undrafted rookie Xavier Nwankpa hauled in, allowing Kansas City to end the game in victory formation.
Karlaftis finished with eight pressures, double his output from any game through the first three weeks. When the defense needed a play to close it out, he delivered it as he did all afternoon.
The penalty gaffes will still drive Chiefs Kingdom crazy, but the unit made two plays that directly changed the game's outcome. The first came immediately after Walker's opening fourth-quarter score.
As Dareke Young was being tackled on the ensuing kickoff return, linebacker Jeffrey Bassa punched the ball clean out of his hands for fellow linebacker Jack Cochrane to recover at the Raiders' 22. Walker needed one play to run it in for his second touchdown and push the lead to 30-19.
The second ensued after a Raiders touchdown and a Chiefs three-and-out, when punter Matt Araiza booted a 52-yarder that Xavier Nwankpa downed at the one-yard line, forcing Las Vegas to go 99 yards to tie or win. Araiza placed all five of his punts inside the 20 on the afternoon.
Wide receiver Nikko Remigio also contributed a 27-yard punt return into Raiders territory in the third quarter, and Araiza picked up 12 yards on a fake punt for a first down, though neither led to a score. It was the unit’s best performance of the season.
Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton would have been just below Walker in the winners column if not for how his afternoon ended. After setting a career high with five catches for 111 yards and two touchdowns, including a 42-yarder and a 55-yarder that got the deep ball going for Kansas City, he suffered a dislocated ankle late in the game .
Doctors put the ankle back in place Sunday afternoon, and he flew back with the team, but he will miss significant time, and a season-ending injury is presumably not out of the question.
It is a particularly cruel twist of timing. Rashee Rice exited earlier with a hamstring injury, and Thornton stepped up in his absence as the team's most reliable passing-game threat, though Xavier Worthy had by far his best game of the season. Thornton’s emergence was starting to feel like a real development for this offense. For now, that will have to wait.
Exploiting the middle of the field against this Chiefs defense was always going to be the Raiders' game plan, and Las Vegas executed it well. The numbers were ugly.
Slot corners, linebackers, and safeties were targeted 34 times, allowing 26 catches for 301 yards, according to PFF. L'Jarius Sneed allowed nine catches on 11 targets for 88 yards, extending a troubling trend in coverage. Linebacker Nick Bolton was not far behind, allowing seven catches on eight targets for 79 yards.
Tight end Brock Bowers lived up to the billing with six catches for 86 yards and a touchdown, but he was not the only problem. Las Vegas had six pass catchers finish with 32 yards or more. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo will need to find answers in the middle of the field during the bye week.
Given the final result and their personnel, you will walk away feeling acceptable about the offensive line's performance. But acceptable is a relative term when you look at the details.
Mahomes took eight hits, three of them from Maxx Crosby. Right tackle Jaylon Moore allowed a team-high four pressures, and Mahomes finished 15-for-30 for 225 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions, his least efficient outing of the season, though he still averaged 7.5 yards per attempt.
To be fair, the Chiefs were without both Josh Simmons and Kingsley Suamataia (coach's decision) , and they allowed just two sacks against an extremely talented defensive end unit. The passing game got the job done when it needed to. But the offensive line needs reinforcements, and the bye week could not have come at a better time for this group to regroup.

title: Andy Reid Remains Tight-Lipped on Kingsley Suamataia’s Unexpected Chiefs Benching
full_text:
In the Kansas City Chiefs' 30-27 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a key piece on the offensive line was nowhere to be found. Kingsley Suamataia relinquished his starting left guard role to veteran Mike Caliendo for the entirety of the action.
During the contest, ESPN's Nate Taylor revealed that Suamataia's absence was a "coaching decision." He hadn't been listed on the injury report all week, making it clear that it was due to something behind the scenes. There were questions about whether Suamataia was out for personal reasons or being disciplined by the coaching staff. In his postgame press conference , Andy Reid didn't necessarily give reporters much to run with, addressing the situation before anyone could even ask.
"As far as the Kingsley thing goes, before you guys ask, that's between Kingsley and I," Reid said. "But we'll figure it out down the road. We'll be better as a team for it, and Kingsley will be better for it."
The decision to start Mike Caliendo over Kingsley Suamataia is a coaching decision, not injury related, per Chiefs. Caliendo is still lined up in the huddle for the first snap of the second quarter.
The 2024 second-round pick out of BYU had played all 201 offensive snaps at left guard prior to today. Instead, Caliendo received the nod at guard opposite Trey Smith on the right side.
Without speculating too much, it does sound like the decision was made based on something Suamataia did, potentially breaking a team rule or standard. Then again, it's evident that we're not going to get much information beyond Reid's comments.
Patrick Mahomes also addressed the situation after the game and acknowledged the importance of Suamataia. Then again, the Chiefs' signal-caller made it known that he had plenty of confidence in his replacement today. "Kingsley knows how important he is to the team," Mahomes said. "Like coach said, he'll keep it between him and Kingsley. But at the end of the day, we have a guy like Mike Caliendo who's played in a lot of big games and had a lot of reps. He stepped right in and did a great job against a really good defensive line. I have a ton of trust in him, and then we'll get Kingsley back in the fold here soon."
Suamataia is a tackle-turned-guard who excelled at his new position in 2025 , starting all 17 games there. It remains to be seen whether this coaching decision will extend beyond this week or if it will just be a one-time benching to teach him a lesson.
Overall, the offensive line wasn't particularly clean tonight. Mahomes was sacked twice on the afternoon, but the Raiders were in Kansas City's backfield on many occasions. Obviously, the best version of this Chiefs roster includes Suamataia at left guard. We should find out more about his status for Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers after the bye.

title: Biggest Decision Mike McDaniel Got Wrong Against Seahawks and it Needs to Stop
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-4 and to say their 2026 season is barely on life support would be an understatement. For any chance to make the postseason, the Chargers need to go at minimum 10-3 over the next thirteen games. The team's struggles have been a major source of confusion, specifically for a Jim Harbaugh-led football team.
Procedural penalties, ball security and special teams gaffes have haunted the Chargers at every turn. But, the biggest and most shocking aspect of LA's struggles is that of the offense. The gameplan against the Seahawks did not lean into bread and butter simple offense, it maintained a level of complexity that has yielded rough results.
This past offseason, the NFL world was on the Chargers hype train. The pairing of franchise quarterback Justin Herbert and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was viewed as a dream scenario. Upon McDaniel's arrival in Los Angeles, McDaniel and Herbert began tweaking some of his footwork and mechanics to emphasize the quick game. The idea at the time was to be able to get the ball out quickly to reduce the pass rush on Hebert in the same way Tom Brady had limited the Chargers pass rush with Joey Bosa and Melvin Ingram over the years.
The idea to change up Herbert sounded like a good idea at the time and most of the NFL world bought in. The results have been awful and the exact opposite of massive expectations. Herbert may look uncomfortable in the offense and appears to be thinking too much, but the rest of the offense looks to be on similar shaky ground.
The Chargers, through four games, have been penalized a league high 14 times for false starts. The entire offense is struggling with the snap count in the midst of all the other complexities of the offense.
The biggest example of this came when wide receiver Tre' Harris was flagged for a false start because he did not know he was supposed to go in motion. Herbert signaled for the motion and Harris looked at him confused and eventually he started a motion but the ball was snapped resulting in the false start.
Procedural errors cost the Chargers offense yards but most importantly they cost rhythm. The Chargers have been struggling to move the ball with any consistency and seem to shoot themselves in the foot far too often.
Mike McDaniel continues to call incredibly complex designer plays and they rarely appear to work.  The design in itself could work, but the offense is struggling with basic protections and the snap count, expecting them to be able to block up a play with so many moving parts is an unrealistic demand at this point in time.
The design of this jet sweep is just too much. Seattle gets five guys behind the LOS. LB Drake Thomas flies right by Keaton Mitchell untouched. QJ ends up stiff arming him into the earth but the damage is done and he had no where to go. pic.twitter.com/vkEL4F8zf1
McDaniel has been at the helm of elite offenses before but the Chargers are struggling to grasp the complexity of his offense. The mistake of the game and gameplan was just much complexity. A Philly special at the goal line down multiple scores should not be in the arsenal. McDaniel boasted about being able to adjust to players and highlight their strengths, but can he adjust his play calling for the unit to thrive.
Have yet to see any adaptations from him https://t.co/dbOThe44xT
The Chargers may have to start three or four rookies on the offensive line against the Denver Broncos this Sunday. There should be zero expectation that that unit will be able handle the Broncos defensive front and significantly complex protections and trick plays.

title: 5 Khalil Mack Trade Destinations if the Chargers Start Tanking
full_text:
If the Los Angeles Chargers continue down the path they are on, the possibility of making a major move before the trade deadline becomes harder to ignore. With a winless record , the Bolts have to start thinking beyond simply trying to salvage the current season. Which could put several veterans in an interesting position.
Khalil Mack is one of the biggest names who could become available if the organization decides that collecting future assets is more valuable than keeping its veteran core together.
Mack would immediately become an intriguing option for teams looking to add experience and another disruptive presence to their defense. He has spent his career playing in high-pressure situations and has the kind of veteran presence that can make sense for a contender looking to strengthen its pass rush for the second half of the season.
The selling factor would be his contract, and it’s really cheap considering the player Mack is. With his signing bonus already paid, teams would only have to pay this elite pass rusher Eight million dollars.
After two trades last week, here are more names to monitor ahead of next month’s #NFL trade deadline. pic.twitter.com/i9XdEC0oPQ
This only feels right of course. I mean, Mack has stated how much his time in Chicago meant to him. A reunion would make the most sense if you really think about it.
With Sweat and Odeyingbo as the anchors of the Bears edge rushers, Mack would fit right in with plenty to contribute to. The veteran would be a marvelous mentor, as well as a wrecking ball for team that has the potential for a successful season.
Khalil Mack reflects on his time with the Bears and says he has developed a great appreciation for it over the years and now understands how rare championship caliber teams are: “Looking back on it, you realize how important those moments are…those teams that you got..that… pic.twitter.com/dgUcx4xUgp
The Cowboys have been looking for ways to make their defense more dangerous. Adding someone with Mack’s experience could immediately give that unit another legitimate threat off the edge. He would not have to be the player carrying the entire defense either, which could allow him to be used more strategically.
Mack also brings something that cannot really be taught at this point in his career. He knows how to prepare, he knows how to attack opposing quarterbacks and he has been through almost every situation an NFL player can experience.
They need another weapon on the edge, especially since the departure of Micah Parsons. The Cowboys would be smart to field some offers over to the Chargers if he becomes available.
San Francisco has consistently valued having a strong defensive front, and putting Mack into that type of environment would give the team another experienced pass rusher who knows how to create problems without needing to dominate every single snap.
With multiple injuries to the defensive line like Nick Bosa , it would make a lot of sense for them to acquire Mack. The 49ers are a very competitive team that always falls short due to injuries, this new addition would be a safetey blanket in a way.
Carolina would be a more interesting option, but I actually think it could work. The Panthers need to continue building a defense that can consistently pressure quarterbacks.
Even if he is not putting up the same numbers he did earlier in his career, his presence alone would make him valuable.
This would also be a situation where Mack could take on more of a leadership role. A younger defense could benefit from having someone around who has spent years playing at an elite level.
Arizona is another team that could make a lot of sense if Mack decides he wants a different opportunity. The Cardinals have a pretty bad defense in points allowed per game . If they brought him in, the talent level would automatically elevate.
The Cardinals have been building toward a more competitive defense, and adding a veteran of Mack’s caliber would give them another piece that offenses would have to account for every week.
The Cards have allowed 434 points over the 14 game stretch. Arizona's franchise worst points allowed previous to last season's 488 was 455.

title: Jim Harbaugh's Spat With Reporters Hints at Bad Things for Chargers
full_text:
There are usually public, obvious signs that things are going bad for an NFL organization before a reset.
The Los Angeles Chargers might’ve just had one of those moments with Jim Harbaugh.
Harbaugh, usually the aw-shucks dad-jokes guy, found himself on the grill with reporters ahead of Week 5 and the exchange was, in a word, tense.
Background context first: Harbaugh’s Chargers are 0-4 and look like the worst team in football . A fundamental mishandling of roster construction , summer and preseason prep and overall strategy have led to this point.
Naturally, reporters had questions.
Harbaugh had answers, but not so much about the topic as much as where things stand for the Chargers, it seems.
Harbaugh and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel have stressed since the latter’s hiring that the goal is to make sure Justin Herbert doesn’t need to play hero ball and do it all on his own.
But this season has been more of the same, if not worse. There’s more than ever on Herbert’s shoulders as nothing works around him.
As it should, ESPN’s Kris Rhim raised this topic and found Harbaugh suggesting the question was an insult.
"Yeah, that just sounds more like an insult than it does a question, but if that's the way you look at it,” Harbaugh said. “I'm saying that it's the kind of competitor that he is where I've never seen him flinch. I've never seen him rattled.”
It doesn’t sound like all that big of a deal, but the video of Harbaugh’s hesitation and the back-and-forth paint a different story:
Video of the exchange, via @chargers pic.twitter.com/shK0n4XniE
One could argue Harbaugh just doesn't want to throw McDaniel or the offensive line or somebody else under the bus. But when the reaction to a question is to suggest insults and have a back-and-forth while otherwise speaking in general cliches again, it’s worth a raise of an eyebrow.
Michigan fans can probably attest to this sort of thing with Harbaugh down the stretch before he left. And that’s not to suggest he’s on the way out with the Chargers, but there’s no cheeky “11 wins, Pop,” coming from Harbaugh or Joe Hortiz directed at reporters right now.
This is a bit of history repeating itself:
🎥 2019 After losing to Ohio State Very similar exchange from Jim Harbaugh and reporter compared to answer addressed to Kris Rhim's question yesterday. pic.twitter.com/fIDFwFKdMv
One has to think that if the Chargers don’t start winning and don’t start actually taking care of Herbert in the way they proclaim they want to, it won’t take the season ending for jobs to be lost and a full program reset could be on the way.
In hindsight, with the Chargers at 0-4 already, one might be able to circle this little event in red as the first big sign of where things were headed.

title: Grading Every Chargers Position Group After Week 4 Disappointment vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are now 0-4 and more than half of their original starting lineup on offense are now injured. LA marched into Lumen Field in Seattle on Sunday already banged up and still searching for an identity on offense.
The Chargers dropped the game to the Seahawks and now have more questions than answers. They looked on the brink of complete surrender in the first half before Justin Herbert appeared to throw the playbook and caution to the wind and brought them back to within one score, but the late-game theatrics were too little too late. The defense played winning football and did what they needed to do to give their team a chance.
The game unfolded in truly two different halves for the offense. The defense battled but when the offense and special teams made bone-headed mistakes that put them in tough positions, the defense quickly yielded points. The LA Chargers are at the edge of a cliff for the season, grading every position group is tough, but let's at least highlight the performances that really stood out, good or bad, but the best deserve some recognition too.
Justin Herbert may have played his worst half of football in his career to start the game. He opened the game by throwing an interception directly to Seattle's Drake Thomas. I predicted the Chargers would try to attack Thomas in the passing game but Herbert might as well have thrown it right to him. He followed that perfect throw to the defense with another that led to the Chargers being down 20-3.
I'm not sure what switch flipped in Herbert but he appeared to throw the playbook out and started trying to make something happen. He managed to scramble for a big gain before the half ended and helped get within Cameron Dicker's field goal range to at least get three points before the half. The scramble and throw continued into the second half where Herbert led the Chargers to claw back to within one score.
The Jekyll and Hyde Herbert performance is confusing. Where was this playmaker the whole time? Was his attempt to run the offense just too much? Did he have to take several horrific hits to wake up? Did he have to have three of the five starting offensive linemen go down to switch modes? The entire performance is confusing but the first half cannot be ignored.
The Chargers three running backs all got snaps and carries in this game and Kimani Vidal and Omarion Hampton both averaged five yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell averaged 3.9 yard per carry and he and Hampton both had an explosive run on the day. Hampton and Vidal both scored on the ground and both scores came off of angry "I will not be denied," runs.
The backs did have a few collective drops in the passing game early but overall were consistent and performed well.
Quinton Johnston and Tre' Harris came up big in the final stretch of the game but were nonexistent in the first half. It's hard not to question where the root of the problem was simply because, everyone looked bad in the first half and when the offense found life, so did the receivers.
They weren't asked to do too much but had a rough time blocking. Hayden Rucci had a decent day blocking although did give up a sack. Oronde Gadsden caught five of seven targets on the day including a clutch fourthdown conversion.
It was not pretty and both Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater went down. The Chargers on the final two drives were down to zero reserve offensive linemen and four rookies on the field.
This might be the single worst all-around blocking effort I've ever seen by a team. The Chargers have a 7v6 advantage (including chip help). Yet, not a single guy wins their rep except for the LG who's arguably holding. Disband this franchise immediately. pic.twitter.com/rYJTm6rP4N
For the second week in a row, the Chargers defense fought their hearts out. They got the ball back to the offense at a critical moment.
Tuli Tuipulotu was a game wrecker and the whole front kept the Seahawks running backs in check and applied pressure on quarterback Sam Darnold. They answered the bell when it was time to put their foot down. Teair Tart was a menace consistently harassing the interior offensive line and getting penetration.
The Chargers secondary has been battling injuries. Derwin James was not active, Elijah Molden returned to the lineup, while Donte Jackson left for the second week in a row for separate injuries. The rotations have made communication difficult but multiple missed tackles from both the defensive backs and linebackers lead to explosive plays.
The linebackers played well overall but many of the big plays allowed resulted in the linebackers getting swallowed up by blockers or not getting enough depth in their coverage drops.
However, the defense did relatively limit Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He entered the game attempting to catch and tie Randy Moss with four straight games of 100 more more yards and a touchdown to start the season. The Chargers defense held Smith-Njigba to his lowest totals of the season with only five receptions for 76 yards.
Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba has recorded 100+ receiving yards and a touchdown in each of Seattle’s first three games. With another game like today vs. the Chargers, JSN would tie Randy Moss’ Super Bowl-era record of four straight games to start a season, set in 2007. pic.twitter.com/7GPZcROEip
The specialists did their jobs but Derius Davis' muffed punt was an early back breaker.

title: Chargers Possibly Trading Justin Herbert Gets Shaky Matthew Stafford Comparisons
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are in a hole of their own digging so deep that the Justin Herbert trade suggestions have arrived.
So have the comparisons to Matthew Stafford and the Detroit Lions.
No wonder. The Chargers are 0-4 and have looked like the most uncompetitive, unprepared team in football . Jim Harbaugh has no answers. Mike McDaniel’s offense and every single one of his former Miami Dolphins players look lost. Herbert has played one good half of football, which is even pushing it a bit.
And incredibly, there’s no viable path to a turnaround despite the Chargers still sitting on roughly $30 million in cap space.
Hence, the budding idea that a full-blown organizational reset should be on the table.
For the Chargers, there’s no escaping the Stafford-Lions comparisons and suggestions.
Those Lions shipped away Stafford for multiple first-round picks and shrewdly used the resources to build a contender. Stafford went West and blossomed in a better organization and surroundings.
The parallels to Herbert and the Chargers are simple enough. Gilberto Manzano of Sports Illustrated is one prominent name suggesting it’s time to consider the move: “If the Chargers net multiple draft picks for Herbert and land a top-five pick as a result of their own miserable season, they could get a top quarterback and top wide receiver in what should be a loaded NFL draft.”
It’s early October, but Chargers fans know some of the names: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah. It goes on and on.
The Chargers’ own ineptitude has led to this point. Harbaugh and general manager Joe Hortiz seem more focused on compensatory picks than protecting Herbert. The organization paid up for Harbaugh and McDaniel, but Hortiz has done a supremely poor job of putting good weapons around the quarterback. McDaniel, and those before him, don’t take the guard position nearly seriously enough for the modern NFL, either.
The result is Herbert looking checked out. Who can blame him? It’s not fun to have a top-10 passer and trade him at the age of 28, but selling high while the Chargers can net potentially a trio of first-round picks is starting to become a more interesting conversation.
With core names like Khalil Mack, Derwin James and even Denzel Perryman getting up there in age and so many holes on the roster, starting over with an entirely new program post-Herbert trade becomes a tad more interesting with each loss.
Will a Herbert trade happen? Unlikely for a tidal wave of reasons. But it’s getting hard to fault those who float the idea.

title: Does Khalil Mack's Contract Make Him an Appealing Trade Candidate?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are sitting at a winless record going into Week 5 of the NFL season. Every team throughout the league's history who have had a similar situation as the Bolts, have one specific thing in common. They are succumbed to various amounts of trade talk.
The Chargers who have struggled immensely, are now the talk of the town when it comes to available players. One of those players is star edge Khalil Mack.
ESPN senior reporter Dan Graziano predicted Khalil Mack as a possible trade candidate. He explained that the value of his contract would be the selling point. The elite veteran's contract is only $8 million because of the $10 million signing bonus already paid. For a player like Mack, that is a crazy deal for a team trying to bolster their defensive line. However, would the chargers even consider this?
The biggest question is what the Chargers would actually be getting by moving Mack. If the team is already struggling this badly, trading one of its best known defensive players could be a sign that the front office is ready to make some changes.
There is still a lot of value in having a player like him on the roster. Mack has been around the league for a long time, and he has been through pretty much every type of situation an NFL player can go through. For a team trying to get a better front on the defensive side, Mack would be a dream come true. He is one of the main stars no matter what team he is on.
Another note is that the Chargers have to be realistic about where they are.
If the losses keep piling up, it becomes harder to justify keeping every veteran player simply because they are an important part of the current team. At some point, the Chargers have to start asking what their roster could look like a year or two from now. That is where Mack becomes an interesting situation.
The contract makes him easier for another team to look at, but that does not mean Los Angeles has to move him. They would still have to receive something that makes the decision worth it obviously.  There is also the possibility that the Chargers could turn their season around. NFL seasons can change quickly, and moving a player too early could come back to hurt them if the team suddenly starts playing better.
That is why this situation is not as simple as putting Mack’s name on a list of potential trade candidates.
Khalil Mack is a likely trade candidate from the Chargers after their 0-4 start, per @AdamSchefter . Mack, who’s on an $18 million expiring contract, has three sacks in four games. pic.twitter.com/iDbru5w6JW

title: Chargers Snap Count Analysis: Biggest Winners, Losers and Role Changes From Week 4
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are now 0-4 after losing to the reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks. An effort that was, quite frankly, much better than what we have seen all season long, but it was still not enough for the team to overcome, shooting themselves in the foot over and over again.
With that, who were some players who made this game as close as it was, and who were some players who helped make this loss occur?
Kimani Vidal had himself a nice day, scoring his first TD of the 2026 NFL season. With his role increasing and his ability as a runner and pass blocker continuing to make a difference in the offense, expect Vidal to continue his ascent in this offense.
Role Change: 26 snaps last week -> 25 snaps this week
Omarion Hampton has continuously played fewer and fewer snaps under Mike McDaniel. It is puzzling to see, as he brings a physicality that cannot be replicated and does well at masking the issues seen on the offensive line. He is also underutilized as a pass catcher, making his smaller role even more puzzling.
*Overall, his talent and ability are not being highlighted in this offense. He falls in the losing category for that reason alone, not because his play is any worse.
Role Change: 29 snaps last week -> 25 snaps this week
Travis Burke had to step into a crucial role in Sunday's matchup against the Seattle Seahawks. With swing OT Trey Pipkins III out for the foreseeable future, Burke has had to be the swing offensive tackle. Joe Alt went down with an injury, yielding the need for Burke to step in.
Depending on the severity of both Alt's and Rashawn Slater's injuries, expect to see the rookie out there more. It should be noted that he also played quite well against the loaded Seahawks defense.
Role Change: 9 snaps last week -> 49 snaps this week
Genesis Smith has been a winner in multiple weeks as a guy climbing the depth chart and taking his opportunities that have been given to him and running with it. He is coming off a two-interception game against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. This week, he recorded one tackle and not much else. He will need a strong Week 5 to regain the "winner" category.
Role Change: 42 snaps last week -> 39 snaps this week
Tarheeb Still maintains his ability as a starting-caliber cornerback, playing quietly as one of the league's better corners since he entered the NFL. Today, he had the tough task of matching up with Jaxson Smith-Njigba, one of the league's best. Smith-Njigba still had 76 yards, but this total was his season low by over 50 yards.
Role Change: 63 snaps last week -> 59 snaps this week
Trevor Penning was once again named the starter at the guard position, playing the role until he was injured and replaced by Logan Taylor/Jake Slaughter. However, before his injury, he was playing extremely poorly, which should not be much of a surprise to most of the fanbase.
This poor play + injury make him a player in a losing position after the Chargers' Week 4 loss against Seattle.
Role Change: 69 snaps last week -> 43 snaps this week
Offensively, Tre Harris played a larger role, gaining an increase in snaps from 40 to 66, leading the receivers in snaps. As mentioned before, Logan Taylor saw playing time, the first of his NFL career. The same can be said for Jacob Spomer , the backup center. Marquez Valdes-Scantling played 26 snaps for the Chargers, playing over 20 more than last week.
As for the defense, Del'Shawn Phillips returned to a full-time role, playing 52 snaps, just two behind Daiyan Henley. Phillips only played 31 snaps last week. Troy Dye went from 24 snaps in Week 3 to just two in Week 4; he had a sack in Sunday's game.

title: Justin Herbert Looks Broken, Rashawn Slater is on Crutches and Chargers Overreactions
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are done.
It’s a simple summation, but fitting. The Chargers limped into Seattle and took a 30-23 beatdown at the hands of the Seahawks to fall to 0-4, a score only made better by a late push . Predictable as it gets, based on just how horrendous the team had looked over the first three weeks.
And now come the overreactions. Which, at this point, are close to moving from overreaction to just straight-up reality .
There’s no sugar-coating it: This isn’t Justin Herbert. Down 20-6 at halftime, the Chargers quarterback had thrown two interceptions right at defenders.
At the half, Herbert was 5-of-14 with 26 yards and the two interceptions. He had been pressured a bunch, yes, but it was an inexplicable, weird showing. Sideline pans didn’t exactly show a guy rallying the troops, either.
Yes, he turned things around a bit down the stretch. Maybe something changed with the scheme or something else. But that small sample size isn’t going to override the larger season he’s had to date just yet. Things have felt off since the offseason, if we’re being honest.
Somebody has to go . A message has to be sent, right?
The entire operation is broken, too. It’s not just Mike McDaniel’s offense, which doesn't make any sense. At halftime, Omarion Hampton gained 26 yards on four carries (6.5)...but only had four carries. Two other backs, for whatever reason, had three or more carries, too.
Harbaugh has already admitted they mishandled the summer and preseason, at least to a degree. It’s four weeks in and the Chargers still look underprepared. Take away the labels, and one could believe these last four weeks have actually been preseason action…but only for the Chargers.
Here come the injuries. Joe Alt left in the first half and was declared questionable to return.
Alt had injury woes last year, obviously, and has fought through some stuff this year.
Rashawn Slater also left with an injury and reporters saw him after the game with a walking boot and crutches .
For those keeping track, here’s a brief breakdown:
So let me get this straight: - Joe Alt went down, rookie Travis Burke in at RT - Trevor Penning went down (3rd LG), rookie Logan Taylor is in - Rashawn Slater is out, so starting center moved to LG, rookie UDFA Jacob Spomer at center, and Logan Taylor moved from LG to LT The…
As fans of any team that hit 0-3 or worse know, the concern now is just how much wear and tear piles up across the roster. If the season is largely already statistically lost, Sunday, which featured Derwin James as inactive already, one has to wonder just how many starters will consistently be out there on a weekly basis.

title: History Favors...and Doesn’t Favor Chargers Climbing Out of 0-4 Hole
full_text:
To date, Jim Harbaugh’s third season at the helm of the Los Angeles Chargers has been anything but charming. The Bolts dropped to 0-4 with a 30-23 road setback to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. Talk about digging yourself a hole? The Kansas City Chiefs (4-0), Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) and Denver Broncos (2-2) have combined for a 9-3 record and have one fewer loss than Harbaugh’s club.
The franchise has been down this road before—most recently in 2017 when Anthony Lynn’s club lost its first four games in what actually proved to be a 9-7 campaign.
Of course, there was 1992. The then-San Diego Chargers brought in a new head coach in Bobby Ross—who had guided the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets to a co-national championship in 1990. He had inherited a team which coach Dan Henning had led to a 4-12 finish. Ross’s club kicked off the year with a home loss to Marty Schottenheimer’s Chiefs. There would be three more setbacks. The Chargers were outscored a combined 95-29 during their 0-4 start.
Then the light came on. Ross’s team would win 11 of its final 12 games to finish 11-5 and capture the AFC West. The lone loss in those final 12 contests was a 16-14 defeat at the hand of the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. However, the Chargers would avenge both of those losses to Schottenheimer’s club with a 17-0 win at “The Murph” in the wild card round. The team’s season ended a week later with a 31-0 loss to the Miami Dolphins in the AFC Divisional Playoffs.
All told, the ’92 Chargers remain the only team to reach the playoffs after a 0-4 start. So what are the chances that history can repeat itself with Harbaugh’s troubled team this season?
The good news is that this time around, each conference sends seven teams to the playoffs instead of six. And each NFL team plays 17 games instead of 16 contests.
JUSTIN HERBERT THROWS HIS SECOND INTERCEPTION OF THE GAME 😬 That’s already his 6th pick of the season 🫣 pic.twitter.com/C54SZqe1RW
Now the bad news. The Chargers’ offense has produced seven touchdowns in four games, while Harbaugh’s squad has turned over the ball 10 times. Quarterback Justin Herbert, with seven of those turnovers, is completing only 59.7 percent of his passes, and has already been sacked a dozen times. Harbaugh’s club has trailed at halftime in three of its four games. The lone exception was the loss to the Bills in which the Bolts actually owned a 10-0 lead after one quarter.
Elsewhere, the team has lost its opportunistic touch. The Chargers forced 21 turnovers in Harbaugh’s first season and came up with 23 opponent miscues in 2025. This year, there’s been seven takeaways in four games—five of those in the 24-16 loss at Buffalo. Does the loss of defensive coordinator Jesse Minter play a role in the falloff?
So far, Herbert and new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel don’t seem to be on the same page. Simply put, it’s a team that seems like it’s waiting for the next thing to go wrong.
For now, the next thing is the rival Broncos and a clash at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. Does this team have the capability of making history repeat itself. All told, another home loss to a divisional rival and the Chargers could be history when it comes to being a significant factor this season.

title: 3 Winners and 5 Losers After Chargers' Flop vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Chargers walked out of Seattle still searching for their first win after a 30-23 loss. A disastrous opening half put them in a major hole, and while the offense showed enough fight to make the final minutes interesting, the early mistakes ultimately proved too costly.
There were still some encouraging individual performances, but several players and position groups left the afternoon with plenty to improve on.
Cameron Dicker once again provided reliable production when his team needed it. He went 3-for-3 on field goals and converted both extra-point attempts, accounting for all 11 of his points.
With several drives failing to reach the end zone, getting points whenever possible was important. Dicker gave his team that consistency and avoided adding another problem to an afternoon already filled with them.
Omarion Hampton did not get an enormous number of touches, but he made his opportunities count. The rookie carried the ball nine times for 45 yards and scored the team’s opening touchdown.
His five yards per carry suggested there was room for the running game to make an impact if given a larger role. Hampton also caught both passes thrown his way, showing that he can contribute outside of the backfield.
Finding more ways to involve Hampton should be a priority going forward.
Tuli Tuipulotu was one of the few defensive players consistently making things happen. He recorded six tackles, half a sack, a forced fumble and the first interception of his NFL career.
The interception was particularly important because it gave the offense another chance to generate momentum. Even with Seattle finding success early, Tuipulotu continued creating disruption near the line of scrimmage.
THE CHARGERS DEFENSE GET IT RIGHT BACK!! ⚡️ @LACvsSEA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d17s4Ng7cL
Justin Herbert had an afternoon he would probably like to forget. He threw for 189 yards and a touchdown, but two interceptions and a lost fumble played a major role in the outcome.
The slow start was particularly damaging. Herbert entered halftime with only 36 passing yards, leaving the offense struggling to keep pace while Seattle built its advantage.
There was a different version of Herbert in the fourth quarter, when he helped spark a late comeback attempt. By then, however, the turnovers had already created too much ground to make up.
Some of the best and worst from Justin Herbert today from the end zone angle pic.twitter.com/BXFWsHvfMF
Derius Davis made one of the game’s most costly errors when he muffed a punt. Seattle capitalized immediately, turning the short field into a touchdown.
Mistakes like that become even more damaging when an offense is already struggling to put together productive drives. Davis finished with just one catch for six yards, meaning there was little offensive production elsewhere to make up for the turnover.
Protection was a major issue throughout the afternoon. Herbert was sacked four times, and the constant pressure prevented the offense from developing any consistent rhythm. The most damaging moment came toward the end of the game, when a strip-sack wiped out one of the final opportunities to complete the comeback.
The offense showed considerably more life after halftime, but it is difficult to sustain that momentum when the quarterback is constantly under pressure.
Ladd McConkey was barely involved in the passing game. He received only two targets and finished without a catch.
That lack of involvement stands out, especially considering how important McConkey is to the passing attack. Playing from behind should have created even more opportunities for one of the team’s primary receiving threats. Seattle deserves credit for its defensive performance, but finding ways to get McConkey involved has to be a priority.
The opening two quarters were the biggest overall disappointment. The offense managed just six points before halftime and repeatedly struggled to stay ahead of the chains.
By the time the team found its rhythm, Seattle had already built a 20-6 advantage. Four turnovers made the comeback even more difficult.
The second half offered a glimpse of what this group can accomplish when everything starts clicking. The problem is that waiting until the game is nearly out of reach leaves almost no room for another mistake.
FINAL: #SEAHAWKS 30, CHARGERS 23

title: The Rams Have a Problem on Offense — And It’s Matthew Stafford
full_text:
Looking at the raw numbers of the Los Angeles Rams’ offense through the first four weeks of the NFL season, it would be easy to come to the conclusion that they are one of the best units in the NFL.
The Rams rank second in total offense with 417 yards per game behind only the Chicago Bears. They also rank second in passing offense with 290.3 yards per game, trailing just the Carolina Panthers.
Those numbers would seemingly tell you that quarterback Matthew Stafford is on his way to repeating as the NFL MVP. However, that has been far from the case. In fact, an argument can be made that Stafford has been one of the weakest links of the Rams’ offense .
The Rams rank just 19th in points per game with 21.3 and their -0.05 offensive EPA per play ranks 16th. On a play-by-play basis, the Rams’ offense is one of the best. They rank sixth in offensive success rate, but it’s a team with a quarterback that can’t get out of his own way to start the season.
To be clear, the Rams’ offense is its best version with Matthew Stafford at quarterback. This isn’t to say that the Rams need to bench Stafford or go to that level of extreme, even if they have a first-round pick on the bench. However, the Rams do need him to be better, especially if they are to reach their goals and be the team that many expected them to be coming into the year.
Stafford has shown the ability to make the high-level throws and bring the team back as he did last week. However, he's lacked consistency and made too many mistakes that have cost the offense in critical moments.
When Stafford turned the ball over on the opening drive on Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, it marked the first time in his career that he has thrown an interception in the first four games to start a season. In the first four games, Stafford has six touchdowns and six interceptions.
Matthew Stafford has thrown an interception in every game this season. According to ESPN Research, this is his longest streak to open a season in his career.
Heading into Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills, Stafford ranks 17th in ESPN’s QBR. His 80.5 quarterback rating ranks 21st and trails Cam Ward, Aaron Rodgers, Tyson Bagent, Jacoby Brissett, and CJ Stroud. It’s only 0.1 better than Bo Nix.
In the more advanced stats, Stafford’s -0.01 EPA per pass ranks 19th and trails quarterbacks like Deshaun Watson. It simply hasn’t been good enough from Stafford.
Yes, it’s true that not many quarterbacks could have brought the Rams back from 10 points down in the fourth quarter on the road in Philadelphia in the rain. At the same time, there are a lot of other quarterbacks who would not have had the Rams in that position to begin with. The interception at the end of the first half simply cannot happen.
Coming into Sunday’s game, the Eagles hadn’t forced a single turnover on defense. Stafford gave them two and was directly responsible for 10 of Philadelphia’s 20 first-half points.
The Rams’ defense has three interceptions this season. On two of those occasions, Stafford has given the ball right back with an interception. According to Pro Football Focus, he has eight turnover-worthy plays in 2026, which is tied for the fourth most in the NFL.
The Matthew Stafford interception regression is real. Stafford through 8 INTs last year, and is already at 5 picks in 3+ games in 2026. He led the NFL with a +6.8 "net luck" rating during the 2025 season. Was due for more INTs. pic.twitter.com/oQRwZMbWah
In a sense, a regression back to the mean was always going to happen for Stafford after his MVP season. However, his turnover-worthy-play rate of 4.3 percent is the worst since his rookie season with the Detroit Lions back in 2009. Fantasy Points Data actually has his turnover-worthy throw rate even higher at 6.7 percent, behind only Trevor Lawrence.
Stafford has always been a quarterback that is going to take risks and trust his arm a little too much sometimes. That’s been the case on a few of his turnovers this season.
It’s not just the turnovers that have been an issue for Stafford. He has also lacked accuracy on deep targets. Last season, Stafford had a success rate of 46.7 percent with an EPA per pass of 0.74 on deep targets. His success rate ranked fifth and EPA per pass ranked sixth.
This season, Stafford’s EPA per pass of -0.17 ranks 26th and his 28.6 percent success rate ranks 24th. His success rate has dropped 18 percentage points. That’s a significant drop-off. Against the Denver Broncos, he missed Davante Adams a few times on the deep ball. He also slightly overthrew Adams after he had won at the line of scrimmage with a double move.
Again, it hasn’t all been bad for Stafford. There are moments where his arm talent has still been evident. His seven ‘big-time throws’ via PFF rank seventh. On tight-window throws, Stafford’s 0.55 EPA per dropback ranks third behind Patrick Mahomes and Brock Purdy.
Stafford typically improves as the season progresses. Since 2023, Matthew Stafford has averaged 0.08 EPA per dropback in Weeks 1-4. From Weeks 5-18, he’s averaged 0.14 EPA per dropback. That’s roughly a 77 percent jump in efficiency per play after the first month of the season.
If we widen that gap to Weeks 1-6 instead, he averaged 0.06 EPA per dropback compared to 0.16 in Weeks 7-18. Stafford is approximately 2.5 times more efficient per dropback after the first month and a half of the season. This has especially been the case over the last two seasons.
The Rams are officially out of the first month of the season and following Monday night’s game against the Buffalo Bills, the schedule does lighten up slightly. With Puka Nacua already back and Terrance Ferguson eventually returning, the Rams will once again be fully healthy at their skill positions. We have yet to see what the offense truly looks like with both those players on the field.
For the Rams to reach their ceiling, they don’t need Stafford to replicate his MVP-level play from last season. However, he does need to stop being one of the main reasons for the offense’s struggles and inconsistencies. The turnovers need to get fixed. Stafford’s history suggests that better football is coming and he’s still the best option at quarterback for the Rams.
At the end of the day, the Rams will only go as far as Stafford takes them. If the Rams are going to go from an offense that piles up yards to one that consistently puts points on the board, that improvement needs to start with Stafford.

title: Rams Rookie Report Cards After Week 4 (And an Update on the Ones That Got Away)
full_text:
Through four weeks of the NFL season, the Los Angeles Rams haven’t gotten any production out of their rookie class. Ty Simpson has been the emergency third-string quarterback on game days. Despite head coach Sean McVay saying that Max Klare would get more snaps last week with Terrance Ferguson’s injury, he played one . Keagen Trost started the season on injured reserve and CJ Daniels has been inactive on game days. Lastly, Tim Keenan didn’t make the initial 53-man roster.
The Rams have gotten about as little production as a team could get out of a rookie class. In a way, it makes sense. This class was clearly one for the future. The Rams see Ty Simpson as the future after Matthew Stafford. With Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen set to hit free agency next year, Klare will be expected to step up at that time.
Trost was always a depth pick and some insurance if the Rams lose Warren McClendon or one of their two guards next offseason in free agency. Keenan may have been a disappointment on Day 3, but CJ Daniels was at least showing some upside in training camp.
Still, the Rams have gotten some production out of undrafted free agents. Wesley Bailey has been a good rotational player and both Dean Connors and Maximus Pulley have stepped up on special teams.
Given some of the injuries at tight end and wide receiver, it’s fair, to an extent, to question some of the choices the Rams made in the draft. However, given that this was more of a class for the future, it doesn’t seem right to grade this class after four games. With that said, let’s check in on this rookie class and then look at some players that the Rams could have drafted.
During the first four games, Ty Simpson has been the weekly third-string emergency quarterback. Given how he performed in the preseason, an argument can be made that Simpson should have been the backup. However, the Rams seem to value Stetson Bennett’s experience, which will put them in an awkward spot in the case that Stafford does have to miss a game at some point. Simpson had a good preseason and can only do what the coaching staff asks of him, and they seem pleased with his current body of work.
“He’s so conscientious,” said McVay before the season. “I think you really saw his preparation and his comfort of doing the things that he's coached to do, reading with his feet, getting through progressions. I thought that really showed up in the preseason.”
If Simpson ends up as the franchise quarterback, nobody will be questioning this pick in five years. However, given the lack of production and some needs on the roster due to injuries, it’s fair to question it in the moment. Grade: B
The player that many wanted the Rams to take at 13th overall was wide receiver Makai Lemon. Given the Rams’ shift to 13 personnel and the fact that he would have been WR3 at best, Lemon didn’t make sense at that spot. Lemon struggled during the summer with the Philadelphia Eagles and through four games, he has 10 receptions for 65 yards. The Rams’ current third wide receiver, Konata Mumpfield, has six receptions for 112 yards.  Now, Lemon is undoubtedly the better player than Mumpfield, but the early production proves that the Rams were right not to take the USC wide receiver.
Not many expected Rueben Bain Jr. to be available at 13 and when he was there, some thought the Rams might select him. Instead, he went 15th overall to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Bain looked good in the preseason but has been credited with just two pressures since. Even without Myles Garrett, the Rams are getting more production out of Josaiah Stewart in his place.
Rueben Bain Jr. had 0 sacks, 0 pressures, 0 stops, and just 1 tackle on 41 snaps in his NFL debut It’s always rough for rookies in the trenches, I expect him to improve as the season goes on pic.twitter.com/YUsxMnIYsK
With the projected shift to more 13 personnel, there were some who thought the Rams could take Kenyon Sadiq out of Oregon. Sadiq has 12 receptions for 143 yards and is producing with the New York Jets. Given the injuries to Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson right now, maybe the Rams could use Sadiq. Among tight ends with at least 15 targets, Sadiq ranks fifth in yards per route run.
Unlike Lemon, an argument can be made that the Rams should have taken KC Concepcion. He brought value as a wide receiver and a returner. Right now, the Rams could use a third wide receiver and a punt returner. Concepcion has 17 receptions for 144 yards and four punt returns for 21 yards. He also brings a creative element that the Rams don’t have outside of Nacua.
Browns WR receiving yards so far this season Denzel Boston*         269 KC Concepcion*       138 Jerry Jeudy                   26 Isaiah Bond                  12 *Rookies pic.twitter.com/nICwiNCiQQ
While Denzel Boston went in the second round, it wouldn’t have been unheard of for the Rams to take him at 13 or potentially trade back for him. Boston has 13 receptions for 284 yards and is an early Offensive Rookie of the Year candidate . Like Lemon, he doesn’t have the special teams upside, but at least he’s producing in a Cleveland Browns offense.
If there is a pick to question in the Rams’ draft, it’s the Klare pick. Again, it’s easy to see the logic here . Next offseason, the Rams have a huge need at tight end. Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are both free agents. Additionally, the future of Tyler Higbee is a bit of an uncertainty.
“I've seen a guy that's maximized a lot of opportunities in practice and done some things on special teams,” said McVay last week. “Got a lot better throughout the course of camp. [He] hasn't taken quite as many reps just because of the top four guys for the most part being available.”
It’s true that there is quite a bit of depth ahead of Klare. At the same time, the Rams had to completely shift their offense back to 11 personnel against the Eagles and Klare only played one offensive snap. A second-round pick should be able to step up in that situation. After watching the preseason, he seemed like he was capable as he finished with 12 receptions and got a lot of playing time. Grade: D
The need for a wide receiver is evident here. This would have been the perfect spot to take one and Williams went 10 picks after Klare. Williams has 12 receptions for 124 yards. He’s been stuck in a Commanders offense without Jayden Daniels, but has stood out in moments and displayed his big-play ability.
Have to love an illegal motion flag being thrown after the WR has caught the ball We Antonio Williams truthers didn’t deserve that pic.twitter.com/xbeBQ3a9E3
Coming into the season, Trost was going to be a depth piece. Unfortunately, an injury in the first preseason game put him on injured reserve . Trost was playing all over the offensive line in training camp and seemed to be someone the Rams were excited about.
“It’s not too big for him. He’s a very mature rookie,” said McVay this week on the Coach McVay show. “Got the ability to play on both the left and right side. Probably a little bit more comfortable on the right, but certainly you see the athleticism, the flexibility to get in and out of right- and-left handed stances. I like what he’s about and think he’s got a bright future for us.” Grade: B
Bell would have been a risk because of his injury history, but he had four receptions for 67 yards last week for the Miami Dolphins against the Kansas City Chiefs. The third round may have been early, but given the Rams’ issues on special teams, they could use someone like Kaden Wetjen at returner. Wetjen had a punt return for a touchdown during the preseason.
Chris Bell showing off his speed 💨 @KCvsMIA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tNbGIYPEGf
Daniels had a strong training camp and preseason. It’s partially why Daniels being inactive every week so far has been surprising. Daniels was a standout during training camp and then led the NFL in receptions during the preseason with 15. Unfortunately, Daniels simply may not have special…

title: Rams Face Key Decisions With Two Offensive Linemen Eligible to Return
full_text:
Prior to the start of the season, the Los Angeles Rams placed two key offensive line depth pieces on injured reserve. Throughout the entire summer, Justin Dedich managed a non-fireworks-related hand injury that he suffered on the Fourth of July. Additionally, third-round pick Keagen Trost injured his hamstring in the first quarter of the preseason opener against the Kansas City Chiefs.
With four games played, both players are now eligible to return to the active roster if they are healthy and the Rams choose to open their 21-day practice window. The question now becomes whether the Rams will decide to bring either player back to the roster.
As it stands, the Rams aren’t hard-pressed to make a decision one way or the other. Through the first four weeks of the season, the Rams have remained relatively healthy on the offensive line. Only Kevin Dotson has missed time and he was only out for three snaps against the Denver Broncos. Filling in for Dotson at the time was Beaux Limmer.
Given the health of the offensive line, there isn’t any pressure for the Rams to make an immediate decision. The Rams can leave either player on injured reserve for as long as they want before deciding to activate either player. Once the Rams open up their 21-day practice window, the player must be placed on the active roster or they remain on injured reserve for the rest of the season.
“Fortunately we’ve been able to stay healthy up-front. Those are guys that we’re counting on that are going to be big time depth guys for us,” said head coach Sean McVay on the Coach McVay Show . “Anytime that you bring somebody back, usually there’s a coinciding move. Now, we’ve had some injuries where sometimes those things have a way of working themselves out, so we’ll look at that.”
Unfortunately for the Rams, it’s not as simple as just adding both to the roster. If the Rams did bring either back, they would have to make a corresponding move on the active roster. It’s possible they could cut players like defensive lineman Larrell Murchison or offensive lineman Bill Murray to make space, but again, it’s not something they’re hard-pressed to do right now.
Additionally, teams are only allowed eight injured reserve activations per season. As it stands, the Rams are already set to use one on Myles Garrett when he returns. The Rams will also very likely bring back Terrance Ferguson. If the Rams were to bring back both Dedich and Trost, they would have used half of their available activations and only have four more the rest of the season.
If the Rams were to bring back only one of them, Trost might make the most sense . He brings left- and right-side versatility at tackle, and can also slide in at guard if needed. Trost was also able to practice in training camp and the coaching staff seemed pleased with him. Meanwhile, Dedich missed the entirety of training camp and only brings depth at guard.
Again, it’s unlikely that the Rams do anything immediately here given the current health of the offensive line. At the end of the day, Dedich and Trost are only depth players and aren’t needed immediately. Until the Rams have to, it makes sense to stand pat and allow Dedich and Trost to continue rehabbing. With that said, it’s still something worth monitoring over the next few weeks.

title: Rams Signing Eric Kendricks Provides More Than Just Linebacker Depth
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams begin preparing for their matchup against the Buffalo Bills in Week 5, they made an addition to the practice squad on Tuesday morning. The team announced the signing of 11-year veteran linebacker Eric Kendricks to the practice squad.
Kendricks is 34 years old and is best known for his time with the Minnesota Vikings early in his career. Over the past three years, Kendricks has bounced around three different teams, most recently with the San Francisco 49ers last season.
In 2025, Kendricks signed late in the year with the 49ers , playing 73 and 53 snaps in their playoff games. While he isn’t the player that he used to be, Kendricks has shown that he is still a reliable tackler. In four games last year, Kendricks missed just one tackle. Additionally, in the NFC Wildcard game against the Philadelphia Eagles, Kendricks had a fourth-down pass breakup to win the game.
Only fitting that veteran LB Eric Kendricks — signed to the practice squad Nov. 26, and now starting after multiple injuries at the position — finishes off a playoff win for the 49ers. Kyle Shanahan and Robert Saleh working miracles all season. pic.twitter.com/46fzMrQy0M
Notably for the Rams, Kendricks also played 52 snaps on special teams. The Rams have struggled on special teams this season, especially with their kickoff and punt coverage units. During the first three weeks of the season, the Rams elevated linebacker Elias Neal twice from the practice squad . Teams are only allowed to elevate a player from the practice squad to the gameday roster three times over the course of the season.
Signing Kendricks allows the Rams to keep Neal and his one remaining practice squad elevation available for later in the season if they need it. The Rams can elevate Kendricks to the gameday roster instead if needed without having to use a spot on the 53-man roster.
However, an added element to this is that linebacker Nate Landman has been managing injuries over the last few weeks . Landman was limited with a shoulder injury on Wednesday and Thursday last week before being elevated to a full participant on Friday. The week before, Landman was limited during all three days of practice.
In addition to his special teams value, Kendricks will also provide the Rams with some experienced depth at linebacker in case Landman’s injuries worsen. There hasn’t been too much concern that Landman wouldn’t play the last few weeks. It’s seemingly been more about the Rams managing him throughout the week. Still, having Kendricks available for depth isn’t a bad thing either.
Kendricks likely isn’t being brought in to play a significant role on defense. However, with Landman managing a shoulder injury and Neal down to his final practice squad elevation, adding Kendricks gives the Rams another option to turn to at linebacker if needed.
