title: Rams Film Review: Chris Shula’s Adjustments Have Transformed the Defense
full_text:
Over the first three weeks of the season, outside of the Los Angeles Rams’ special teams, it was the defense and coordinator Chris Shula taking the vast majority of the criticism . Criticism about ‘soft zone’ and a lack of blitzing were the main concerns, even if it wasn’t always the case.
While they hadn’t played well in Week 1, they also weren’t supported by an offense that only scored seven points. In Week 2, they shut down the New York Giants and Jameis Winston. It may have only been Winston, but the defense held him to a 37.7 passer rating and a completion percentage under 50 percent.
The Rams did blow a 16-point halftime lead to the Denver Broncos, but again, the defense wasn’t put in a good spot. Due to special teams errors, both Broncos’ touchdown drives in the third quarter didn’t travel more than 52 yards. Without a controversial defensive pass interference, an argument could be made that the defense won the game.
After the loss to the 49ers in Week 1, Shula and the defense adjusted. For much of the season, the defense has been without Myles Garrett and has managed injuries to Aaron Donald and cornerback Jaylen Watson. All three players were major offseason additions. Shula was proving that he could do more with less.
In Week 1, the Rams blitzed at a 13.9 percent rate and played zone on 77.8 percent of their snaps. Their blitz rate over the last three weeks is 38.6 percent, which is the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. While they still play zone at a 59.4 percent rate, their 36.6 percent man coverage rate is the fourth-highest in the NFL.
On Sunday against the Eagles, the Rams don’t win without the defense . For 3.5 quarters, the offense was mostly non-existent. Due to special teams errors and turnovers, the Eagles didn’t have to travel more than 40 yards on three of their four scoring drives. In the second half, the Rams’ defense allowed a total of four first downs. They didn’t allow the Eagles to score a single point and got a key stop at the two-yard line.
Another "gotta have it down" for the Rams and Shula blitzes/forces the issue. Rams show 8 guys on the LOS and bring 5. Young once again bullies Mundt and meets Fiske at the QB. Play of the game here from the defense. pic.twitter.com/G2l9XFeji2
Had the defense allowed a touchdown on that sequence, the game is certainly over. While the offense struggled to score points and take advantage of opportunities, the defense kept the Rams in the game and continued giving the offense chances.
Much like the win against the Giants in Week 2, the defense did take advantage of poor circumstances. On Sunday, the Eagles were without Landon Dickerson and Lane Johnson on the offensive line. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith missed the game and Saquon Barkley left with a hamstring injury early. Barkley’s backup, Tank Bigsby, also left the game in the second half.
However, the Rams still took advantage of that and made the necessary plays. Down 10 points in the fourth quarter, the margins were small. For the first time in franchise history, the Rams held an opponent to at least 0-for-12 on third down . It was the Eagles’ most third down attempts without a conversion since at least 1991.
It was only the 14th time since the merge that the Rams have held a quarterback to 93 yards passing or fewer on 25 or more attempts and 12 or more completions. The Rams blitzed Jalen Hurts on every third down dropback except the final one. They generated six pressures and a sack on those plays. Hurts was 5-for-16 when the Rams blitzed.
Eagles went 0-for-12 on 3rd down and the Rams blitzed on all but one of them. Rams drop Stewart and Turner on the left side into coverage. Sets up 3 blocking 4 on the right. Young and Speights meet at the QB. pic.twitter.com/DjKv15b1F0
The Rams blitzed the Eagles at a 53.1 percent rate, which was the third-highest rate in the NFL in Week 4. They especially took advantage of the Eagles’ disjointed offensive line, particularly along the interior and right side.
Throughout the game, the Rams consistently overloaded the right side and forced miscommunications, leading to pressure on Hurts. The Rams had a 56.3 percent pressure rate as Braden Fiske, Kobie Turner, and Byron Young were all credited with more than five pressures.
The Rams absolutely annihilated the Eagles overloading the right side without Lane Johnson. Fiske beats the center and Young meets him at the QB. Should be another sack, but on 3rd down, Rams will take the throw away. pic.twitter.com/ZS9K63xhSL
Despite many wanting to put Shula on the hot seat in the early parts of the season, the Rams have had a top-five defense by most metrics. Through four games, the Rams’ defense ranks fourth in DVOA and third in EPA per play. They’ve allowed a 40.5 percent success rate, which ranks seventh, and despite being put in bad positions, their 20.8 points allowed per game ranks ninth. In less advanced metrics, the Rams’ defense is also second in yards per game allowed behind only the Seattle Seahawks.
Again, this is all without Myles Garrett on defense. The Rams had arguably their best defensive performance last week and Donald had to miss the game with a sore back. They were also without their top free-agent signing at cornerback in Jaylen Watson.
Eagles weren't 100% on the OL and the Rams took advantage. This time it's Kinchens from the second level, which frees up Fiske. Should be a sack, but the throw-away works. pic.twitter.com/CjeXCAvnC7
This isn’t to say that the defense is perfect. Outside of the 49ers in Week 1, the best offense they’ve played has been the Denver Broncos. Right now, the Broncos rank 20th in EPA per play on offense. The Bills will be a good test in Week 5 as they rank third.
Shula and the Rams’ defense played a key role in the win on Sunday against the Eagles. A big part of that was Shula’s creative blitzes and taking advantage of the Eagles’ injured offensive line. This week will be a different story as Josh Allen ranks ninth against the blitz with a 0.11 EPA per dropback. Still, without blitzing, Allen is third at 0.28 EPA per dropback.
The Rams will need to pick their spots against Allen and the Bills and mix in a good balance of man and zone coverage. Against man coverage, Allen has a 0.4 EPA per pass, ranking sixth in the NFL. When throwing against zone coverage, that drops to 0.12.
Since giving up 27 points against the 49ers in Week 1, the Rams’ defense has responded. In each of the last two games, they’ve gone a full half of football without allowing a single point. Shula has listened to the criticism and become more aggressive, and the Rams have found answers because of it.
The Rams have one of the NFL’s better defenses, and Sunday was an example of that even if the Eagles were short-handed. For all the criticism that Shula received early in the season, he deserves just as much credit for how the defense has responded.
Dropping a defensive lineman in coverage isn’t something that defenses should do often, but it can be an added twist as quarterbacks aren’t always expecting them to drop. The Rams did this a few times last year with Kobie Turner, but it has ramped up this season. Turner had nine coverage snaps last year. Through four games, he already has five. It’s something to keep an eye on over the course of the season.
Kobie Turner had nine coverage snaps in his career (all in 2025) before this year. Through four weeks, Turner already has five. Rams are dropping him into coverage and it creates some confusion on who's coming. Pressure gets to Hurts here. Forces an inaccurate throw. pic.twitter.com/QwnHGFuDL2
Without Myles Garrett, Young has stepped up over the last three weeks. Young is seventh in the NFL in pressures and sixth in pressure rate. His 3.5 sacks also rank fourth during that time span. The Eagles tried to block Young with tight end Johnny Mundt several times on Sunday and it didn’t work. Late in the game, when the Rams needed a closer, it was Young with the pressure and sack both times.
Byron Young was…

title: Week 5 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: Are Rams Contenders or Pretenders After Comeback Win?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams may be 2-2, but there is still some growing concern about this team and what its ceiling is. Coming into the season, many saw them as Super Bowl contenders. While they haven’t been healthy, their early-season inconsistency has been glaring . Many saw them as contenders coming into the season, but through four weeks, they have mostly been pretenders.
On Sunday, the Rams only just got past an injured Philadelphia Eagles team that was without DeVonta Smith, while Saquon Barkley left early in the game as well.. Lane Johnson and Landon Dickerson also didn’t play on the offensive line.
With 8:16 to play, the Rams had a 3.2 percent chance to win, and they somehow overcame the odds to come out on top 24-20. Quarterback Matthew Stafford led another fourth-quarter comeback and the two late touchdown drives were enough.
Still, how the Rams are winning is not sustainable. Stafford has thrown an interception in every game this season. He currently ranks 20th in EPA per pass and needs to be better, especially as the Rams get ready to play the Bills. Let’s take a look at how the media feels about the Rams in this week’s consensus power rankings.
The Rams don’t move this week in ESPN’s Power Rankings and stay in the No. 7 slot after coming back from 10 points to beat the Eagles. Again, one of the biggest questions around this Rams team is its consistency. The Rams haven’t found a way to play for 60 minutes outside of their Week 2 win against a New York Giants team that was led by Jameis Winston for most of the game.
“The Rams have been inconsistent and missed significant players because of injuries, including Garrett (three games), Donald (one) and wide receiver Puka Nacua (two),” wrote ESPN’s Sarah Barshop . “Los Angeles might not be playing like a Super Bowl contender right now, but it could be later in the season, especially once Garrett is back from knee surgery.”
Following the win against the Eagles, the Rams are up one spot in Connor Orr’s rankings . Had the Rams beaten a full-strength Eagles team, they might have gotten more respect from the media. A win in Philadelphia on the road is nothing to gloss over, but for 52.5 minutes, the Rams looked like they were going to lose by multiple scores.
Only one ranking has the Rams inside the top five, and that’s The Athletic. The Rams are up three spots from No. 8 last week following their win over the Eagles. Still, despite moving into the top five, The Athletic also noted the concerns around this Rams team, specifically around Matthew Stafford.
“While the defense was great, what is going on with Matthew Stafford?” wrote The Athletic . “The defending MVP is completing just 61 percent of his passes and has six touchdowns to go with six interceptions.”
The Rams don’t move up at all in Nick Shook’s rankings on NFL.com. Shook still has major questions about this Rams team and it’s hard to blame him. Through three quarters, the Rams were staring 1-3 directly in the face. The season could have gone sideways with a loss in Philadelphia.
“For three quarters, serious, nearly existential questions began to build for these Rams. They’d fallen behind in Philadelphia and couldn’t get out of their own way offensively, raising the specter of a 1-3 start to a season that began with immense hype,” wrote Shook. “But Sean McVay’s squad proved something amid the chaos of a fourth-quarter comeback: L.A. is not going to lay down, no matter the odds. Matthew Stafford needs to be better, though.”
Mike Florio has the Rams moving up in back-to-back weeks , but they remain just outside of the top five. The Rams could just as easily be 1-3 as they could be 3-1. A 2-2 record feels right as the Rams find their groove. If this team can find some consistency, they’ll be one of the tougher teams in the NFL, but they have a long way to go.
Through the first four weeks, the Rams have had one of the more grueling schedules in the NFL. They’ve played two teams inside the top 10 in the consensus power rankings. According to DVOA, the Rams have had the sixth-hardest schedule to start the year. It won’t get easier this week as the Rams play the Bills. The Rams play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7 and they look like a good team. However, the schedule does lighten up a little bit after this week. Again, if the Rams can hang around and then find their rhythm heading into their bye week, they’ll set themselves up well for December and January.
“If you ignore the first 52 and a half minutes this past Sunday in Philly, the Rams looked great,” wrote Fox Sports’ Ralph Vacchiano. “Actually, even without Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald, their defense was terrific all game long. It just took more than two hours for Matthew Stafford and Sean McVay’s offense to get moving in the right direction. Once it did, L.A. reminded everyone why it’s still a serious Super Bowl contender.”
The Rams were just clinging to a spot inside the top 10 last week in Pete Prisco’s rankings . With the win against the Eagles, the Rams are still just hanging on to a spot in the top 10, but are up to No. 9. If the Rams can beat the Bills this week, it will certainly solidify their spot among the contenders.
On Monday Night Football, the Rams will host a Bills team that is coming of a loss in Week 4 and hasn’t looked as sharp the last two weeks. They beat the Los Angeles Chargers despite turning the ball over four times and just allowed 29 points to a New England Patriots offense that hadn’t looked good in the first three games.
However, that only means that the Bills are going to come into Monday night focused and with something to prove. The Bills rank fifth in the consensus power rankings, with an average ranking of 4.86. If the Bills play a clean game, they are one of the best teams in the NFL, but they are susceptible to mistakes.
The question will be whether the Rams can make them pay for those mistakes. Through four games, the Bills have a -2 turnover differential. However, the Rams are at -5. When these two teams played in 2024, it was arguably the game of the year as the Rams won 44-42. Monday Night Football could contain some fireworks.
Through four weeks, it’s still difficult to place the top 10. The Vikings are undefeated, but they are the 12th-worst 4-0 team in NFL history according to DVOA. The Raiders may be 3-1, but are they a team we can trust, or are they just last year’s Colts? The next four weeks should separate the contenders from the pretenders.

title: Rams Snap Counts: Max Klare Barely Sees Field Despite Clear Opportunity
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams headed into Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles, it was known that they would likely be short-handed at tight end. On Friday, the team officially put Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve with a medial ankle sprain. Additionally, Colby Parkinson didn’t practice all week with an AC sprain.
Heading into Sunday, the Rams had two options on offense. They could either get rookie second-round pick Max Klare more involved and stick with their 13 personnel identity or go back to operating out of 11 personnel.
The Rams opted for the latter. Against the Eagles, Klare played one snap on offense. That play came in the third quarter on Kyren Williams’ 23-yard run that was called back because of unsportsmanlike conduct on the bench.
During the first three weeks of the season, the Rams operated just 56 percent of their offense out of 11 personnel, which ranked 19th in the NFL. Their 42 percent usage out of 13 personnel led the league. On Sunday, the Rams operated out of 11 personnel at an 88 percent rate . It was their highest usage out of 11 personnel since Week 5 last year. It was also the second-highest rate in Week 4. They ran a single play out of 13 personnel and had only nine plays with multiple tight ends on the field.
While coach-speak is a real thing, head coach Sean McVay seemed to imply that Klare could be leaned on more against the Eagles. McVay was specifically asked whether the injuries to Parkinson and Ferguson meant more opportunities for Klare.
“It certainly does,” said McVay. “Obviously, being able to play with multiple tight ends has become a big part of our identity and so it absolutely does.”
Fast forward to Sunday, and again, Klare had just one offensive snap.Maybe Klare would have gotten more usage had Parkinson played, as the Rams could have rotated their tight ends without having to worry as much about their depth. The fact that he played zero snaps on special teams was also odd as he had four last week against the Denver Broncos and had two the week prior.
It certainly raises questions about Klare’s role going forward. As I wrote last week, the Klare pick was always about 2027 and this year was likely always a redshirt-type season . However, the Rams could have used Klare on Sunday and he was utilized on a single play that wasn’t even a pass.
The Rams also weren’t necessarily having success out of 11 personnel. Out of 11 personnel, the Rams averaged -0.09 EPA per play. In the first half, it was -0.33 EPA per play. Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, and Tutu Atwell combined for three catches on six targets and none had more than 10 yards receiving. The Rams spent most of the offseason designing the offense around multiple tight end sets.It simply seems odd that they wouldn’t use Klare in a game in which logic suggested they could have used him.
In Week 5, the Rams will hope to get Parkinson back on the field. However, they’ll be without Ferguson for at least the next three games. Given the personnel on offense, it may not be sustainable for them to operate solely out of 11 personnel as they did last week and as they have in the past. That could mean having to use Max Klare, but if Sunday is any indication, the Rams may not believe he’s ready to contribute on offense.

title: Rams Get Encouraging Aaron Donald Update Ahead of Week 5 vs. Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could have defensive lineman Aaron Donald back on the field for Monday night’s game against the Buffalo Bills in Week 5. According to ESPN’s Sarah Barshop, head coach Sean McVay said that the hope is that Donald will play and that it is trending that way.
Sean McVay said the “hope” is that Aaron Donald will play on Monday against the Bills. “That’s the direction it looks like it’s trending in,” McVay said.
Last week, Los Angeles Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald was a surprise addition to the injury report with what the team described as a sore back. Head coach Sean McVay said that Donald picked it up after the game against the Denver Broncos and that the team would play it safe with him. Donald didn’t practice all week and was eventually ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported late last week that he understood it to be a relatively minor injury for Donald and that the team sat him out with the hope that it would heal and be in a better spot long-term. The team understands that it’s more important to have Donald available in December and January than for a Week 4 game in October.
Without Donald against the Eagles, the Rams managed to get by with Kobie Turner and Byron Young leading the way. Young was credited with eight pressures via NFL Pro and had a 27.6 percent pressure rate. Additionally, Turner added five pressures, and Braden Fiske was credited with six.
The fact that the Rams were able to generate as much pressure as they did without Donald and Myles Garrett is a testament to the amount of depth that they have on the defensive line. They were able to rely on Young, Turner, and Fiske and put together one of the best defensive performances that the Rams have had this season.
Having Donald available for Week 5 against the Bills will be important as the defense faces quarterback Josh Allen. Donald has been somewhat of a non-factor in games up to this point, as he has yet to record a sack. His 7.1 percent pressure rate also ranks 92nd among qualified defensive linemen. However, he still ranks second among interior defensive linemen in pass rush win rate at 21.4 percent, behind only Gervon Dexter. It feels like once it fully clicks for Donald again, the sacks and impact plays are coming.
The Rams showed against the Eagles that they can generate pressure without Donald or Garrett. Getting Donald back would only add another piece to a defensive front that may be starting to find its rhythm. After sitting out last week, Monday night against the Bills could be an opportunity for Donald to finally make his presence felt against a difficult opponent.

title: Rams Position Grades: Defense Earns High Marks, Special Teams Fails Again
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams beat the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday and certainly didn’t make it easy for themselves. For much of the afternoon, it looked like the Rams were on their way to 1-3 . However, in the fourth quarter, the Rams erased a 10-point deficit to win 24-20. Here are position grades from the Rams’ win over the Eagles.
There are two ways to look at Matthew Stafford’s game . In the first three quarters, Stafford had an adjusted EPA per play of -0.12. That ranked 23rd among quarterbacks in Week 4 through Sunday’s games. In the fourth quarter, his adjusted EPA per play jumped to 0.39. That’s a 0.51 increase. For as good as Stafford’s fourth quarter was, the first three quarters still happened. Stafford’s first-half interceptions both led to 10 Eagles points. He did well to bounce back, but he has to be better going forward.
Blake Corum only had five carries for 14 yards, but Kyren Williams completely took over the second half. Williams scored both fourth-quarter touchdowns, including the eventual game-winner. Williams also hauled in 10 receptions as the Rams needed a third option in the passing game. Overall, Williams was fantastic in this one. His 79.8 rushing grade via PFF ranked fourth in the NFL in Week 4.
The Rams had been without Puka Nacua the last two weeks, and without him on Sunday, they very likely lose. Nacua had nine receptions for 125 yards in his return. However, Adams was credited with two drops and the Rams need more from Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, and Tutu Atwell. That trio combined for three receptions on six targets and none had more than 10 yards receiving.
Without Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson on Sunday against the Eagles, the Rams were down both of their top tight ends. However, that still left them with three tight ends and the potential to promote a fourth. While Tyler Higbee played well, Max Klare had one snap on offense and no snaps on special teams. The Rams were forced to use 11 personnel at their highest rate since Week 5 of last year.
There were times when the offensive line struggled and the pressure got to Stafford. However, when it mattered, they played well. Kevin Dotson doesn’t look 100 percent healthy and Coleman Shelton got blown up on a 3rd-and-1 early in the game. While the offensive line is usually better in the run game, they actually held up well in pass protection, which is encouraging considering Stafford threw the ball 51 times.
A big reason why the Rams were so dominant on defense was because they controlled the trenches and got pressure on Jalen Hurts. They did that without Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald . While they missed a few sack opportunities, they finished with four sacks overall and didn’t give the Eagles a chance on the final drive.
The Eagles didn’t have the personnel to attack the Rams’ linebackers. Without Saquon Barkley, they also didn’t have an elusive running back. The Rams’ linebackers were quiet, and that’s a good thing.
There were two big mistakes from the secondary during the game. Quentin Lake mistimed his jump, allowing Darius Cooper to score a touchdown when it could have been an interception. Additionally, they left Cooper open in the end zone late in the first half for another touchdown. However, Jalen Hurts was held to 93 yards passing. That’s a pretty good day for the secondary without Jaylen Watson.
It’s another week of special teams failures. They allowed Britain Covey to return a punt 41 yards after a poor Alex Bachman return set up the offense deep in its own territory. Harrison Mevis missed a 48-yard field goal and then had a kickoff go out of bounds. It’s not a question of whether the Rams will make a special teams mistake, but when. With that said, the Rams have found some good special teams players on the coverage unit in Dean Connors and Maximus Pulley in recent weeks.
McVay didn’t make any costly decisions. He made the right choice to try to be aggressive before the half to get points. He should be able to trust his quarterback to not turn the ball over in that situation. The Rams were 1-for-3 on fourth down and the decision to go for it on 4th-and-8 in the fourth quarter was the right one. He also rallied the offense to get going, and whatever he said worked. Chris Shula called a masterclass on defense as well.

title: Monday Morning Rambling: Rams Finally Flip the Script in Win Over Eagles
full_text:
Over the last two years, the Los Angeles Rams haven’t just lost games. They’ve found ways to lose in the most gut-wrenching fashion possible . It hasn’t been often that the Rams have lost ‘normally’.
In their first loss of the 2025 season, the Rams fell to the Philadelphia Eagles after not one, but two potential game-winning field goals were blocked. In Week 5, the Rams lost to the 49ers, getting stopped on 4th-and-1 from the 11-yard line in overtime.
How the Eagles' game-ending field goal block on Joshua Karty sounded on Rams radio pic.twitter.com/ZYymbHtcyb
While the Rams didn’t lose again until Week 13 to the Carolina Panthers, Matthew Stafford fumbled with the offense in field-goal range to tie the game late.
Everybody remembers what happened in Week 16 when the Rams blew a 16-point lead to the Seattle Seahawks with the help of a controversial two-point conversion to lose in overtime. When they tried to lose in a normal fashion, they still managed to come back from 21-0 against the Atlanta Falcons to lose on a field goal in the final 30 seconds.
Zach Charbonnet with one of the craziest two-point conversions ever 😳 pic.twitter.com/cVxpndsudN
In the NFC Championship Game, the Rams got stopped on fourth-and-4 from the six when trying to take the lead in the final five minutes. That was after fighting back from 11 points down because of a muffed punt.
Fast forward to this year, and the Rams lost last week to the Denver Broncos after leading 16-0 at the half and then coming up on the wrong end of a defensive pass interference penalty.
Josh Wallace called for DPI against Pat Bryant pic.twitter.com/8QJQNT46Lg
It’s been special teams gaffes, controversial officiating decisions, untimely turnovers and a plethora of other issues. However, when the Rams have lost over the last two years, they’ve tested the sanity and emotional breaking point of fans.
On Sunday against the Eagles, the Rams looked to be dead in the water . They trailed 20-10 and had shown no signs of being able to move down the field to score. While Nick Sirianni got criticized for his decision to go for it from the two-yard line, could you blame him? The Eagles got stopped, but Matthew Stafford and the Rams’ offense faced a 98-yard field in front of them. In their previous five drives combined, the Rams had only picked up 75 yards.
With 8:17 left in the fourth quarter, the Rams had a 3.2 percent win probability according to Next Gen Stats. Even when the Rams took over with 7:26 left in the game, they only had a 5.1 percent win probability according to ESPN Stats and Info.
It was looking to be a box score anomaly. At that point, the Rams were set to become the first team since the 1997 Chicago Bears to lose while holding their opponent to at least 0-for-12 on third down. Teams were previously 2-23 when going at least 0-for-12 on third down and had lost 23 straight. The Rams had significantly outgained the Eagles. Through three quarters, the Rams had 247 yards to the Eagles’ 119.
Stafford hadn’t played well up to that point . In fact, the only quarterback to win a game with 50 or more passing attempts, 300 passing yards, two interceptions and zero touchdowns was Jameis Winston back in 2018. Up until Sunday, quarterbacks were 1-27 with that stat line.
Much like he had in the Super Bowl, head coach Sean McVay gathered his offense to remind them what was at stake and not to lose belief. There may have only been eight minutes left, but the game was far from over.
Sean McVay Having A Meeting With The Entire Rams Offense. Literally The WHOLE Offense 😂 pic.twitter.com/pappnieLtG
The thing with Stafford is that he can play poorly for 3.5 quarters, but more often than not, he plays his best football in that final half of the fourth quarter. That was the case on Sunday. On the Rams’ two scoring drives in the fourth quarter, Stafford was 12-for-15 for 140 yards. When Kyren Williams broke three tackles to put the Rams up 24-20 and give the Rams their first lead of the game, McVay’s speech had worked, and a switch had flipped for the Rams’ offense.
When Kam Curl batted down Jalen Hurts’ pass on fourth down, it was as if a huge weight was lifted off the Rams’ shoulders. For all the times that the Rams had lost in the most gut-wrenching ways possible, they had finally come out on the other end of one. It was the most improbable win since McVay took over as the Rams’ head coach, and it was also one that this team desperately needed.
Over the past two years, I’ve been one of Kyren Williams’ biggest critics. That’s not to say I haven’t been appreciative of his value to the Rams’ offense. At the same time, I have questioned whether or not he should be the bell cow in the backfield. The Rams do not beat the Eagles without Williams. It certainly didn’t look like Todd Gurley, but Williams had a Gurley-esque stat line. His touchdown run to put the Rams ahead in the fourth quarter was iconic and will go down as one of the best plays of the season.
Kyren Williams POWERS IT IN FOR THE LEAD!! @LARvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LW85llHviL
Much like with Williams, the Rams don’t win without the defense. They were consistently put in bad spots in the first half and didn’t let that faze them. In the second half, the Eagles picked up a total of four first downs and didn’t have a single first down in the third quarter. If the defense even allows one touchdown in the second half, the Rams don’t have a chance to come back. They kept fighting and the offense finally rewarded them at the end.
For as consistent as Harrison Mevis has been inside of 45 yards, in today’s NFL, you have to have a kicker you can trust to at least have a chance of making a long field goal. Mevis missed from 48 yards on Sunday, and the Rams opted not to kick from 56 after Jake Elliott made from that distance earlier in the game. Mevis then had a kickoff go out of bounds. Alex Bachman replaced Xavier Smith, but he didn’t look to be the answer either. The Rams need to bring in some competition like they did for Josh Karty last year.
Can I split the game ball or give out two and also give one to the Rams defense? If I only have one game ball, it has to go to Kyren Williams. Again, the Rams do not win the game without him. With Terrance Ferguson hurt, the Rams needed a third option in the passing game to step up. That player was Williams who became the first Rams running back since Todd Gurley in 2018 to record 10 receptions in a game. ​​​​ ​Williams is the first player this season to record at least 10 receptions and at least 10 carries in a single game. Only Christian McCaffrey and Jahmyr Gibbs have accomplished the feat since 2024.
For the first time in franchise history, the Rams held a team to at least 0-for-12 on third down. It’s only the third time that they’ve held a team to at least 0-for-10 on third down. The last time they did it was in Sean McVay’s first game as the Rams’ head coach in 2017 against the Indianapolis Colts. It’s also the first time a defense has held an opponent to at least 0-for-12 on third down since the Los Angeles Chargers held the Denver Broncos to that mark in 2023. What the Rams did against the Eagles, even if they were short-handed, was special.
There’s no doubt Sunday’s win against the Eagles was important for the Rams. The Rams are set to play the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5, and outside of last week, they were looking like the best team in the NFL. They turned the ball over five times and managed to beat the Chargers. Despite not playing as well, they could have still beaten the New England Patriots on Sunday.
Instead of being 1-3 and staring at a potential 1-4 start, the Rams are 2-2 and will be no worse than 2-3 when they face the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6. Given how the Bills have played over the last two weeks, this game at least feels more winnable than it did a few weeks ago, especially at SoFi Stadium. The Rams will have to play much better than they did against…

title: Hondo's Weekly Raiders Mailbag: Getting the Run Game Going!
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) head to the suburbs of Boston this weekend to take on the New England Patriots (2-2), fresh off a Super Bowl appearance but with a disappointing 2026.
The Raiders, meanwhile, are in the midst of a rebuild and are overachieving.
I already dissected last week’s game in my weekly report card and offered my winners and losers , so today we flip the page and look ahead to this weekend, not last.
I asked Raider Nation what they want this weekend, besides the obvious win. This Raiders fan base embraces that role as a way of life , and they know the game and speak it at a high level.
So let’s dig into what you folks are looking for.
Well, we have to get the running game going. To keep that's the biggest opportunity we have.
Mike, getting the run game going is a great point, but when teams sell out to stop it, it's still important to keep running it to keep the defense honest.
While I certainly have a ton of respect for the Patriots' defense, they are not as good as the Chiefs. The Jaguars ran for 137 yards in week three, and on average, they are giving up 103 per game.
No team, I repeat, NO TEAM, they have faced in 2026 has as much talent at RB as the Raiders, and I expect two key adjustments for the Raiders on Sunday.
That said, if the Raiders run for over 125 yards, I believe they will win this game. If Mike Vrabel and the Patriots choose to do an all-out job of stopping the run, I fully expect the Raiders to punish them through the air.
Blowout to shut these critics up
Andres, I love your name. My nephew shares that name. That said, the only critics of the Raiders I am seeing are Raider fans. Outside of Raider fans, and it's fair to say it is a small group, I am seeing nothing but love and respect for the Silver and Black.
This is, without question, a rebuilding year; I have told you since December that was the case, but with a win on Sunday, even I must shift the discussion to a playoff-contending team.
An upset win on Sunday would catapult this team into that echelon of teams rightfully and change the narrative right now.
Consistency and improvement. Continue to be competitive in the tough game(s) and improve in the run game(both sides on the ball)
This tweet is one of the many reasons I love the Raider Nation. No bloviating, just honest answers from people who know and understand the game.
This is a rebuilding year. The Raiders may very well win this weekend. If it were at Allegiant, I would predict a win. Still, Raiders fans are sensible and understand that even if they win and become an NFL Playoff team, they're still lean, have an abundance of youth, and lack enough players to be dangerous long-term in a Super Bowl run.
This fan base wants to see the team be consistent and improve. Even if the Raiders flip the switch and become an NFL playoff-caliber team with the win, the narrative will change, but the roster won’t.  They are still thin and young. Tweets like this separate Raiders fans from all others.
They are smart enough to celebrate the wins and also smart enough to think long-term. Great response; you earned a follow-back, even if you are a Wolverine. Go Green!
Staying healthy and no long term injuries.
James, I applaud another great response.
If this team gets an upset, and I think they very well might, a long-term injury, or even some short-term ones, would derail the winning, and losing valuable NFL Draft space would hurt. The problem with that is simple. This is the NFL. Injuries are expected and will come. There are just so many places on this roster where they can’t afford an injury and still expect to remain competitive.

title: One Simple Thing Stands Between Raiders Rebuild and NFL Playoffs
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) will head to New England on Friday to prepare for their Sunday matchup against the Patriots (2-2) in Boston.
In the Raiders' rebuild, there is no question that they are ahead of schedule in wins, but that doesn’t mean they’ve been perfect. They haven’t, and neither has any other NFL team.
The nature of the game is that the other side has players who are paid millions of dollars, and they have a say in your success or failure. I already gave you my winners and losers from last week; this is not the discussion today.
The iconic Green Bay Packers coach, Vince Lombardi, is credited with being the first football coach to tell the hard truth about this glorious game centered around a pigskin-covered oblong ellipsoid: "Football is a game of inches, and inches make the champion."
​Most people remember it from the awesome pregame speech by Al Pacino's character in the legendary movie "Any Given Sunday."
While Pacino said it in a pretend world, quoting Lombardi, who lived it in the real world, the Raiders are learning that to overachieve, they have to find those inches.
Matt Gay has been an exceptional kicker for the Raiders in 2026. On Saturday, he is credited with four made field goals, but he actually had five.
Kubiak took one of his successes off the board after a Chiefs penalty. This article is not directed towards debating Kubiak’s decision, but when the Raiders' subsequent play failed, it was a total of five drives that ended with only three points, or no points.
After the game in which the Raiders only lost by three points, QB Kirk Cousins said it best.
"I think there's a lot to build on. I felt like our defense did just a great job keeping us in the game. We kicked too many field goals, didn't score enough points but our defense's play allowed us to still have a lead, to still be in it for so much of the game, so it's just tough to not finish."
Cousins wasn’t attacking Gay, far from it. He was making it clear that the offense he leads can’t settle for field goals. In a points-driven league, the Raiders need touchdowns.
If any of those four successful field goals had been turned into touchdowns, those four points would have been the difference in a Raiders win, and us discussing today the Raiders being 4-0.
I am not a revisionist. I stand by my takes. As a football nerd, I love and respect how Kubiak is attacking. Cousins does as well, but for the Raiders to go from simply rebuilding to overachieving and becoming an NFL Playoff option, they have to find the end zone at a higher rate.
I agree with Cousins on this, who made it very clear.
"Klint [Kubiak] felt we needed to be aggressive, we needed to be attacking all game long. If you come in here trying to just hang around with a good football team, it may not pan out the way you want. Felt like we needed to attack, just wish there have been, by me, better execution at moments that would have given us that chance to come out on top."
If the Raiders get the upset on Sunday, and they are very capable of it, they have to find the inches. The Patriots are the reigning AFC representative in the Super Bowl, and the Silver and Black can make a definitive statement.
What is the statement? Rebuild or not, they are ahead of schedule, and the NFL Playoffs are now on the map.
If the Raiders find the inches on Sunday, they will have changed the season's narrative. If they don’t, this rebuild is still clearly on the right road.
The playoffs are made up of teams that find the inches. We will learn on Sunday if the Raiders are one of those teams.
I suspect they might be. We'll see if they can find the inches. I believe in Kubiak; the team does, and on Sunday, I think the nation will as well.

title: What Raiders Learned About Division Rivals in Week 4
full_text:
Despite losing to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Las Vegas Raiders proved they are legitimate playoff contenders this season.
While we learned a lot about the Raiders this past weekend, they also gained invaluable intel on the rest of the AFC West. Here's what the Silver and Black learned about the other three teams in the division.
The Chargers' season was already over, but somehow things have gotten even worse. In addition to losing to the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles also had several key players suffer significant injuries. Ladd McConkey aggravated a foot injury and is now considered week-to-week; Derwin James missed Sunday's game with a hamstring injury and is week-to-week; and Rashawn Slater suffered a high-ankle sprain.
Los Angeles has been the most disappointing team in the league this season after being heralded as a Super Bowl contender during the offseason. Hiring Mike McDaniel as the offensive coordinator has been an outright disaster. At this point, Chargers fans are fast-forwarding to the 2027 NFL Draft, hoping for a top-five pick.
Nix makes playing quarterback look even more difficult than it already is. Despite having one of the best offensive lines in the league, an offensive-minded head coach in Sean Payton, and adding Jaylen Waddle to the wide receiver corps, Denver is one of the worst offenses in the league.
Of Nix's 25 completions, 12 of them went to running backs, with RJ Harvey leading the team with 10 receptions for 68 yards. Excluding two halves, Denver's offense has been dormant, and the third-year quarterback is why. If Nix's struggles stretch all season long and prevent the Broncos from making the playoffs, the front office could consider drafting or signing a quarterback ahead of next season.
This has already been a sentiment shared by many, but Walker III was instrumental in Kansas City's 30-27 win over Las Vegas . Rob Leonard's defense was giving the Chiefs all they could handle. Throughout the third quarter, Kansas City struggled to move the ball. However, on the final play of the quarter, Walker III ripped off a 76-yard run, jumpstarting the offense.
The 5-foot-8, 211-pound running back would score two touchdowns in the fourth quarter, propelling the Chiefs to victory. After four weeks, Walker III leads the league in rushing with 537 yards. After what transpired last season, Kansas City spent up on Walker III, and it’s proving to be the most impactful acquisition of the offseason.

title: Raiders Game Review: Breaking Down Loss vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are no longer unbeaten, taken down by the now-undefeated Kansas City Chiefs at home, 30-27. It was a tough beat for a team that has surprised the NFL through the first four weeks of the season, but many seem to be higher on the Raiders despite the loss.
I spent some time after Sunday's game re-watching how things went down from an in-depth perspective, with more detail on the X's & O's. With that in mind, here are my key takeaways (and some extra notes on the side) from the Raiders' first downfall of the still-young 2026 campaign.
Re-watching the game from Sunday reminded me of prime Kirk Cousins , who was a good quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings after his time with the Washington Commanders. Cousins went 31 of 52 for 365 yards and two touchdown passes, continuing a hot start for the veteran passer.
The Chiefs did a great job in man coverage all game. Cousins did an excellent job finding answers against Kansas City defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, working to his check-downs, ID’ing pressure points, and testing all three levels of the field.
This is a much more aggressive, yet disciplined Cousins than I’m used to seeing, and his accuracy and arm arrogance were on full display, along with impressive mobility for someone who tore his Achilles a couple of years ago. If the 15th-year signal-caller can keep up this, Las Vegas could be in a strong position during this tough eight-game stretch.
I was wondering how Hezekiah Masses would handle the speed and explosiveness of the Chiefs' pass-catchers. The rookie fifth-round pick, currently in the top 20 amongst all defensive backs with a -6.4 coverage expected points added (EPA) per Next Gen Stats, looked impressive once more, as he has fully overtaken Darien Porter for the starting cornerback job.
Masses showcased his coverage versatility, handling man duties against the speed of Xavier Worthy, Cyrus Allen, and others in the lineup for the Chiefs, and Masses has displayed continued improvement in man technique, especially when asked to press the line of scrimmage. The kid has a knack for getting his hands on the football, which includes a PBU during Sunday’s game. Masses is only getting better with each snap and game he plays, and that should excite Raiders Nation.
Elite players perform in big moments, and Crosby’s presence was felt throughout this game. I don’t remember him not being in the backfield when attacking Chiefs tackles Khalil Benson and Jaylon Moore, and the five pressures he tallied felt like double.
As usual, Crosby dominated with an elite move set that features a mixture of power and finesse, showcasing his incredible all-around skill set as a pass rusher. Crosby was also dominant in the run game, acting as a force defender, squeezing gaps, setting the edge, and winning the point of attack. When Crosby wasn’t on the field, the Chiefs took advantage (see Kenneth Walker III’s 76-yard run in the second half), showing how costly any absence can be for the veteran defensive end.
It’s time to have a conversation: Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker may be one of the best linebacker duos in football through four games. The two have been spectacular under defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, and their roles (and health) have allowed the former Georgia Bulldogs teammates to play with supreme consistency.
Walker has lined up all over the front seven, mugging gaps, playing and setting the edge, rushing the passer, dropping into coverage— you name it. Dean has looked outstanding in his run fits, flowing to the ball carrier and getting off blocks.
1. There is an argument that Cody White is the Raiders' No. 2 wide receiver, as the special-teamer turned reliable target has continued to make big plays, including the leaping 27-yard catch in the fourth quarter with nine minutes to play. These reps get you on the field outside of special teams, and White has taken advantage.
2. Rough days for left tackle Kolton Miller and right guard Caleb Rogers , who struggled against the brute power and awesome talent of George Karlaftis and Chris Jones throughout the game. It wasn’t their best performance, especially with Rogers trying to prove he could be a better option than Jackson Powers-Johnson. Miller had a hard time anchoring against speed-to-power, which allowed the pocket to collapse multiple times.
3. Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer are, again, the best tight end duo in football. Both were excellent in the passing game, especially Mayer as a blocker when lined up in-line. Their respective deployments by Kubiak allow them to take full advantage of their skill sets, specifically Bowers as the quasi-No. 1 wideout on the roster.
4. Second-round rookie safety Treydan Stukes nearly had an interception early in the game, but his play was sound all around. His ability to attack downhill from depth, make stout stops in the alley, and close to the ball carrier is phenomenal. Outside of a couple of deep balls, Stukes' return was welcomed.
5. I loved watching head coach and offensive play-caller Klint Kubiak and Spagnuolo go blow for blow, countering each other every which way with their respective wins on either side of the ball. Two masters at their craft, making X’s & O’s people like me fawn over their genius abilities as offensive and defensive play-callers, respectively.

title: Raiders' Week 5 Depth Chart: Biggest Takeaways
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders look to bounce back from their Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs with a road win against the New England Patriots. Las Vegas plans to apply the lessons learned from their first loss of the season to next Sunday's matchup and beyond.
“I think everything you put in your bank of experiences, good and bad, you learn from it. I'll even mention to Fernando [Mendoza] sometimes; I'll be like, Hey, you see that there? Like, take note, because someday it's going to be you. And you're going to want to make sure you do that and not this, or vice versa,” Raiders veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins said after the game.
”So, no, it's just you're learning from every experience, and in this game, you learn that hey, just keep playing. Just keep playing. Tough times don't last. Tough people do. And as long as you protect the football, you know, play through the smoke. You give yourself a chance at the end of the game, and that's what happened today. And we just weren't able to capitalize."
Below is the Raiders' most updated depth chart heading into Week 5 and our analysis.
Analysis: It is not broke. So, do not fix it.
Analysis: It is clear that Jeanty is hurt. However, for as ineffective as he has been on the ground, he has been equally effective through the air. Last Sunday, Jeanty finished tied with the second-most receptions and tied for the third-most targets.
Teams are going all out to stop Jeanty out of the backfield, forcing Cousins to beat them. The Raiders' staff must keep finding ways to get their running backs going, one way or another.
Analysis: Nailor's injury on Sunday quickly put into perspective how thin the Raiders are at this position group.
Analysis: Tucker has been open on several occasions that he did not get the ball. This is bound to happen in any offense, but worth noting here. White continues to perform well on a weekly basis. The chip on his shoulder is an actual tool for Las Vegas' offense.
Analysis: Miller continues to play well overall.
Analysis: Burford is the glue between Las Vegas' top-tier left tackle and top-tier center.
Analysis: Great investment.
Analysis: Rogers still needs further development but is coming along.
Analysis: Glaze has played well this season, matching his undeniable durability.
Analysis: Last Sunday confirmed Las Vegas has one of the best groups of tight ends in the league.
Analysis: Crosby and Koonce will help lead a hungry defensive line.
Analysis: All three of these players make an impact weekly.
Analysis: Laulu being listed as inactive last week was a shock, but it was also a shock when Pegues was listed as inactive earlier this season. This is Las Vegas' deepest position group, which will sometimes force them to name one player inactive from this group.
Analysis: Johnson needs more playing time.
Analysis: Dean is one of the best linebackers in the league.
Analysis: Walker has been as advertised through four games.
Analysis: The Chiefs have targeted Stokes more than he has been targeted this season. Look for a bounce-back game.
Analysis: There were some plays from Sunday's game that Johnson would likely like to have back. However, he has been a solid addition overall.
Analysis: Las Vegas is glad to have Stukes back.
Analysis: Chinn is consistent.
Analysis: Cole makes punts fun to watch.
Analysis: Two consecutive weeks with costly fumbles for this unit. They have to figure it out , as this unit is literally determining entire games.
Analysis: Las Vegas' punt returns have been ineffective. Against the Chiefs, Las Vegas finished with four punt return yards. If you are curious why the Raiders dropped multiple players back on the Chiefs' fake punt, it was likely to help set up blocks to spark a dormant unit.
In this instance, the issue is not the returner.

title: Raiders' Film Room: The Play That Changed Week 4 Matchup vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are 3-1 after their Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Las Vegas entered the matchup looking to confirm where they stand among the league's best. It is still early, but after how close Las Vegas came to beating the Chiefs, it is fair to say Las Vegas might be one of those teams.
Still, Sunday's loss showed the difference between a more experienced staff and roster that have been through many more battles on the field together than their opponent. Kansas City's experience and the Raiders' inexperience kicked in several times, right up until the very end.
The Raiders played complementary football in their first three games, but failed to do so against the Chiefs. One side of the ball failed to hold up their end of the bargain until it was too late. Las Vegas' first loss does not fall solely on any one person's shoulders. It was a team loss.
Las Vegas' mistakes caught up with them, forcing a rushed final drive that fell short. Many believe the Raiders' frenzied final drive was the most costly sequence. Klint Kubiak took responsibility for the drive, and quarterback Kirk Cousins did shortly after, too.
“That's Klint [Kubiak]. He's always going to point the thumb at himself and how he can be better. I think there's a lot going on there. We were trying to get to the optimum play. Clock's running down. I really think in hindsight the mistake I made among hundreds of mistakes probably, but take the delay game, like just take the delay game,” Cousins said after the game.
“Who cares about five yards? We got to get in the right play, get to out of bounds. So I even look there and I say, I was trying to snap the ball to avoid the penalty. And you look and you say, we don't want to be in that position, but if we are, is a penalty better? These are all the things I'm going to probably not sleep tonight and ask myself."
As Cousins alluded to, the Raiders made plenty of mistakes against the Chiefs. Las Vegas' long list of self-inflicted mistakes set the Chiefs up to steal the win. The Raiders failed to score any points in the third quarter. They allowed a run for over 70 yards and registered several penalties.
The Raiders' defense failed to force a turnover, which is uncharacteristic for this year's defense. There is plenty of blame to go around for Las Vegas' loss, and collectively, they were too much for the Raiders to overcome. Still, one play was undoubtedly more costly than all of the others combined.
Las Vegas fielded a kickoff with less than two minutes left to go in the game while trailing by less than a touchdown. There was reason to believe the Raiders' offense could make a legitimate push down the field for a game-winning touchdown drive. However, receiver Dareke Young fumbled the ball.
Kansas City recovered and scored shortly after. There were plenty of mistakes before that one. However, that was the single-most damaging play on the day for Las Vegas. The Raiders still fought admirably, nearly pulling off the improbable comeback. Still, a loss is a loss.
The fumbled kickoff was a microcosm of how the Raiders' day went on Sunday against the Chiefs. Any time Las Vegas started to make its way back, a self-inflicted mistake set them back. After all of the mistakes the Raiders had made before the fumble, they still had a legitimate shot at winning the game.
Yet, the costly mistake of their own doing made it nearly impossible for the unit to actually make a comeback. Most would say that one play does not determine a game, even in this case. Still, giving the ball back to Patrick Mahomes while already playing from behind with time running out is not ideal.
Las Vegas' kickoff return team has fumbled the ball twice in the past two weeks. Considering the defense just allowed a score, there are few plays that are more of a waste than a kickoff return in which the returner fumbles the ball back to the other team.
The Raiders still have plenty to work on.

title: Hondo’s Weekly Raiders Report Card: What 'Shocked' NFL Execs
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) walked out of Allegiant Stadium on Sunday Night after their loss to fellow AFC West rival, the Kansas City Chiefs (3-1), disappointed but with something else.
They had tangible evidence that they can, and will, compete with everyone on their schedule. Despite mistakes, miscues, talent gaps, and youthful errors, the 2026 Raiders are better and will compete.
The Chiefs and the rest of the NFL know it, too.
Much more on that when we talk about the coaching.
I have already shared my winners and losers, but as we do each Tuesday, after analyzing the film and speaking with NFL executives, I'm offering you my weekly report card.
The Raiders scored enough points to win (27), gave up zero sacks, and saw Kirk Cousins throw for 365 yards. All that with a backup RG, no WR1, and their WR2 injured.
Kubiak said of Cousins, "I thought Kirk [Cousins] played excellent. I thought he played excellent. Gave us a chance to win the game."
Now, you have to be honest and acknowledge that the Raiders only rushed for 72 yards, but not crediting the Chiefs' defense that sold out to stop it would be unfair as well.
The Raiders' offense, despite terrific game planning and an attacking mindset, is still in development and far from finished.
Kubiak said of the run game, “I put it on myself. I got to do a lot better job of putting us in better position. We’ve got solid backs, we’ve got a solid offensive line. And myself and the coaching staff, there's plenty of things we can do better for our players."
That grade, given they just gave up 30 points, may be a shocker. But once you turn on the tape, you see a different story, or as Paul Harvey used to say, “The rest of the story.”
The Raiders defense held the perennial powerhouse Chiefs, led by the best QB and the reigning Super Bowl MVP running back, to those aforementioned 30 points, though several of them were aided by the Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes starting in great field position due to mistakes the defense had nothing to do with.
The Raiders went into the game with a game plan to try to contain Kenneth Walker. I said the goal was to keep Walker under 125 yards. They didn’t; he ran for 177, and the entire Chiefs RB room accumulated 189.
You can certainly credit the Chiefs' rushing attack as elite, but that can’t happen if you want to be competitive at any level of football. Kubiak diagnosed part of the issue.
“They targeted well. They had explosive runs, and there's plenty of problems in that game of us setting the edge, so that has to get better."
The Raiders made the best player in the NFL, Patrick Mahomes, look human, throwing for only 225 yards, but the balanced Chiefs attack told the truth. The Raiders are young and thin, so this rebuild is not complete.
Kubiak said of the terrific rookie CB Hezekiah Masses, "I think that Kansas City did a great job of attacking a lot of things on our defense. I think there's a lot of things he can learn from in that game, and it's not just him. It wasn't his best game, but we expect him to rebound."
In this rebuild, there are many reasons for long-term optimism, such as ILB Nakobe Dean. He is playing like an All-Pro, and despite the loss, his impact can’t be ignored by the media, fans, or even his head coach. Kubiak praised his presence on this team.
"I think that Kansas City did a great job of attacking a lot of things on our defense. I think there's a lot of things he can learn from in that game, and it's not just him. It wasn't his best game, but we expect him to rebound."
That grade is hard to give when you look at K Matt Gay, who went 4/4 on field goals, made his extra point, and P AJ Cole was sensational. But Dareke Young's fumble essentially cost the Raiders the game.
The Raiders also chose to kick the ball out of the end zone at one point. An interesting decision that Kubiak addressed by saying, "Yeah, that was mine and Joe [DeCamillis]'s decision. Didn't work out."
Another play was a successful fake punt on the Chiefs' first drive. Although it resulted in zero points because the defense held them, it was still successful, and again Kubiak didn’t shrink when addressing it: "It's a play that we want back, a call that we want back, and it was a poor call."
Unless you hate the Raiders or hate Klint Kubiak, it is hard to give an honest assessment below a B when you realize the masterful job Kubiak and his entire staff have done building this team.
We know they are rebuilding, we know they are young, and thin at multiple positions.
That is why one NFL executive I spoke to this morning offered me a shocking observation.
“I think what Klint has done with that team, this fast is shocking. No joke, I'm shocked. They went toe-to-toe with what most people in this league think is a Super Bowl squad. But, I was talking to a GM yesterday [Monday] from another team who said it best when we were discussing the Raiders.”
The NFL executive expounded, “He told me, ‘Did you see those guys? Used to be able to look over and see that they thought it was over. When the Raiders we[re] down 11 after the fumbled kick late in the fourth and they were down 30-19 you would have always seen the Raiders give up. Quit. They looked mad, f---ing pissed. They thought they were going to win. F—k, I thought they were gone win.’ He was right, I saw it, that is all Klint.”
The effort from @Raiders CB Taron Johnson to chase down Kenneth Walker III and save a touchdown. pic.twitter.com/5pAFzMptn7
He added, "You saw it week one with [Cody] White's rundown on special teams to catch the guy, and you saw it on Sunday with Taron [Johnson] running down K9 [Kenneth Walker III] those are two news guys, that are all Maxx Crosby like total effort."
You can question Kubiak taking points off the board; I don’t. Not because Madden’s philosophy of never doing it is wrong, but because he is trying to instill the new Raider way, which means going back to the old identity: they are going to attack you.
Kubiak knows the Raiders are playing with house money, and he didn’t do that for you. He did it for his team. He spoke to his team, and his message was clear: always attack.
Kubiak addressed the mentality of this team: “They're disappointed, and they're a very mature group that wants to win. So, we're fixing the corrections. We're trying to make ourselves better. Whether we win or whether we lose, we're telling each other the truth and just seeing what we can do to be a better team moving forward."
The stadium was plenty red, but from a noise standpoint, it was a Raiders home crowd. The first since they moved to Las Vegas and have played the Chiefs at home.
From the outside tailgating to the familiar inside chants of "RRRAAAIIIDDDEEERRRSSS," Raider Nation did their job.
Once again, the fan base that sees being a Raiders fan as a way of life demonstrated it and gave their team a major advantage.
Kubiak doesn’t sugarcoat anything with this team. He is blunt, direct, and honest. There are plenty of reasons to be excited if you are a Raider fan, and plenty of reasons for the players on a young, thin team to see that they left a lot of meat on the proverbial bone in Sunday’s loss.
Kubiak has made some decisions this year that he won't make in 2028. He will have a complete team then. He doesn't right now. He has to take risks, risks that Reid doesn't, like the fake punt on the Chiefs' first drive. Kubiak is acting like Reid because he knows where the Raiders are going, and he isn't trying to be popular; he's trying to win.
Kubiak discussed his blunt evaluation style and how it affects his team.
“I just think that's the easiest way. Here's the tape. Here's what we got right. Here's what we got wrong. Here's where we're not correct as coaches. Here's where we didn't make the play as a player. And if we can just put it in front of those guys and everyone sees it, and as a team we can learn from it and get better, then we're going the right direction."

title: Key Improvements Raiders Must Focus on After Week 4
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders gave the Kansas City Chiefs all they could handle on Sunday, yet, as they often seem to do, the Chiefs found a way to win. After a 3-0 start, Sunday's loss reminded everyone how quickly things can change in the National Football League.
Yet Sunday's loss to the Chiefs was still productive in several ways. Not only did the loss confirm where the Raiders have improved the most, but it also confirmed that the Raiders can compete with any team in the league, whether they make mistakes or not.
The Raiders' Week 4 matchup against the Chiefs preceded several upcoming matchups that will likely test Las Vegas just as much. A loss is a loss, but Las Vegas has reason to believe in the progress they have made as they prepare to face some of the league's top teams.
Still, before Las Vegas can prepare for the New England Patriots, Buffalo Bills, and Los Angeles Rams, head coach Klint Kubiak knows it will be vital for both the coaches and players to be honest with themselves and each other to address the many things they need to fix moving forward.
"We just got done meeting with them. They're disappointed, and they're a very mature group that wants to win. So, we're fixing the corrections. We're trying to make ourselves better. Whether we win or whether we lose, we're telling each other the truth and just seeing what we can do to be a better team moving forward.”
“I just think that's the easiest way. Here's the tape. Here's what we got right. Here's what we got wrong. Here's where we're not correct as coaches. Here's where we didn't make the play as a player. And if we can just put it in front of those guys and everyone sees it, and as a team we can learn from it and get better, then we're going the right direction."
The Raiders struggled to run the ball again on Sunday, finishing with fewer than 80 rushing yards. This issue has plagued them for several seasons. This season, Las Vegas' lack of a consistent vertical threat seems to have given defenses the luxury of focusing on stopping the run.
Until Sunday, the Raiders' coaching staff had found ways to compensate for the lack of a ground game. However, injuries to Jackson Powers-Johnson and Jack Bech weakened the unit on Sunday and allowed the Chiefs to focus even more on the run, which they did.
Las Vegas also must find a way to eliminate turnovers altogether. Or, at the very least, not do so in critical moments that back their defense against the wall. In nearly every game this season, the Raiders have turned the ball over in their own territory.
Not all turnovers are the same, as the past two weeks have confirmed for the Raiders. Las Vegas overcame its turnovers in previous weeks, but none came at as bad a time as their turnover against the Chiefs did on Sunday. Still, eliminating turnovers altogether is ideal.
Kubiak's coaching staff also can't fix everything on their own. Most notably, for this young Raiders team, Kubiak and his coaching staff cannot provide playing experience for the players. Games like their loss to the Chiefs and their upcoming games will be valuable experience.
Everyone knew Las Vegas would depend on a large number of younger players in 2026 and beyond. However, youth and inexperience bring mistakes, which was the story of the game for the Raiders on Sunday. With 13 games remaining, the Raiders are in a good position.
Las Vegas will go through its fair share of growing pains, but they are headed in the right direction. The Raiders will approach their Week 5 matchup against the Patriots much like they have approached every other game this season. However, they will do so after fine-tuning things.
Kubiak is only four games into what will likely be a long tenure in the desert. Las Vegas' front office got the head coach they wanted in Kubiak. As the Raiders continue building out their roster, both the players and the coaches have plenty to learn and fix.

title: How Raiders Can Prove Themselves Over Daunting Upcoming Stretch
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders lost their first game of the season on Sunday to the Kansas City Chiefs, 30-27. However, you wouldn’t think they did, based on the reactions from national pundits to the game.
Many have come away impressed with the Raiders' start to the season, even as they came down to the wire against the Chiefs in a game where they led multiple times. ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky called Las Vegas a “legit playoff team.” Yet we’re four games into the regular season, and the toughest stretch of football for the Raiders is set to begin.
. @danorlovsky7 sees the Raiders as a “legit” playoff team. These are the reasons why ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/XTbHFvTYYu
No doubt the Raiders have been impressive, and their play has suggested a much better team that should have higher expectations each week. We have to remember, though, that Las Vegas is still in a rebuild year despite a defense and Kirk Cousins playing great football. They showed on Sunday that they still have work to do.
Things won’t be easy going forward; head coach Klint Kubiak and the rest of his team will have to prove themselves over the next eight weeks against the following: at New England Patriots, vs. Buffalo Bills, vs. Los Angeles Rams, at New York Jets, at San Francisco 49ers, vs. Seattle Seahawks, at Denver Broncos, and at Cleveland Browns.
All eight opponents were either playoff teams last season or are proving to be much better than expected (Cleveland). This is a gauntlet, one no team would want to have on their schedule, but that is what happens when you have to play in the AFC West and play the NFC West in the same season.
For Kubiak, this is another opportunity to show what the 2026 Raiders are all about.
When you play the opponents Las Vegas is set to face, you’ll need to have a defense like the one they have now. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has single-handedly kept the Raiders in games this season and even won them on a couple of occasions. Furthermore, Kirk Cousins has been turning back the clock, with the real possibility that No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza never sees the field as a rookie.
That is now, and what could be later may not be pretty. Yet the next eight weeks give the Raiders a chance to see who they are, know exactly what they need to continue building within their organization, and re-evaluate when the bye week rolls around.

title: Raiders' Rookie, Sophomore Power Rankings Following Loss to Chiefs
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders entered this season with big plans for several of the young players they added to their roster in the past two drafts. Four games into the season, with a 3-1 record, it's clear that the plan is in full swing, and the Raiders are ready to let those players learn quickly.
Las Vegas' surprise start to the season has bought them more room for mistakes from a young roster. Still, a tough loss against the Kansas City Chiefs put those mistakes on full display. The vast experience of Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes, and others was too much for Las Vegas .
Las Vegas' 3-1 start to the season was more than they could have realistically asked for entering the season. The Raiders will now take what they learned from a tough loss to possibly the best team in the league and move on to their upcoming road matchup against the New England Patriots.
However, before Las Vegas can worry about the Patriots, it must address what it needs to fix as a team. Veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins shared his thoughts on how a young roster like the Raiders' can make the most of the time they have before game day.
“All I know is to have good habits and to watch and make sure my teammates have great habits, and if we do that, I believe process over outcome that you're going to be pleased with the outcome more often than not,” Cousins said following the game.
“So, the way we work Monday through Saturday is really what I pay attention to, and then I believe that if you're doing the right things there, Sunday you're going to give yourself the best chance. I think we've had good habits, and we just have to keep growing together. Just as I'm talking, I'm just thinking of a play here or play there that we should have been able to execute, and maybe it would have been the difference. That's pro football. It's why it's a great league, but it's also why it'll beat you up."
The Raiders are leaning into putting a lot of responsibility on their young players. The hope is that the early experience will pay off for Las Vegas down the road.
Below are Las Vegas' most impactful rookies and second-year players from Sunday afternoon.
The rookie cornerback faced Chris Olave in Week 3 and a Chiefs offense that was determined to bring him back down to earth after a strong start to his career in the first three games. It was a tough outing for Masses, but he still did well overall.
Masses should expect the Raiders' remaining opponents to target him moving forward after his performance on Sunday. Luckily, Las Vegas has one of the best pass rushes in the league that Masses will continue to benefit from playing behind.
Stukes' return to the field against Kansas City confirmed there is a difference between him and Isaiah Pola-Mao. The Raiders must keep developing Stukes while also figuring out their plans if he's unavailable to play again later this season.
Jeanty's stock rarely ever goes down, as he rarely has a bad game because of his own doing. Right now, it is clear he is far from healthy, and it is affecting his game. Still, Las Vegas needs Jeanty on the field, as Jeanty at 75% is still their best running back.
Jeanty is a foundational part of Las Vegas' rebuild. The cuts and moves Jeanty is known for require healthy ankles. Jeanty's injury shortly before the season started is impacting their ground game right now.
Rogers filled in for Jackson Powers-Johnson on Sunday. Like everyone else on the field, Rogers shone in some areas but still needs improvement in others. Still, the Raiders' offensive line allowed zero sacks on over 50 passes from Cousins.
Rogers needs more work, but Sunday confirmed he can hold his own on an offensive line like Las Vegas has right now. Still, Rogers must improve, as there were a few weaknesses displayed.
