title: Vikings' Snap Count vs. Dolphins: Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 4
full_text:
The Vikings defeated the Dolphins on Sunday to remain one of three undefeated teams in the NFL. The 15-10 victory at U.S. Bank Stadium was far from pretty , but the Purple and Gold figured out a way to get the win , and that's all that matters.
A lot of credit for the win has to go to how head coach Kevin O'Connell used the players he had available for the game.  The snap counts for Week 4 were interesting since they might not have worked out the way many thought they would.
Let's take a look at two winners, two losers, and one player who saw their role with the Vikings change against the Dolphins.
There wasn't a bigger winner on Sunday than Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. The starting tight end played 65 of a possible 78 offensive snaps against the Dolphins and was the most efficient offensive player by far.
Hockenson led Minnesota in receiving by catching all 13 targets thrown his way and gaining 119 yards on the day. With his backup, Josh Oliver, on injured reserve with a torn biceps muscle, Hockenson saw his role expand significantly .
When talking about tight ends who should have gotten some playing time with Oliver out, Gavin Bartholomew should have been in line to be Hockenson's direct backup in Week 4. However, he only played 17 offensive snaps and 15 special teams snaps against Miami.
Bartholomew caught one pass for four yards on his solo target, but Minnesota couldn't take Hockenson off the field since he was the player who was having the most success through the air on Sunday.
In his first game since being signed to the 53-man roster , edge rusher Kyle Van Noy played 21 of 39 possible defensive snaps to not only give the Vikings a strong pursuit of Dolphins QB Malik Willis, but also give Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel some rest.
Van Noy only had two tackles on the day, but they were both solo efforts for a loss. He also finished with solid Pro Football Focus grades for tackling (72.4) and run defense (73.7) . If he can continue playing well in his limited role, his value for Minnesota will continue to increase with every passing week that he suits up.
The Vikings couldn't have game-planned for Aaron Jones Sr. to play 57 offensive snaps this week. That kind of workload on a player who is working through a knee injury at 31 years old—with his extensive injury history—is scary.
Jones did turn his 24 touches into 128 total yards between his rushing and receiving. It felt like the only way Minnesota could move the chains was if Jones and Hockenson were on the field to spark the offense.
While Bartholomew was supposed to be the tight end to get extra work with Oliver on injured reserve, the Vikings turned to offensive lineman Caleb Tiernan instead. The rookie offensive tackle was called upon to be an extra lineman against Miami.
It might not sound like a lot, but Tiernan's eight offensive snaps and five special teams snaps are a massive improvement from a player who had been inactive all season up to this point. It's nice to see the Vikings find a role for him, especially if starting left tackle Christian Darrisaw misses time .

title: Harmon's Longship Week 4: Key Takeaways as Vikings Start 4-0 After Successful Dolphin Hunt
full_text:
MINNEAPOLIS, MN — Say what you will about how they’ve gotten here, but the Vikings are a perfect 4-0 to start their 2026 campaign. They emerged victorious once again on Sunday after defending their home shores from a feisty pack of Dolphins in a 15-10 victory.
Despite their own mistakes and continued inconsistency on offense, the Vikings have yet to taste defeat this season.
If you were looking for a convincing victory against a winless team from Miami, Sunday’s game was certainly anything but. Luckily, the win column doesn't care how you got there.
Here’s what happened and what’s on the horizon as the Vikings' longship sails on.
Would Sunday be the game that finally proved Kyler Murray’s fit with head coach Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings’ offense? Not exactly, but potential started to flash late.
The first half was especially dull as Murray and the passing game finished with only 89 net passing yards at halftime. It should also be noted that a Vikings offense missing Justin Jefferson shouldn't be expected to reach its peak. Left guard Donovan Jackson also left the game with a season-ending knee injury .
Star left tackle Christian Darrisaw also left the game temporarily with what was labeled a neck injury, but later showed concussion-like symptoms (h/t: ESPN’ s Kevin Seifert)
The offense eventually found more flow as the game went on. Aaron Jones Sr. had another gritty performance, finishing with 94 rushing yards on 20 carries for a whopping 4.7 yards per attempt. Murray would also start to flash signs of momentum as O’Connell found ways to set him up for success by moving the pocket and providing simple completions, many of which went the way of tight end T.J. Hockenson.
The former Hawkeye finished with 119 receiving yards and a “would-be” touchdown , choosing to go down short of the end zone to let the offense kneel out the clock. Murray flashed his ability to hit tight-window throws as the game went on, a trend the team will need to see continue (h\t: NFL)
Vikings dial up a big play on second down! MIAvsMIN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MHWiSLbGmk
The Vikings' defense had another dominant day, holding the lowly Dolphins to 198 yards of total offense. With extra motivation for defensive coordinator Brian Flores against his former team, the performance wasn’t quite as flashy as some expected, but Miami’s offense couldn’t catch its breath.
Anytime a defense holds its opponent to under 200 yards, it's an unbelievable accomplishment, regardless of who they are matched up against. Dallas Turner had yet another impressive day with two sacks and a forced fumble. His emergence as a true defensive weapon at only 23 years old should have Vikings fans ecstatic.
Then, there’s the man who may single-handedly save the Vikings’ scoring efforts this season: Will “The Thrill” Reichard. Reichard had another stellar performance yesterday, going 5-for-5 and accounting for all 15 points Minnesota scored. Through four weeks, Reichard has accounted for more points on his own than the entire Vikings offense combined.
Total points this season- Vikings offense: 36 Will Reichard: 42 📸: Alli Rusco pic.twitter.com/LwSYmjSdxN
The Minnesota Vikings offense will eventually need to start scoring touchdowns if their undefeated streak is going to continue. It’s hard to tell exactly where the issues lie. While Murray often looks uncomfortable in O’Connell’s base offense, it's ultimately on the head coach to set his hand-picked QB up for success.
O’Connell desperately needs to help Murray find the rhythm he flashed late in the game. Shotgun formation, rollouts, and play action all seem more natural for Murray than traditional under-center dropbacks. Flores’s defense and Matt Daniels’s special teams unit are simply playing too well for the offense not to step it up, and quickly.
Myles Price for 33 yards. pic.twitter.com/0TQ0JxCnON
The Vikings continue to stand in sole possession of first place in the NFC North.
The Bears have notched two victories with two different backup QBs in the last seven days. Caleb Williams’ eventual return will almost certainly supercharge the Ben Johnson-schemed offense. They sit at 3-1, with the Vikings representing their single loss so far. The Packers left Tampa with a close 17-14 win over the Bucs to reach 2-2, but offensive inconsistencies and further defensive injuries could cost them. The Lions fell to 2-2 after losing to Bryce Young and the Panthers on Sunday night football, in a game where their defense allowed 445 yards of total offense.
The Vikings are one of three remaining undefeated teams after the Chiefs beat the previously loss-less Raiders 30-27 in Vegas. The Niners are the only other undefeated team in the NFC after defeating the Broncos 24-14. Their matchup with the Vikings in Mexico City on Nov. 22 is quickly becoming one of the season's more intriguing games.
Minnesota's record says they're among the NFL’s elite, even if the on-field product often indicates otherwise.
Next up for the Vikings on their list of attempted conquests is a trip to  New Orleans to battle the Saints at the Caesars Superdome. Luckily, the Vikings have never had a game go against them on that field (cue 2009 NFC Championship flashbacks).
But first, the 1-2 Saints will host the Falcons for Monday Night Football. Their offense has been largely underrated, totaling the ninth-most yards per game in the league through their three games. Tyler Shough and the passing game’s 281.3 yards per game are the fourth-highest average in the league.
The Saints' passing defense has been largely middle of the pack in yards allowed so far, meaning Kyler Murray and his weapons should have a chance to find a spark, especially if Justin Jefferson’s ankle injury is cleared for his return against his hometown team. The Saints are unlikely to go down easily, especially at home, but the Vikings should be able to remain undefeated if the offense can actually move the ball.

title: Patriots Week 4 Snap Count Analysis: Explaining Heavier Personnels
full_text:
The New England Patriots are back in the win column, and it took a lot of players that you might not have expected. The 29-26 upset against the Buffalo Bills was one of the team's best wins in several seasons — and gets the Patriots right back into the conversation of being a solid football team.
"It gets us back in the race, and our guys worked extremely hard this week," Mike Vrabel said postgame , "and we knew that it was going to be a battle."
Here's a snapshot at all the snaps the Patriots played on Sunday, and what we can learn from them.
OG Alijah Vera-Tucker (76, 100%), OG Ben Brown (76, 100%), OT Will Campbell (76, 100%), OT Morgan Moses (76, 100%), QB Drake Maye (76, 100%), C Jared Wilson (76, 100%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (50, 66%), WR Romeo Doubs (49, 64%), TE Hunter Henry (49, 64%), TE Eli Raridon (44, 58%), WR DeMario Douglas (35, 46%), WR Efton Chism III (34, 45%), WR Mack Hollins (31, 41%), RB TreVeyon Henderson (28, 37%), OT Caleb Lomu (20, 26%), WR Kyle Williams (19, 25%), FB Reggie Gilliam (17, 22%), TE Cameron Latu (2, 3%), RB Corey Kiner (2, 3%)
The Patriots ran 76 offensive plays this week, the most all year (they ran 71 against the Seattle Seahawks in the season opener). They also used a lot of new formations to help try and get something going. Part of that was having rookie offensive tackle Caleb Lomu start the game as a jumbo tight end. He played 20 snaps, and took some of those from the backfield.
One thing that also jumps out? The discrepancy in snaps between Efton Chism III (34) and Kyle Williams (19). Both second-year receivers have started to trend in opposite directions, with the undrafted one soaring after his game-winning touchdown while the third rounder remains limited.
CB Marcus Jones (59, 100%), LB Christian Elliss (59, 100%), CB Carlton Davis (59, 100%), S Craig Woodson (59, 100%), S Kevin Byard (59, 100%), LB Robert Spillane (59, 100%), DT Milton Williams (46, 78%), EDGE Dre'Mont Jones (44, 75%), EDGE Elijah Ponder (41, 69%), CB Charles Woods (35, 59%), DT Cory Durden (34, 58%), EDGE Gabe Jacas (25, 42%), DT Leonard Taylor III (20, 34%), DT DaQuan Jones (18. 31%), DT Joshua Farmer (16, 27%), LB Darius Muasau (8, 14%), CB Kindle Vildor (8, 14%)
The Patriots didn't run any three-safety looks against the Bills, opting to go more heavy on the front end. Part of that was to shut down all the explosive plays that Josh Allen could make at quarterback. Plus, getting Craig Woodson back after a one-game absence gave the Patriots their usual safety pair back together.
Robert Spillane — in his second year as a Patriots captain — continues to be an iron man. He's played every single snap this season for New England's defense, and Sunday was more of the same. Spillane finished with eight tackles and a forced fumble.
LB Darius Musaua (23, 88%), LB Namdi Obiazor (23, 88%), S Mike Brown (23, 88%), TE Cameron Latu (22, 85%), LB Erick Hunter (19, 73%), CB Karon Prunty (18, 69%), EDGE Elijah Ponder (17, 65%), EDGE Jose Ramirez (15, 58%), EDGE Gabe Jacas (14, 54%), CB Jaylen Reed (13, 50%), CB Charles Woods (12, 46%), RB Corey Kiner (8, 31%), K Andy Borregales (8, 31%), LS Julian Ashby (7, 27%), P Mitch Wishnowsky (7, 27%), DT Cory Durden (7, 27%), WR Kyle William (6, 23%), CB Kindle Vildor (5, 19%), WR Efton Chism III (4, 15%), CB Marcus Jones (4, 15%), DT Milton Williams (4, 15%), DT DaQuan Jones (4, 15%), OT Caleb Lomu (3, 12%), OG Alijah Vera-Tucker (3, 12%), OG Ben Brown (3, 12%), OT Will Campbell (3, 12%), DT Leonard Taylor III (3, 12%), OT Walter Rouse (3, 12%), TE Eli Raridon (2, 8%), FB Reggie Gilliam (2, 8%), LB Christian Elliss (1, 4%)
The Patriots have consistently gotten a lot of special team snaps out of their linebacker pair of Darius Muasau (who started on defense) and Namdi Obiazor . But they've also gotten plenty out of safety Mike Brown, who was elevated for a second-straight week off the practice squad.
Erick Hunter, an undrafted linebacker, played 19 snaps — and some of those coming at gunner . He had four tackles in what was a really good game for the rookie.

title: Most Important Patriots Postgame Quotes From Week 4 — And What They Mean Going Forward
full_text:
Stop me if you've heard this one before. An October win on the road in Buffalo jumpstarting a turnaround for the New England Patriots. It happened last year, and now this year's team is enjoyed the 29-26 upset win they pulled off on the Bills on Sunday . It took a lot of players up and down the roster for what might have been the best regular season win since Mike Vrabel took over as head coach .
"You have to believe that you’re the reason, whether you make 1 play or 15 plays, that you’re the reason that we’re going to win," Vrabel said postgame.
Here are some of the biggest quotes from after the win, and what they mean for the Patriots moving forward into Week 5 and beyond.
It wasn't a pretty game by any stretch of the imagination (two turnovers from Drake Maye, plus a few defensive breakdowns didn't help), but the Patriots used a one-handed touchdown catch from Efton Chism to pull back in front late. It was one of those games that winning football teams seem to always play in .
Mike Vrabel on what this win does for the Patriots: "It gets us back in the race, and our guys worked extremely hard this week, and we knew that it was going to be a battle. I mean, Josh (Allen) is unbelievable, you know what I mean? But I felt like Drake went toe-to-toe with him. We had a couple turnovers that we have to be able to continue to eliminate, but we knew that if we took advantage of some opportunities, we’d get some too."
Drake Maye on his mindset after getting back to .500: "You’re 1-2, we come to this game and just earned a second win, 2-2. You can’t hang your hat. This is the league, and I know I have to play better and still left some stuff out there today. So, we have to build on it and know that this isn’t a point in the season where you can end the season on this. You have to get back and keep going."
Efton Chism III on his game-winning touchdown catch: "Shoot, when I'm out there and the ball's in the air, I kind of black out. I'm kind of in that little flow state. I saw it in the air and Drake (Maye) gave me an opportunity and you got to come down with those opportunities."
Rhamondre Stevenson on the running game: "It felt good. I felt like the linemen were moving the d-tackles and things like that, giving us entry points to run through. I felt like we took care of the ball as a running back group today and you know, ran hard."
Charles Woods on Craig Woodson's interception to seal it: "That's our mentality. We always preach next man up, so (I'm) very excited. And Craig coming back, first game (back from a shoulder injury), so I'm very happy for him.
The Bills came into this matchup leading the AFC East at 3-0. Allen looked like the potential MVP, while their running game also was among the league's best. It was set up perfectly for another win for the Bills.
Instead, the Patriots came into Highmark Stadium (the new one) and gave the Bills their first loss in their brand-new stadium. Everything seemed to be trending upwards, from Maye's three touchdown passes to the running game getting better.
There were a few breakdowns along the offensive line — Will Campbell allowed six pressures off the left side — but Maye's ability to evade pressure helped limit the damage . Those were the plays that New England was missing in the first three games of the season, and they suddenly re-appeared.
Limiting the Bills offense was a top priority, and the Patriots did just that. Allen, a mobile quarterback, ran for just four yards on five carries, while Dalton Kincaid was held to just one catch. The Patriots defense carried their weight to begin the year, and they haven't slowed down much.
If the Patriots are able to use this performance and carry it into a stretch of relatively weaker teams (Las Vegas Raiders, New York Jets), a winning streak could start forming.

title: Patriots Roster Moves: Rookie CB Signed, Edge Rusher Released
full_text:
The New England Patriots, enjoying their second of two-straight off days after Sunday's win over the Buffalo Bills , made a trio of moves on the back-end of their roster.
The team announced Tuesday that they released edge rusher Jose Ramirez from the 53-man roster, signed rookie cornerback Al'Zillion Hamilton to the practice squad and released rookie OT Da'Metrius Weatherspoon from the practice squad.
Releasing the 27-year-old Ramirez, who had signed to the active roster after a short stint on the practice squad , now opens up another spot on the roster. He was promoted to the roster ahead of the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, recording one special teams tackle.
"Been a really good practice player for us," Mike Vrabel said about Ramirez. "I think he's improved since the time he's been here, multiple times being recognized. He's taken the reps that we talk about being on the show team and using those to his advantage. So, whether they'll be an opportunity, we'll see, for him to be able to help us this week when we get down to the 48-man roster."
Ramirez was drafted back in 2023 by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before having stops with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats of the Canadian Football League and the Philadelphia Eagles.
With two open roster spots, that likely leaves room for offensive tackle Marcus Bryant (injured reserve) and safety Brenden Schooler (non-football injury list), who become eligible to join the 53-man roster after missing the beginning of the season.
The Patriots brought in Hamilton, who began his NFL career as a member of the Los Angeles Rams. The 24-year-old cornerback played in 54 games during his college career with Fresno State and recorded eight interceptions. He was named to the All-Mountain West Second Team last fall, and joins fellow cornerback Kindle Vildor on the practice squad .
Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) and Channing Canada (hamstring) missed the Bills game this weekend, highlighting the need for depth on the roster for the secondary.
The rookie Weatherspoon arrived in New England last week ahead of their matchup against the Bills. Weatherspoon, who played for Howard and Syracuse in college, signed with the Bills as an undrafted free agent in the spring.
Part of why the team brought him in was likely because of his connection with the Bills offense, as well as a need for offensive line depth. Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten were both placed on IR after lower-body injuries, leading to the acquisitions of Weatherspoon and veteran Matt Pryor.
The Patriots return to the practice field Wednesday to prepare for their Week 5 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders.

title: Ethan Hurwitz: Patriots Remain Ultra-Confident in Drake Maye Following Comeback
full_text:
FOXBORO — It was a shaky three weeks for Drake Maye . Plenty was said — on television, on the radio, on this website from yours truly — about the New England Patriots quarterback's less-than-idea start to the season, and how it might be time to be a tad worried.
But the NFL is a "what have you done for me lately" league, and Maye's recent performance against the Buffalo Bills (22-for-37, 269 passing yards, three touchdowns) has the Patriots right back into the thick of things in the AFC Eas t.
And while pundits off the field might have wavered in their confidence in Maye, his teammates have kept the faith. The upset in Buffalo, which was capped off by a perfect, 23-yard touchdown throw to Efton Chism III late in the fourth , is the reason why the Patriots never got concerned with their captain.
"Everybody in here believes in him and knows what he can do and bring to this team," offensive tackle Will Campbell said about Maye, via MassLive's Mark Daniels . "And I think it showed."
It still wasn't the greatest showing from Maye, who turned the ball over two more times. He fumbled it after the pocket collapsed around him, and also threw a funky interception at the end of the first half (which led to a Bills field goal).
And yet, Maye didn't wilt away. In the past games, especially in losses to Seattle and Jacksonville , he looked shaken, the confidence just not all the way there. This week? He looked like a changed man. Maye operated the huddle and line of scrimmage with conviction, and the results showed for themselves.
"I think that really has to exemplify what we want to be, who we want to be as a team and who we want to be as an organization," Mike Vrabel said Monday. "There's going to be things that happen, things that we don't plan for. But certainly, the play isn't over, the game isn't over, and I think that really sums up everything that we want to do."
There's still work to be done. Maye has yet to reach the level he was at a season ago. But beating the undefeated Bills in their home stadium has to count for something more than just a victory. If he can help snap Maye out of his September funk, this will be the start of another fun season.
His teammates see the work that the quarterback has put in. So this outcome might not have been as surprising to the roster as it was to the rest of the outside world.
"I see Drake every single day and he freaking works his ass off," rookie linebacker Erick Hunter told Patriots On SI. "I'm most impressed by his poise. The media might look at it one way, but I walk into the locker room with this guy. I'm in the training room with this guy. I'm at practice with this guy. He talks to everyboyd in the locker room, he's a really good leader."
Now Maye just needs to lead this team onto a winning streak — just like a season ago.

title: Patriots Rookie LB Erick Hunter Shines in Surprise Special Teams Role
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots got some really impressive snaps out of an unsung rookie linebacker in Sunday's win over the Buffalo Bills .
Erick Hunter, an undrafted linebacker who the team signed on Sept. 1 , was used as a gunner on the punt unit. The 6-foot-3, 224-pound rookie, who played his college games for Morgan State, shined. He recorded four tackles, including a thundering hit on Bills returner Greg Dortch.
On Monday, Mike Vrabel praised the efforts of Hunter — and his strengths that led him to earning that spot.
"Thought he did fantastic. I thought Erick's really progressed every day since he's been here," Vrabel said. "I think (special teams coordinator) Jeremy (Springer) and (assistant special teams coach) Tom (Quinn) have done a fantastic job of working with him in our special teams, and he's trying to work with our defensive coaches. A lot of new things for Erick, and he's willing, he's got a really good length and he can run.
"We just figured, as we get guys that are down, we need bodies or DBs have to play or go down, why don't we give Erick a try? He didn't disappoint."
It's unusual for a linebacker, especially one of Hunter's stature, to split out wide to cover punts. The Patriots have historically used slimmer players to fill that need, including Charles Woods and Brenden Schooler ( who made the trip to Buffalo and should be activated off the non-football injury list in the coming weeks).
Instead, it was Hunter. He shined, and was busy answering congratulatory texts from his father in the locker room after the win.
"I take a lot of pride in any role that I'm given the opportunity to have," Hunter told Patriots On SI after the Patriots won 29-26. "So (the) biggest thing is when you get that opportunity, just make sure you make the most of it and go onto the next one."
Hunter's college career spanned five seasons, where he tallied 298 tackles (second-most in program histort) and was named an HBCU All-American. He signed with the Detroit Lions as an undrafted free agent, but was released this summer. Now, he's enjoying the journey with New England.
And even though he hasn't had that large of a role to begin his tenure with the Patriots, Hunter knows the twists and turns are part of the game.
"At the end of the day, it's football," he said. "It's ups and downs in this. (A) momentum shift is what we needed at the moment, and coach has been talking about being the answer all week. I feel like every guy on this team, every guy on this roster, came out this week."
The Patriots have a deep linebacking core with Robert Spillane, Christian Elliss and Darius Musaua. For now, Hunter has taken just three defensive snaps and hasn't carved out a very large role in that department.
But until that time comes, the 23-year-old is making his name known on special teams.

title: Patriots Don't Have Immediate Injury Update on WR Mack Hollins
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots, already down A.J. Brown for at least one more week, suffered another hit to their wide receiver room.
Mack Hollins left Sunday's 29-26 comeback win over the Buffalo Bills with a calf injury. The veteran got banged up during one of the team's drives in the third quarter, and walked off the field. He would pace around on the sideline for a brief time before heading into the Patriots locker room with members of the medical staff.
On Monday morning, head coach Mike Vrabel was asked about Hollins' status and if where he stands health-wise as the team prepares for Week 5.
"I think we’ll probably know more here in a little bit," Vrabel said. "I don’t know if he’ll be able to practice here for a couple days, but again, I don’t have every detail.
"I’ll get in there with (head athletic trainer) Jim (Whalen) here afterwards and kind of see where we are, and then make sure we have guys that are ready to go, and everybody’s preparing as a starter, and we know the energy that Mack brings, and next guy has to be ready to go."
Hollins has stepped up to be the Patriots' top target since Week 1, and he caught three of four passes for 53 yards before leaving the game. Through four games, he has 20 targets, 15 receptions and 209 yards.
After Hollins went down, the Patriots leaned on Efton Chism III a lot more in the passing game. A close friend with Hollins, Chism grabbed two passes on the team's game-winning drive — including a one-handed, 23-yard touchdown to reclaim the lead .
Chism could be a player who gets a larger role without Hollins on the field. The Patriots could also look outside the organization for someone to fill that hole left by the 33-year-old. Currently, the Patriots have Chism, Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams on the active roster, and Cameron Dorner, Kyle Dixon an Chandler Brayboy on the practice squad.
Brown will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week as he works his way back from a high-ankle sprain suffered in the season opener.
"Sure. Anybody that can help us, we'll go explore in here shortly," Vrabel said when asked about potentially adding another receiver.
One name that's sure to draw attention? Tyreek Hill , who's reportedly been in conversations to sign with a team after a prolonged time on the open market. The former Super Bowl champion was released by the Miami Dolphins after a gruesome leg injury a season ago.
The Patriots could also kick the tires on Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars) or Marvin Harrision Jr. (Arizona Cardinals) via trade.
The Patriots are off both Monday and Tuesday, and will return to the practice field Wednesday for their home bout with the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders.

title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel Claps Back at Bills CB After Postgame Dig
full_text:
FOXBORO — Mike Vrabel , one day after the New England Patriots' 29-26 upset win of the Buffalo Bills , talked some smack after an opposing veteran made a comment postgame.
The Patriots walked out of Buffalo winners after Efton Chism III snared a one-handed touchdown in the final minute to give them the lead. Chism, who had just one touchdown to his name before that game, became the hero in Western New York.
It drew comments from Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, referring to Chism as an elevated practice squad player. Chism has never played on the practice squad in his two-year career, making the 53-man roster each season out of training camp.
That led Vrabel to make some funny remarks about the Bills defensive back's own career path.
"For a guy that’s been on eight teams in four years? I mean, I guess he knows the drill," Vrabel quipped on his weekly radio hit on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show.
Gardner-Johnson, however, has bounced around from team to team since arriving in the NFL in 2019. He finished with four tackles in what turned into the Bills' first loss of the season.
"We’re not getting into no bulletin board material," Gardner-Johnson said in the locker room. "An elevated guy made a helluva catch. Probably won’t hear from him again. Respectfully. I say that with a lot of confidence, because it’s like (Drake Maye) didn’t put his confidence in his best player. He would have thrown to (Romeo) Doubs or somebody, but they won the game.
The Patriots went onto the road to beat the Bills in an offensive showing that was a complete change from the previous weeks. Maye threw for three touchdowns in their second win of the season. Chism's touchdown helped give the Patriots a one-point lead, and a successful two-point conversion bumped it to three.
"Whatever, they didn’t do (expletive) better than us. We gotta play better. They can mark that, we’ll be back to see them again. So, they better have that same energy," Gardner-Johnson continued. “They put up what? Twenty-something points? They barely scored. They struggled all game. … A practice squad player made a helluva play. You do it again, he probably won’t make it again. Simple."
Chism had two catches in the win. Earlier in the game-winning drive, the 24-year-old caught a 19-yard pass that forced hi to leap into the air. It was a big showing from the young receiver, who might be in line for more targets in the coming weeks.
"Guys continue to take advantage of their opportunities," Vrabel said Monday to reporters. "(He) certainly did a lot of things well, and I know that he'll continue to do a lot of things well for us."
Gardner-Johnson and the Bills will travel to Gillette Stadium to face this same Patriots team in Week 13.

title: 5 Winners, 2 Losers from Patriots' Upset Win Over Bills: Young WR Saves The Day
full_text:
After an ugly loss a week ago, the New England Patriots are back in the win column after a divisional upset over the Buffalo Bills. A season ago, the Patriots' win over the Bills was a chief catalyst for the team to carry momentum.
For now, it remains to be seen if this year's win will do the same.
Until then, here are the five biggest risers, and two biggest fallers, from New England's 29-26 win over Buffalo.
Cbism's role for 2026 was expected to be a minimal one. The second-year receiver was a healthy scratch in Week 1, a trend which quickly changed once A.J. Brown went down with injury.
Fast forward a few weeks and Chism has finally earned his place in the receiver room. On Sunday, he made a pair of acrobatic catches, including the go-ahead touchdown , to help New England take home the win.
"When I'm out there and you know the ball's in the air, I kind of black out," Chism said when asked abut his go-ahead grab. I'm kind of in that little flow state. I saw it in the air. Drake gave me an opportunity and I just, you know, you got to come down with with with those opportunities. You don't know how many you get. So just trying to take advantage of all of them."
Campbell has grown accustomed to seeing his name as a riser on this list. Sunday, not so much.
The second-year left tackle had his struggles on Sunday, allowing five pressures in the first half and one more in the second. The LSU product didn't have his best day against the Bills defensive line, plus was called for two penalties.
Prior to this week, Campbell's performance at left tackle has been impressive. He has been a force to be reckoned with at the tackle positon, a clear step up from last year's playoff performances.
Although Maye had a pair of turnovers , but both could be argued not to be his fault. The first, a fumble, came due to the entirety of the offensive line collapsing. The second, an interception, simply took an unlucky bounce through WR Romeo Doubs' hands.
Other than that, the young quarterback was surgical. Maye gained more than 320 yards through the air and ground, plus threw for three touchdowns.
"He just (was) extremely prepared)," head coach Mike Vrabel said. "Focused. And a good week of practice."
Heading into the day, Woodson had been awaiting the first regular season interception of his career.
He wound up grabbing what may end up being the most important video of that play. The second-year player tallied three tackles on the day in addition to his forced turnover.
The interception could not have come at a more perfect time. With a minute left on the game clock, Bills quarterback Josh Allen tried to play hero-ball. With his intended receiver blanketed in double coverage, it does not work. Woodson got the easy interception to take home the win.
Although Wishnowsky has performed acceptable in lieu of Bryce Baringer, who is aiding an injury, today was a signifcant step in the wrong direction. The 34-year-old punted four times on Sunday for a season-low average of just 38 yards.
Wishnowsky also added multiple touchbacks to his catalogue, struggling to flip the field against a high-powered Bills offense.
As per usual, Ponder makes the winners-losers list as a riser. He finished the day with a sack and a trio of tackles. The 2025 undrafted free agent has also marked a half-sack in each of the Patriots' past three matchups.
The most important part about Sunday for Ponder? He was able to do so in a near-healthy Patriots edge rusher room. Even with starter Dre'Mont Jones back in the lineup after missing a game-plus due to a shoulder injury, Ponder still stepped up to the plate.
Although Maye was marked for an interception on a drop by Doubs , the turnover was simply a stroke of misfortunate for the pass-catcher. Other than that, the former Green Bay Packer played near-perfect football on Sunday.
Doubs tallied six receptions on his nine targets, racking up 58 yards and his first two touchdowns of the year. WIth Brown still out for at least the next week, New England will certainly continue to need to lean on its receiver.

title: Patriots Secondary Overjoyed after Sealing Bills Win with Interception
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The New England Patriots locker room, fresh off a thrilling 29-26 win over the division rival Buffalo Bills , was elated. Everyone seemed to be in a good mood after the team's second win of the season.
But there might not have been a happier bunch of players than the secondary — a group that battled injuries before and during the game before a Craig Woodson interception ended the game in the final seconds.
"God empowered me for moments like this," Woodson told reporters after the game. "Moments to make plays like this. To have the opportunity to go out there and put the skillset he gave me on display, and go out there and give him the glory. That's all I thought about.
"Once the play happened, the ball went in the air. It was like it was slow motion, honestly."
His interception — coming just a few plays after the Patriots reclaimed the lead with a 23-yard touchdown from Efton Chism III — quieted the Highmark Stadium crowd. It was Woodson's first interception since his one against the Houston Texans in last season's AFC Divisional game.
This one, though, handed Josh Allen and the Bills their first loss of the season. That made it a little bit more special.
"We needed this win," cornerback Carlton Davis told Patriots On SI. "We needed this win for the division, so the urgency. It was an urgency win. ... That s--- was f------ huge, bro.
"We needed players to step up. Like having lost our best corner, having lost C-Woods ... It's that next man up mentality."
This was not a secondary that was at his best. Dell Pettus was placed on IR a week ago after suffering an ankle injury. Christian Gonzalez missed the game with a shoulder issue . Charles Woods left the game in the fourth quarter after suffering what he called a "stinger" in his shoulder.
And yet, this unit battled against an offense that has been at the top of its game all year.
"That's a team win," Woods told Patriots On SI. "That's what you call a team win right there. Just guys playing complimentary football, special teams, o(ffense), defense. Beautiful."
Some things will need to get cleaned up from this unit. The Bills grabbed the lead in the fourth quarter after Allen connected with Keon Coleman for a 34-yard laser down the middle of the field. Khalil Shakir had a 50-yard gain, while Joshua Palmer would have had one if he hadn't dropped the ball.
But ultimately, this unit was happy to be the ones to clinch it.
"I'm very psyched," Woods said. "That's our mentality. We always preach next man up, so you know, very excited. I'm very happy for (Woodson)."
It was Woodson's first game back after missing the team's Week 3 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He suffered a shoulder injury the week prior, and his absence clearly hurt this team. Now that he's healthy and ready to go, he hopes to build on what the Patriots put on tape in Western New York.
"Just because we were 1-2 doesn't mean anything," Woodson said. "We can win as many games as we want."

title: Mike Vrabel Explains Unusual Unsportsmanlike Conduct Penalty in Patriots Win
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — With the Buffalo Bills driving at the end of the first half, New England Patriots cornerback Marcus Jones was called for a holding penalty. After that, Jones' head coach was also issued a penalty — but for a different reason.
Vrabel , sharing with reporters after the Patriots' come-from-behind 29-26 win over the Bills, said that he swore at a member of the officiating crew as he voiced his displeasure with the call.
"I told him it was a terrible — I'm not going to say — effing call," Vrabel said, also sharing it's something he's probably said around 87 times during his career as a head coach. "There was nothing derogatory. You'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive.
"Once I get the word from upstairs that it wasn't what we felt like was a good call, which I'm going to trust Stretch (vice president of football operations and strategy John Streicher) with my life."
The penalty added 15 yards to the Bills, who eventually would go down and punch it into the end zone on a Josh Allen two-yard quarterback keeper. That touchdown would tie the game at 14-14, and the Bills would head into the locker rooms at halftime leading by a field goal after a Drake Maye interception that bounced out of the hands of wide receiver Romeo Doubs.
"I probably shouldn't have swore," Vrabel continued. "But I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that. And I apologized to him."
ESPN's Mike Reiss, who is the Patriots pool reporter , spoke with Vinovich after the game about what led to the infraction.
Q: What led to Mike Vrabel being assessed an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty?
Vinovich: "He was out of the box, came up to the official and said, "That was a (expletive) terrible call."
Q: In a situation like that, is there any warning given?
Vinovich: "I don't know how you're going to give a warning. It's not something that is going to happen twice. When you use language like that, it's pretty much a given."
The Patriots were penalized six times for 35 yards, while the Bills were penalized five times for 31 yards. Those 15 yards didn't end up costing the Patriots the win, as Drake Maye connected with Efton Chism III on a 23-yard touchdown in the final minutes to give them their second win of the season.
"And again, players responded," Vrabel said. "It was unfortunate and I have to be better in those moments."

title: What Kellen Moore, Saints Players Said After Embarrassing Loss to Falcons
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints gave the city little reason to celebrate after their crushing 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday evening.
On a night commemorating the 20th anniversary of the Domecoming , Atlanta spoiled the occasion by jumping on New Orleans early and never relinquishing control. The Falcons rushed for 205 yards, produced several explosive plays and sent the Saints to 1-3.
Afterward, head coach Kellen Moore and several Saints players addressed the slow start, defensive breakdowns, turnovers and the disappointment of falling flat on such a meaningful night.
On his opening thoughts after the loss:
“Really disappointing game for us. Obviously, I thought the Dome was an incredible night, incredible energy. We obviously did a poor job just preparing our football team. We really, in all three phases, did not do enough to win this game. Atlanta came in and played a lot better than us.
“I didn't coach well enough, play well enough, so obviously, it wasn't good enough. We're at where we're at. We're a 1-3 football team with some good moments, but not enough consistent football to be where we ultimately want to be. We have a lot of work to do. There's a path for us, but it's going to take a lot of work to get there. We've got to keep going.”
On the Saints' continued slow starts:
“It is just disappointing. Obviously, not coaching it well enough, not executing well enough. They came out, went right down the field and scored. We went three-and-out and didn't score until the second quarter.”
On whether the Saints have tried changing things to start faster:
“We have tried a number of different things. Obviously, we have to solve this. We have to find a way.”
On the team's preparation:
“I just think, at the end of the day, they executed better than us. They played faster than us. They, obviously, ran the ball really well, created some explosive plays in the pass game. On our side of it, we weren't able to run the ball well enough. We turned the ball over, and that's a challenging formula.”
On the struggles running the football:
“We weren't able to run well, and we weren't able to put ourselves in position to have the opportunities to continue to run it and find that ability to finally get it going. When you fall behind, you play in some different circumstances. Obviously, you are going to have to adjust the plan.”
On the significance of the Domecoming game:
“We talked about it at the beginning of the week. The guys were fired up. I thought there was good energy. We just didn't execute well enough in the beginning, and they got going.”
On whether preparation was an issue:
“I don't think there's a lack of preparation. I think there's a lack of execution on some of it. We were prepared. I think the turnover early killed us, and we've got to be able to put some of those early drives together and score more points early on to get it going.
“As an offense, we knew exactly what went wrong and what went right. We just have to clean up those little things and take responsibility for that. I have to be able to put us in the right position to go out and do that. There's a lot to learn from. It obviously sucks, but we're going to keep going.”
On his left hand getting hit in the first quarter:
“Yeah, I took a helmet or something to it. I think it was just bruised up, so it should be good. I was able to play the rest of the game.”
On whether the injury affected his grip or throwing:
“No. It was just part of it. It didn't affect my right hand, obviously, so it was just something to deal with.”
On the disappointment considering the significance of the game:
“It is extremely disappointing. It is embarrassing. You can't say enough good things about the fans showing up and the entire process, what this game meant, and we fell short as a team to not get that win. That was our mission. That was my message, and we did not win.
“It was a team loss. We've got to do better on all fronts. As an offense, we have to start faster when we are going against another really good offense and be able to do our part. We've got to do a lot better there, and it starts with myself.”
On the mood in the locker room:
“Disappointed. More than anything, you lose to the Falcons like that, especially on a Monday night game, and it sucks. You can't say, ‘Oh, man that doesn't suck.’ It definitely does.
“But I do know as a team that we're extremely close and that we're going to keep going and keep our eyes forward. We have really good leadership, and our leadership admits that we've got to get better. We have to get better, watch the film and evaluate that. There's no hiding that.
“But at the same time, it is a long season, and there are a lot of games yet to be played where we can do that. There's nothing set in stone. We know that, and that's the best part about this business is that we're going to keep climbing.”
On the disappointment of the loss:
“I hate that we had a slow start. We got punched in the mouth early and look at the response. It's one of those games where we weren't good on offense, defense or special teams. You look at the second half and are ready to fight back.
“When you play a division rival it's like playing two games. When you have the Falcons coming into our building, you have to be ready. They had an early score with Bijan [Robinson]. At that point with 60 yards on the ground, we have to figure something out.
“They had almost 200 yards rushing (205). That's on the defensive line. When you have a ground game like that, then you have to tell the defensive line to tighten up. Our secondary had to come down and try to focus on the run and then that's when they have their way. They had their way tonight. It's embarrassing.”
On why the Saints couldn't stop Atlanta's rushing attack:
“Without sounding redundant. A 60-yard (59) touchdown. We didn't shut down our run defense. Our run defense did not show up to play early on. A 60-yard touchdown.
“From there, they see that their zone schemes are working, so they relied on that. For whatever reason, we couldn't tighten up our gaps. Our gap integrity has to be at a premium, especially when you have a top-tier back like Bijan or any running back the way that we were playing. It just wasn't good enough.”
On what the Saints should expect moving forward:
“Football is not always what you expect it to be. It is a good thing that we have 17 weeks. We have to stay encouraged. We have to have the mindset that this is not a defining moment.
“We can't take a step back because the rear view mirror is smaller than the front mirror. So, let's just keep it there.”
On whether someone needs to speak up after the loss:
“Nobody has to speak for it. Nobody says we have to step it up. Everyone knows that. Go make plays. Make this happen. We start with turnovers. We start with shooting ourselves in the foot. It's all obvious.
“We know that and we all have to be intentional about it. We play smarter ball and the results are different. These are all things that we can control. The outcome will be the outcome. We just have to control what we control and let the results speak for themselves.”
On whether Atlanta's play-action game surprised the Saints:
“We weren't surprised. We feel like we knew what they were going to do, but we just have to be better. Keep your eyes open and be ready to defend anything that you are going to get.”
On what hurt the Saints defensively:
“No, we just feel like we didn't play our best game and they played one of their best games. Congrats to them.”
On whether Atlanta's running game opened everything else up:
“I mean, we know that they are going to get some runs off. We just have to be better all across the board including the run game and pass game.”
On the offense's performance:
“There are a lot of things that we have to fix. We started out slow. We talk about starting fast and we didn't do that. We lost the ball as well. There are a lot of things here and there.
“There was a lot of emotions this game. Obviously, it was a tough…

title: Saints Humiliated by Rival Falcons in 45-24 Monday Night Rout
full_text:
In what was supposed to be a night of celebration for New Orleans and its resilience following Hurricane Katrina, with the game designated as the 20th anniversary of the Domecoming, the Atlanta Falcons made it a night of dread.
The Falcons defeated the New Orleans Saints 45-24, and it was not close from start to finish as the Falcons led the entire way . The Falcons outgained the Saints 410-320, but the margins really separated them in yards per play. Atlanta averaged 7.5 yards per play while New Orleans averaged 4.6.
While Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix threw efficiently, completing 15 of 20 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown, its rushing attack killed the Saints.
The Falcons rushed for 205 yards after Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson ran roughshod over the Saints’ depleted defense.
Bijan Robinson had 19 carries for 145 yards and two touchdowns, while Brian Robinson had 14 carries for 62 yards and three touchdowns.
Tyler Shough did have a decent game, completing 30 of 48 passes for 288 yards and a touchdown. Chris Olave had a quiet but productive day, catching 8 for 114 yards, but it was overshadowed by the beatdown the Falcons put on the Saints.
Tyler Shough did have a decent game, completing 30 of 48 passes for 288 yards and a touchdown. Chris Olave had a quiet but productive day, catching 8 for 114 yards, but it was overshadowed by the beatdown the Falcons put on the Saints.
Otherwise, the Saints had no bright spots offensively, rushing the ball 15 times for 50 yards, an average of 2.6 yards per carry. Meanwhile, Atlanta averaged nearly 6 yards per carry.
The first half was another slow start for the Saints as they trailed 24-7 at halftime.
The Falcons had the ball on the first possession and needed only three plays to score.
After Penix found Drake London and tight end Austin Hooper for gains of 12 and 9 yards, Bijan Robinson got the handoff, bounced to the outside and proceeded to go 59 yards to the house untouched to take an early 7-0 lead with 13:43 left in the first quarter.
On its second drive, New Orleans looked as if it were finally going to get something going offensively. However, a third-down stop by Atlanta led to a 52-yard field goal attempt by Daniel Carlson that he hooked to the left.
Luckily, the Saints’ defense made up for it with a quick three-and-out. Then disaster struck.
Saints running back Kendre Miller coughed up the ball on the first play and the Falcons recovered it. Miller was originally ruled down before an official review reversed the decision.
A few plays later, Bijan Robinson scored his second touchdown rush of the game to give Atlanta a 14-0 lead with 52 seconds left in the first quarter.
The Saints responded quickly as Shough unloaded a 44-yard pass to Olave that put the Saints on the 10-yard line. Two plays later, Alvin Kamara scored his first rushing touchdown of the season from 3 yards out to cut Atlanta’s lead to seven points.
That’s where the fun stopped.
Atlanta scored on the ensuing possession as Brian Robinson reached paydirt on a 4-yard touchdown run to finish off a 10-play, 65-yard drive to take a 21-7 lead.
The Falcons scored the final points of the half on a 29-yard field goal from Nick Folk .
The Saints entered the second half needing something close to a complete reversal after Atlanta built a 24-7 halftime lead. Instead, the Falcons continued to control the game and never allowed New Orleans to seriously threaten their advantage.
New Orleans opened the third quarter with one of its better sustained drives of the night. Tyler Shough moved the offense downfield with completions to Olave, Juwan Johnson and Kamara, but the Saints stalled before reaching the end zone and settled for a Carlson field goal to cut Atlanta's lead to 24-10.
Atlanta immediately answered.
Penix connected with Jahan Dotson for a chunk gain before Bijan Robinson continued to punish the Saints on the ground. London later moved the chains through the air, and Brian Robinson Jr. finished the possession with his second rushing touchdown of the night, stretching Atlanta's advantage to 31-10.
The Saints finally found the end zone again early in the fourth quarter. Shough connected with Devaughn Vele and Kamara during the drive before Kamara powered into the end zone for his second touchdown, trimming the deficit to 31-17.
Any hope of a comeback disappeared almost immediately.
Atlanta responded with another explosive scoring drive, highlighted by a 28-yard catch-and-run from Kyle Pitts and Penix's 31-yard touchdown pass to Dotson. After the Falcons' defense stopped New Orleans on downs, Brian Robinson broke loose for his third touchdown of the game to make it 45-17.
New Orleans added a late touchdown when Shough found Vele in the back of the end zone, but by then the outcome had long been decided.
Vele finished with six catches for 54 yards
The Saints were able to move the football more effectively after halftime, but nearly every positive stretch was answered by Atlanta. The Falcons scored 21 second-half points and consistently prevented New Orleans from turning the game into a legitimate comeback, finishing off a 45-24 victory.

title: Saints vs. Falcons: 3 Keys to Victory for New Orleans on Monday Night
full_text:
Sign up for the daily Saints Newsletter by clicking here .
As NFC South action kicks off on Monday Night Football, the spotlight turns to the Crescent City for one of the NFL's most heated rivalries.
At the Caesars Superdome, the New Orleans Saints welcome the Atlanta Falcons . Both teams hold 1-2 records, making this divisional showdown a key chance to get back to .500 and seize early momentum in the division.
The Saints are eager to recover from a disappointing 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders , a game in which four consecutive second-half giveaways squandered a double-digit lead. The Falcons, meanwhile, arrive in New Orleans buoyed by a convincing 35-14 victory over the Green Bay Packers .
Monday's contest represents the Saints' initial Monday Night Football home game since hosting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2022. It also marks their first night game overall since an Oct. 17, 2024, clash against the Denver Broncos —a pair of games that both ended in New Orleans losses.
If the Saints want bragging rights and to stay on the right path, here are three keys to victory against the Dirty Birds.
While Atlanta boasts the league's top-ranked run defense—yielding only 47.7 yards per game without allowing a single rushing touchdown—their secondary has proven to be a major vulnerability.
With the Falcons surrendering 263 passing yards per game (29th in the NFL), New Orleans has a strong tactical edge. The Saints enter averaging 281.3 yards through the air, ranking third overall.
This presents a clear opening for quarterback Tyler Shough . Instead of stubbornly challenging Atlanta's stout front line, New Orleans should capitalize on Shough, Chris Olave , and the aerial attack to generate downfield shots against a struggling Atlanta secondary.
And with Travis Etienne Jr . out for the foreseeable future, the Saints’ rushing attack will take a hit, so they might just need to throw the rock around.
Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson enters the NFC South matchup as one of the NFL's most productive offensive players. Through three games, the Falcons running back has rushed for 349 yards and two touchdowns on 66 carries, averaging 5.3 yards per attempt. Add his 13 receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown, and Robinson leads the NFL with 467 yards from scrimmage.
The Saints also will be dealing with a player coming off his best performance of the season. Robinson shredded Green Bay for 194 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries, including a 55-yard run, while adding two catches for 19 yards. Atlanta finished with 242 rushing yards and controlled possession for more than 37 minutes in its 35-14 victory. Robinson was subsequently named NFC Offensive Player of the Week.
This one should be straightforward after what happened against Las Vegas.
New Orleans committed four consecutive turnovers in the second half of its 35-27 loss to the Raiders, turning what had been a double-digit Saints advantage into a frustrating defeat. The Saints enter Monday with a minus-4 turnover differential, ranking near the bottom of the NFL.
Atlanta has its own turnover problems — the Falcons enter at an NFL-worst minus-6 — making possession potentially one of the biggest deciding factors Monday night.
The Saints have shown they can move the football and score. They simply cannot give Atlanta extra possessions, especially in a rivalry game that could come down to one or two critical mistakes.

title: Saints-Falcons Staff Predictions: Will New Orleans Bounce Back on Monday Night?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will take on the Atlanta Falcons in another clash between the two longtime rivals on Monday Night Football in New Orleans.
New Orleans (1-2) is coming off a tough 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in a game the Saints held a double-digit lead in the third quarter. Meanwhile, the Falcons are coming off a 35-14 upset win over the Green Bay Packers on Monday Night Football.
Here are the staff predictions.
Despite the Falcons having the best run defense in the NFL, allowing just 47.7 yards per game and zero rushing touchdowns, they have been extremely vulnerable through the air.
Atlanta ranks 29th in pass defense at 263 yards allowed per game, which creates an enticing matchup for Tyler Shough and a Saints offense averaging 281.3 passing yards per game, third best in the NFL.
That might be exactly how New Orleans has to win this game, especially considering the state of its backfield. The Saints’ rushing attack hasn’t been the strongest, rushing for 101.3 yards per game, tied for 16th in the league.
On top of that, Travis Etienne Jr. was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, leaving Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller to carry the load against the NFL's best run defense. Starting left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. also remains sidelined after undergoing ankle surgery, making pass protection another concern.
The bigger reason I expect a shootout, however, is what's happening on the other side of the ball.
New Orleans will be without Kaden Elliss , Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings , while Pete Werner is questionable after missing all three practices with a shoulder injury. That leaves an already vulnerable Saints defense potentially without four significant pieces of its front seven against an Atlanta offense built around Bijan Robinson and one of the NFL's most productive rushing attacks.
Atlanta enters the game averaging 173 rushing yards per game, second in the NFL, while New Orleans ranks 27th against the run at 128.7 yards allowed per game. That's a bad matchup before even accounting for the Saints' injuries.
Moreover, Michael Penix made his first appearance in more than 10 months, and completed 18 of 25 passes for 256 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Atlanta's 35-14 victory. He averaged 10.2 yards per attempt, posted a 101.4 passer rating and wasn't sacked as the Falcons piled up 498 total yards.
So I don't expect New Orleans to shut Atlanta down. I expect the Saints to have to outscore them.
The Falcons should be able to move the football on a depleted New Orleans defense, but Atlanta's inability to consistently stop the pass gives Shough an opportunity to answer. If the Saints can protect him and avoid the turnovers that doomed them against Las Vegas, I like their chances of producing enough explosive plays through the air to survive.
Emotions were high in the Superdome last weekend when the Raiders visited New Orleans. None of it counted, as Las Vegas left the Crescent City the same way they arrived: undefeated.
Of course, the fourth quarter was the undoing for the Saints in their home opener. In Week 1, it was a slow start in Detroit that led to defeat. In Week 2, it was a win in Baltimore despite an even slower start than Week 1.
Though not the most hobbled of teams, the Saints still have 10 players on injured reserve, the latest of which is Travis Etienne Jr., plus two more on the Designated to Return IR.
The Falcons got back Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback after the debacle of QBs in the first two weeks of the season. He has never played against the Saints, after sitting behind Kirk Cousins in 2024 and tearing his ACL in 2025, missing the entire season. Running back Bijan Robinson is solid, but in the Superdome last season, Robinson ran 14 times for 70 yards and no touchdowns. He did even worse at home against the Saints, getting 15 carries for a measly 33 yards.
With that said, the question that keeps popping in my head is will the Saints learn from these mistakes they've made this season?
They learned from their slow starts in Games 1 and 2, turning that around against Las Vegas last weekend. Will they learn from that fourth-quarter letdown? Tyler Shough says they have. By the way, he said the same thing about the slow starts in the first two weeks of the season, and sure enough, he was right.

title: 2 Saints Whose Stock Is Falling Entering Monday Night vs. Falcons
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints don't have much time to dwell on what went wrong against the Las Vegas Raiders .
Now they must shift their attention to their game against the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football, who come to the Caesars Superdome for the Saints' first NFC South matchup of the season. With both teams sitting at 1-2, New Orleans has an opportunity to not only get back to .500 but claim bragging rights over its longtime divisional rivals.
But there are a few individual performances from that loss that become even more concerning when looking ahead to Atlanta.
Here are two Saints whose stock is down — and who will be under the microscope against Atlanta.
It was a difficult afternoon for Justin Reid , and the numbers backed it up.
Reid received a 28.2 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the lowest among Saints players who logged at least 20 snaps. His biggest struggles came in coverage, where PFF gave him a 29.6 grade.
PFF charted Reid as the nearest defender on six completions for 74 yards and a touchdown, with opposing quarterbacks producing a 150.3 passer rating when targeting his coverage. That doesn't mean Reid was at fault for each completion because coverage assignments can make nearest-defender statistics imperfect, but it does show how frequently Las Vegas found success in his area.
Reid also drew an unnecessary roughness penalty in the end zone, adding another negative play to an already difficult outing.
The veteran safety was brought to New Orleans to provide stability and experience and, for the most part, has been on the back end, but Week 3 was easily one of those performances he would like to shake off.
While Chase Young continues to generate pressure from one side of the Saints' defensive front, Cameron Jordan hasn't been nearly as productive from the other.
Jordan finished with a 45.6 overall PFF grade, the second-lowest mark among Saints players who played at least 20 snaps. His 24.8 tackling grade was the lowest defensive grade in any individual category highlighted by PFF's Week 3 numbers.
The pass-rush production was also limited. Jordan rushed Kirk Cousins 21 times but generated only one pressure, according to PFF.
The contrast with Young was noticeable. Young recorded two sacks and earned an 81.1 overall grade and 87.1 pass-rush grade, while Jordan struggled to consistently affect Cousins.
At 37, the Saints aren't asking him to carry their pass rush anymore, but they still need more impact from one of the most experienced players on the defense.

title: Giants CB Deonte Banks Named NFC Defensive Player of the Week
full_text:
New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks' bounceback season continues, as the fifth-year defender was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week for his performance in the team's 36-24 Week 4 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
Banks showed resilience by bouncing back after giving up a touchdown to Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in the first quarter. The Giants' 2023 first-round pick went on to deliver four tackles, four pass breakups and a huge 98-yard pick-six on the final play of the game.
Banks' interception, the league's second-longest touchdown with no time left on the clock since the 1970 merger, per Stats Perform, snuffed out the Cardinals' last-ditch scoring drive, in which quarterback Jacoby Brissett had driven his offense down to the Giants' 44-yard line.
Banks picked off the pass intended for receiver Michael Wilson at the 2-yard line and took it to the house, sealing the Giants' win.
Banks, who regained a starting job on defense after struggling to find his footing the last two years, currently leads the Giants' defenders with six pass breakups. He also has eight tackles through the first four games.
This is Banks' first Defensive POTW award, and he is the first Giant to be named NFC Defensive Player of the Week since linebacker Bobby Okereke won the award after the 2025 season finale.
Banks, who returned to action after missing the previous two games with a calf injury, becomes the second member of the Giants' defensive secondary to be recognized for outstanding play in as many weeks.
Last week, safety Jevon Holland was named NFC Defensive Player of the Month for September after starting his 2026 campaign with an interception in each of his first three games.

title: Former Giants WR Odell Beckham Jr. Joins Vikings Practice Squad
full_text:
Former New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has a new home for the foreseeable future.
Beckham has signed with the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad , where he will seek a larger role than he did in his second short stint with Big Blue.
Head coach John Harbaugh, who once said Beckham was one of his favorite people , took the blame for the coaching staff’s inability to find a role for Beckham , who was limited to just 20 snaps on offense, including one pass target.
Beckham took to social media to air his feelings about how his second stint with the Giants turned out, saying the decision to release him blindsided him .
Beckham, the Giants’ first-round pick in the 2014 draft out of LSU, began his NFL career looking like he might become a legendary NFL receiver, recording 1,000-yard seasons in four of his first five NFL campaigns.
He was traded to the Cleveland Browns after the 2018 season just months after signing a new contract extension. He then had one more 1,000-yard receiving season before his production began to fall, partly due to knee injuries.
Beckham, who won a Super Bowl championship with the Los Angeles Rams, continued to fight through injuries, including two torn ACLs.
His last truly productive season in the league came in 2023 when he was with Harbaugh in Baltimore. That year, Beckham, returning from a season of inactivity, appeared in 14 games with six starts and posted 565 yards on 35 receptions, his best numbers since 2021, when he split that season between the Browns and Rams.
Beckham and the Giants hoped that history would repeat itself this year. He missed the 2025 season to get his body and mind right, then signed with the Giants on a one-year, veteran-minimum deal with no guaranteed money.
He vowed to be a good teammate and do whatever he could to be helpful. Unfortunately, the coaches’ inability to find a bigger role for him, combined with his lack of special teams snaps and the mounting injuries on the roster, made the arrangement impossible to continue.
Beckham will now get a chance to continue his career on his terms with the Vikings.

title: From J.J. McCarthy to the Center Spot: Giants Storylines Heading Into Week 5
full_text:
That’s the mantra New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has been preaching to his players and staff these days, which makes sense since no one knows what tomorrow brings, let alone a week or two from now.
So for the Giants, who hold a 3-1 record for their best start to a regular season campaign since 2022, it’s all about taking care of business against the Washington Commanders on the road, a team that is expected to welcome back its starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels, from his elbow injury.
That won’t be easy, according to Harbaugh, given all that Daniels can do when he plays.
“He's a premier quarterback who can operate just in all those modalities. He's proven himself to be a very dangerous quarterback, so, yeah, we're going to have to be at our best,” he said.
Daniels is good, but he’s also beatable. The Giants' defensive game plan will likely include a spy to help contain the signal caller’s running ability, and perhaps a little trickery up front to collapse the pocket and force the quarterback into errant throws.
How the Giants prepare for Daniels is just one of many storylines for Week 5, as New York looks for its third win in a row for the first time since the 2023 season when they beat Washington, New England, and Green Bay between Weeks 11 and 14 (they had a Week 13 bye that season).
Despite their early-season success, the Giants still aren't getting any respect from Vegas, which, per FanDuel , has them as a 3.5-point underdog .
And yes, the players have noticed.
“Yeah, for sure. I mean, stuff like that, definitely,” said cornerback Greg Newsome II when asked if the players have taken note of the odds.
“You always want something to go into a game and just give you an extra motivating boost.”
While the players know where they stand in Vegas’ eyes and are seemingly motivated by the diss, Newsome said they’re not about to let the disrespect consume them.
“We don't really care what the outside world believes,” he said. “We know what we have on this team. We know what we're all about, so at the end of the day, no matter who we play, we just have to go out there and just play to the best of our ability and try to find a way to go 1-0.”
Last week Harbaugh admitted that they had a package of plays ready for newly acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy to run. However, the flow of the game meant they couldn't get to those plays.
So with McCarthy having had several more days to get up to speed on the offense and the protection calls, it stands to reason that he will not only be QB2 this week, but may also have a bigger package of plays that will be whipped out at some point, right?
Harbaugh wasn’t willing to commit to that part, but he did admit that McCarthy being promoted to QB2 ahead of Jake Haener (on the practice squad) is “definitely on the table.”
Last week, Harbaugh decided to play Bryan Hudson at center over John Michael Schmitz, who missed a couple of days of practice (Friday and presumably Saturday’s walkthrough) after welcoming his first child.
Hudson played rather well in place of Schmitz, allowing no quarterback pressures in 33 pass-blocking snaps. So given that, one would think that Hudson deserves another chance to start.
Harbaugh, naturally, wasn't ready to commit to that.
“We’ll see,” he said. “Huddy played really well, and we were excited about him going in. So, maybe create some options for us, but (Schmitz) was playing really well too. So, a very good problem to have.”
And again, if the coaches agree with PFF’s take on his pass blocking, it's a very easy call.
As usual, there are some injured players to watch for the coming week, starting with safety Jason Pinnock (concussion), who played well in place of Tyler Nubin last week until Pinnock got hurt.
Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) is also on the injury report, and the Giants are likely to manage his practice reps moving forward.
Defensive lineman Chauncey Golston (neck) was the other Giant injured on Sunday. Golston has been quietly having a solid season after last year’s injury-plagued campaign limited him to just 10 games. But there are concerns that he could miss a little bit of time.
No, Dante “Turbo” Miller isn’t returning to the roster. But the Giants' running game could sure use a little juice.
Currently, they're averaging 3.7 yards per rushing attempt, 23rd in the league, despite having the 12th highest total rushing yards (442).
Part of the problem has been ball security—the Giants lead the league with four fumbles by running backs.
They’re also not getting into the end zone, having scored just one touchdown on 119 carries, which ties them for 29th in the league with the Raiders. They're lacking in explosive plays as well, with just one run of 20-plus yards, by quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 1.
That’s not good news for a unit that will face a decent Commanders run defense that has allowed just 374 yards  (sixth in the league) on 94 carries to opponents . It’s also not good news for the Giants if they can’t put together a balanced, effective attack and end up relying on the passing game to move the chains.

title: Giants Open as 3.5-Point Underdogs at Commanders as Jayden Daniels Eyes Return
full_text:
For the second straight week, the New York Giants left the gridiron as victors after an impressive defensive stand, capped by a game-sealing interception returned for a touchdown by cornerback Deonte Banks in a 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
The Giants are now sitting at a 3-1 record and lead in the NFC East standings through the first quarter of the 2026 season, and they'll look to lift themselves another notch as they hit the road to visit the Washington Commanders.
Surprisingly, they won't be doing it with the initial backing of oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook , which, in its opening lines for Week 5 in the NFL, has the Giants set as 3.5-point underdogs against their division rivals.
The spread marks the first time that Big Blue began the week as the underdog since Week 2 when they faced the Los Angeles Rams and tied for the second-largest spread from the season opener against the Dallas Cowboys.
In addition to the spread, the sportsbook has opened the total points line at over/under 43.5 points, matching last weekend's total against the Cardinals.
The Giants are riding into Washington with a two-game win streak and a defense that has finally lit the fuse in both pressure and turnover.
Meanwhile, the Commanders, who sit last in the division with a 1-3 record after their 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London in Week 4, look like a team that has underperformed despite offseason improvements on both sides of the roster.
The Commanders have been without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels, whose potential return this week could be the lone factor pushing oddsmakers to back the home team.
Daniels has been sidelined since Week 2, when he dislocated his left elbow against the Dallas Cowboys. It was the same elbow he injured in the same manner in Week 9 of the 2025 season, and the impact of the consecutive ailments would make one think his season was all but finished this time.
The LSU product has reportedly been cleared to be a full participant in the Commanders' preparation for the Giants, opening the door for him to return to the starting role after Washington fill-in starter Marcus Mariota sprained his MCL in the loss to the Colts.
Despite his injury problems over the last two seasons, Daniels instantly improves the Commanders' offense with his dual-threat ability to escape pressure and extend plays that test an opposing defense's stamina.
The Giants have yet to face a quarterback of Daniels' caliber, making for an interesting matchup as they hope to build on their dominant pass-rushing performance against Cardinals gunslinger Jacoby Brissett, on whom they generated 14 total pressures on, including two sacks and five hits, in the win.
In three career meetings with New York, Daniels has completed 70.4% of his pass attempts for 668 yards and three touchdowns. He also added 29 carries for 147 yards, averaging 5.1 yards per carry.
Washington enters Week 5 with the 15th-ranked scoring offense in the NFL, along with the eighth-most passing touchdowns (eight) and a top-10 standing in rushing attempts and yards.

title: Giants Sign WR Dontae Fleming to Practice Squad
full_text:
The New York Giants are signing wide receiver Dontae Fleming to their practice squad, per the league's transaction report. Fleming visited the team on Tuesday.
Fleming, 6-foot-2 and 180 pounds, previously spent time on the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad after signing as an undrafted free agent following the 2025 NFL Draft.
This past summer, the Vikings placed him on injured reserve when they made final roster cuts at the end of training camp, then waived him with an injury settlement on Sept. 3.
Fleming, who also worked out for the Giants on Sept. 22, played his college ball at Louisiana and later at Tulane. In five total seasons split between the two college programs, he appeared in 59 games with 17 starts and had 95 receptions for 1,372 yards and seven touchdowns.
He also had four rushing attempts for 16 yards.
Fleming has not yet played in a regular-season NFL game. This past preseason, he played in all three games for the Vikings, catching nine of 13 pass targets for 81 yards. Against the Giants in the preseason opener, he caught three of four pass targets for 10 yards.
Fleming returned three punts for the Vikings in the 2026 preseason for 41 yards, and had two fair catches.
The Giants lost receiver/return specialist Braxton Berrios to a foot/ankle injury that, per a social media post by Berrios himself , will require season-ending surgery.
Berrios, who turned 31 on the day he found out his season was over, was clearly dejected by the news.
“Two of my last three seasons ended this way, and I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t miserable right now,” he wrote. “I felt I belonged here this year and everything finally fell in place; now it feels like everything I’ve poured into the last 9 months is gone in the blink of an eye.
“The timing that I thought had arrived feels like a punishment again, but the good news about God is I know it’s coming.”
Berrios, who began the 2026 season on the Giants practice squad, was signed to the 53-man roster last week after his three standard elevations were used up. This season, he has returned five kickoffs for 138 yards (27.6 avg.) and four punts for 10 yards (2.5 avg.).
