title: No Moment Is Too Big for Giants Rookie Kicker Dominic Zvada
full_text:
New York Giants rookie Dominic Zvada is not your typical first-year NFL kicker.
Since joining the Giants as an undrafted free agent in late April, the former Michigan Wolverine has been one of Big Blue's most reliable players. Through New York's first four games, Zvada has gone 9-for-9 on field goal attempts and 5-for-5 on extra points.
Unsurprisingly, the soon-to-be 23-year-old is earning rave reviews.
Still, Zvada refuses to let any moment become too big for him. With the Giants clinging to a three-point lead in the fourth quarter of their Week 4 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, coach John Harbaugh trusted his rookie to kick a 52-yard field goal, giving New York a 30-24 lead with just over two minutes remaining.
The kick not only gave the Giants an added cushion in a game they would eventually win 36-24 at MetLife Stadium, but it also showcased Zvada's ability to deliver in clutch situations yet again.
"For me, my job is to go out there and do my part no matter what, and so for me, that was the mindset going into that kick," Zvada told reporters earlier this week.
"It's just another opportunity to display what I'm able to do," he added. "The operation was great. Never really had a problem, never had a problem the entire game with pressure or anything like that, so I knew going into that kick, all I had to do was focus on my job."
Having earned both First-Team All-America honors and Big Ten Kicker of the Year with Michigan in 2024, Zvada is no stranger to making kicks in high-pressure situations.
His 52-yard field goal in Week 4 tied for the third-longest by a rookie kicker in franchise history, the same feat he accomplished in New York's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2.
Since then, Zvada has made three 50-plus-yard field goals, making him the first Giants rookie to kick three or more 50-plus-yard field goals in a single season.
Though he rightfully deserves the accolades he is receiving, Zvada credits some of his success to playing under Harbaugh, who spent several years coaching special teams at both the collegiate and pro levels. In that regard, he continues to work diligently to validate the trust Harbaugh showed when naming him New York's kicker in late August.
"It's an amazing thing. You can really trust what he's saying, and he uses the same terminology as a specialist used, so when you hear someone talk like that, you know that they have a great idea of what they're talking about," Zvada said of his head coach.
"And so, yeah, to be able to play for Coach Harbaugh has been an absolute dream, and I'm just excited to keep rolling with him."
With their Week 5 road matchup against the Washington Commanders fast approaching, Zvada remains determined to stay focused.
At 3-1, the Giants can maintain sole possession of first place in the NFC East with a win over their divisional rival. To do so, they may need Zvada to extend his streak of perfection, perhaps under high-stakes circumstances.
Fortunately for the Giants, Zvada will be ready to do his job, as always.
"I feel like I always have that mentality," Zvada said.
"Even from very early on, I always had that belief in myself, even when maybe other people didn't. I think that's what kind of helps drive a person to get to this point. And so, that's how it is."

title: Giants Rise in Week 5 MMQB Power Rankings
full_text:
The New York Giants ’ 36-24 Week 4 victory over the Arizona Cardinals at MetLife Stadium kept their home record undefeated and their season record 3-1 overall with a first-place grasp on the NFC East.
New York's dramatic win, punctuated by cornerback Deonte Banks’ 98-yard interception return for a touchdown, which put an end to the Cardinals' threat of snatching the win away from Big Blue, was enough to prompt SI's Conor Orr to move the Giants from No. 24 last week to No. 21 in this week’s MMQB NFL power rankings .
While Banks received a ton of love from his teammates and the Giants faithful after his game-sealing play, Orr saved his analysis to praise linebacker Arvell Reese.
"Arvell Reese vs. David Bailey was going to be a made-for-talk-radio feud for the decade in New York," Orr said.
"Through the first month of their respective professional careers—which, for the record, means very little—it’s not looking like much of a fight. Reese has major “that dude” energy. His stat line against the Cardinals was beastly.
Reese certainly deserves kudos for shifting momentum during the back-and-forth brawl that saw three lead changes between the late minutes of the second quarter and the end of the third frame.
His moment came with 3:15 left in the second quarter, with the Giants trailing the Cardinals 14-12 after a Jameis Winston-to-Malachi Fields touchdown connection and a failed two-point conversion.
The Cardinals were ready to ride their wave of stopping the game-tying score with a solid drive that could have extended their lead to double digits. Three plays into the drive, Reese came through with his first career interception after Shelby Harris batted down a pass.
While Reese and Banks were critical to flipping the game from a potential rout to a thrilling, 1986 Giants defense-esque victory, the name that hides behind the scenes in the defining win was head coach John Harbaugh.
Harbaugh's influence has been floating in the air at 1925 Giants Drive from the first day he arrived at the facility. The culture he brought in has been widely accepted by the players and established a belief that his locker room could compete with anybody in the league on Sundays.
It wasn't until these last two weeks, and more importantly in the final two minutes against the Cardinals, that we saw that attitude translate to a period of intense adversity on the football field.
In prior seasons, the Giants' fragile secondary would have worked against them. In such a situation, big plays and untimely penalties would have likely caused them to crumble and let their opponent score a touchdown and steal the game.
Not anymore under Harbaugh, who has preached to his players to hang together when things get tough on the gridiron, and two consecutive turnovers just outside the end zone to stall potentially horrible losses prove his players have bought into and exemplified their coach's motto.
That's the difference having a proven coach like Harbaugh provides to an organization that has had to make too many leadership changes amid grueling late-game collapses that have marred them in recent years.
The hope is that more wins will come from moments like the one that replayed itself in Week 4, so the Giants can continue pushing toward their postseason aspirations and climbing Orr's power rankings in future weeks.

title: Giants' Bryan Hudson: The Good, the Great and the Ugly From His First Career Start
full_text:
New York Giants backup center Bryan Hudson made his first career start against the Arizona Cardinals. Starting center John Michael Schmitz missed time for the birth of his first child, and Hudson benefited.
He performed well in the Giants' 36-24 win, sparking discussion about who should start at center when the Giants travel to DC to take on the Washington Commanders.
Let’s dig a little deeper into why so many think Hudson deserves another start at center. We'll look at the good, the great, and the ugly of Big Blue’s backup in his first start.
Hudson showed quick feet and the ability to climb to the second level to block linebackers and other defenders who showed.
He executed combo blocks by starting on a double team with a guard and then climbing to the second level.
The Good of #NYGiants center Bryan Hudson against the Cardinals was his second level run blocking. pic.twitter.com/4FCENUcJS4
He also showed the ability to attack the second level quickly when he was left uncovered.
He provided protection and cutback lanes for the backs to pick up extra yards. With linebackers more athletic than ever, it helps to have a center who can be aggressive and effective at the second level.
Schmitz has really struggled early this season in pass protection; that is where Hudson shined against the Cardinals. He did not surrender a defensive pressure under his protection, and that was impressive.
He moved his feet laterally and prevented defenders from getting on his shoulder to turn him open. He showed excellent change of direction, constantly shuffling left and right to pick up stunts, shut down secondary moves, or prevent second-level pressure.
The Great of #NYGiants center Bryan Hudson VS the Cardinals was his pass pro. pic.twitter.com/BL4NmItLwC
He looked consistently balanced in his pass pro. He never really looked like he was reaching for defenders because his feet were heavy. He shuffled well because his feet looked light and not caught in quicksand.
Was it perfect? No. Was it effective? Yes! There is no doubt that Schmitz had extremely tough matchups to start the season, but it is difficult to ignore how good of a job Hudson did in pass pro.
The mark of the elites at center is how they handle bigger, stronger defensive tackles in run blocking.
Hudson, like so many other centers, weighs just over 300 pounds, and while that may seem heavy to the average person in the trenches, it is light. Nose guards’ weights are usually listed between 320 and 360 pounds.
The Ugly of #NYGiants center Bryan Hudson was his 1v1 blocking in the run game.. pic.twitter.com/IY8LF41xxK
They are built to anchor down and create a wall that is hard to move. Hudson struggled against the Cardinal nose guards, who routinely controlled him at the point of attack and even threw him out of the way when they needed to detach.
With help from a guard, it was easier for him to handle, but still not perfect. When he was left alone to run the block, it was as adventurous as many considered Jameis Winston’s performance.
The debate on whether Hudson deserves another start will not die down, even if Schmitz is named the starter for Week 5.
Giants fans should understand that you are getting two different centers with completely different strengths, so be prepared to deal with the negatives from both.
Schmitz is the superior run blocker. He gets movement on double teams and handles 1v1 blocks well in the run game. He has struggled in pass pro.
Meanwhile, Hudson has done well in pass pro, but he is not the strongest run blocker. Now that defensive coordinators have film on him, they will likely make sure he needs to deal with a nose guard in his face every play.
So, as good as he has been in pass protection, if the team's identity is supposed to be a downhill power rushing attack, does he help or hurt the mission?
In a perfect world, you could use Schmitz in the rushing attack and Hudson in pass protection, but that isn't realistic. There is clearly more value in being a better pass protector than a run blocker, even on a team that wants to run the ball.
The Washington Commanders do not have an elite interior pass rush like the Cowboys, Rams, or Titans. Those three teams had three of the best interior defensive linemen in the game.
Schmitz should get the chance to start against the Commanders, but there should be a quick hook if he struggles in pass rush against a team that has only 1.5 sacks from interior defensive linemen in four games.

title: Harbaugh's "1-0" Mindset Is Just What the Giants Need Right Now
full_text:
The New York Giants are 3-1 and lead the NFC East.
Let that sink in, Giants fans, because it’s been a long time since the second part of that statement has been true.
But at the risk of throwing cold water on the euphoria head coach John Harbaugh has brought to the Meadowlands, Giants running back Cam Skattebo reminded reporters in the postgame locker room on Sunday that the team “hasn’t accomplished anything yet.”
That sentiment, when relayed to Harbaugh, drew a smile.
“That's a very wise statement. He's exactly right,” he said. “We have a game this week, a very pivotal game, a very big game in terms of the opportunity that it presents our football team now, where we're at.”
To keep the focus on the present and not the past, Harbaugh had black T-shirts emblazoned with “1-0” across the chest distributed to players, coaches, and staff members as a reminder.
Rightfully so, as a 3-1 start is not an automatic ticket to the postseason. According to The Athletic , since 2020, only 75% of the teams that started a season 3-1 made it to the postseason .
The Giants obviously have their sights set on the playoffs. But it’s going to take discipline and focus on what’s ahead rather than resting on their laurels.
“We have an opportunity to make headway on the season, and we’ve got to do it one play at a time in one game that we have to play this week. So, we're excited about it,” Harbaugh said.
After Sunday’s game, Harbaugh said he started Bryan Hudson over John Michael Schmitz at center because Hudson has been doing well and Schmitz missed a couple of days of practice due to the arrival of his first child.
“We felt like he's got the reps. He's made the calls, and we were thinking about starting to work him in a little bit here and there, even some extra line stuff, if possible,” Harbaugh said of Hudson.
“And it just made sense. I mean, JMS, he'd been up; his wife had the baby. He didn't get much rest. It just made sense, and I think it paid off. It's not a long-term thing. I mean, we have two centers we really like.”
Great, but only one center can play at a time. And does it really make sense to alternate centers in a game?
The answer is no. But backing up a bit, does anyone think that if, for example, Andrew Thomas, Arvell Reese, Malik Nabers, or Abdul Carter missed a Friday practice and a Saturday walkthrough due to a child’s birth, they’d be replaced in the lineup?
If that’s not enough to convince you a switch was made for football reasons, consider that Hudson played extremely well in his 2026 debut as a starter.
Per PFF, he was the Giants’ highest-graded offensive lineman in overall blocking and, in 33 pass-blocking snaps, did not allow a single quarterback pressure .
Schmitz, in 96 pass-blocking snaps this year, has already allowed five pressures .
And if you buy into PFF’s run-blocking grades, Hudson’s 72.1 season grade easily trumps Schmitz’s 49.7 mark .
Harbaugh, as he’s done all year, refused to say if Hudson will get the start again this weekend against the Commanders, but the evidence from last week’s game is hard to ignore.
“We haven't had that personnel meeting yet, but I'll say Huddy played really well, and we were excited about him going in. So, maybe create some options for us, but JMS was playing really well too. So, a very good problem to have,” Harbaugh said.
If there was ever any doubt about the Giants’ intentions regarding quarterback J.J. McCarthy, let’s put it to rest right now.
First, the Giants didn’t simply give up a fifth-round draft pick just for fun. Harbaugh has a clear enough vision for the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 draft, and that’s not to sit and let him marinate on the sidelines.
McCarthy is poised to become the No. 2 quarterback, perhaps as soon as this weekend against the Commanders.
“I think that's a possibility,” Harbaugh said when asked about it. “We'll see how it goes during the week, but that's definitely on the table.”
As McCarthy becomes more entrenched in his knowledge of the Giants’ offense, it is only a matter of time before he becomes the starter.
How soon, you might ask? In an ideal scenario, Big Blue gets through the first part of their schedule with Jameis Winston as the starter.
However, if Winston continues to be up and down, it might be sooner.
But with New York’s  next three opponents (Washington, New Orleans, and Houston) boasting a combined 2-10 record, New York has a chance to enter their Week 8 bye with a 6-1 mark.
Winston is one of 11 players on offense but he is a key part of the unit. So far, while he hasn’t cost the Giants a game, this past weekend against Arizona might have been too close for comfort for Harbaugh, which is why we could see McCarthy sooner than anticipated.

title: How John Harbaugh's Staff Rebuilt Deonte Banks' Confidence
full_text:
The 12-yard touchdown pass that Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. caught against New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks might have spelled trouble for the former Maryland defensive back.
But not this year, and certainly not this version of Banks. The fourth-year cornerback is more confident than ever, and that starts with his coaches’ trust in him, has enabled him to weather storms that in past seasons might have sabotaged him.
“They allowed me just to keep going,” Banks said after the game, his face beaming with a smile after helping clinch the team’s third win of the season with a 98-yard pick-six.
“Like I let up the first touchdown of the game — they just like, ‘Calm down, you missed two weeks. Like settle in.’ And I settled in.”
That hasn’t always been the approach with Banks, who came to the Giants in the first round of the 2023 draft. Not long ago, former position coach Jerome Henderson called out Banks' after what he viewed as an unacceptable effort from the defender in a game against Dallas.
It also wasn’t long ago that Banks’ coverage was so poor he was benched at halftime in a losing effort against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
But with head coach John Harbaugh in place and Harbaugh’s handpicked assistant coaching staff, of which Addison Lynch handles the defensive backs, the approach has been rather simple: teach and believe in the player, even if he makes a mistake.
“We just taught the defense really and talked to him about playing technique the right way, and he was just really amenable to it,” Harbaugh said.
“We didn't really have any in-depth conversation about the past. You know, that really wasn't part of it. Just said, ‘Hey, man, we know what you're capable of, let's go play some good football.’”
Banks has done just that. Per PFF, Banks’ 77.2 overall coverage grade ranks ninth among the 110 cornerbacks with at least 40 coverage snaps.
And his current allowed reception rate of 43.8% is even better than his rookie season, when he posted 57.6% while playing in a defense similar to the one he plays now.
The only negative? He missed two games due to a calf injury, which Banks hopes is the last time he’ll miss this season.
A lot is on the line for Banks, who beat out Paulson Adebo at the start of training camp for a starting job this season.
The Giants did not exercise the option year in Banks’ contract, meaning that after this season, he will become a free agent. So he needs to apply his unique blend of talents to deliver consistent production.
But again, it all begins with the mental part of the picture, which has been the biggest obstacle for Banks to overcome. And so far, that confidence the current coaches have in him, even when he makes a mistake, is paying dividends.
“I do think he felt confident. I think he felt happy about the opportunity, maybe. Maybe he was freed up a little bit from the past, whatever happened,” Harbaugh said.
“He had a great year, his first year. So, maybe he leaned into that a little bit more. I'm not really sure, but it just wasn't something we thought too much about. We just made it about football  more than anything.”
And based on his two-game sample size so far this season, Banks is locked into letting the positives of the game overrule any doubts that might have crept into his mind in the past to sabotage him.

title: Nate Lynn's Jets Promotion Comes at Perfect Time as Joseph Ossai's Struggles Continue
full_text:
It's been hard to find many positives amid a 1-3 start to the season, but the New York Jets have shown flashes of improvement through the first four weeks. The offense is more reliable with quarterback Geno Smith under center, and the secondary isn't as big of a concern anymore , especially after offseason addition Minkah Fitzpatrick ended the interception drought last week.
That said, being two games below .500 means Gang Green still has improvements to make, with their pass rush among the most pressing concerns.  Sure, they're tied for the 14th-most sacks (nine), but the Jets' pass rush enters Week 5 with the fourth-worst grade (58.3) on Pro Football Focus. On top of that, the unit lost Braiden McGregor, who was placed on injured reserve earlier this week with a season-ending pectoral tear.
Throw in the help that a big free-agent signing like Joseph Ossai hasn't given New York much pass-rushing help, and it's easy to see why general manager Darren Mougey needs to act fast before it's too late.
With no time to waste, the Jets added reinforcements, signing preseason darling Nate Lynn to the 53-man roster on Wednesday .
We've signed Nate Lynn to the active roster and placed Braiden McGregor on injured reserve We've also signed EDGE Nathan Voorhis to the practice squad
Lynn won't single-handedly fix the Jets' pass-rushing issues, but his promotion could be exactly what the unit needs as Ossai's production remains a concern.
The Jets penned Ossai to a three-year, $34.5 million contract in free agency, hoping he'd provide the pass rush with a much-needed boost. The former 2021 third-rounder was arguably being underused by the Bengals, and the Jets hoped a move to Gotham could unlock his full potential as a quarterback-seeking missile.
Instead, Ossai's start with the Jets has been rocky. A foot injury limited his availability throughout the summer, forcing him to miss the first two regular-season games. He eventually made his debut against the Detroit Lions in Week 3 and still hasn't done much, recording zero pressures and a career-low 52.6 pass-rush grade on PFF . He's also missed two of his 11 tackle attempts, giving him a lowly grade of 34.9.
Nonetheless, Ossai still has time to turn things around , but until that happens, his production is a problem. That's why it'd be huge for the Jets if Lynn could make an immediate impact against the Cleveland Browns this weekend.
Glenn & Co. have leaned on a five-man pass rush, featuring Ossai, McGregor, David Bailey, Kingsley Enagbare and Will McDonald IV. But with McGregor's season over, Enagbare missing last week's loss due to a knee injury, and Bailey and McDonald still looking for consistency, there's an opening for someone like Lynn to make some noise.
When McGregor was placed on IR, Lynn was the first potential practice squad promotion candidate that came to mind . The former Lions/Titans EDGE won Jets fans over with a strong preseason performance despite joining the team in mid-August, and now it's time to see whether his exhibition performance was a mirage or a sign of things to come.
Even though he appeared in two preseason games, Lynn made the most of his opportunities, recording five tackles (two solo) and six pressures (three sacks and three hurries) across 58 defensive snaps. His effort earned him an 80.4 PFF pass-rush grade , which actually led all Jets in the preseason.
Lynn isn't guaranteed to make a similar impact in the regular season, but everyone knows anything can happen on any given Sunday. The Browns' offensive line is solid for the most part, but still allowed Deshaun Watson to be sacked 11 times over four games, including a whopping five sacks in Week 1. Cleveland's signal-caller also struggles under heat, owning a 48.5% completion rate, 5.2 yards per attempt, and a 34.2 passing grade when pressured this season , per PFF .
Regardless of how many snaps he sees, Lynn needs to capitalize on every opportunity against the Browns. Despite both teams sporting inverse records, the Jets have a legitimate shot at winning on Sunday, and that starts with the pass rush—from Lynn to underperformers like Ossai—doing their job immediately off the bat.

title: Confidence Meter: How I Feel About the Jets' 2027 NFL Draft Outlook One Month Into the Season
full_text:
The 2026 season has just moved into October, and yet it already feels like the Jets' campaign is at a crossroads .
That only happens, of course, after you lose three straight games to NFC North foes. The Jets' most recent loss to the Bears has dropped the organization to 1-3. If the season ended today, it would be their 16th year of playoff-less football , and 11 years since they finished above .500.
Fans won't be ready to give up on the team just yet, but if the losses continue to pile up, it's clear that the team will once again be competing for a top draft pick.
Unlike in past years, though, the Jets' draft outlook is far greater than others around the league.
The Jets own three first-round picks this year: their own, the Colts' first from the Sauce Gardner trade and whoever of the Packers and Cowboys finishes with a worse record. That gives the Jets plenty of ammo to improve the roster across the board just on Day 1.
It also gives them more bites at the apple of finding their future franchise quarterback.
The best way to secure that, of course, is by getting the top overall pick. Unfortunately for the Jets, the Colts, Packers, and Cowboys all sit at 2-2. Currently, New York heads into Week 5 owning the sixth, 11th and 12th overall picks , according to Tankathon .
Those picks could get better as the season goes on. Neither the Colts nor the Packers look relatively good at the moment. But as things stand, the Jets would be on the outside looking in if they hope to potentially grab their franchise quarterback early in Round 1 .
Will that continue for the remainder of the season? Luck may be on the team's side.
According to ESPN 's FBI breakdown, the Jets have a 37% chance of getting a pick inside the top 10 , but only a 9% chance of getting in the top five. Much of those tallies, though, center around the Colts, Packers, and Cowboys—all with two wins—and teams like the Buccaneers, Dolphins and Titans all without a victory.
Things change quickly in the NFL, though. While the Bucs, Titans, and Dolphins have all been bad, improvement comes later in the year.
These numbers could also drastically change if injuries continue to pile up for the Colts or Packers.
Would the Packers win games without Jordan Love? The Cowboys without Dak Prescott? How about the Colts without Jonathan Taylor?
For as daunting as the Jets' outlook looks for their draft future and their prospects of actually winning games, the team is actually in a can't-lose situation.
The more losses that pile up, the better their draft standing is. The more they win, the more improved the team will be going forward.

title: Jets' Best Offseason Addition Clear One Month Into the Season (and It's Time to Extend Him)
full_text:
When it comes to free agent additions, the New York Jets have not had a ton of success in 2026. Some, like Joseph Ossai and Kingsley Enagbare, have dealt with injuries to start the season. Others, like Demario Davis, have  struggled to keep up with the changes to the modern game.
Of all the acquisitions made by general manager Darren Mougey, Belton has been the most successful by far. Through four games, he has managed to record a Pro Football Focus grade of 78—good for 11th among 92 safeties in the league. While his pass defense grade continues to improve, it's not what the Jets have valued most from him.
It's what he's done at the line of scrimmage that has turned the tide for Gang Green's defense.
When Belton was first signed by the Jets, the measly one-year, $4 million offer was seen as a solid value pickup. Belton recorded 120 tackles last season as a member of the New York Giants, but never got a chance to be an every-down player.
With the Jets, Belton has received that chance, and he's rewarding them with the same kind of elite play against the run that he's been providing for years now. Belton ranks seventh by Pro Football Focus in run defense. He's been a sure tackler and one of the more consistent players in New York's secondary.
Against the Bears in New York's 23-12 loss, Belton tallied 14 tackles, one pass defense and only allowed 12 yards on three receptions. It's the kind of performance you see from All-Pros, not players on one-year deals.
"He can come in and he can play basically the same role that Minkah (Fitzpatrick) had of being able to play the big nickel, playing safety," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said of Belton in Week 2. "He’s an impressive player. Intelligent, smart, and he can take up that slack.”
ith how well Belton is playing, there's really only one outlook the Jets must consider moving forward.
Maybe the Jets aren't able to win a lot of games this season. Perhaps Glenn and the coaching staff are fired by the end of the year. One thing the team's struggles should not do, though, is stop the front office from rewarding high-performing players.
The worst thing the Jets could do is watch Belton continue to play well, and then simply move on from him and pick up a compensatory pick in the 2028 draft. Good teams retain talent. The Jets may not have a lot of players to extend at this point after a 1-3 start, but Belton is deserving of it.
And the sooner the team gets a long-term extension done, the better they will be having Belton continue to play at this level.

title: 3 Potential Nahshon Wright Trade Destinations After Jets' Healthy Scratch
full_text:
When the Jets signed former Pro Bowl cornerback Nahshon Wright to a free-agent deal this offseason, the goal was to have him help address a major issue going back to last year.
At the time, New York had failed to record an interception for 17 straight games—an NFL record. Wright, having led all cornerbacks in interceptions last season with five, was thought to be a perfect fit for what the team needed.
Wright was beaten out by second-year cornerback AZ Thomas and, over the last two weeks, has been a healthy scratch on the Jets' game-day roster. Gang Green ended their interception drought in Sunday's loss to Chicago, but the inactive list updates have left one basic reality for Wright and the Jets.
They are doomed to separate.
As the trade deadline draws closer on Tuesday, Nov. 10, and the better Thomas plays, general manager Darren Mouge would be better served trading Wright for any late-round asset the Jets can get in the 2027 NFL Draft .
And plenty of teams could come calling. Here are the top three trade destinations if the Jets look to move Wright in the coming weeks.
It's not just the Jets' defense that has played poorly in the last few weeks. The Lions have given up over 24 points in each of their four matchups this season. They rank dead last in passing yards allowed, third-worst in passing touchdowns allowed and are the worst unit in points allowed.
The Lions need bodies. They need better corners, with Rock Ya-Sin currently hampered by a hamstring injury .
The former Bear knows the NFC North well (two of his five INTs came in divisional games) and could come in and fit with what the Lions want to do defensively. If anything, it makes more sense for Detroit to make a move while the team is still trying to compete for a playoff spot than anything else.
Not to be outdone, the team that just dominated the Lions on Sunday night could also use some cornerback help. For the Panthers, they are without both of their starting cornerbacks, as Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve .
Wright could come to Carolina and provide a veteran presence to what has become a very young secondary. As the Panthers compete for their second straight NFC South title, the more help in the secondary they can get, the better.
Wright should at least balance the Panthers out.
Much like Carolina, the Steelers already have starting-caliber cornerbacks. Asante Samuel Jr. and Jalen Ramsey are quality secondary pieces. Sean Murphy-Bunting and Jamel Dean are also quality role players behind them.
That said, Pittsburgh needs more reinforcements as Ramsey and Samuel are battling injuries .
Wright could give the Black and Yellow a cornerback who is capable of jumping routes and baiting opposing quarterbacks into mistakes. While he does get beat a fair amount, the Steelers just need bodies they can count on right now.

title: D'Angelo Ponds Suddenly Staring at a Bigger Jets Role Amid Jarvis Brownlee Jr. Injury Concerns
full_text:
It is back to the drawing board for the Jets after a 23-12 loss to the Bears on Sunday in a game that was completely one-sided, putting a dent in any progress Gang Green seemed to make in the first three weeks of the season.
From another rough showing in the trenches and quarterback Geno Smith's disastrous performance to a poor coaching job from head coach Aaron Glenn and his staff in terms of keeping the team disciplined and failing to contain the league-leading rushing attack of the Bears, it was an uninspiring loss that has put this team in a precarious position as it continues to deal with a rash of key injuries.
As the Jets return home to face the Browns on Sunday, rookie D'Angelo Ponds could be in line to take on an expanded role .
His availability was limited due to an offseason calf strain, but  Ponds finally made his NFL debut against the Lions in Week 3, playing only two defensive snaps. He then played a career-high 18 snaps in the loss to the Bears, ultimately coming at the expense of cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr., who left the game after colliding with teammate Dane Belton and is now in concussion protocol , per ESPN Jets reporter Rich Cimini.
Jarvis Brownlee Jr. left the game after this play, a collision with teammate Dane Belton. Brownlee now in concussion protocol. One of those days for the #Jets . pic.twitter.com/kd0B4282Ay
As injuries continue to ramp up and an opportunity has opened for Ponds, the second-round pick out of Indiana has a chance to leave a strong impression and potentially increase his snap count for the rest of the season if he performs well.
Being without Brownlee for any length would be a blow to the Jets. The 25-year-old defender leads all of New York's defense with 110 slot snaps , according to Pro Football Focus , with the next closest player being Jamien Sherwood at 23. On top of that, Brownlee's 82.6 tackling grade and 74.0 coverage grade are top-20 marks among cornerbacks this season.
Along with his 18 snaps, Ponds played 14 of those in the slot and recorded a run stop despite failing to come away with a pick or defended pass. While he made little overall impact in relief of Brownlee, that isn't to say he can't in Glenn's secondary.
After all, Ponds had 167 total tackles and seven interceptions (two for a touchdown) in his collegiate career at Indiana and posted the eighth-best overall grade (88.8) out of 895 qualified CBs last season , per PFF .
That is a good indicator of what he is capable of doing when the snaps are coming his way, even if his 5'8" frame is smaller than most at his position. This is also a secondary that did not exactly play well in the Windy City against Bears backup QB Tyson Bagent, although All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick did his part by coming away with the team's first interception in 636 pass attempts (h/t NFL).
Minkah Fitzpatrick gives the Jets their first INT in 636 pass attempts NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CQUCl4JVnt
Aside from that, this group was not at its best collectively throughout the game and contributed to two of the three interceptions from Bagent that were ultimately negated due to penalties. One of those was on Ponds, who was called for holding on a third-and-eight with just over six minutes remaining and gifted the Bears a fresh set of downs, as they would go on to run the final 9:16 off the clock on an 18-play, 76-yard drive to end the game.
Although Ponds only allowed one reception for 21 yards, he committed two penalties and struggled in coverage. That said, he also found success against the run, earning a respectable 65.7 run-defense grade from PFF. So, there was certainly enough in a limited role to suggest the rookie can become a quality contributor to this defense and provide a spark if he takes on a larger role.
Along with his run-defense skills, Ponds has the versatility to play in the slot and on the perimeter and was someone coming into the season with the potential to become a Year 1 starter . To be fair, this could be an opportunity that could lead to even more playing time down the road, considering Brownlee's snap count in the slot has decreased in each passing game:
For now, Brownlee's status is up in the air, as he must clear the NFL's five-stage concussion protocol . If Ponds can use this opportunity to his advantage and put his best foot forward, the Jets' rookie could set himself up for additional playing time as the season continues.

title: Jets Need to Stop Making the Same Garrett Wilson Mistake to Save Their Season
full_text:
It's safe to say the Jets' effort against the Bears in Week 4 was a mixed bag , featuring more bad than good.
On one hand, for the first time in 21 games, the Jets finally recorded an interception. On the other hand, the lengthy drought ended in another double-digit loss, as the Bears dominated Gang Green, 23-12 , at Soldier Field.
Nothing went right on either side. The Jets' defense allowed an atrocious 232 rushing yards and was on the field for over 42 minutes. The offense wasn’t any better, registering just 157 yards and going zero for seven on third down.
New York’s offensive failure can be attributed, in large part, to its inability to get Garrett Wilson involved. The former Ohio State standout had been the Jets' go-to guy through the first three weeks and is coming off an incredible performance against the Lions, where he recorded 10 catches (13 targets) for 105 yards and a touchdown.
Against the Bears, however, Wilson was targeted just four times, recording three catches for 27 yards. His lack of targets was awfully surprising, considering the Jets were without four of their six best pass catchers, including running back Breece Hall.
After Sunday's loss, Wilson made it clear that he wants to be involved more .
“ I just take a lot of pride in when the ball does come my way, making a play on it ,” Wilson told reporters (h/t SNY Jets). “Being a receiver, being one of the guys this organization believes in, long-term contract with them. And when the ball come my way, I got to make the play, and yeah, I’ll say that. I want more on my plate, for sure.”
"I take a lot of pride in when the ball does come my way, making a play on it...I want more on my plate, for sure" - Garrett Wilson pic.twitter.com/zwXuEnR6rM
With New York amidst a three-game losing streak, the coaching staff must find more ways to get the ball in Wilson’s hands before it’s too late.
The Jets understand that they won’t win games if Wilson isn’t a factor. When head coach Aaron Glenn was asked about his limited involvement, he acknowledged that the team needs to find ways to get him more opportunities.
“ That’s a good question ," Glenn said (h/t SNY Jets). "We have to find a way to try and get him the ball. He’s basically one of the engines that get us going.”
Glenn’s comments put the responsibility on offensive coordinator Frank Reich to find creative ways to get Wilson more touches. While his usage against Chicago was disappointing, Reich has done just that, as Wilson ranks ninth in receptions (24) and is tied for 16th in targets with 31. Still, his target count has been all over the place:
Week 1: 23-10 win @ Titans
Week 2: 20-17 OT loss vs. Packers
Week 3: 31-24 loss @ Lions
Week 4: 23-12 loss @ Bears
If you remove Week 3, Wilson averaged only six targets in his other appearances, which is a major drop from his career average of just over nine.
Reich needs to figure out how to fully utilize Wilson more consistently while also prioritizing spreading the ball around.
“ We want to get Garrett a lot of targets ,” Reich said (h/t Jets). “I promise you, the number one guy in the progression is gonna be him on more plays than anybody else.”
Garrett Wilson 🤝 masterpiece pic.twitter.com/4bPQ7t4ntk
Although Reich makes it clear that he wants to target Wilson, the next step is figuring out how to maximize the Jets' WR1.
According to Pro Football Focus, Wilson has lined up out wide on 79.7% of his snaps and in the slot on just 20.3%. This marks the first time in his career that he has lined up in the slot on fewer than 30% of his snaps.
While this change is a result of Wilson wanting to be used more on the outside, Reich shouldn’t exclusively use him as a boundary receiver. Putting Wilson in the slot for 10 to 15 plays a game can create favorable matchups and give him more opportunities to make plays with the ball in his hands.
Wilson has recorded just 39 yards after the catch this season, so finding ways to get him the ball in open space should be at the top of the Jets' priority list. Whether it’s screen passes or quick throws, Reich must find ways to use Wilson’s athleticism to move the chains instead of always relying on him to create separation and win downfield.
Speaking of deep shots, Wilson has been targeted 20 or more yards just three times. He’s proven throughout his five-year career that he can win one-on-one opportunities with the best of them, and this season, Wilson has posted an 88.9% contested-catch rate per PFF .
This one isn’t entirely on Reich, as he’s dialed up some downfield shots. Some of the responsibility falls on quarterback Geno Smith. Known for his aggressive downfield approach, Smith must trust that Wilson is going to come down with it.
The Jets don’t need to force-feed Wilson every play, but there’s no reason Wilson shouldn’t be getting at least eight targets a game. Getting him more involved isn’t just about keeping him happy ; it’s about giving the Jets their best chance at winning.
Sitting at 1-3 with the Browns and Patriots up next, the Jets must get a win soon, or their season could be over before October ends. That means making Wilson the absolute offensive focal point sooner rather than later.

title: 5 Jets Officially on Thin Ice After Crushing Loss to Bears (Will McDonald IV's Outlook Plummets)
full_text:
Through four games to begin the 2026 NFL season, the Jets own an uninspiring 1-3 record. Losing to the Bears on Sunday marked their third straight loss , leaving Gang Green in danger of seeing their season slip away before it even begins.
There are a number of reasons why the Jets have struggled as of late , and rising pressure and expectations have left five players and coaches on thin ice heading into Week 5 and beyond.
Let's dive into that list.
When the Jets first acquired Jowon Briggs last offseason, the team hoped he would be the kind of consistent interior pass rusher they needed . Four games into his first full year with the team, and not only has Briggs struggled, but he's been borderline unplayable throughout the year.
Briggs ranks as the 114th-best defensive tackle in the game this year , with a grade of 44.5 on Pro Football Focus . His pressure rate sits at 137th in the league. His run defense, always considered a weakness before, has him ranked 123rd at his position.
In short, Briggs is unplayable right now. Unless something changes, this acquisition could end up being a bust in its second year.
We know sacks come in bunches for Will McDonald IV. We also know that he is in a key contract year and needs to show something on the field to be worthy of getting a long-term extension .
Instead, McDonald has been almost like a ghost on the field. Sure, he recorded the only pressure recorded by Jets edge rushers on Sunday, but he remains a weakness in run defense and isn't making enough impact plays when it comes to getting close to the quarterback.
It's safe to say McDonald has been one of the more consistent players on the defense simply because he's stayed healthy and isn't terrible, but for a first-round pick and someone who wants a new deal, production has to follow.
And there's been nothing close to that so far.
Remember when the Jets signed Joseph Ossai in free agency to a deal worth $13 million per year? The argument was that Ossai simply didn't play enough, but he was a solid rotational piece with the Bengals, recording five sacks in each of the last two years.
Through two games, Ossai, like McDonald, has been a nonfactor .
Through two games and 85 snaps, Ossai has zero pressures, zero quarterback hits, zero sacks, nine tackles, and has been one of the worst run stoppers on the team. That's not going to cut it if the Jets hope to get the most out of him.
So far, Ossai has looked more like Carl Lawson than Trey Hendrickson. While he missed most of camp with an injury, there's gotta be more production going forward.
It has not been a very good reunion for Jets linebacker and captain Demario Davis. The 37-year-old was called for multiple penalties in Sunday's loss and looked slow in coverage.
To summarize, it looks like Father Time has finally caught up with him.
PFF has Davis graded as the 64th-ranked linebacker (51.0) out of 74 qualified players in the NFL so far this season. He's also been credited with seven missed tackles this season.
The Jets are stuck with Davis for the remainder of the season. They have no one who can confidently get the rest of the unit lined up correctly, and he's still an important locker-room presence. But when an elite player loses a step, it tends to be obvious and cascades into further struggles.
The worse Davis plays, the harder it will be for the Jets to claim that his leadership alone is enough to keep him on the field.
It truly is now or never for the Jets coaching staff.
Many fans will point to the start the 2022 Lions had (1-6) before they rattled off a bunch of wins, but the Jets don't necessarily have the kind of schedule to help them as head coach Aaron Glenn's former team did.
If the Jets are going to turn into a winner, they can not afford to wait until the latter months of the season. It has to happen now. Glenn is 4-17 through 21 games . That isn't going to cut it at all.
And that goes for the entire coaching staff. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich cannot have some games where the offense looks competent and others—like on Sunday—where the Jets fail to pick up a single third-down conversion.
While the defensive numbers have been better than last season, Gang Green is getting killed by elite offenses.
It's not enough to accept those results. They have to be better. And with the team already 1-3, it isn't exactly rocket science to point out why the coaching staff is on thin ice.

title: The Biggest Decision Aaron Glenn Got Wrong Against Bears (And What It Means Moving Forward)
full_text:
Unlike the previous two games, when the Jets put up a valiant effort and suffered close losses to the Packers and Lions, respectively, it was a totally different story on Sunday in a 23-12 loss to the Bears that was not nearly as close as the final score would indicate following a fourth-quarter touchdown.
The late TD connection from quarterback Geno Smith to wide receiver Isaiah Williams was a rare bright spot in an otherwise abysmal offensive performance, but aside from that, the Jets were 0-of-7 on third down and were outgained 492-157 in what turned out to be a clear mismatch on the field.
Once again, though, a lot of the blame rests on the shoulders of head coach Aaron Glenn , whose defense could not get off the field on Sunday and allowed the Bears to pick up more first downs (34) than the number of plays the Jets offense ran for the entire game (32).
One week after keeping pace with the explosive Lions offense, a number of mental mistakes and an inability to contain Chicago's league-leading rushing attack proved costly in a disappointing all-around effort .
With three straight losses to their credit, it is time for Glenn and his staff to get this team back on the right track before the season is officially lost. After another missed opportunity in the Windy City, there are some decisions that Glenn will want back and areas to  improve on moving forward.
There are a number of areas the Jets would like to correct in hindsight, but something that especially bit Glenn and his defense was situational discipline. The Jets committed 12 penalties for 76 yards and had three potential interceptions negated due to penalties, two of which occurred on Chicago's final drive of the game and allowed the Bears to run the clock out on an 18-play, 76-yard drive that took up the final 9:16 of the game.
Glenn had some familiarity with Bears HC Ben Johnson during his time as defensive coordinator with the Lions, as the latter served as the offensive coordinator on those same teams. That did not seem to matter, as the Bears ran an absurd 89 plays to New York's 32 and completely dominated the time of possession, 42:45-17:15.
It was a lousy coaching performance , to say the least, from both sides of the ball as offensive coordinator Frank Reich failed to establish any level of consistency offensively and barely involved WR1 Garrett Wilson at all, with just three catches for 27 yards. While the offensive line's continued struggles and a disastrous showing from QB Geno Smith limited that group and kept them from establishing any momentum in the game, Glenn's defense did not exactly do anything to take the pressure off of them, either.
Granted, All-Pro safety Minkah Fitzpatrick came away with the Jets' first interception in 636 pass attempts (h/t NFL) and provided a spark to a struggling unit. That said, the defense still allowed backup QB Tyson Bagent to throw for a career-high 268 yards and an average of 7.9 yards per attempt, and Glenn was not about to let the long-awaited interception overshadow the frustrating loss and hide the issues that obviously exist on this team.
Minkah Fitzpatrick gives the Jets their first INT in 636 pass attempts NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CQUCl4JVnt
The inability to get off the field on third down was frustrating on both sides of the ball, but it was clear coming into this game that Chicago was going to utilize a ground-and-pound approach with its stout ground game. It did not seem to matter, as the Bears totaled 232 rushing yards, including 146 yards and two TDs from Kyle Monangai.
Offensively, the lack of a consistent run game (14 carries for 59 yards) made the Jets more one-dimensional and prevented them from sustaining drives and keeping the clock moving. It was the complete opposite on the other side, as the defense had no answer for Chicago's rushing attack.
Simply put, an unwillingness to adjust to certain aspects of the game plagued the coaching staff, particularly Glenn's defense. Sure, Bagent was efficient, but if the Jets had tightened up their rush defense and at least put some more pressure on the Bears' backup QB to beat them by himself, that would have likely led to more opportunities for Gang Green to exploit.
As a Week 5 meeting with the Browns looms at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, time continues to tick as it relates to Glenn's future in Gang Green if he cannot start turning things around fast.
It is easy to point blame at the Jets' offense for not sustaining drives against the Bears, but the defense gave up seven drives of at least nine plays and did absolutely nothing to provide any optimism. From the costly penalties to the lack of run defense, Bagent could essentially do what he wanted and never really faced much adversity becasue New York beat itself.
In years past, a game against the Browns would have seemed like an opportunity, and it still could if the Jets can get their act together and overcome the injury bug that continues to plague them . That said, QB Deshaun Watson has looked more like himself from his days with the Texans and has this Browns team in first place in the AFC North through four games, with a pair of talented 2026 draft picks, Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, to throw the ball to.
As someone who already entered the season on the hot seat, it is now or never for Glenn to save his career in Gotham. Going forward, Glenn needs to make discipline a huge priority for his defense to ensure the offense can get into a better rhythm, regardless of the opponent.

title: Jets Rookie & Sophomore Week 5 Power Rankings: (D’Angelo Ponds, Azareye’h Thomas Continue to Rise)
full_text:
Unfortunately for Jets fans, Sunday’s 23-12 loss to the Bears was more than a nightmare . Even with the Bears relying on backup Tyson Bagent, Chicago steamrolled the Jets, dominating time of possession and the line of scrimmage.
Although it was another rough outing for New York, several rookies and second-year players played well and showed some flashes in the loss.
Others, meanwhile, saw their stock take a hit.
With that in mind, let’s take a look at where every Jets rookie and sophomore ranks heading into Week 5.
Note: Anez Cooper and VJ Payne are currently excluded from the list. Both Cooper and Payne are on injured reserve but are eligible to return after missing the first four games of the season.
After suffering a torn ACL in Week 2, Arian Smith won’t play for the rest of the season. But with each passing game, his future with New York is on the line.
Since he didn’t establish a role on offense in his two years with the organization, Smith must watch the Jets’ receivers get opportunities to earn a role. While he’s recovering, players could pass him on the depth chart and make it even more difficult for him to find a role once he returns.
We may have already seen the last of Smith in green and white.
The Jets got their first underwhelming game from Geno Smith. Attempting just 15 passes, Smith completed eight of them for 119 yards and a touchdown.
Even though Smith wasn’t productive or efficient, we can’t put all the blame on him. Three of the top five pass catchers on the team didn’t play, and the receivers who did play weren’t able to create much separation.
Additionally, the Bears dominated time of possession, and as a result, New York wasn’t able to get into any rhythm. Despite falling to 1-3, New York won’t turn to Cade Klubnik anytime soon.
There’s no reason to cut the cord on Smith yet, as he continues to provide competent play at quarterback. For now, the rookie will remain on the sidelines.
For the second straight week, Kiko Mauigoa was sidelined with a quadriceps injury. Even if the second-year linebacker out of the University of Miami played, he wouldn’t have changed the outcome, as he’s played exclusively on special teams in the first two games.
However, he could have made his season debut on defense. With the game out of reach in the fourth quarter and the Bears controlling the clock, there was no point in keeping Demario Davis or Jamien Sherwood in.
If Mauigoa suited up, he could have given them a breather while also having an opportunity to prove his value in limited snaps. Instead, New York continues to deploy two linebackers.
Another week, another Malachi Moore special teams tackle. The second-year player out of the University of Alabama has emerged as one of the more productive players, registering four tackles across four games.
While he’s proven to be a core contributor to the special teams, he remains a non-factor on defense. In the last two weeks, Moore hasn’t appeared in a single defensive snap, and he played just one snap in Minkah Fitzpatrick’s absence.
With how well the safeties Fitzpatrick, Andre Cisco and Dane Belton are playing, Moore will remain a depth option until further notice.
If there’s one thing we learned in the Jets' loss to the Bears, it’s that they need their pass-catchers need to get healthy fast. Without Omar Cooper Jr., Adonai Mitchell, and Mason Taylor, the offense struggled to get into a rhythm, recording just 119 passing yards and failing to convert on seven third-down attempts.
Although Cooper wouldn’t have made a substantial difference, they could’ve used the playmaking ability he showcased in Week 1 against the Titans to help their offense get into rhythm.
Unfortunately, fans must continue to wait for his return, as Cooper must miss one more game before being eligible to come off injured reserve. But that doesn’t mean he’ll be back in Week 6, as Cooper will only play if his ankle is healed.
Hopefully, Cooper’s recovery has gone smoothly, because this team needs him back ASAP.
Heading into this game, it was unclear whether New York would use D’Angelo Ponds in a depth role or give him more snaps. For the most part, Ponds was on the sideline but saw an expanded role once Jarvis Brownlee Jr. went down.
Ponds appeared in 18 defensive snaps, logging three tackles. While he proved to be a factor against the run, recording two stops and earning a 65.7 run-defense grade , per Pro Football Focus , he struggled in coverage.
Although he gave up just one reception for 21 yards, he committed two penalties, one of which negated what would’ve been his first career interception. It was an up-and-down game for the former Indiana Hoosier, but he showed enough to suggest he can be a quality contributor moving forward.
Sunday’s game was a learning curve for the rookie, and we should expect a bounce-back game against the Browns.
It’s been a rough start to Year 2 for Mason Taylor.
After leading the team in receptions last year with 44, Taylor hasn’t been nearly as impactful, recording two catches (three targets) for negative two yards across two games. New York’s additions to the receiver and tight end rooms play into this; however, the former LSU Tiger just hasn’t looked like his former self.
On top of that, he’s missed the last two games after suffering a thumb injury against the Packers. With multiple pass catchers sidelined and the offense struggling to move the ball downfield against the Bears, the Jets need Taylor back and, hopefully, to return to the form he showed as a rookie.
Darrell Jackson Jr. continues to receive an increased workload. After playing 23 snaps against the Lions, Jackson logged 41 snaps against Chicago and recorded four tackles.
While he bounced back from his quiet game against Detroit, he did, however, commit a costly facemask penalty on the first drive, which moved the Bears up from the 30-yard line to the 15.
The former Florida State Seminole hasn’t stood out or made much of an impact yet, but considering that his snap count keeps going up each week, it’s evident the coaching staff wants him on the field.
Hopefully, with more reps and as the season progresses, Jackson can develop into the contributor the Jets envision he can be.
Things were looking up at this time last week. Kenyon Sadiq introduced himself to the NFL world, recording seven receptions for 105 yards and a touchdown.
With his impressive performance , Gang Green fans anticipated that the former Oregon Duck would be just as involved in the game plan against Chicago. Those hopes were crushed rather quickly, as Sadiq finished the day with zero receptions on three targets.
Although it’s disappointing that Sadiq wasn’t able to provide a spark, we can’t expect him to post career highs every week. With Sadiq being a rookie, he’s going to experience the highs and the lows.
Besides bouncing back against the Browns, the best we can hope is that Sadiq steadily progresses throughout the season and stays healthy.
AZ Thomas has been one of the few standout players for the Jets this season.
Through four games, the second-year player from Florida State has excelled in coverage, allowing just 17 receptions (21 targets) for 123 yards and two touchdowns. His strong play in coverage continued against the Bears, allowing just three catches (four targets) for 20 yards.
Despite this, Thomas committed a costly hands-to-the-face penalty in the first quarter, which negated an interception by T’Vondre Sweat and led to Chicago taking an early 7-0 lead.
While his three penalties in the last three games are somewhat of a concern, it shouldn’t erase how impactful he’s been against the pass, earning a 72.4 coverage grade , per PFF , ranking 17th out of 101 qualifying cornerbacks.
If he can clean up the penalties and continue building on his quality play in coverage, Thomas could potentially climb up in the rankings.

title: Under Microscope After 21 Games: Analyzing If Jets' Aaron Glenn Is a Good Head Coach
full_text:
Aaron Glenn has been the head coach of the Jets for 21 games after Week 4's loss to the Bears . It hasn't even been two seasons. To some fans, the push for patience is clear; the team was never going to be able to magically become a winner after a single season.
To others who are watching other coaches around the league find success, though, patience has just about run out.
And it seemed to reach a tipping point in the Jets' 23-12 loss at the hands of the Bears on Sunday. New York was dominated by a Chicago squad missing their starting quarterback and left tackle. Chicago came into the game with one of the most high-powered offenses in the league, with a head coach who Glenn coached with in Detroit.
If anyone knew how to defend the Ben Johnson scheme, it would be Glenn.
Instead, New York's defense gave up nearly 500 yards of total offense and 232 yards on the ground. Adding insult to injury, the team committed 12 penalties and failed to convert a single third down offensively—areas that are under the microscope with Glenn as a no-nonsense coach who has already changed his offensive coordinator once since taking the top job.
Now, the Jets sit at 1-3. They are running out of time to prove to the world that things are different this time around. And Glenn's record as coach, compared to others around the league in a similar boat, leaves one question in mind:
Can he ever become a good head coach?
You are what your record says you are in the NFL. For Glenn, his record tells much of the story. Through 21 games, the Jets are 4-17 under Glenn. They have more than twice as many double-digit losses during this time (10) as they do wins (4).
To fully understand those numbers, here is the record of the list of coaches who were hired during the same cycle as
And here is the record of coaches who were hired in this cycle.
It is not a good look for Glenn that 1) he has the least number of wins of the remaining coaches during his cycle, and 2) that six coaches in this year's cycle have nearly matched his win total in just four games.
Many coaches didn't walk into the same situation, of course, but Glenn was the one who wanted the Jets job. He wanted to be the man to fix the organization. Through a season and four games, the team clearly has not been good enough.
And the numbers tell of a coach who is more than just struggling. He's failing to do the thing Jets fans have been begging for for more than 15 years .
Jets fans may not want to hear it, especially after such a dismal loss on Sunday, but there are still good things that the team has done so far this year. Despite the poor numbers, New York's defense was very good in the red zone on Sunday, holding the Bears to just two offensive touchdowns.
Glenn also didn't sugarcoat his frustration with what has been another three-game losing streak for the Jets under his watch.
"Very disappointed on a number of different levels," Glenn said. "We have too many people that want to think about history.  We just have to circle the wagons and not let any of that come inside our locker room. We've been working our butts off to change that."
Glenn is far more accepting of his failings and where the team needs to improve than past coaches who have donned the Jets colors in the past. While that does not excuse the lack of success, it does highlight an acknowledgment of where he hasn't been up to par.
The other positive for Glenn is that the locker room remains tight-knit and behind Glenn. There is no inkling of a mutiny or overall frustration at any level. The team is behind their coach.
Until that changes, it will be a positive for Glenn, and even veterans like safety Minkah Fitzpatrick know that.
"I've been in this situation many times before, and I know the most important thing to focus on in these moments is our execution," Minkah Fitzpatrick said on Sunday. "It's also important to look at ourselves and say, and be real and acknowledge that this isn't working. We've got to stop doing it or find a way to do it better."
New York is not about to fire Glenn before the season ends. That doesn't appear even close to happening at this time. It means the Jets and Glenn will have 13 additional chances to prove to their fans and the rest of the league that they are better than the results they showed on Sunday.
There is even past precedent on Glenn's side to show a bad loss like this can be overcome.
In Detroit, Dan Campbell started his second season 1-6 after a dismal three-win campaign the year before. During their slow stretch in 2022, the Lions were shut out in a game by the Patriots and lost a three-score game to the Cowboys. In many ways, Glenn's first two years are matching Campbell's in Detroit more and more by the day.
But the Lions still won eight of their last 10 games of the season that year. Can the Jets even get to half of those wins throughout the remaining slate of their schedule? It's not as though the organization has proven it can at this point, but Glenn is confident better days are ahead.
The Jets have upcoming contests against the Browns, Raiders and Patriots. Their margin for error has evaporated with their 1-3 start. Wins must begin piling up, or the seat will only get harder for Glenn going forward.
With a record of 4-17, there isn't much left to say about the Glenn regime in New York. It looks similar to the Robert Saleh regime, the Adam Gase regime, or the Todd Bowles regime. The point is, until this team wins and looks competent, questions surrounding the coach will continue to grow.
And in this case, Glenn won't have many chances to get the ship righted.

title: 3 Eagles on the Trade Block in October
full_text:
It has been a long time since the future of the Philadelphia Eagles has been as clouded as it is right now.
Perhaps that is what happens when a franchise cornerstone retires as a losing streak begins to form. Lane Johnson calling it a career stunned Philadelphia sports fans, but also leaves a massive vacuum for the team moving forward.
And there are still 13 more games left to play in the 2026 season.
With Johnson gone, the Eagles' holes along the offensive line will remain a problem. They are dealing with a plethora of injuries that could derail their season across the board. As the trade deadline draws near, the Eagles are in a rare position.
If their hobbled roster cannot right the ship soon, it might be time for general manager Howie Roseman to trade some talent in order to gain extra draft picks for the future. A true tear-down for a team that, just two years ago, was the most dominant playoff champion in NFL history.
Much of Philadelphia's current core will be safe, but three names in particular could be traded if things don't get better. Let's get to that list now.
For the last two years, it has seemed like the Eagles weren't willing to give a long-term extension to their star tight end, but also didn't have a good backup plan behind him either. With Eli Stowers on injured reserve, it's hard to count on him to fill that role either.
That said, Goedert is on an expiring deal and could be looking for a chance to win another Super Bowl. With other contending offenses in need of tight end help, the Eagles could get quality draft compensation for one of the more complete tight ends in the league.
Remember, the Eagles traded Zach Ertz in 2021 in similar circumstances. The same fate could be coming for Goedert.
Philadelphia has already extended Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter. That leaves former seventh-round pick Moro Ojomo as the odd man out. Ojomo, like Milton Williams before him, is going to command a massive long-term deal in free agency this offseason. It won't be in Philadelphia.
While the Eagles could wait for a third-round compensatory pick, it wouldn't hurt the team if they tried to pry a second-round pick out of a contending team in need of an excellent defensive tackle. Ojomo hasn't recorded a sack this season, but has been doubled more than Carter along the line.
He's an excellent player who could make a contending team very happy.
During the offseason, the Eagles signed Woolen to complete an elite cornerback trio with Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. So far, the secondary has been pretty solid through four games despite some late-game hiccups over the last few contests.
On an expiring deal, and looking for a chance to compete for another title, the Eagles could look to get anything from Woolen on the trade market. It would open up a need on the outside opposite Mitchell, but the lure of adding a draft pick will be too much.

title: 3 Free Agents the Eagles Should Call to Help Replace Lane Johnson
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles opened the new week looking to rebound from back-to-back losses to the Chicago Bears and Los Angeles Rams, in which they were outscored a combined 51-27. Before Tuesday was even over, Philadelphia had a new problem to navigate heading into Week 5: star right tackle Lane Johnson's NFL retirement .
Eagles fans knew Johnson wouldn't be around forever, but many assumed that the future Pro Football Hall of Famer would at least stick around until the end of the 2026 campaign. Instead, the beloved fan favorite did what was best for him and his family, ultimately walking away from football and the franchise to prioritize his mental health, as made clear in his retirement letter posted on social media .
Third-round rookie tackle Markel Bell made his first NFL start against the Rams last week, and while he was decent, the Eagles should add more depth now that Johnson is no longer an option. The pickings might be slim, but there are at least three free-agent tackles for the Eagles to target as they attempt to navigate a major loss.
Former Pro Bowl tackle Taylor Decker is still a free agent as the fifth week of the season begins. The former 2016 first-round pick has spent all 10 seasons of his career with the Detroit Lions, even signing a three-year extension ahead of the 2024 campaign. That partnership ended in March, though, when Detroit approved Decker's release request, with the ex-Ohio State Buckeye citing that the two sides "could not find common ground."
Even though he hasn't played Week 18 of the 2025 season, rolling the dice on Decker is still worth the effort for the Eagles. It wasn't at the same level as his Pro Bowl performance, but Decker was still solid across 894 offensive snaps with the Lions last season, allowing only two sacks and 33 total pressures en route to a 69.5 pass-block grade on Pro Football Focus . Not even close to Johnson's level, but then again, who would be?
Decker has exclusively played left tackle throughout his pro career, but the Lions occasionally used him on the right side. You can't always teach an old dog new tricks, but maybe Decker would be willing if the potential of challenging for a Super Bowl with Philadelphia is alluring enough. Bell and Fred Johnson (when healthy) can also hold down the fort at RT until Decker gets up to speed.
Throw in the fact that the Eagles had clear interest in Decker leading up to the 2016 draft over a decade ago, and it makes sense in the world to give him a call.
If the Eagles want someone with more RT experience, Jack Conklin could be there guy.
Conklin is another free agent with a solid list of accomplishments, which includes first-team All-Pro appearances in 2016 and 2020. Injuries have limited him to single-digit appearances in three of the five previous seasons, but that doesn't mean the 32-year-old right tackle can't be a decent contributor for head coach Nick Sirianni & Co.
Conklin was a disaster in pass protection last season, but he was actually playable as a run blocker, finishing with a 67.1 run-block grade —a higher mark than he had in two of the three seasons before that. He also allowed only five pressures (one sack) in his last three games after surrendering 19 (three sacks) in his first five, making it clear that he was improving until his season-ending concussion.
Also, there might be some familiarity between Conklin and Sirianni's staff after the Eagles-Browns joint practices during the 2025 preseason. Every small connection counts when teams are desperate for help.
Former 2022 seventh-round pick Thayer Munford Jr. is looking for a fresh start after a whirlwind ride to begin his NFL career. The Ohio State product spent the first three seasons of his career in Las Vegas before bouncing between the Patriots, Browns, and Pats again throughout the 2025 calendar year.
All five of his appearances came in a New England jersey, and though he didn't do enough to stick around, Mundford's performance could land him on Philly's radar. The 27-year-old allowed one pressure (a QB hit) on 40 pass-blocking downs, ending the season with a career-best 75.9 grade on PFF . Was it a smaller-than-usual sample size? Yes, but that gives the Eagles every reason to see what he can do in an expanded role.
With the ability to play both tackle spots and inline tight end, Munford is the kind of Swiss Army knife Sirianni should want to have on his roster.

title: Learning Curve About To Begin: It's Time To See What Eagles Have In Third-Round Pick
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Talk about replacing Lane Johnson came up the last few springs when the NFL Draft got closer. Then the draft arrived, and the first round would come and go without that replacement.
The last offensive tackle they took in the first round was seven years ago, when they moved up to select Andre Dillard in 2019. That didn’t work out well. The last time the Eagles went tackle in the first round before Dillard? Johnson in 2013, and that worked out better than great.
Maybe they found their answer in the third round this past spring when they took offensive tackle Markel Bell in the third round, using the pick they received by trading Haason Reddick to the New York Jets on March 29, 2024.
It could be Bell time now that Johnson has decided to retire after nearly 14 years in the NFL, all with the Eagles. Fred Johnson is still a possibility, though he has a knee injury that he is working through. Plus, the Eagles and everyone else know what Fred Johnson is. Bell is a great unknown, and it should be time to start finding out about him.
The rookie was thrown into the fire on Sunday when Lane Johnson woke up that morning unable to play. Sean Mannion said the game plan remained the same despite Bell not preparing like a starter during the week of practice.
“Nothing changed,” said the offensive coordinator. “Markel, he's been working his tail off. He's been up every game so far this year and stepped in and did some nice things. It was obviously kind of thrust in the moment, his first NFL start, but he's been preparing. He's been ready to go all year.”
He may end up going for the rest of the year. Still, it was just his first start. Johnson made 171 of those. There will be start-up costs.
The bigger issue in the short-term is Fred Johnon’s health. He has been the team’s top reserve behind Lane and Jordan Mailata. If Bell has to start – and he will likely do that – the Eagles don’t have a backup if Fred cannot play.
That would require a practice squad elevation, probably John Ojukwu. Kiram Amegadjie could also be a possibility. He was a third-round pick of the Bears out of Yale in 2024, and a player the Eagles showed interest in leading up that year’s draft.
Whatever the answer is, the Eagles’ offensive line is much different now than what was expected only a month ago. Landon Dickerson is out, and the Eagles moved Cam Jurgens to left guard and inserted Drew Kendall at center. Now, Jurgens may not be available after he self-reported a concussion on Monday morning and is in concussion protocol. If he cannot play, the Eagles could turn to either Willie Lampkin or rookie Micah Morris.
Not only is the line impacted, but the Eagles offense will already be without Tank Bigsby and could be without DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, and Dallas Goedert.
“It's part of the game and feel good about our roster from top to bottom and guys have been practicing hard, guys have been stepping up,” said Mannion. “I feel confident with all the guys that have been thrust in action. There's no flinch in them. They don't blink. They're ready to go in and execute. They're well prepared by our staff. They put in a ton of hard work and effort every day in practice. They're attentive in the meetings.
“It's the unfortunate part of this game; guys may go down, but guys are right behind them, and they've been working quietly, preparing themselves, and they're ready to go.”

title: Eagles Lane Johnson Says Goodbye, Retires From Football After Nearly 14 Seasons
full_text:
Just like that, Lane Johnson is done. There wasn’t a two-week notice, or even a two-month head-up. The Eagles right tackle, 36, released a statement on Tuesday afternoon that he is officially retiring after 13 years and three games.
This was going to happen sooner or later. It wasn’t supposed to happen until the end of Year 14, when Johnson said this would “probably” be his final season. Yet, here it is, two days after he informed the Eagles on Sunday morning, hours before they kicked off against the Los Angeles Rams, that he would be unable to play due to personal matters.
Longtime friend and teammate Brandon Graham spilled the beans on Sunday evening during an Eagles show that Johnson was considering retiring immediately. Graham was right.
Johnson said in a statement: “I’ve given it my all for 14 years; season after season pushing my body to the max and tirelessly working my craft to not only live up to the legacy of the guys that came before me, but to set a new standard of success for the best franchise in all of sports.”
Thank you. 🦅 pic.twitter.com/up2kH1K40p
Johnson cited the need to continue to focus on his mental health and to spend more time with his kids and family.
“I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year to take the field with my brothers for one last season, but after a lot of reflection, I’ve realized that my personal and family priorities in my life have changed," he said. "Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health. I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization, and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game, and right now my heart is telling me that it’s time to say goodbye to football.”
Johnson is a two-time Super Bowl champion and cited the two championship parades as highlights of his career.
“Riding up Broad Street as a world champion, not once, but twice, and seeing the city in all its glory was the ultimate privilege; I’ll never forget,” he said.
pic.twitter.com/T39yp5Phnd
In addition to the two Super Bowls he helped deliver, Johnson was a six-time Pro Bowler and five-time All-Pro. He ranks eight in all-time games played with the Eagles at 171, all of which were starts.
The clock can now begin to tick on what could, and should, be an induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
“Lane Johnson is an all-time Eagle and one of the best players ever to play his position in NFL history,” owner Jeffrey Lurie said in a statement. “Lane was a major contributor to our team’s success for 14 seasons, helping to bring two Super Bowl championships and many other memorable moments to the organization and the city of Philadelphia.”
