title: Why We Could See More From Eagles Rookie After A "Solid" Debut
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Nick Sirianni talked to the media via Zoom in his day-after-game news conference and said he was "pleased" with the play of Cam Jurgens in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Then came news that Jurgens self-reported concussion-like symptoms on Monday.
Whehter that happened before or after Sirianni spoke is unclear. The coach never mentioned it, though NFL rules surrounding concussion protocol may not have allowed him to say anything at that point.
Sirianni said this: “I'm pleased with where Cam is. Obviously, we didn't put out there the product that we want to put out there offensively yesterday, and then also combine that with a loss. There's going to be plays he wants back, but there's good moments also. I think that's the consistency of everybody, from our coaches to our players, has to be the thing that continues to rise. That's Cam, that's everybody. But Cam is definitely doing good things and like us all, got to be more consistent at times as well.
Perhaps that explains Jurgens' subpar play, which was highlighted in several social media clips. One showed him blowing up a crucial third-and-goal from the 2 as the Eagles looked to go up 17 points. He pulled to his right and knocked the ball loose from Jalen Hurts, who hung on, but it disrupted the timing of the play. A swarm of Rams tacklers stopped the quarterback in his tracks for no gain.
Another showed him missing badly on a block on a third-and-one sweep that lost five yards and led to a field goal.
Lane Johnson could be an even bigger story that is developing. The right tackle wasn’t able to play on Sunday due to personal reasons, something the team wasn’t aware of until only a couple of hours before the 1 p.m. kickoff. Afterward, former Eagles defensive lineman Brandon Graham said on a postgame show that Johnson could end up retiring immediately rather than wait until the end of his 14th NFL season.
Sirianni was asked on Monday if he knew anything more about Johnson’s situation.
“No update,” was all he said.
The reason for the late callout isn’t clear – whether it was due to his ongoing battle with anxiety and depression or something to do with his aging parents’ health, something he alluded to as the reason he missed time in training camp. Perhaps it's both - his parents' health triggering his anxiety and depression.
Johnson’s sudden absence thrust rookie third-round pick Markel Bell into the starting lineup, because veteran reserve Fred Johnson was ruled out 48 hours before the game with a knee injury.
If Johnson can’t get healthy, Bell could be in line for his second career start, albeit with better preparation and the bulk of first-team reps at practice.
“I think Markel did some really good things,” said Sirianni. “…by no means did he play a perfect game, but he did some really good things. I think that watching the tape with the team (Monday), he had some really good movement on some double teams, and second-level stuff that we were able to show (to the team during their rewatch of the game on Monday), and highlight and point out for his teammates to see. …I thought he was solid.”

title: Eagles RB Gloom: Tank Bigsby Headed To IR, Status Of Saquon Barkley Still Unknown
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Tank Bigsby is the first known casualty from Sunday’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Nick Sirianni doesn’t give health updates during his day-after-game press conferences, but word eventually leaks out. And it did with the Eagles’ running back.
NFL Media reported that Bigsby suffered a core muscle injury and will need surgery. He will be put on injured reserve. Ian Rapoport, who reported it, said the hope is Bigsby can be back in six weeks.
The Eagles had several key players knocked out of the game, too, in the 24-20 loss, including running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard (ankle), and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee).
Perhaps word will leak out with them as well.
The news on Bigsby broke less than two hours after Sirianni’s news conference. The Eagles head coach was asked about the plethora of injuries suffered in the defeat. Specifically, he was asked about Barkley.
“We'll see,” he said. “These guys are going through different things with treatment and all those different things. We'll see how everything responds and have more answers for you, probably Wednesday.
“I know he'll work to do everything he can do to get himself back. Obviously, he's a great player and a great teammate. We always need him on the field.”
This is already Barkley’s second injury this season. He suffered a shoulder stinger in the win at Tennessee in Week 2 and played just 12 snaps in that game. He has carried the ball 36 times for 182 yards and a healthy 5.1 yards per rush average. After scoring seven touchdowns last year, Barkley is still looking for his first of the season.
He is 29 now, so maybe that has factored into his injury-plagued season thus far, but when he has played, Barkley looked just as quick and explosive as he normally does.
Bigsby has been Barkley’s top backup for the past two years. He had 14 carries for 55 yards against the Rams and has 98 yards and a TD on 28 rushes for a 3.3-yard-per-carry average this season.
If Barkley cannot play against the Jaguars in London on Sunday, the Eagles will be down to just Will Shipley. They have three running backs on the practice squad who could be elevated for the game or added to the roster in place of Bigsby. They are Carson Steele and Dameon Pierce, who were both with the team throughout training camp, and Jaydon Blue, a fifth-round pick of the Dallas Cowboys last year who was released and claimed by Philly.

title: McMullen: No More Hedging; The Eagles Need To Commit  On Offense
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Nick Sirianni said the quiet part out loud after Sunday’s 24-20 collapse against the Los Angeles Rams.
An offseason of hype had some casting Sean Mannion, a relative novice, as the next great offensive mind in the NFL. If anything, the Eagles have taken another step back from the version of this offense Kevin Patullo was vilified for running.
“Obviously, it hasn’t been good enough,” Sirianni understated . “... You’re trying to make sure as you find out who you are that you’re playing with detail and you’re playing together and you’re playing with toughness, and we’ve still got a ways to go there and it’s obvious that we’re still trying to figure [an identity] out.”
Four games into a season quickly losing steam that sentiment felt more like a confession than a nod to a process with light showing at the end of a tunnel.
The numbers from Lincoln Financial Field made the confession unnecessary.
The Eagles managed 172 total yards, their lowest in a dozen years, and 68 net passing yards, their lowest in a regular-season game in 23 years. They went 0-for-12 on third down, the first time they have failed to convert a single third down since at least 2000, and they have now failed on 17 straight third downs dating to the second half in Chicago.
Quarterback Jalen Hurts finished 12-of-27 for 93 yards. The two touchdowns to Darius Cooper were gift-wrapped by the defense and special teams. The Eagles' second-half offense continues a historically poor run and ranks last in the league in points, yards, yards per play, and expected points added.
Hurts’s answer, repeated until it lost any real meaning, was “poor execution.” Execution is real, but it only matters when the plan is sound and the players fail to carry it out. What is happening to Philadelphia right now does not look like that.
Mannion’s scheme was sold as a Shanahan/McVay-like wide-zone, under-center attack that would keep defenses honest and better marry the run and the pass. Through four weeks, it is a disjointed mess and those coaches may want to sue for libel for being connected to this disaster.
The Eagles’ under-center snaps have produced negative EPA that ranks near the bottom of the league. Defenses stack the box when Hurts is under center. When Philadelphia falls into obvious pass downs, it is getting blitzed as if Brian Flores had been cloned by every opponent.
The deeper problem is the gap between the roster and the idea.
This is still a team that needs to be built around Hurts’s dual-threat ability, Saquon Barkley’s gravity, and a line that has been among the league’s best when healthy. Mannion has not yet turned any of that into anything viable in his version og whatever you want to dub this offense.
Until the Eagles decide who they are — a wide-zone team that lives under center, a Hurts-centric spread attack, or something in between — the “poor execution” line will be used as cover for the more basic failure. Nobody is sure what this is even supposed to look like.

title: Grading Each Position After Eagles Loss To Rams: Bad Marks Across The Board
full_text:
If Philadelphia Eagles losses couldn't get any worse, Nick Sirianni's team found a way .
The Eagles blew a 10-point fourth quarter lead in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams, a game they somehow led despite not having five starters on offense. This was a game the Eagles weren't supposed to win , yet they found a way to lose in the worst of ways.
The defense collapsed and the offense was worse. Nick Sirianni made questionable decisions , and the Eagles are 2-2 as a result.
The report card for this week is ugly, and it might be the ugliest report card of the year. Here are the position-by-position grades for this week:
This may be a generous grade for Jalen Hurts, given he finished 12-of-27 for 93 yards. Hurts averaged just 3.4 yards per attempt, but he also threw for two touchdowns and ended up with a 78.2 passer rating.
Hurts was 2-of-9 for 10 yards and a 39.6 passer rating in the second half -- 1.1 yards per attempt. He couldn't get anything moving on offense, but was also without DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson and Lane Johnson on offense.
While Hurts has to elevate the offense, this offense is an absolute mess. Hurts is a square peg in a round hole right now, and teh Eagles don't have the personnel to help him out.
The Eagles have failed Jalen Hurts with the way this offense was built, and Hurts has struggled to adapt.
When Saquon Barkley is out for the game on his second carry, it's going to be a poor day for the running backs. Tank Bigsby didn't have a bad day (14 carries, 55 yards), but the explosiveness isn't there without Barkley and a healthy offensive line.
Even if the offensive line were healthy, the holes weren't there for the backs outside of one drive. Will Shipley had six carries for 23 yards and the two combined averaged 3.9 yards per carry.
The Eagles are what they are at running back without Barkley.
Without DeVonta Smith, the wide receiver position isn't strong. Dontayvion Wicks is a good player, but the mindset changes as a WR1 compared to a WR2. He finished with just three catches for 18 yards, and couldn't make a play to get the pass game going.
Darius Cooper could, as his two touchdown catches are the only reason this grade is as high as it is. Makai Lemon was also open on a few plays, but Jalen Hurts couldn't get the ball to him due to the offensive line not protecting him.
The Eagles needed Smith on Sunday. They won't have him for a few games, so this group will be tested.
This position isn't good, relying on 36-year-old Zach Ertz to even be competent. Ertz had two catches for 13 yards, while Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins had a goose egg in the box score.
Mundt played an overwhelming majority of the snaps (80%), compared to Ertz's 21% and Jenkins' 20%. Known as a good blocker, Mundt wasn't good at doing that Sunday either.
This is a bad tight end group that really needs Goedert.
Somehow this unit gets worse and worse by the week.
Without Lane Johnson, Markel Bell is called upon to start in emergency duty -- and his first start didn't go well. Bell allowed six pressures and an 18.8% pressure rate allowed per dropback, completely being exposed on the right side.
Cam Jurgens allowed five pressures and a 12.5% pressure rate allowed per dropback. Drew Kendall allowed three pressures and a 9.4% pressure rate allowed per dropback. All three players were awful in pass protection on Sunday, and they're the different players from the Week 1 offensive line.
The Rams blitzed Jalen Hurts obsessively because they could. Bell and Jurgens weren't stoping them , as the right side and interior of the offensive line were exposed. The push up front wasn't good either on run plays as Bigsby averaged 0.57 yards before contact per carry and Shipley was at 0.67.
This is a bad offensive line, and will be slightly better if Johnson does decide to come back.
The pass rush just don't get enough pressure on the quarterback, no matter when it occurs in the game. Nolan Smith did have a sack, but he also had two missed tackles and a 5.7% pressure rate. Jalyx Hunt had three pressures and a 7.7% pressure rate.
Jonathan Greenard is a difference maker, and his pressure did lead to the Andrew Mukuba interception in the first half. Greenard did have a 21.4% pressure rate, but this unit took a major hit once he left with an ankle injury.
Greenard is a good player, but it's fair to question that contract. He just can't stay on the field.
The wrist injury is affecting Jalen Carter, who had three pressures in 52 pass rushing snaps. Carter wasn't a difference maker on Sunday, although the Eagles are paying him to be one. He did have a quarterback hit for what it's worth.
Jordan Davis played 25 snaps and didn't have a pressure, not even seeing close to as many snaps as Carter and Moro Ojomo. While Ojomo had a 9.1% pressure rate, his plays doesn't make up for the lack of production the Eagles are getting from Carter and Davis.
This is an overpaid, underperforming group.
The missed tackle on the Kyren Williams touchdown late in the game is the play that highlighted Jeremiah Trotter Jr. -- but he had a good game. Trotter Jr. finished with 15 tackles, five of which were against the run (10 were solo tackle).
Jihaad Campbell had nine tackles and two pressures, and has shown he can rush the passer. Now for the coverage numbers for both...
Campbell was targeted 12 times and allowed 80 yards, as Matthew Stafford had an 85.4 passer rating targeting him. This was better than Campbell has performed in previous weeks. Trotter. Jr. allowed 7-of-8 passes targeted his way for 49 yards and a 92.2 passer rating -- but no 20+ yard completions.
Trotter Jr. deserves to be on the field somewhere.
Seeing the fire from Quinyon Mitchell on Davante Adams was excellent to see, but the Rams passing game challenged the outside cornerbacks. Mitchell allowed just three catches for 27 yards, but Tariq Woolen was picked on throughout the game.
Woolen allowed three catches for 91 yards and a 99.8 passer rating when targeted (one touchdown), with two 20+ yard completions and one coverage penalty. This was Woolen's worst game with the Eagles, but he's been very good through four games.
Cooper DeJean had an interception and allowed a 0.0 passer rating in coverage. DeJean has either been great in the slot -- or horrible. The Eagles got a great game from DeJean Sunday.
Surprised to see a grade this high? That's because the safeties played well on Sunday.
Mukuba did have two missed tackles, but he also had an intercpetion and allowed just two yards in coverage. He was all over the field, and not getting exposed as much.
Perhaps that's because Michael Carter was playing next to him. Carter was targeted three times and allowed just seven yards in coverage. His range in coverage showed when targeted and appeared to get more comfortable playing safety as the game went on.
The safeties were good on Sunday, which is way better than they've been the first three games.
Jake Elliott hit a 56-yard field goal and was 2-of-2 on field goal attempts, remaining perfect on the season. Britain Covey averaged 19.7 yards per punt return, including a 41-yard return that led to a touchdown two plays later.
Smael Mondon made plays on kickoff coverage to prevent big returns and Kelee Ringo had a good tackle in punt coverage. Braden Mann was his usual self, having two punts inside the 20-yard line and averaged 43.8 net yards per punt.
The Eagles may have been awful Sunday. Their special teams were not.

title: Eagles Stock Report After Rams Collapse:  How Offense Is Affecting Jalen Hurts' Future
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - What looked like a story of perseverance turned with a Nick Sirianni gamble with 7:32 left in the game and the Eagles leading the Los Angeles Rams by a 20-10 margin.
Instead of taking a chip shot Jake Elliott field goal and extending the lead to 23-10, Sirianni went for the kill shot. Philadelphia's problematic passing game came up empty leaving the door for a talented but underachieving Rams team, which took the momentum shift and sling-shotted it to 14 points over the final 7:26, culminating with a tremendous Kyren Williams 7-yard run with 70 seconds remaining.
The collapse ruined a storybook ending in which the Eagles' lost three of there top stars. Right tackle Lane Johnson was ruled out 90 minutes before the game due to a personal matter while running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee) were lost to injury. Philadelphia had also come in knowing it would be without star receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and All-Pro linebacker Zack Baun (knee).
Six days ago the Eagles could do nothing to stop Case Keenum during an ugly loss to the Chicago Bears. On Sunday, Philadelphia made the reigning MVP and future Hall of Famer Matthew Stafford looks like a third-string quarterback for most of the game, stunning the overhyped Rams for 53 minutes of football.
You have to play 60, though.
A mistake prone LA offense, featuring two interceptions by Stafford and two mind-numbing personal fouls calls that wiped out positive plays was complemented by an awful special teams performance and a defense without Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald that allowed just enough big plays to falter.
Aesthetic football has rarely been the Eagles thing in the Sirianni/Jalen Hurts era but winning has and no other number proved that more that Sirianni's personal record of 4-0 against the highly-regarded Sean McVay.
That formula almost worked again until it didn't
Turnovers: The Eagles defense forced their first turnover of the season on the Rams' first drive when a ferocious Jonathan Greenard rush resulted in a Drew Mukuba interception. The takeaway drought marked the second most defensive snaps before the first turnovers for a Vic Fangio unit since 2016. The longest came in 2019 when Fangio was the head coach in Denver, which did not have a defensive takeaway until Week 5 that season.
The idea that turnovers come in bunches was boosted later when Cooper DeJean hauled in a no-look Stafford pass that set up the Eagles to steal a late touchdown right before halftime. Winning the turnover margin only goes so far when you're outgained by a 415 to 172 margin.
Coop! - No, not that Coop. DeJean certainly played well and is starting to come out of his early-season funk but Darius Cooper was the one receiver Hurts seemed to trust without Smith and Dallas Goedert. The 2025 undrafted free agent saved Hurts from an interception by high-pointing the football over Quentin Lake for one TD, and then uncovered in the back of the end zone for the second consecutive week for No. 2.
Jake the Make: Jake Elliott looks back to the old Jake Elliott. He's 2-for-2 outside of 55 yards so far this season. Overall he's now 4-for-4 on FGs on the season and hasn't missed an extra point.
Being Bold: While Sirianni will take plenty of heat, the analytics argue that the Eagles would have only needed a 13% chance to convert the fourth-and-two that kickstarted the Rams. The value of leading by 13 vs. 10 is negligible and actually would have given the Rams far better field position on the subsequent kickoff with the goal of two touchdowns only clearer for Los Angeles.
Third-downs: The Eagles were a dismal 0-for-12 on high-leverage downs and dating back to Chicago, they've failed to convert their last 17 tries on third down. Sirianni noted everything is contributing but the hear is growing on the idea of hiring a first-year offensive coordinator with no play-calling experience.
The Tush Push: Philadelphia failed on a fourth-and-one tush-push attempt despite super-charging it with the presence of Willie Lampkin to push Hurts. The Eagles should transition to spreading out opposiing defenses who are now plugging the A-gaps and allowing the powerful Hurts to pick and choose.
The pass rush: Greenard provided some juice early but at the end of the day the Eagles had just one sack by Nolan Smith and are on pace for just 17 sacks this season.
Right-Handed: Hurts has always had a propensity to flush right when in trouble and that default setting is only increasing. The Eagles' QB1 is flushing right on his dropbacks 16.7% of the time through four weeks, according to SumerSports. That number was 11.9% last season, 12.8% in 2024, 10.5% in 2023 and 10.4% in 2022.
Blitzkrieg: Hurts was just 5 of 15 for 46 yards when blizted by the Rams. The lack of effiency was glaring and it's been consistently bad so far this season. This was Hurts second-lowest EPA performance against the blitz out of the 89 games where he was blitzed at least five times. Week 1 was his sixth lowest EPA performance and Week 3 was his ninth lowest per SumerSports.

title: 4 Biggest Takeaways From Eagles Collapse: Letting Jeff Stoutland Go Was A Mistake
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles collapsed. There's no other way to describe a blown 10-point lead midway through the fourth quarter,
There are many ways to digest the latest defeat that put the Eagles to 2-2, a game that wasn't expected to be a win at kickoff put played its way into a potential victory. Only to see the win taken away from them.
Nick Sirianni is partially to blame . So is the offense, along with the defense allowing 14 points in the final 7:31. Let's focus on the offensive incompetance in the biggest takeaways from this loss, and why this offense is a major problem.
The Eagles tried to downplay Stoutland's impact on this offensive line. The new scheme was easier and favorable to players, a few of the offensive linemen said this summer.
That doesn't mean the scheme is better. That doesn't mena the players are coached up better, or developed.
Markel Bell allowed five pressures in his first start, a late entry at right tackle after Lane Johnson couldn't go for personal reasons. His pressure rate allowed per dropback was 15.6%.
Cam Jurgens isn't a left guard, as he allowed three pressures on Sunday -- a pressure rate allowed per dropback of 9.4%. Through three games, Jurgens has allowed a pressure rate allowed per dropback of 7.5%.
Drew Kendall has been okay at center, but he had a pressure rate allowed per dropback at 6.3% on Sunday. Tyler Steen was at 6.3% too, not taking the next step from last season.
This offensive line was mediocre last season -- with Stoutland. The Eagles partially blamed him for the struggles and the development of players, thinking Chris Kuper was the answer.
We're seeing why Kuper was available, and why his contract wasn't renewed. The proof is in the pudding.
Evaluating Jalen Hurts is hard enough, whether he has the personnel around him or not (he doesn't this year). Take away the Eagles' RB1, TE1, WR1, LG1, and RT1 and the puzzle is even harder.
Hurts was bad on Sunday, there's no sugarcoating it. He was 12-of-27 for 93 yards and two touchdowns -- somehow finishing with a 78.2 passer rating despite 3.4 yards per attempt. He was 2-of-9 for 10 yards in the second half -- 1.1 yards per attempt.
Hurts is 2-of-10 for 18 yards on third and fourth down. He was 5-of-16 for 46 yards and a touchdown in the pocket -- 2.9 yards per attempt (61.5 rating).
While Hurts was bad, what chance did he have to execute at a high level -- especially after Barkley injured his hamstring on the first series? Zach Ertz wasn't even on the team two weeks ago, and he was the best receiving tight end. Makai Lemon just isn't ready for a starting role at wide receiver either.
Dontayvion Wicks is a good player, but he's not a WR1. Darius Cooper was the only playmaker on offense, and that includes Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley (who are backups for a reason).
The offensive line is bad and can't protect Hurts either. It was impressive Hurts threw for two touchdowns given the circumstances. The Eagles can't even run the offense they want to run given the personnel they have on the field.
Hurts just disn't have a chance to make plays with what he had on Sunday. That's the reality.
Prior to the game, there were plenty of questions when it came to how this football team was built. The Eagles had three quarterbacks active for the game, and already made a change at QB2 with Tanner McKee taking over for Andy Dalton.
With Lane Johnson out, the Eagles had just two tackles on the active roster -- Jordan Mailata and Markel Bell (Fred Johnson was also out). The Eagles also had four tight ends active, two of whcih weren't even on the team two weeks ago.
The Week 1 center is now the left guard. The current cneter played guard all summer. The right tackle played just one snap in his career.
The first-round draft pick isn't ready for the role he's in. The second-round draft pick is on injured reserve, and was poor when he was on the field in training camp. The third-round pick was the right tackle on Sunday, as he's learning a new position this year.
More than fair to criticize what Howie Roseman give Nick Sirianni and his coaching staff to work with. The depth on this offense just isn't there and there are too many players at certain positions that aren't necessary.
The Eagles were hoping Makai Lemon would be the WR3 or the primary slot option. They traded up for him to specifically play that role. Lemon had three catches for 27 yards in his 42 snaps, good for him but not what the Eagles thought they'd get when they drafted him.
Lemon was supposed to make an instant impact, not have 10 catches for 65 yards through four games. he hasn't helped this passing attack -- or lack thereof.
Eli Stowers was bad in the spring and in the summer. He was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring and quad injury, but he wouldn't have helpe dthis tight end room immediately either.
Stowers was supposed to be the TE2. The Eagles had to keep four tight ends, and expose this offense to Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins more due to Stowers' lack of development.
Markel Bell learned right tackle this summer, but immensely struggled in his first start. A 15.6% pressure rate allowed per dropback shows Bell wasn't ready to fill in on short notice.
This is only chaper one of their careers. but the Eagles banked on Lemon and Stowers to help this team immediately. This is the result of that reliance.
The offense is bad, and both are playing a major role in that.

title: Steelers Have Never Needed DeShon Elliott More
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are 2-2 after their first four games of the 2026 season. Things haven't reached a total sense of panic, but any time you lose to the Cleveland Browns, you have to take a long look in the mirror.
And that's what Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy called for as the team begins their Week 5 preparations. He described the team's need to "clean our own house," highlighting his intention of getting the team back on track before they take on the Indianapolis Colts.
It's a startling, but necessary admission as the Steelers still try to establish an identity under their new head coach. The team needs to face their failures and try to improve before it's too late, but there's also one missing piece.
The Steelers have a huge need in their secondary. They need a starting cornerback to fill the void of Joey Porter Jr.'s departure, but even more pressing is the need a tone-setter on the back end. Which is why this team can't get back on track until safety DeShon Elliott returns to the field.
During McCarthy's weekly press conference, he offered an encouraging update on Elliott. He was placed on the Injured Reserve at the start of the regular season, but came with the designation of a return. Having served the mandatory four weeks on the IR this designation carries, the first assumption is that Elliott's practice window would be opened and he would return some time in the coming three weeks.
McCarthy said that he's progressing once again when he next spoke to reporters, but the real test was whether or not he would participate in practice. Once that happens, it officially opens his practice window before returning. Unfortunately, coach McCarthy shared that he had "nothing to report" regarding Elliott's practice window, according to The Athletic's Mike DeFabo.
Asked if DeShon Elliott’s 21-day window will be open, Mike McCarthy said the safety is getting closer but there’s “nothing to announce.”
And while it's a formality in the recovery process, those 21 days are crucial. If he is going to return in 2026, those days are the true ramp-up period. Should anything go wrong, they could shut him down for the year. Should everything go right, he could be back on the field by their Week 7 game in Paris, France.
Where things currently stand, that Week 7 game feels like a long shot for Elliott to return.
If the Steelers don't get Elliott back before the end of the month and the secondary continues playing like they currently are, it won't matter how good the veteran safety is upon his return. At that point, the Steelers might be 2-5 and staring up at the rest of the AFC North.
Best-case scenario is that Elliott's practice window is opened without the intention of utilizing all 21 days the player will be allotted before the team has to make a decision on his roster status. As McCarthy noted, he's made progress and is nearing a return. Hopefully, with a few practices and time to get into game shape, he is back to making an impact as soon as possible.
In the meantime, the Steelers' defense is in need of a player to change the momentum. Elliott is exactly the player the secondary and the defense needs to right the ship.

title: Steelers Re-Sign Recently Waived CB
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are reuniting with a cornerback that they previously waived at the beginning of the week.
Per an announcement from the Steelers, they have re-signed Doneiko Slaughter to their practice squad after he cleared waivers.
Slaughter was elevated from the practice squad in each of the first three weeks of the season while Joey Porter Jr. was inactive despite remaining on the 53-man roster amidst his contract dispute.
Once Porter Jr. was traded to the Dallas Cowboys last week for a 2028 second-round pick and 2027 conditional sixth-rounder, Slaughter was signed to the 53-man roster.
After Pittsburgh signed Sean Murphy-Bunting to its 53-man roster off the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad, however, Slaughter was let go.
Because the Steelers have already used up all three of Slaughter's elevations, they'd have to sign him to the 53-man roster once again in order for him to appear in another regular season game this season.
Over the four contests he's appeared in for Pittsburgh this year, Slaughter has posted a total of two tackles while garnering 26 snaps on special teams and none on defense.
Coming into the season, cornerback looked like one of the stronger position groups on Pittsburgh's roster.
With Porter Jr. coming off a breakout, borderline-elite 2025 campaign and now having Jamel Dean as his running mate on the outside while Jalen Ramsey handles the slot, the Steelers were in fantastic shape until they weren't.
Porter Jr. never ended up playing in a game for the franchise this year after failing to strike an agreement on an extension before Week 1, and now Dean is set to miss multiple games with an ankle injury he suffered against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4.
Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette are now Pittsburgh's starters on the boundary with Ramsey remaining the primary option out of the slot.
The Steelers have added Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith to their 53-man rosters off the practice squads of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Washington Commanders, respectively, over the past few days as a means of bringing in sufficient veteran depth.
Whether either player ends up seeing the field in any meaningful manner remains to be seen, but Pittsburgh certainly hasn't rested on its laurels when it comes to fixing the issues currently plaguing the team at cornerback.

title: NFL Injuries Give Steelers Bigger Hopes
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are 2-2 entering their Week 5 contest, but the sense within the organization is that the next few weeks are must-win games. Facing some less-than-fearsome opponents in the Indianapolis Colts, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France, the Steelers have the chance to right the ship and get back on track.
Not only do the Steelers have to "clean up" their own house, as head coach Mike McCarthy stated, but they also have to take advantage of their opponents' weaknesses.
Finding those exploitable areas is key, but this year it's a bit easier. Several teams on the Steelers' schedule are dealing with injury issues or roster personnel turnover. Either way, there are roster weaknesses that benefit the Steelers . If they can take advantage, it could help them turn this tough start into an impressive 2026 campaign.
The Colts signed free agent defensive end Arden Key this past offseason, and it looked like a smart move immediately. Over the first few games, Key created 20 quarterback pressures, the 20th-most in the NFL among qualified edge rushers. He suffered a hamstring injury in Week 4, and Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he is going to miss some time recovering.
That bodes well for the Steelers, as they try to keep quarterback Aaron Rodgers upright and give him a clean pocket to deliver passes from. Key was a big test for the tackles, but without him on the field, the Colts' firepower significantly decreases.
When the Steelers play the Buccaneers in Week 6, they won't have to worry about the team's veteran threat at quarterback, Baker Mayfield. Instead, the Steelers will face rookie Jalon Daniels. Daniels impressed during the preseason, but has been thrust into a starting role due to Mayfield's injury.
The 23-year-old has talent, but he's a far cry from a legitimate starter currently. In his first start, he completed 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards, while throwing for a touchdown and two interceptions. He also did damage on the ground, running the ball eight times for 55 yards.
The Steelers will have their work cut out for them going up against the athletic Daniels, but Pittsburgh still holds the edge. Historically, this Pittsburgh defense has devoured rookie QBs, and with their experience they could force Daniels into more turnovers and mistakes.
One of the key pieces of the Philadelphia Eagles' Super Bowl-winning teams over the past decade has been tackle Lane Johnson. A top-10 draft pick in 2013, he is the second-biggest name to come out of that first round behind DeAndre Hopkins, but has the most accomplished career of those first 32 picks.
Without him on the field, the Steelers' pass rush should have a much easier day against the Eagles. Containing Jalen Hurts is the big challenge for this team, but without the protection of a perennial Pro Bowl tackle, the Eagles might be an easy target for this potent Pittsburgh pass rush.
The Steelers aren't the only AFC North team battling through early injuries. Pittsburgh's fiercest rivals, the Baltimore Ravens, are also dealing with some early-season issues. Quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered an ankle sprain during their Week 4 contest, and that is a tough blow for Baltimore. Off to a strong start, Jackson is now unlikely to play in Week 5, and his exact timeline is unknown.
The Steelers don't meet the Ravens in 2026 until Week 15, giving Jackson plenty of time to recover. But with Jackson already banged up after four games, it's a legitimate question to ask whether or not he can hold up for all of 2026?
In Week 16, the Steelers will take on the Carolina Panthers. Really, they will take on whatever version the Panthers can muster. Carolina's offensive line has been decimated this year, with both of their starting tackles last season on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List or the Non-Football Injury List (NIL). Add on to that rookie starting right tackle Monroe Freeling, who has suffered a concussion and a knee injury already. Then you have star edge rusher Jaelen Phillips now dealing with a hamstring injury of his own, and it's a tough time for Carolina.

title: Punturi Panic Meter: Steelers Reaching Boiling Point
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Some losses sting more than others, and for the Pittsburgh Steelers, their Week 4 defeat at the hands of the Cleveland Browns was just that.
Any AFC North loss is a difficult blow, but the Steelers were exposed in Week 4. Their flaws in the secondary were exploited repeatedly. Their offensive line's struggles were exacerbated by the Cleveland defensive front. Their aging quarterback never looked older.
Is it time to panic in Pittsburgh? Thankfully, the Punturi Panic Meter is a foolproof scale for measuring dread. Graded on a spectrum from 1 to 10, this is how different Steelers positions and roles grade as they prepare for a Week 5 battle against the Indianapolis Colts.
The Steelers are no longer the organization that created the standard for the NFL, and the majority of that falls on current ownership. The same old tired ways have brought this team nowhere since their 2011 Super Bowl loss to the Green Bay Packers.
If things don't get on track soon, there is seemingly no one left to blame.
Omar Khan was supposed to be the voice of reason, not a puppet for ownership. A cap guru who could make any extension work and a prime talent evalutor, he's now traded two bonafide talents for day two draft picks and failed to adequately replace them.
The clock is ticking on Omar Khan.
No position is more worrisome in Pittsburgh than wide receiver. DK Metcalf finally had a 100-yard game on Thursday Night Football, but was that a breakout performance or a one-off? Behind him, veteran Michael Pittman Jr. and quarterback Aaron Rodgers aren't on the same page. Roman Wilson is the team's most reliable pass-catcher, but comes with a few mistakes that directly hurt the Steelers' cause. Rookie Germie Bernard can't find his way into meaningful snaps, despite playing well when he is given opportunities.
What's going on with kicker Chris Boswell? The veteran is one of the best in Steelers history, but he's off to a poor start.
Boswell has the track record to suggest he will bounce back, but that can't be said for the rest of the special teams unit. Kick and punt returns are nonexistent, and they are giving up too many yards on kick-offs. Rookie Kaden Wetjen looks outmatched, despite being brought in specifically to be a playmaker on punt and kick returns.
Rounding out the top three most concerning roster positions is the secondary as a whole. Their cornerbacks are in serious jeopardy and in need of a leader. Veteran Jamel Dean is expected to miss some time with a lower-body injury, leaving Asante Samuel Jr. and rookie Daylen Everette as the primary outside corners. That's trouble.
Safety doesn't get any better. DeShon Elliott has yet to have his practice window opened, the first step in returning to game action, and it's not clear when the team will officially open said window. Meanwhile, Rayshawn Jenkins, brought in to help hold down the fort, has done nothing to prove he is still an NFL-capable safety. Rookie Robert Spears-Jennings is the best performer so far, and that's a bad sign moving forward.
Head coach Mike McCarthy said his team needed to clean up their own house, which is 100% true. But to admit that they needed a day of self-reflection heading into Week 5 doesn't send the brightest message. His offensive game plans have worked well once out of four tries so far. Meanwhile, the defense has struggled the past two contests, putting more pressure on defensive coordinator Patrick Graham.
The Steelers were supposed to have multiple Pro Bowl contenders along the offensive line, but the best player through four games is left guard Mason McCormick. Center Zach Frazier and left tackle Troy Fautanu have taken their licks, and rookie Max Iheanachor is learning on the job as the new right tackle. It's been a tough go for this group, and despite the promise and potential, there is real concern facing this unit.
What is even going on with Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson? It's like a tale of two linebackers week in and week out. One game they are all over the field, the next they are invisible. They can't operate like this all season, and it's beginning to be a huge issue.
At 42 years old, Aaron Rodgers is far from the biggest concern, except for one area . His lack of mobility is costing him sacks as often as the offensive line is. He has to evade pressure more regularly to give himself a chance. If he can't, this offense is absolute toast.
Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth are dependable and available. They need to find more separation in the open field, but they remain low on the priority list for the offense. But when both are in the game plan, good things happen.
T.J. Watt has 4.5 sacks and Alex Highsmith has 3.0 sacks through four games, so it's hard to be too concerned with their production. The only question plaguing this group is how do they get Nick Herbig more involved, other than as an off-ball linebacker?
Without Rico Dowdle, Jaylen Warren has excelled. He's carried the ball 34 times in the past two games, compiling over 200 yards in the process. He's also been a heavy part of the passing game, receiving at least six targets in each game this season. Unless injuries stop him, Warren is the only player not worth worrying about.

title: Steelers LB Cole Holcomb Makes Life Announcement
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are trying to regroup ahead of their Week 5 contest, but as the team prepares for another game, life just became a bit more hectic for one of their defensive veterans.
Steelers linebacker Cole Holcomb shared some big life news as the new week began. His wife, Casey, delivered the family's second child.
The family shared the news via Casey's Instagram account , where they announced the birth of their new baby boy, Drew Jarrett (DJ).
The season is nearly a quarter of the way through, but there remains plenty of work ahead for the Steelers. Despite a 2-2 record through four games, this team is far from a complete product.
Still, life keeps moving forward. For Holcomb, he now has to adjust to a whole new set of rules and conditions as his family welcomes their newest member. The family now has a young daughter running around plus a newborn, and that sounds like a recipe for chaos.
It mirrors the chaos of the NFL season in a lot of ways. You have to keep adjusting and reacting to what your opponent (or children) throw your way. The Steelers are in the midst of that right now, and Holcomb gets to keep living that dream whether he's at work or at home.
While Holcomb clearly has some priorities to attend to off the field, the Steelers could really use him on the field. The team's inside linebacker group is struggling through the first four weeks. Starters Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson have delivered some shining moments over the opening four contests, but they've also made costly errors.
As the team seeks stability in the middle of the defense, perhaps a turn to the veteran is needed. Holcomb is not a three-down linebacker at this stage of his career, but he still excels at stopping the run. He's a traditional downhill thumper who brings a nasty energy to the field. As the team navigates a huge issue of missed tackles, Holcomb may be a helpful part of the solution.
The most notable play Holcomb has been involved in this season was a special teams snap in Week 3. The NFL ruled that Holcomb delivered a blindside block on the Cincinnati Bengals defender during the opening kickoff. As a result, he was fined $11,041 by the league.
If he is fined twice more for the same type of hit or any of the other five major penalties (hip-drop tackles, horse-collar tackles, launching, illegal blindside blocks and hits on defenseless players), he will be suspended, as per the latest agreement between the NFL and the NFLPA.

title: Joey Porter Jr. Calls Out Steelers: 'Can't Wait For That Matchup'
full_text:
Joey Porter Jr. can't wait for the opportunity to face the Pittsburgh Steelers down the line.
During an appearance on Michael Irvin's "The White House" podcast following his trade to the Dallas Cowboys, Porter Jr. made it clear that he's impatiently awaiting his next meeting with the Steelers.
"I'm waiting for that... I'm overly looking forward to that, OG. I can't wait for that matchup," Porter Jr. said. "Whenever it happens, I'm looking forward to it. I'm licking my chops."
Though it was always rather clear, Porter Jr.'s absence over the first three weeks of the season was likely never about a back injury.
With his camp and Pittsburgh ultimately unable to reach an agreement on an extension before Week 1, Porter Jr. essentially made the decision to hold himself out of games due to a lack of a new deal in the final year of his rookie contract.
During his first media availability as a member of the Cowboys last week, Porter Jr. stated that he felt "disrespected and undervalued" by the Steelers.
"It was a hard process, a lot of ups and down," Porter Jr. said, per the Forth Worth Star-Telegram's Nick Harris . "Definitely felt disrespected and undervalued. But that’s old news now. That’s how I look at it. I’m onto new beginnings and new chapters, that’s how I’m looking at it.”
The relationship certainly appeared to have reached a point where it was untenable. Porter Jr. went on to play 25 defensive snaps for Dallas in Week 4, and the fact that he did so without an extension in place or any guarantee that one would come was telling about his thoughts and feelings towards Pittsburgh.
He wasn't alone in that regard, as Joey Porter Sr. stated , "They tried to take me away from football for four weeks,” and, "They held us down for three weeks... Football is back," while celebrating the Cowboys' victory over the Houston Texans, so it doesn't seem like there's much love lost from the Porter's as a whole towards the Steelers.
Pittsburgh won't face the NFC East again until the 2028 campaign. It will take on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, however, since the two teams both finished in first place last year while the AFC North and NFC East last played one another two seasons ago.
There's a world in which Porter Jr.'s wish will be granted sooner than 2028, though. Should he fail to come to terms on a new contract with Dallas in the offseason and doesn't stick around via the franchise tag, thus allowing him to join another team for the 2027 season, it's possible he could find himself in a situation where the Steelers are on the schedule next year wherever he ends up landing.

title: Steelers Sign Second CB, Poach Commanders Veteran
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are bringing in additional help at cornerback before they take on the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5.
According to PennLive's Nick Farabaugh , the Steelers have signed Terell Smith off the Washington Commanders' practice squad.
Farabaugh reported that Smith was seen in Pittsburgh's locker room with a locker, and that the team must keep him on their 53-man roster for at least three weeks.
Smith is the second cornerback the Steelers have poached from an opposing team's practice squad over the last few days, first bringing in Sean Murphy-Bunting from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on October 6.
After trading Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys and watching Jamel Dean go down with an ankle injury in its Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football, which seems likely to force him to miss some time, Pittsburgh has been aggressive in supplementing its cornerback room before facing the Colts.
Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette should continue to garner the lion's share of the snaps on the boundary while Jalen Ramsey mans the slot, though Smith will offer some much-needed veteran depth at the position.
In 26 career games and six starts for the Chicago Bears between the 2023 and 2024 campaigns, Smith posted 68 tackles, 10 passes defended and an interception.
A fifth-round pick by Chicago in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Minnesota, Smith logged a total of 584 snaps on defense over the first two seasons of his career. He also garnered 232 special teams reps over that stretch.
During his rookie campaign, Smith spent 344 snaps on the outside, 19 in the box and six in the slot (per Pro Football Focus ). He allowed 25 receptions on 43 targets for 239 yards and a touchdown that year as well.
In 2024, he finished with 176 reps on the boundary, 21 in the box and five in the slot. Smith gave up nine receptions on 15 targets for 142 yards (per PFF) to go with an interception across that span.
He later suffered a torn patellar tendon during the preseason last season, which kept him out for all of 2025.
The Bears then let him go at final roster cuts back in August, and he signed to the Commanders' practice squad shortly after before being poached by the Steelers .

title: Steelers’ Rico Dowdle Details Gruesome Toe Injury, Return Process
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers running back Rico Dowdle opened up about his toe injury and where he stands in the recovery process after missing each of the team's last two games.
While speaking with reporters, Dowdle stated that he's taking the situation "day-by-day" and that he'll have a better gauge of his timeline to return to the field once he practices.
"Feeling alright," Dowdle said. "Getting better, taking it day-by-day. As far as getting back on the field, we're gonna see how it go tomorrow but I'm supposed to be working in a little this week so we'll see how I feel."
Dowdle, who also noted that he's dealing with turf foe at the moment, revealed that he dislocated his toe twice in Week 2 against the New England Patriots.
"It's real annoying," Dowdle said. "I dislocated it twice in the Patriots game. But yea, just a foot sprain. Very annoying honestly, I'm missing games because of a toe. I've played with broken hips and stuff like that, but it's definitely there."
Dowdle was carted to the locker room during the second quarter of Pittsburgh's loss to the Patriots after appearing to suffer his injury while attempting to recover the ball after Aaron Rodgers was strip-sacked.
The 28-year-old later returned in the third quarter, though he stated that his toe popped back out a second time from there, prompting the Steelers to pull him from the contest for good.
"The first time I did it, I came to the sideline and I was like, "I think my toe broke,'" Dowdle said. "So I went to the tent and it was dislocated and they popped it back in, did the X-rays. Nothing was broken or whatever, but once they popped it back in, I felt good, so I'm like, 'I wanna go back in the game and play.' Dr. [James] Bradley was like, 'No, we're playing on turf, think I'm gonna be done,' because when you get it, you hurt the plate at the bottom or whatever. So I ended up talking him into going back in, and he was like, 'If it pop out again, you've gotta be done,' and it popped out again, so I had to be done."
Besides working in at practice and seeing how he feels from there, Dowdle explained that the key is allowing the tissue to heal to ensure that his toe doesn't keep popping out, as otherwise he'd need to undergo surgery and have a pin inserted.
"It's about letting the tissue heal, like the scar underneath so it don't keeping popping out because if it keeps popping out, I'll have to get surgery and put a pin in there," Dowdle said. "It's just about trying to let the tissue come back together... It's painful obviously, 'cause it's like I got knots in the bottom of my feet."
Jaylen Warren has been fantastic in the two contests Dowdle has missed, posting a combined 302 yards on 40 touches.
Pittsburgh certainly won't rush him back onto the field and risk Dowdle's injury situation worsening by shortening his recovery period, though his eventual return will offer a nice boost for an offense that could use one.

title: Steelers Sign Former 49ers Camp Darling
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are adding another veteran defensive player to their practice squad.
Ahead of their Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo has reported that the Steelers have signed defensive end KJ Henry.
The #Steelers are signing DE KJ Henry to the practice squad after his workout yesterday. Henry was impressing with the #49ers in camp before an injury cut his summer short. pic.twitter.com/woTSL0PE4w
As Garafolo noted, Henry was a training camp standout for the San Francisco 49ers before being waived with an injury settlement on August 18.
This won't be Henry's first stint with the Steelers. It'll be his third in fact, as he first signed to the team's practice squad last October before being cut in early November.
Pittsburgh later signed Henry to a reserve/futures contract in January, though he was waived about a month before training camp began in late June.
A fifth-round pick by the Washington Commanders in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Clemson, Henry has also spent time with the Cincinnati Bengals, Dallas Cowboys, Philadelphia Eagles, Cleveland Browns in addition to the Steelers and 49ers.
The 27-year-old has played in a total of 15 regular season games, including one for the Browns in 2025.
Over that span, Henry has logged 22 tackles and 2.5 sacks.
After giving up 27 points and 372 yards on offense to the Browns in a three-point loss on Thursday Night Football, Pittsburgh is shuffling the deck just a bit on defense before it takes on the Colts.
The most consequential move the organization has made up to this point is signing veteran cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' practice squad.
The 29-year-old did not play in 2025 while recovering from a torn ACL he suffered during the offseason, though he does have 65 starts and 11 interceptions under his belt.
With Jamel Dean expected to miss some time due to an ankle injury he suffered vs. Cleveland, Murphy-Bunting offers proven depth at corner for a Steelers team that desperately needs it, especially after trading Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys last week.
Doneiko Slaughter, who initially took Porter Jr.'s spot on the 53-man roster, was waived in order to make room for Murphy-Bunting.
Alongside the addition of Henry to the practice squad, the Steelers brought in former New England Patriots and Houston Texans linebacker Marte Mapu as a hybrid defender who can also help out on special teams if called upon.

title: Mike McCarthy Puts Steelers Entire Roster on Notice
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are a 2-2 football team that doesn't look consistent, physical or like a winning program. Right now, there are serious concerns about how the 2026 season is going to continue to unfold if something doesn't change.
Head coach Mike McCarthy knows this.
During his weekly press conference, McCarthy got honest about the struggles of the Steelers through four games and how it needs to change, starting with him. And the way he's looking to go about it is by finding all of the problems and fixing them, or "cleaning" them, as he says.
"You have to play your best football each and every week to win in this league. Definitely play better than your opponent," McCarthy said about the lack of consistency with the team. "So that's really part of why we're going about tomorrow the way we're going about it because we need to clean our own house. Our house is not clean right now. And I get it, it's Week 5. So, you're hard-pressed to find a team or two that feels really good about where they are right now. That's the norm. So we're going to stay after the focus of what we need to work on. So that's what this weekend was about for me, and we've been working on it as a coaching staff, and we'll have clear factors of what we need to do as far as cleaning our house and then we'll get ready to go beat Indianapolis. That's the plan."
McCarthy didn't say they need to "clean our own house" and mean that it's time to sell the farm. He's not looking to replace everyone and have a fire sale before the trade deadline.
What he meant was that it's time to improve. It's time for the group as a whole to play better and more consistently. And it's time to find out who can meet that challenge and who can't, because those who cannot will be replaced. He's already started to do that.
Rookie Robert Spears-Jennings replaced Rayshawn Jenkins at safety, and it doesn't appear that's going to go back to Jenkins starting. Jenkins has struggled, and Pittsburgh decided it was time for something new.
The same thing happened at cornerback against the Cincinnati Bengals and at offensive tackle and guard in the same game.
McCarthy is open to change. He understands the urgency of it. And if players can't fix their problems, he clearly has no issue pulling them and trying someone new.
So, the Steelers better improve or watch out. Their head coach is here to fix things, not let the ship sink. And that means everyone is on notice.
McCarthy is ready to clean the house, even if step one is cleaning from the inside.

title: Seahawks Named Potential Suitor For Veteran RB Trade Target
full_text:
Following their Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, the Seattle Seahawks began kicking the tires on options to reinforce their backfield. With Jadarian Price heading to the IR , they met with veteran Joe Mixon .
Initially, it was reported that Mixon would sign with the Seahawks practice squad . Seattle also brought in Robert Henry Jr. , who was signed away from the Washington Commanders practice squad.
On Tuesday, it was reported that Seattle reversed course and decided not to sign Mixon , after having him in for a physical. That means there are still concerns about their depth with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani as their top backs.
That’s why Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox believes the Seahawks would be a suitor for veteran running back Kenneth Gainwell , who hasn’t been getting many opportunities with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Gainwell is coming off a strong season, and while he has the talent to help a team like Seattle, his contract makes him a potential trade target since Tampa Bay doesn’t seem to have a major role for him.
“Gainwell signed a two-year, $14 million deal in the offseason to back up Bucs starter Bucky Irving. The Buccaneers would save just $2 million in 2026 cap space by trading the 27-year-old, but they could clear his 2027 $7 million cap hit from the books while getting a reasonable return,” Knox wrote.
“While Gainwell did score his first touchdown for Tampa in Week 4, he has still logged a mere 21 touches through four weeks. However, he racked up 187 touches, 1,023 scrimmage yards, and eight touchdowns with the Steelers last season.”
As for compensation, Knox believes the trade value for Gainwell would be a 2027 5th-round pick, which is something the Seahawks should be willing to part with to fix their backfield.
Originally selected by the Philadelphia Eagles in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL draft, Gainwell was a key member of the Eagles backfield. He was also utilized as a return man at different times during his four-year stint in Philly.
That said, he truly broke out in 2025 with the Steelers. Gainwell recorded 537 yards and five touchdowns on the ground and added another 486 yards and three touchdowns on 73 receptions. Gainwell added 633 yards on 26 kick returns.
He’s proven to be a versatile back and would give them even more than Mixon would have, making him an ideal trade candidate for Seattle to consider.

title: The Best, Worst and Likeliest Scenarios for Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are starting to practice as they prepare to face off against the NFC West rival San Francisco 49ers for their Week 5 matchup at Lumen Field.
The Seahawks are hoping to get to 4-1 , while the Niners are one of three teams that remain undefeated through the first month of the year. Here's a look at the best, worst, and likeliest scenarios for the game between the two rivals.
The ideal script is exactly what happened in the divisional round game back in January. The Seahawks returned the kickoff from Rashid Shaheed all the way to the end zone to score on the game's first play, and the crowd energized them throughout. Seattle put their foot on the gas and won 41-6 against San Francisco, eliminating them from the playoffs.
It's hard to imagine an outcome like that happening again, but given how that was the previous meeting, the two teams are likely going to go all out for this game. If one team pushes all the right buttons and makes the right adjustments from their previous game, it could work out in Seattle's favor. Having Brian Fleury as the team's offensive coordinator could play a big role in the Seahawks' matchup.
As simple as the Seahawks made it look against the 49ers in the divisional round, there's a chance that San Francisco could pull an Uno reverse card.
The 49ers have been one of the best teams in the league so far this season, winning three of their four games by 10 points or more. Their closest win came in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals, when they scored 36 points. San Francisco has found a way to score at least 24 points in each of their first four games, and that momentum could play a big role in this game against the Seahawks.
Most of the players on this year's team were there last season when they saw their season get cut short in Seattle. This is a return to the scene of the crime, and the 49ers have a score to settle. That could end up really hurting the Seahawks this week.
These are two very evenly matched teams, and the stakes are very high for playoff implications. Even though it is only Week 5, this game could have the feel of a playoff matchup. It could also serve as a potential preview for what's to come in January for the NFC playoffs.
Seattle has been in every single game they've played this season, as their only loss came to the Washington Commanders by two points on the road. It's been just over a year since the Seahawks have lost a home game, dropping their Week 5 matchup a year ago against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Lumen Field. It's possible that the 38-35 score is similar to what could happen on Sunday. The real question is: Which team will have the higher score?

title: 3 Reasons Why 49ers vs. Seahawks is Week 5's Best Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are getting ready to face off against the NFC West rival San Francisco 49ers in Week 5 at Lumen Field.
It's a game that has a lot of past, present, and future storylines , making it one of the more exciting games to keep an eye on going into the weekend. Here are three reasons why NFL fans should look forward to this game the most on Sunday.
This game marks the first time the Seahawks and 49ers have met since mid-January, when the Seahawks hosted the Niners in Seattle for a divisional round matchup. The Seahawks started the game with a kickoff return from Rashid Shaheed that gave them all the momentum they needed for a blowout 41-6 victory to advance to the NFC Championship.
It's safe to say both teams haven't forgotten about the game, especially the Niners, who will be looking to put those demons behind them. Since that loss back in January, the Niners have not lost, and they have the momentum to carry them into the Pacific Northwest.
With Klint Kubiak, a 49ers assistant in 2023, going to the Las Vegas Raiders to be their head coach, the Seahawks were in need of a new offensive coordinator. They wanted someone with a similar background to Kubiak, which is why they hired Brian Fleury, who spent the last seven seasons under head coach Kyle Shanahan's staff.
Fleury's experience under Shanahan should play a large role in the Seahawks' preparation for the upcoming weekend. That being said, the Niners know the Seahawks very well in their own right, so this should only make things more intriguing for both teams.
This game will have a long impact, possibly on how the NFC West is won. The winner will take over first place in the division. Either the Niners will extend their lead and earn some leeway in a tiebreaker over the Seahawks, or Seattle will overtake first place once again.
With the Niners, Seahawks, and Los Angeles Rams all incredibly tight at the top of the standings last year, there is reason to believe that a similar outcome could take place in 2026. Therefore, these games are incredibly crucial to the standings in the long run, and Seattle should treat this game like a playoff game because San Francisco will as well.

title: Grading the Seahawks Through Four Games This Season
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are four games into the 2026 season, which means we have enough of a sample size to fully evaluate how the team is doing.
At 3-1, the Seahawks' record looks promising , but there are definitely places where the team can improve. Here's a look at how each unit graded for the first four games of the season.
The offense got an immediate shock to their system on the first drive of the season, as quarterback Sam Darnold suffered a glute injury that held him out for Week 2. Drew Lock stepped in and did a tremendous job, leading the team to a victory on the road and holding the fort down until Darnold returned in Week 3.
As a team, the Seahawks rank 13th in the league in yards per game at 347.3, which is a fair spot in where the team has performed. The Seahawks have scored 30 or more points in each of the last three weeks, which is a great sign for what's to come.
Seattle has struggled finding enough bodies that can run the football, which is going to be a mounting issue as the season wears on.
Defensively, the Seahawks started the season incredibly strong, holding their first two opponents, the New England Patriots and Arizona Cardinals, to a combined 17 points in the first two weeks. That was a sign that the defense was picking up where they left off last season, and they emerged as one of the top units in the league.
So far this season, the Seahawks are one of two teams to allow fewer than 1,000 yards, joining their NFC West rival, the Los Angeles Rams. As the team that's allowed the fewest yards in the league, it's hard to say that the team could do much better.
The Seahawks have run into some issues over the last two weeks. They struggled to get stops against the Washington Commanders on the road, and they didn't have their foot on the gas pedal during the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers. Their four forced turnovers certainly helped them grab the win.
Special teams have been a mixed bag for the Seahawks so far. Some aspects have been great, while others have been simply poor. Seahawks punter Michael Dickson has landed eight punts inside the 20-yard line, which is among the best in the league.
On kickoffs, the Seahawks are also doing a solid job, starting around the 33-yard line on average. That's the fourth-best mark in the NFL behind the Carolina Panthers, Philadelphia Eagles, and Las Vegas Raiders.
Coverage on kickoffs, however, has been inconsistent, specifically in their one loss against the Commanders. Special teams is arguably the reason why the Seahawks don't have a perfect record at the moment, but they have showed signs of bouncing back.
If they can play at an elite level for the rest of the season, the Seahawks will emerge as Super Bowl contenders once again.

title: NFL Mock Draft: Seahawks Fill Biggest Need in First Round
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are just four games into the 2026 season, but the scouting department is keeping an eye on the 2027 NFL draft class.
This year's class is expected to be very strong at the top on both offense and defense. Seattle went offense in the first round this past season by selecting Notre Dame running back Jadarian Price , so it might make more sense for them to target someone on the defensive side. That's why NFL draft analyst Justin Melo suggested the team should select Clemson EDGE rusher Will Heldt with the No. 25 overall pick.
"Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald loves rotating EDGE rushers. DeMarcus Lawrence and Dante Fowler Jr. will eventually need replacing. Clemson defensive end Will Heldt has edge-setting size on early downs, and can move around the line as needed on third-and-obvious," Melo wrote.
Heldt is off to a strong start in his senior season at Clemson. After recording 7.5 sacks in 13 games during his junior season, he's already at 4 sacks in 5 games in 2026. He has a knack for getting after the quarterback, and that should translate well in the NFL.
His experience playing two years at Purdue, followed by another two at Clemson, has given him the development needed to be a top contributor right out of the gate in his rookie season.
The only edge rushers taken ahead of Heldt in this mock draft are Colin Simmons out of Texas, Dylan Stewart from South Carolina, and Yhonzae Pierre from Alabama.
This selection makes a lot of sense for the Seahawks if they were to pick from around this spot in the draft. The team is in need of adding some youth to the pass-rushing unit, so Seattle should anticipate selecting at least one pass rusher in next year's draft. The team currently has six draft picks, but they could receive future compensatory selections as a result of this year's free agency.
The Seahawks need someone who can plug directly into DeMarcus Lawrence's spot in the rotation because he will be retiring after the 2026 season . Heldt is someone who can fulfill that role if the Seahawks are able to take him in the draft.

title: Seahawks NFL Power Rankings Week 5: Seattle Climbing Despite Injury Concerns
full_text:
Before taking the field against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4 , the Seattle Seahawks were dealt another blow. They already had to play essentially two games without quarterback Sam Darnold, and not long after his return, running back Jadarian Price suffered an injury .
Price was moved to the IR, meaning he will miss at least four games, which is a blow for a team that has yet to see Zach Charbonnet play in 2026 . The good news is that Emanuel Wilson has been playing well and could help the Seahawks stay the course until Charbonnet returns.
Their ability to push through adversity and start the season 3-1 is impressive and it has them once again climbing up the boards in NFL power rankings. Here's a roundup of some of the major outlets, which all seem to be firm believers in Mike Macdonald and the Seahawks .
"After surviving the last gasp of the Chargers’ season, the Seahawks are reviving the career of one-time running game bully Joe Mixon to fill the gap prior to Zach Charbonnet’s return. The signings of random name-recognition veterans by playoff-bound teams are one of my favorite time-honored traditions in all of sports."
Orr was ready to see if Joe Mixon would pan out, but it turns out the Seahawks won't be bringing him in. Adam Schefter reported that they decided not to sign him, meaning they will continue to lean on their current stable of backs.
"Even with RB Jadarian Price joining Zach Charbonnet on the shelf, they're doing a nice job with a patchwork running game that's incorporating KR/WR Rashid Shaheed and, perhaps, veteran Joe Mixon eventually."
Emanuel Wilson has been a strong replacement for the Seahawks. He had 81 yards and a touchdown in Week 4 and while you would like to see his yards per attempt improve (3.6 on the season), he hasn't been a liability. That's all you can ask for when you turn to your RB3.
"Quarterback Sam Darnold sustained a glute injury on the season's fifth play and missed most of the first two games. No. 1 running back Jadarian Price, Seattle's first-round pick, lost fumbles in consecutive weeks and is now on IR because of a chest injury. The Seahawks won in Week 4 despite a franchise-record 150 penalty yards," Brady Henderson wrote.
The real story from Week 4 was the fact that Seattle bounced back from losing to the Commanders and were able to win ugly. Now, they prepare to take on the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5, which will be a huge NFC West showdown. They must be better prepared in that one, because giving the 49ers 150 yards from penalties would be a recipe for disaster.
"They bounced back from their loss to the Commanders with a dominant showing against the Chargers. The defense, as usual, led them in the victory."
Seattle understands that defense wins championships, which is why Macdonald is the right man for this franchise. Even with injuries slowing them down, their defense is able to make plays when it matters most, and that's why they remain one of the top teams in the NFL entering Week 5.

title: Seahawks Rookie Report: Rough Quarter Season Start
full_text:
There were signs early in the NFL Season that a team's draft class is either good or bad. Coming out of the Seattle Seahawks ' 30-23 Week 4 win over the Los Angeles Chargers , the 2026 NFL Draft is looking rough after the latest health concerns about rookie running back Jadarian Price. That worry about a questionable draft class is starting to look even more concerning.
​This is the first time this season that the Seahawks shouldn't be feeling great about their 2026 NFL Draft class. The rookie who played the most in Week 4 was right guard Beau Stephens, who might have had his most difficult performance this week. Starting left guard Christian Haynes is the superior interior offensive lineman at this point in the rotation , while Anthony Bradford is on IR.
​Once again, cornerback Julian Neal didn't appear in a defensive snap in a game. This is the second consecutive game and the third time in four games that he didn't appear in a game for the Seahawks' Dark Side Defense. He is now behind the starters, Nehemiah Pritchett and Trevon Diggs, who made his first regular-season appearance on Sunday . Neal, however, played in 23 special teams reps, which is nine more than in the Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
​ Cornerback Avery Smith was a healthy inactive for the Seahawks in Week 4 . This is the second consecutive game that he was a healthy inactive for the Seahawks, but he still remains on the 53-man roster. The Seahawks have eight rookies on their practice squad, including two new faces in Week 4.
​Seattle replaced Uso Seumalo on the roster with another rookie defensive tackle in Gary Smith III. There is no indication that any of the other rookies, including guard Evan Beernsen, cornerback Michael Dansby, defensive tackle Deven Eastern, cornerback Andre Fuller, wide receiver Emmanuel Henderson Jr., edge rusher Aidan Hubbard and wide receiver Malick Meiga, are likely to be moved to the active roster anytime soon.
Running back Jadarian Price has the talent and the development to be a top-tier starter. Through the first three games of the season, Price has rushed for 119 yards on 28 carries. He has been hit with inconsistencies and fumbling issues. To make matters worse, the Seahawks were forced to put Price on IR with a chest injury .
The Seahawks will have their starting young running back out while the team faces the San Francisco 49ers (4-0), on the road versus the Denver Broncos (2-2) on Thursday Night Football and the Kansas City Chiefs (4-0).
​The beginning of the Seahawks’ rough streak of the 2026 NFL Draft class began with the season-ending ankle injury of safety Bud Clark. He was training to be a key backup and a special teams player for the Seahawks this season. Clark would’ve likely played and started his fourth game of the season, with Ty Okada yet to play a game this season.

title: Seahawks Reverse Course, Won't Sign Joe Mixon After Physical
full_text:
With Jadarian Price being sent to the IR , the Seattle Seahawks were in the market for running back help. On Monday, it appeared they found that in former Pro Bowl running back Joe Mixon .
The former Cincinnati Bengals and Houston Texans star was set to sign with Seattle, giving them depth behind Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. On Tuesday, the Seahawks reversed course.
According to Adam Schefter, Mixon was given a physical by the team and afterward, they decided not to bring him in. Mixon, who turned 30 years old this summer, had a foot and ankle issue which caused him to miss the entire 2025 season and he was subsequently released by the Texans this year.
"As it turns out, the Seahawks decided not to sign veteran running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after he underwent a physical for the team, per league source. Mixon will remain a free agent," Schefter wrote.
Mixon spent seven years in Cincinnati and ran for 6,412 yards and 49 touchdowns. He played just one season with the Texans, recording 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns. Mixon earned his second career Pro Bowl nod that year, but was unable to play in 2025.
As Seahawks On SI’s Jeremy Brener said when the move was announced, there was a chance this addition wouldn’t work . While he did give Seattle some much-needed experience in the backfield, there was a reason he was entering Week 5 without a contract. Brener said his knowledge would be beneficial but apparently that wasn’t enough for him to stick with the practice squad.
Seattle did add a running back, however, as they picked up Robert Henry Jr . He was signed to the active roster after being poached from the Washington Commanders practice squad.
A rookie out of UTSA, Henry has yet to take a snap in the NFL. He will compete for time behind Emanuel Wilson and George Holani as the Seahawks wait for Price and Zach Charbonnet to return to full health.
As a redshirt senior in 2025, Henry had a breakout season. He racked up 1,045 yards and nine touchdowns. For his career, he had 2,339 rushing yards with 27 touchdowns and was efficient out of the backfield with 58 catches for 428 yards and three touchdowns.
