title: 3 Risers and Fallers After Seahawks' Week 4 Win vs Chargers
full_text:
The good news for the Seattle Seahawks (3-1) after the incredibly ugly 30-23 home win over the Los Angeles Chargers is that it has given the coaching staff a lot to work with. The Seahawks' coaching staff is going to take all the great attributes and the sloppiness and turn it into something this week to get ready for a pivotal Week 5 home game versus the San Francisco 49ers (4-0).
​Sunday's game against the Chargers highlighted a lot of performances that will be evaluated to determine how they are utilized moving forward. There were several great performances in Sunday's win that will give players more playing time or more roles. Some players are also seeing much more impact moving forward.
​It is hard to believe that, when healthy, second-year nickelback Nick Emmanwori can still see a rise in role status. With Emmanwori back at 100%, the Seahawks can use him in many ways , including slot corner or the box linebacker. Head coach Mike Macdonald even put Emmanwori as an edge rusher to maximize his speed, athleticism and aggressiveness. He generated two quarterback hits, two tackles for loss and a sack as a result of playing much closer to the line of scrimmage.
​Things might be looking up for wide receiver/return specialist Rashid Shaheed , even if he wasn't a huge contributor in either of these areas. Shaheed caught one reception for 20 yards on three targets, only averaged six yards on two punts and returned three kickoffs for 83 yards. It was in the running game where Shaheed excelled by taking a 28-yard run for his first offensive touchdown as a Seahawk.
​It isn't every day that a backup linebacker is one of the big reasons why the Seahawks' Dark Side Defense and special teams are so efficient. Connor O'Toole continues to be one of the top backup defenders for the Seahawks as he can efficiently pass and run coverage. O'Toole is also one of the most reliable special teams defenders as he recovered a muffed punt. He also delivered a great hit on the Chargers' punt return that was improperly called for a personal foul penalty.
​The Chargers' matchup should be an indication that second-string running back George Holani might be demoted when veteran Zach Charbonnet returns from his ACL injury. Holani only rushed for 18 yards on seven carries while also catching one reception for two yards. This was the first game where he didn't contribute on special teams. If the Seahawks are going to give Joe Mixon and/or Robert Henry Jr. some serious reps, then Holani is on the outside.
​For the second consecutive game, second-year tight end Elijah Arroyo accounted for no receptions. Not only is Arroyo not being targeted, but he is being surpassed by Eric Saubert in terms of usage. Arroyo still remains a key player on the Seahawks' roster due to his special teams contributions and his route-running.
​The closer it gets to the NFL Trade Deadline, the more it feels that the Seahawks will make a move for a veteran edge rusher. One edge rusher who is earning less attention each week is fourth-year defensive end Marcus Morris. In Sunday's win over the Chargers, Morris only played in seven defensive snaps while playing 24 snaps on special teams.

title: The Seahawks Have an Elijah Arroyo Problem
full_text:
When the Seattle Seahawks hired Brian Fleury, a former tight ends coach who had spent much of his career working with George Kittle, no one should have been more excited than Elijah Arroyo. After a quiet rookie campaign of just 15 catches, he now had a coordinator who would doubtlessly work to get the most out of him. At least, that’s what made sense.
After four games, Arroyo is on track to be even less impactful than he was last season. He has just one catch, a seventeen yard strike over the middle from Drew Lock in week 2. It was a nice looking play that gained a big chunk of yards. You’d think the Seahawks would have a vested interest in trying to make more plays like that happen.
Maybe even more shocking is that that catch is also his only target of the season. On 117 pass attempts this year, Seattle QBs have thrown it at him just once. He’s played 63 snaps total, just barely over a quarter of the total offensive snaps, and the same number as Eric Saubert . He’s yet to play 20 or more snaps in any one game. He’s not really a part of the offense right now.
All this to say, this isn’t even really an indictment of Arroyo individually. Unless he’s playing so poorly in practice that Fleury just doesn’t feel comfortable giving him significant opportunities, this isn’t really his fault. He’s not even getting on the field very much, and despite being a clear physical mismatch, he doesn’t get solid opportunities when he does get snaps.
I understand that this is a low-volume passing attack dominated by Jaxon Smith-Njigba . But there’s no universe where Eric Saubert and Brady Russell should be getting targeted more than Arroyo. I understand Elijah offers little as a blocker, but there are a lot of tight ends in this league who don’t block. Other teams find a way to get them involved. So far, this one hasn’t.
Ignore, for a moment, the fact that I wasn’t impressed with Arroyo coming out of college and had him graded in the fifth round. That doesn’t matter. What matters is that John Schneider viewed him as worthy of a top 50 overall draft pick. And after the draft, John went as far as to claim that Elijah was a ‘top 15’ talent who had his stock drop due to injuries.
Ten tight ends have been drafted in the top 15 of the draft since 2000. That statement is putting a lot of stock in his abilities. Even if Schneider is getting overzealous with that statement, the fact that he can value a player that highly and then the coaches that he hires can’t even give him a chance to impact games is truly confusing and disappointing.
Right now, the Seahawks are struggling to run the ball. They don’t have their typical allotment of running backs, and the run blocking has been inconsistent. The offense probably needs to open up and throw it more than they’re comfortable with. A player like Arroyo could be very impactful in that circumstance. Times like this demand a player like him.
AJ Barner, the top Seattle tight end, took on such a heavy workload last year that he had multiple surgeries and took months during the offseason to rehab. I’d say getting him a lighter load of action is important as well. That won’t happen with Arroyo barely touching the field. More work for Arroyo means a healthier Barner down the line. These are the stakes. Figure it out.

title: 49ers S Malik Mustapha has a Prime Opportunity in Front of Him
full_text:
One of the losses the 49ers suffered in their Week 4 win against the Broncos was safety Marques Sigle spraining his ankle.
Sigle is expected to miss “some time” with a high ankle sprain. It’s unclear if the 49ers are considering placing him on Injured Reserve, but I think it’s unlikely given how crowded the list is.
It’s a bummer for the 49ers and Sigle, as he was playing well this season. He really took it up a notch as the starter. However, his absence will provide a prime opportunity for Malik Mustapha.
Mustapha can retake his starting job with Sigle on the mend. He was never supposed to be a backup. The 49ers wanted him as a starter, but a hamstring injury derailed him in training camp.
Kyle Shanahan’s belief in Mustapha never wavered despite the injury. That’s why the 49ers were slowly incorporating him into the defense in the last few games.
“Malik just had some unfortunate injuries during training camp, so he got a late start, but got his first practice out there in Australia and I think he's been awesome this whole month,” Shanahan said. “That's why we've been mixing him in there more regardless, even with all those guys healthy. We started mixing him in last week trying to get him some series and stuff.”
It’s clear the 49ers wanted Mustapha to take back the starting job with his incorporation into the defense. They just couldn’t justify it with Sigle and, surprisingly, Ji’Ayir Brown playing well.
Unfortunately for Sigle, he’s bound to be the odd man out now that he’s injured. And if Mustapha continues to make plays like the pass breakup he executed against the Broncos, it’ll be tough to get it back.
“Every time he's come in, I think he's played at a high level,” said Shanahan. “I thought he did that yesterday and made one of the biggest plays in the game yesterday on that third-and-five when he broke that pass up. I'm real excited with Malik and how he's looked.”
Retaking the starting job is right there for Mustapha. This is his chance with Sigle out. He’s looked shaped with his limited opportunities so far this season.
His pass coverage skills seem to have improved, but that will be fully confirmed in the next few games. If he can check that box, he’ll have taken advantage of his prime opportunity.

title: Why the 49ers’ Defense Won’t Skip a Beat With Marques Sigle Out
full_text:
As sweet as it was for the San Francisco 49ers to defeat the Denver Broncos in Week 4, there was a downside to it.
Starting safety Marques Sigle suffered a high ankle sprain in the game. He’s expected to miss some time, which could be through their Bye Week. Sigle’s injury is a real bummer, as he’s been playing really well this season.
He’s stepped it up a ton with every facet of his game. He hasn’t been the liability that he was last season, especially in pass coverage. It’s been impressive to see him improve. Even Kyle Shanahan knows it.
“I think he's been playing his ass off in the run and pass game,” said Shanahan. “The way he's filled on some of these tackles, just how solid he's hit people and how quickly he's done it getting up in there.
“I thought he's done it good in the pass game too. He did a lot of good stuff last year, but I think he has taken it to another level, just playing a little bit faster, hesitating less, knowing what he's doing and really playing well before that injury.”
The 49ers will miss seeing Sigle ascend, but it doesn’t mean their defense will see a significant drop-off. In fact, the 49ers won’t skip a beat with Sigle out for a while.
They have Malik Mustapha, who can fill in perfectly. He’s been doing an excellent job in the limited snaps he’s had in the last few weeks. There’s even a chance that he can be an upgrade from Sigle.
“Every time he's come in, I think he's played at a high level,” Shanahan said of Mustapha. “I thought he did that yesterday and made one of the biggest plays in the game yesterday on that third-and-five when he broke that pass up. I'm real excited with Malik and how he's looked.”
The only reason Sigle is starting is because Mustapha hurt his hamstring early in training camp. He didn’t return until before the 49ers flew out to Australia.
Credit to Sigle for performing well and ascending, but he isn’t an impactful player yet. Mustapha has demonstrated more of an impact so far, especially in the last game when he had a pass breakup on third down, as Shanahan alluded to.
If Mustapha has more plays like that with Sigle, he most likely will hold onto the starting job.

title: 49ers Offensive Line is Emerging as an Elite Unit
full_text:
Entering Week 4's matchup against the Denver Broncos , the San Francisco 49ers faced one critical question – is their offensive line elite?
The 49ers' offensive line had been on a tear in the first three games this season. They hadn't allowed a single sack on Brock Purdy and led the league with the lowest pressure rate (22.5%) allowed.
However, that could be a product of the matchups. The 49ers hadn't faced any lethal defensive fronts yet, which could be the direct cause for their great start.
The Broncos would be the first lethal pass rush they'd face, so the 49ers' offensive line was going to be truly tested. This game would prove whether or not their great start was real.
Turns out, the offensive line is legit. They passed this test against the Broncos with flying colors, as Purdy wasn't sacked and was pressured only nine times on 33 dropbacks.
The 49ers' offensive line is emerging as an elite unit. It's wild to see, considering all the slander they received in the offseason and even during parts of the 2025 season.
In reality, they were always a middle-of-the-pack offensive line. Some games they'd look lowly, and some games they'd perform at a high level.
But so far through four games this season, they're elite. They're the only offensive line not have allowed a sack this season and still leads the league with the lowest pressure rate (23.8%) allowed.
They also rank No. 2 in ESPN's pass-block win rate at 59%. A round of applause is deserved for Connor Colby, Jake Brendel, Dominick Puni, and Colton McKivitz.
Trent Williams was always viewed as the only skilled player on the offensive line. But the rest of the guys have been performing admirably.
They all proved their mettle when it was tested against one of the better defensive fronts in the NFL this past week. And while it doesn't cement their elite status, it does prove they are good.
More games will be needed to prove whether they're truly elite, but they're on the right track. They can easily raise their stock further if they can manage well against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.
No team will push the 49ers more than Seattle's vaunted defensive front. They got whooped in their last two games against them, which will make this game a perfect measuring-stick evaluation.

title: Why the 49ers Must Trade for Khalil Mack
full_text:
Defeating the Denver Broncos was an impressive win for the San Francisco 49ers .
One reason it's impressive is that they did it without an effective pass rush . Bo Nix had all day to throw on practically every dropback. His time to throw was 3.02 seconds.
He was never sacked and was only pressured 13 times. If the 49ers had faced a good quarterback, or a somewhat decent one, they might've lost the game.
Their pass rush is almost as nonexistent as it was last season. That's going to remain with Nick Bosa out, which should coerce the 49ers into making a trade.
And the trade to execute is for Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack . John Lynch has to be working the phones with the Chargers to see if they can broker a deal.
It's time. Their performance against the Broncos should've been enough to convince them how bad it is. The week before, against the Arizona Cardinals, it was the same as well.
Jacoby Brissett was only pressured 13 times on his 54 dropbacks. Yes, he was sacked twice, but one of them was a cleanup sack when Brissett rushed up the middle.
The 49ers' pass rush is lost without Bosa, and while it's been awesome to see the defense play well under Raheem Morris, that won't last for long if their pass rush continues to be a ghost.
Trading for Mack makes too much sense for them, especially with the Chargers at 0-4. They're bound to be sellers sooner rather than later, as they have no hope in sight.
Mack has tallied three sacks and 16 pressures so far, which would lead everyone on the 49ers. Only Keion White comes close with two sacks and 11 pressures.
If the 49ers acquired Mack now, they'd take on $6.22 million on their salary cap. That's an easy deal to take on, so it would come down to what the 49ers would need to give.
A third-round pick would be an easy one to give up, but I'm not sure if that will be sufficient for the Chargers. Given how great the 49ers look, their draft picks will be near the end of every round.
A first-round pick is out of the question, so the 49ers will have to offer their second-rounder. It's a bit steep for a half-season rental, but Mack will drastically boost their defense.
They cannot waste the opportunity in front of them by waiting on Bosa. And if he comes back healthy and doesn't miss any more games, the 49ers will have a monstrous defense.

title: The 49ers are Underutilizing Rookie Running Back Kaelon Black
full_text:
The 49ers desperately need a quality backup running back to split carries with Christian McCaffrey. That's why they drafted Kaelon Black in Round 3 this year. Unfortunately, they're not using him nearly enough.
McCaffrey is 30, and he's not the player he once was. This season, he's averaging a pedestrian 4.4 yards per carry. This past Sunday, he averaged a mere 3.5 yards per carry against the Denver Broncos. And yet, the 49ers still gave up 15 carries. That's too many.
Last year, the 49ers' backup running back was Brian Robinson Jr. -- they traded a sixth-round pick to Washington for him just before the season started. And then, they hardly used him all season. He averaged a career-low 5.4 carries per game and scored a career-low 2 touchdowns in 17 games.
Robinson was a complete afterthought in the 49ers' offense. He came into the game for a play or two here and there when McCaffrey needed a breather, which meant Robinson never got into the flow of the offense.
Now, Robinson Jr. is the backup running back for the Atlanta Falcons, whose starting running back is Bijan Robinson, the best running back in the league. And he's young. And yet, the Falcons still have given Robinson Jr. 11 carries per game so far this season. Just this past Monday night, he scored three touchdowns against the Saints. That's more than he scored all of last season with the 49ers.
And that's because the Falcons are committed to using their backup running back. They give Robinson Jr. entire drives to be the main running back -- not just the occasional snap. This makes him better, it makes Bijan Robinson, and it makes their offense better.
Kyle Shanahan should take a page out of what Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski is doing. Actually use the backup running back. Let him settle into the game so he doesn't press every time he touches the ball.
Right now, Kaelon Black is pressing. He gets only a few carries per game, so he runs as fast as he possibly can, which means he runs into the backs of his blockers and doesn't let holes or lanes develop. He's rushing to impress the coaching staff so he can stay on the field.
It's not coincidence that Black's best game this season was his first game. That's because the 49ers gave him 14 carries. Since then, he hasn't gotten more than 7 carries in a game.
If he's healthy, he needs to split time with Christian McCaffrey this Sunday in Seattle, because the Seahawks own McCaffrey. They haven't faced Black yet.

title: 5 Pleasant Surprises Fueling 49ers’ 4-0 Start
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have gotten off to a 4-0 start through the first quarter of the season. As the team moves into the end of the first half of the 2026 season, which players have been the most pleasant surprises?
Purdy is easily the biggest surprise for the positive. It was not crazy to think that Purdy would play well this season. However, he has 11 touchdowns and one interception and is playing some of the best football of his career. Right now, you would be hard- pressed to give anyone else an MVP . That is quite the pleasant surprise.
In the four weeks leading up to the season, the team did not even play Colby at left guard. They had him work at right guard so they could give Carver Willis and Robert Jones looks. Jones was cut, and Willis remains a backup. Colby has improved significantly since his rookie season. He still has issues, but he has a stronger hold of his job in 2026 than he did in 2025.
Morris is not a player, but he is quite the pleasant surprise. There was a huge question as to how different the defense would be with Morris after Robert Saleh came in and did so well that he earned a new head coaching job.
Morris brings a different style, changed some personnel, and the defense looks different. Still, the group looks as good, if not better than the season prior. They do not even have Nick Bosa. If they get him back, they could be a feared unit.
Odighizuwa has been a great offseason addition. He has 201 snaps played due to the injuries in the room. The next highest is Gracen Halton with 118 snaps played. Sebastian Valdez is third with 56 snaps. The room is quite thin, but somehow it is still much improved from last season. That is because of Odighizuwa.
Last year at this time, the team was preparing to bench rookie Marques Sigle. The Los Angeles Rams exposed him early in the season. This year, he played great against the Rams in Week 1. He has followed that up by being the 49ers' best safety this season. The team brought back both starters from last year. Coming into the year, he was expected to be depth. That is quite the surprise.

title: 5 Biggest 49ers Overreactions After 4-0 Start
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are 4-0 and won their most impressive game of the season against the Denver Broncos. What are the biggest potential overreactions from the first four weeks?
It is only four weeks, so it is too early to declare it a bad draft class. However, through four weeks, it has not quite lived up to expectations. De’Zhaun Stribling is hurt. Kaelon Black had more rushing yards in Week 1 than he did in Weeks 2-4 combined.
Romello Height has just three pressures on 65 pass rush attempts. His win rate is lower than Ogbo Okonkwo and Keion White. So far, Gracen Halton and Jaden Dugger are the best picks. This is not great.
On paper, Juszczyk was not producing much. However, he is the straw that stirs the drink. He is a blocking, rushing, and pass-catching threat, which stresses defenses when deciding what personnel to use.
Juszczyk joins Jake Tonges on the injury list, and both were in line to fill this similar role in different manners. Without Tonges, they were leaning into Juszczyk more. Now, they do not have another strong option.
Kittle only had 12 receiving yards in his first game back from his Achilles injury. Still, since then, he has averaged 77 yards per game in the three weeks since then. That would be the second-best rate of his career if he stayed healthy for a full season. Considering Kittle could get even better as he continues to heal, this might be the tip of the iceberg.
The 49ers have not been tested yet, but Denver looked like a formidable bunch. However, they quickly lost both of their cornerbacks, including Patrick Surtain, who is the best player on their team. They beat a tired Rams team, two of the worst teams in the NFL, and now a Broncos team that lost big names during the game. Have they been tested?
The 49ers are 4-0, and their roster has big holes in key areas. Any of their defensive line spots could be upgraded. Receiver, tight end, and now even fullback could be addressed. The 49ers need to buy at the deadline.

title: One Thing Holding Back the 49ers from Being the Super Bowl Favorite
full_text:
Through four games, it's hard to find a reason not to pick the 49ers to win the Super Bowl this season.
Sure, they have a ton of injuries , just like most years. But they're still undefeated, they have the highest-rated quarterback in the NFL, future Hall of Famers at left tackle, running back, tight end, wide receiver and linebacker, an elite offensive play caller and an outstanding defensive coordinator, and a ton of cap space plus enough picks to make a serious trade before the deadline. At the minimum, they should reach the NFC Championship Game this season.
But should we expect the 49ers to actually win the Super Bowl for the first time since 1995?
Before the season started, general manager John Lynch said he wanted to make sure the 49ers had a dominant defensive line this season. Most Super Bowl-winning teams have excellent pass rushes, if not excellent defenses. Through four games, the 49ers certainly have a good defense, but they don't have a good pass rush.
The 49ers have just six sacks this season -- seventh-fewest in the league. Their big offseason addition, Osa Odighizuwa, has zero sacks. Which means Lynch hasn't accomplished the goal he set for himself when the offseason began.
Because the 49ers have virtually no pass rush, they have intercepted just one pass this season. They can't pressure quarterbacks and force them into rushing and making mistakes. At least not right now. Which makes you wonder how they'll fare when they face an elite quarterback who's mobile such as Patrick Mahomes.
Maybe the 49ers' defensive line will become dominant when Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams return. And maybe Lynch will make a big trade for a serious pass rusher such as Khalil Mack. If those things happen, the 49ers will have no glaring weaknesses.
But Lynch hasn't made a big move yet. And Williams might take a few months before he returns to his peak performance, considering he missed the entire offseason and isn't close to being in football shape yet, even if his surgically repaired knee is healthy.
And then there's Bosa. On Monday, head coach Kyle Shanahan spoke to the media on a conference call and ruled out Bosa for Sunday's game against the Seahawks. Didn't even wait until the first practice of the week on Wednesday to see how Bosa and his injured calf are doing.
I'm skeptical that Bosa will return to form this season. He's recovering from this second ACL tear in the same knee, and the second surgery typically takes 12-18 months to fully recover. So far this year, Bosa hasn't shown that he can practice fully or play more than two games in a row without getting reinjured. Until he shows otherwise, the 49ers should assume that he won't make a full recovery this season.
That's why the 49ers desperately need to trade for an edge rusher before the deadline. Williams is not an edge rusher -- he's an interior rusher. And Bosa might not be fully healthy for a long time.
Let's see how serious the 49ers are about winning a Super Bowl this year. How they act at the trade deadline will reveal so much.

title: 8 Winners and Losers From 49ers Week 4 Win Over Broncos
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are only one of three undefeated teams left after their Week 4 win over the Denver Broncos . Let's dive into the eight winners and losers from the tough win.
For a fourth consecutive game, the 49ers' offensive line didn't allow a single sack on Brock Purdy. He was also only pressured nine times in this game.
The 49ers' offensive line has proven that they are legit. To perform so well against one of the better pass-rushing fronts in the league is impressive.
Entering this game, I was wondering if the offensive line was playing great because they were facing weak teams, but after what they did against Denver, there's no mistake. They're sweet.
Mike Evans shouldn't have played this game, but the fact that he did proves how tough and dedicated he is. He's most likely playing with fractured ribs.
Evans was seen grimacing in pain throughout the game. Yet he managed to lead the 49ers in catches with five and yards with 76. Just a gutsy performance from him that deserves a round of applause.
What an addition Deebo Samuel has been to the 49ers. He's playing as well as he did in 2023 and has given the offense a nice boost.
Every week, Samuel has shown he's a vital part of the offense. He's contributing as a runner and a receiver, giving the offense an annoying dynamic for defenses to face.
It's still crazy to see George Kittle playing football less than nine months after he tore his Achilles. Not only is he playing, but he's playing at a high level.
You never would've believed he tore his Achilles this year, given how amazing he looks. Every week he plays, Kittle proves that he's probably the biggest winner on the 49ers after coming back from a devastating injury.
No other player on the 49ers was locked in to play the Broncos more than Dre Greenlaw. He's been vocal about how unhappy he was with his tenure with them last season.
Coming back to the 49ers has revitalized him and has him playing his best ball since 2023. The fact that the 49ers won, helping him complete his revenge, makes it oh so sweet.
It was a disappointing performance from Kyle Shanahan against the Broncos. The game plan he had for this game was very confusing.
He couldn't sequence his plays as sharply as he had in the first three games either. Brock Purdy bailed him out a few times, including the first touchdown of the game. He'll need to be much better next week against Seattle.
The first offensive series of the game saw Jacob Cowing receive two touches. The first was a jet sweep, where he only managed two yards.
Shortly after that, Purdy targeted Cowing on third down and missed him. However, Cowing turned the wrong way on the curl route he ran. It would've been a first down had he turned the right way. Failed chances like this will hurt his usage moving forward.
After reeling in two explosive catches for 60 yards in Week 3, Jordan Watkins was limited to only eight routes run against the Broncos.
It seems he still has a long way to go before he can be relied upon. Shanahan clearly didn't trust him the same way against a strong defense as he did against a weak one.

title: Buccaneers Get Starter Back vs. Cowboys, But Depth Takes a Hit
full_text:
TAMPA — The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play a talented Dallas Cowboys team on Thursday Night Football. Every game is crucial for Tampa Bay from here on out, as the Bucs are 0-4 and are looking for their first win to kickstart some sort of turnaround.
Tampa Bay had a few interesting names on the injury report heading into the final Wednesday practice, and head coach Todd Bowles gave some clarification on who will be available and who will not be on Thursday. Here's who will play and who will sit out against the Cowboys:
The good news is that kicker Chase McLaughlin appears to be alright, per Bowles. McLaughlin stretched with the team in warmups and should be good to go for Tampa Bay on Thursday despite appearing on the injury report with a groin and hip injury on Tuesday.
Additionally, first-round draft pick Rueben Bain will play for the first time since Week 2 after injuring his groin against the Cleveland Browns. Bain hasn't produced much in the limited time he has played, but he's still a vital part of Tampa Bay's plans at pass rush and should help to bolster the edge rushing group against the Cowboys.
The bad news? The Bucs will be missing some depth pieces. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison and linebacker SirVocea Dennis will miss Thursday's game against the Cowboys, per Bowles.
Both players don't directly affect the team's starting lineup on defense, but both will affect Tampa Bay's special teams unit. As it stands, Dennis has played 61.95% of special teams snaps so far in 2026, and Morrison has played 27.43%. Both are reliable teams options, and the Bucs will have to pivot on Thursday.
Morrison and Dennis also contribute to the team's depth at cornerback and linebacker, respectively. Linebacker Josiah Trotter is dealing with a nagging knee injury, and although the team also has Christian Rozeboom, Dennis' lack of presence could hurt the team if further injuries occur at the position.
Likewise, Morrison is the first corner up behind Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish. If either outside corner gets hurt, the Bucs will likely have to turn to undrafted free agent Ayden Garnes, who impressed the team in preseason and made the 53-man roster.

title: One Player Buccaneers Must See More Playing Time From
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers offense has struggled for the majority of the season under offensive coordinator Zac Robinson through four games.
However, the running game, while not the best, has been one of the only bright spots thanks in large part to Bucky Irving carrying the load.
Free agent acquisition Kenny Gainwell has struggled since arriving in Tampa Bay, and Sean Tucker saw his first action of the season in the loss to the Green Bay Packers.
Tucker scored one of the Bucs' two touchdowns on the day, and when Robinson was asked why he didn't see more snaps following his touchdown, it didn't really provide confidence that he would get more moving forward.
"Yeah, I think those were situational plays that we had in. Then, it just so happened that we had the next guy up on the next series," Robinson said. "But yeah, that's where we've got to continue to evaluate when we can mix them in there. But yeah, it just so happened to be the next guy's series up, and we roll from there."
The next guy's series doesn't make a ton of sense given that Robinson has refused to utilize Tucker at all until the Bucs' fourth game of the season, or else we would have seen him in the previous three contests.
It seems like a cop out taking this avenue and playing it as situational, especially with how unproductive Gainwell has been on the ground.
Gainwell has averaged just two yards per carry on 13 rushes and zero scores.
With how lackluster the offense has been and Gainwell's struggles, one would imagine you would look to bring the third guy in to see what he can provide. But Robinson has refused to do that.
Tucker has shown that he is more than just a goal-line, short-yardage back in the past. In fact, he is probably one of the more explosive backs the Bucs have on the team.
It would be wise for Robinson to at least attempt to give Tucker more snaps moving forward, because obviously, it's tough to get much worse than where you currently are.
If he does well, then great, and if not, so be it. But it's time for Robinson to do something, and a part of that should be incorporating Tucker more into the offense.

title: Buccaneers’ Todd Bowles Now Has Best Odds to Be First NFL Coach Fired
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have had a rough start to the 2026 NFL season.
Literally everyone associated with the organization is underperforming across the board, whether it be the players, position groups, coaches or the front office. As a result, it's no surprise to see many of the fans in Tampa voicing their displeasure with some combination, if not all, of the aforementioned contributors.
When things go wrong, the first person who gets blamed is the head coach. And that reality is certainly taking place right now with the Buccaneers, as the majority of fans have been extremely outspoken regarding their desire to have Bowles relieved of his duties as the team's head coach.
However, the fans don't get to decide who is at fault, who stays, or who goes. That responsibility falls squarely on the shoulders of GM Jason Licht and the owners of the team, the Glazers.
The oddsmakers in Las Vegas feel pretty confident that Bucs' coach is the most likely to be axed first this year. BetOnline has Bowles as a heavy favorite (-140) to be the first NFL head coach fired this season. Houston Texans' head coach, DeMeco Ryans, has the second best chance, but his odds are significantly longer at +150.
It's no surprise to see these two coaches at the top of the list, considering both the Bucs and Texans find themselves without a win almost a quarter of the way through the season despite high expectations coming into the year.
There's no question that Bowles has worn out his welcome in Tampa Bay. There was a time when his complex and highly aggressive defensive scheme was a major advantage for the Buccaneers, but as time has gone on, he has, in many ways, failed to adapt his scheme to match both the growing trends around the league and the specific personnel he has at his disposal.
His lack of success as a head coach further cements his status as a coach who deserves to be fired. Not only has Bowles been atrocious with his timeouts and overly conservative game management decisions, but he has also had a disappointing record of 35-37 in the regular season and is 1-3 in the postseason since being appointed the Bucs' head coach back in 2022.
Considering the depth of talent he's had on the roster during that time and the lack of quality competition in the NFC South, that lack of success in the win-loss column is simply inexcusable. Dating back to last season, the Bucs have also lost 11 of their last 13 regular-season games, which is the worst record in the entire NFL during that time.
Despite everything working against Bowles' job security moving forward, the unfortunate reality for Bucs fans who want to see him fired is the fact that the Glazers have proven unwilling to do so to previous head coaches during the season, despite similarly dreadful results.
For those seriously considering taking betting action on the Bowles being the first head coach fired this season, I would proceed with extreme caution.
Despite some truly horrendous coaching performances from the likes of Lovie Smith, Greg Schiano and Raheem Morris since the Glazer family purchased the organization back in 1995, they have never once fired a head coach during the season.
So even though the results that Bowles has provided as head coach (especially recently) would undoubtedly warrant a midseason firing, the historical trends of the Buccaneers' ownership group contradict that action.
Barring some sort of miracle, it feels like Bowles being fired is a foregone conclusion. That being said, it would come as a big surprise to see the Glazers relieve the Bucs' head coach of his duties before the season's end.

title: Buccaneers Reveal Concerning News Ahead of Cowboys Matchup
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 0-4, and they need all the help they can get to beat the Dallas Cowboys on a quick turnaround. Unfortunately, the Bucs may be in danger of losing their leading points scorer before that game on Thursday night.
Tampa Bay released its Tuesday injury report for its game on Thursday, and even though the practice was just a walkthrough, it came with some interesting news. Tampa Bay's kicker, Chase McLaughlin, suddenly appeared on the report with a hip and groin injury.
The Bucs conducted a walkthrough on Tuesday, so the report was generated with participation levels estimated if the team was conducting a full practice. Even so, McLaughlin appeared on the injury report after being absent from it on Monday.
McLaughlin missing Thursday's game could be very bad news for Tampa Bay for a number of reasons. For one, McLaughlin is the Buccaneers' leading points scorer, putting up 34 of Tampa Bay's 76 points so far this year. He has hit 100% of his field goals and his extra points, making him arguably the NFL's best kicker so far in 2026.
There's also the matter of what Tampa Bay would do without him. The Bucs do not have a kicker on their practice squad and do not have the extra roster spot to add one at the moment. If McLaughlin is hurt but not hurt enough to sit out, his accuracy could be in question — if he's too hurt to play, what will the Bucs do with a game in just two days?
Field goal range and extra points would suddenly become daunting prospects if McLaughlin could not play and the Bucs did not have time to replace him. The team will hope he's good enough to go on Thursday night, and if he isn't, Tampa Bay's game against Dallas will become even more of an uphill battle while starting a UDFA rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels.
The Bucs will face off against the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Oct. 8 at 8:15 p.m.

title: The Buccaneers’ Offense Has a Major Problem, and One Stat Proves It
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have problems everywhere — that much is apparent. But one of the biggest problems the Bucs have is with the offense, and namely, getting the ball down the field at a rapid rate.
The Bucs lost 17-14 to the Green Bay Packers in Week 4, and although UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels was expected to be shaky in his first start, he didn't get much help. Tampa Bay simply isn't generating explosive plays on offense, and it's crippling the team's effectiveness over the course of the first four weeks.
Explosive plays are counted various ways by different offensive coordinators. The most common way to count them is a run play of 10-plus yards or a pass play of 20-plus yards — and right now, the Bucs aren't really generating either.
Per NFL data analyst Sam Hoppen, the Buccaneers are 30th in the NFL in explosive plays overall (5.0%). They're 25th in explosive run plays (8.3%) and 30th in receiving explosive plays (2.8%).
Offensive and defensive explosive play rates: pic.twitter.com/A0SuYaZQxj
They aren't the definitive stat that makes an offense hum, but all great offenses tend to generate a lot of them. The Buccaneers are a top-10 defense in preventing them, but the offense cannot repay the favor by generating them.
So why is that? There could be a number of factors. Tampa Bay is having trouble getting the ball to its wide receivers — tight end Cade Otton has 23 targets and is the team's leading wideout.
The Bucs are also one of the league leaders in passes behind the line of scrimmage, clocking in tied for eighth with 28 passes behind the line. That's not very conducive to explosive plays, so that could be part of the problem, too.
Either way, the Bucs need to figure out how to generate explosive plays at a higher rate. That may involve getting the football to deep-ball threats like Ted Hurst more often, and in the run game, utilizing the strengths of Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell (and perhaps giving Sean Tucker some more carries?).
The Buccaneers play the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football on the road at 8:15.

title: Buccaneers Legend Tom Brady Back in the NFL? Biographer Isn't Ruling It Out
full_text:
Things have taken quite a turn in Tampa Bay since the days of Tom Brady, and it hasn't been for the better.
During the Brady years, the Buccaneers were rolling and included a Super Bowl victory. The culture was set, and there was no denying them as one of the league's best teams.
That has taken a drastic turn since his retirement, with middling seasons capped by early playoff exits.
It doesn't seem as if Brady will be returning to the league, but in a recent interview with Front Office Sports , his biographer Lars Anderson gave insight into his possible regrets.
“I think he wishes he got number eight,” Anderson said, referring to an additional Super Bowl championship. “I think he wishes circumstances could have been different and he could have kept playing... I do think that if Tom had his druthers, he would be playing right now, and I would not be shocked if he somehow tries to play next year.”
It isn't a shocker that the man who has won the most Super Bowls as a player would have wanted more, but with Anderson saying that Brady wishes he could have kept playing after his second retirement announcement, that bit is a surprise.
We all understand how things ended for Brady. His football career had become such a huge part of his life that his wife, Gisele Bundchen, decided that it was enough and ultimately parted ways with the greatest quarterback to ever play the game.
She had sacrificed so much over the two decades that he played that it was time for her to focus on her and the family, something that she had hoped Brady would do eventually, but something he never could.
By the time Brady called it quits and tried to put things back in place when it came to his relationship and family, it was too late.
That meant that Brady now was without his two loves in life: Bundchen and football.
While one is gone for good, Brady has found solace in the game he loves. He has been deeply invested in broadcasting for FOX Sports and also in helping turn around the Las Vegas Raiders as a minority owner.
And while there will continue to be speculation regarding him coming back to play in the league until it's obvious he can't, it's highly doubtful to happen at this point, since it hasn't happened in the three years he's been retired from the game.

title: Todd Bowles Makes His QB Decision For Buccaneers-Cowboys Matchup
full_text:
Well, it's hard to imagine that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 0-4 for the first time since 2013, but that is where things currently stand after their 17-14 loss to the struggling Green Bay Packers.
There was plenty to take away from the Bucs' loss, but the one thing everyone had their eyes on was how well undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels would play with Baker Mayfield out with an injury.
It wasn't a pretty debut for Daniels, but he did show some promise in certain areas throughout the contest. And when speaking to the media following the game, head coach Todd Bowles spoke highly of his competitive nature while confirming that he will remain under center for the team's upcoming Thursday Night Football matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.
“Yeah, he’ll be the quarterback Thursday night," Bowles said "He had some ups and he had some downs, but for his first time out there, he didn’t panic, he didn’t do anything. He escaped, used his legs well at times. It’s his first game — he’s going to have some ups and downs."
It's not much, but it seems like everyone is content running Daniels back out there over veterans Easton Stick and Brett Rypien.
Daniels didn't have the best day throwing the ball, completing 70% of his passes for 148 yards and a touchdown with two interceptions. However, he was able to utilize his legs, running for 55 yards.
It would have been nice to see Daniels have a better game given how lackluster Green Bay's defense has been this season, but that didn't materialize. Questionable play calling and rookie mistakes were at the forefront of why he couldn't be more successful.
Daniels and the offense will have a chance to bounce back, but it will have to be on a short week.
The Cowboys' defense has yet to come together after overhauling that side of the ball this offseason. However, it could also be their chance for them to get it right, as the Bucs' offense has struggled mightily through four games this season.
We know that the Cowboys' offense will put up points, so if the Bucs hope to shock most of the world and win, then they must rely on Daniels to play well above his potential and try to match the Cowboys blow for blow.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' 17-14 Loss to the Packers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 0-4 after a dreadful start to the season. Head coach Todd Bowles is on the hot seat, and that seat is growing hotter after the Bucs lost 17-14 to the Green Bay Packers at home.
It was quarterback Jalon Daniels' debut for the team, but the offense wasn't able to get much going all day. Although there was one bright spot, most of Tampa Bay's performance was lackluster, and it ended with yet another loss.
Here's the good, bad and ugly from the Bucs latest home loss:
The Bucs' secondary played well on Sunday.
They had an interception on Jordan Love when Jacob Parrish made an excellent play on the ball to stop a red zone scoring attempt. Before that, the Bucs secondary comboed for another red zone turnover — safety Tykee Smith knocked the ball out of Packers running back Kaleb Johnson's hands and defensive back Zyon McCollum jumped on top of it.
Those two game-changing plays were huge for Tampa Bay's defense.
Given that Daniels was a UDFA rookie in his first start, he didn't play nearly as bad as he could have — he made plays with his legs and had a touchdown pass to his name.
That being said, he did throw two interceptions, and he also self-admittedly missed a protection call on 4th & 11 that allowed a free blitzer. With 148 yards through the air, it wasn't a great performance, but that was to be expected from the rookie and there's still a lot of good to take away from the experience.
The Bucs were hoping to rely on the run game to help Daniels in his first start, and that didn't quite happen. Outside of Daniels' 55 yards on the ground, the running backs were lackluster.
Running back Bucky Irving averaged just 3.8 yards per attempt, Sean Tucker just 3.3 yards per attempt (more on that later) and Kenny Gainwell a dreadful 1.7 yards per attempt. Tampa Bay wasn't able to get much going on the ground consistently, and if it can't run the ball and has trouble passing it, then what does it have as an identity?
Prior to this game, Packers quarterback Jordan Love had been hit in the pocket 31 times — eight more than the next most-hit quarterback. On Sunday? He was hit just twice.
The pass rush has been a problem for the Bowles and the Bucs for almost his entire tenure as head coach, and even with a few new additions, it remains a problem. Bowles told reporters Sunday that Love was getting the ball out fast, but other teams have seemed to get to him where the Bucs could not.
What's the way forward for Tampa Bay's pass rush? It's hard to say. But something has to change.
Tampa Bay's personnel usage remains interesting at this stage of the year.
Tucker may have averaged just 3.3 yards per carry, but that's because he had only three carries. One saw him get stuffed, but another saw him get eight yards on fourth-and-one and another saw him find the end zone for a touchdown — he wasn't used after that.
Outside linebacker David Walker got the most snaps he's ever gotten in a game on Sunday, but he should be getting more. He moved Jordan Love off his spot on a one pressure to force an incompletion and remains Tampa Bay's best pass rusher via pressure rate (26.1%, via SumerSports). Walker simply must get on the field more, but instead, he was the fourth-most played edge rusher against the Packers on Sunday.
Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson's playcalling remains interesting.
The Buccaneers ran 11 personnel on 55 of their 61 offensive snaps in Week 4, despite having four tight ends on the roster and using 12 and 13 personnel quite a bit in Week 3. What's even more baffling is that tight end Cade Otton, who is the one tight end in most of these plays, was the second-most targeted player on the team with 6 targets.
On top of that, screen passes are very common and plays behind the line of scrimmage continue to be a notable problem. The Bucs had eight passes behind the line of scrimmage on Sunday, which accounted for almost 30% of Daniels' attempts over the course of the game. That included a screen pass on 3rd & 16 with the game on the line, which doesn't do much for the offense.
This offense is currently too timid to push the ball down the field and can't find a way to get the ball to its wide receivers. That's a bad place to be.

title: Star Buccaneers Defender Out For Multiple Weeks After Week 4 Injury
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost their Week 4 matchup against the Green Bay Packers 17-14 in Week 4, but the loss wasn't the only fallout.
The Buccaneers' star safety, Antoine Winfield Jr., went down on the field toward the back half of the game holding his abdomen, and he did not return to action. Head coach Todd Bowles told media after the game that the team was running tests on Winfield Jr.'s injury, and those tests didn't come back the way Bowles or Winfield likely hoped.
Bowles confirmed to reporters on Monday that Winfield Jr. fractured his ribs, and he's expected to be sidelined anywhere from two to four weeks with the injury.
"We won't have Winfield Thursday. He has a slight rib fracture — he'll be out two to four weeks probably, from what I'm hearing."
Winfield is Tampa Bay's starting safety, and as a former All-Pro, he's crucial to the defense. Winfield signed a four-year, $84.1 million extension with the Bucs after a dominant 2023 season, and he's been playing alongside safety Tykee Smith for the last two years.
So far this season, Winfield has netted 15 solo tackles and one forced fumble. With him out of the picture for the next few weeks, the team will turn to safety Ifeatu Melifonwu to take his place — Melifonwu played for Miami last year and came to Tampa Bay in the offseason.
The depth behind Winfield remains precarious. With both Melifonwu and Smith starting, the only other safety on the roster is Miles Killebrew, who is mainly a special teams player. The Bucs have two safeties on the practice squad in JJ Roberts and Silas Walters, so the team may be forced to elevate one of those two players to replace Winfield.
The Bucs also have a spot on the practice squad open after defensive back Sean Murphy-Bunting (who could also play safety) was signed to the Pittsburgh Steelers' 53-man roster. The Bucs may look to add another defensive back there, too.
Tampa Bay is set to play the Dallas Cowboys in just three days on Thursday Night Football.

title: Buccaneers Lose Super Bowl Champion Corner to the Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' defensive back depth got a little thinner on Monday, just one day after the Bucs lost to the Green Bay Packers in Week 4.
The Buccaneers brought on defensive back Sean Murphy-Bunting at the beginning of the season to the practice squad to shore up cornerback depth and add a veteran presence to the roster. Through the first four games, Murphy-Bunting, who won a Super Bowl with Tampa Bay in 2020, was not elevated.
Keeping a player on the practice squad has some risks, and the Bucs faced the brunt of that on Monday when Murphy-Bunting was signed away from the team.
The Pittsburgh Steelers have signed Murphy-Bunting to their active roster, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero.
The Steelers are signing veteran CB Sean Murphy-Bunting off the Bucs' practice squad, per source. Murphy-Bunting has played in 82 NFL games (65 starts) and has 11 career interceptions. Some experienced depth for Pittsburgh after the Joey Porter Jr. trade. pic.twitter.com/waUZp7F8Jg
The move gives Pittsburgh some cornerback depth after the Joey Porter Jr. trade, where the Steelers sent Porter to the Cowboys. Another reason why Pittsburgh is bringing on Murphy-Bunting has to do with another Super Bowl-winning Buccaneer who played alongside Murphy-Bunting in 2020.
The Steelers signed cornerback Jamel Dean in free agency after the Bucs let him walk this year, and just like in Tampa Bay, Dean has had some trouble staying healthy. Murphy-Bunting is an option for the Steelers while Dean recovers, and he may be thrust into a playing role sooner than later.
Murphy-Bunting recorded no stats in Tampa Bay this year, but last year, he had three interceptions with the Arizona Cardinals and recorded five pass deflections. The Bucs have been using a rotation of Benjamin Morrison, Jacob Parrish and Zyon McCollum on the outside, so Murphy-Bunting has never needed to be elevated so far this season.
Now that he's off the practice squad, however, the Bucs could find another corner to fill his spot. Morrison recently injured his quad in practice and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. is also dealing with an oblique injury, so another defensive back — perhaps one who can also play safety — could be a good move for general Jason Licht and the Bucs after Murphy-Bunting's departure.
The Bucs play the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football on the road, and it will be interesting to see if they replace Murphy-Bunting's spot on the squad before that game in just three days.

title: Titans' Cam Ward Has Less Time to Prove He's "The One" Than You Might Think
full_text:
The journey for every young QB is different. It took Bryce Young the better part of three seasons to settle in with the Carolina Panthers after being thrown into the fire as a first overall pick. Fernando Mendoza, on the other hand, was just taken first by the Las Vegas Raiders to sit and learn behind Kirk Cousins. Cam Ward's scenario with the Tennessee Titans leans toward the former, of course.
Only, Ward may not have the same benefit of time to come into his own. Four games into his sophomore year, the Miami product seems to be battling regression. His accuracy has hardly improved, and looks downfield have become more scarce.
Where other passers have a runway paved for their progression, Ward appears to be falling behind his fellow young playmakers in Tennessee. Quickly, at least as far as I'm concerned, what was "Carnell Tate has to make things easier on Ward" has become "Ward has to make things easier on Tate."
Ward himself said as much in Wednesday's press conference.
Some things were bound to change when Robert Saleh was brought in to replace Brian Callahan. It was Callahan, after all, who was here when Ward was drafted. That's an offensive-minded coach being fitted with weapons that suit his profile.
Tate may have been drafted under Saleh, but EDGE Keldric Faulk and LB Anthony Hill Jr. were, too. To that point, it's unsurprising that the Titans' offense has been the team's weaker side this season. Saleh's defensive play-calling is the closest thing this team has to an identity right now.
The history of QBs picked first overall suggests that their development will come along eventually. In fact, every QB taken first from the 2016 NFL Draft on still has a starting job today, save for the aforementioned Mendoza.
Ward, however, has the worst record of any of those guys through the first 21 games of his career, at 3-18. I'd argue that he has less room for error within the walls of a desperate franchise facing their second straight failed rebuild.
Saleh is far from a surefire failure, that's not a discussion. He's winless through four games, but we haven't really seen what the head coach will do when his back is against the wall and a tough decision has to be made. Ward being benched has already been brought up.
After the Titans' QB threw a game-losing interception to the New York Giants in Week 3, Saleh was asked about the possibility of sitting Ward. Mind you, the Panthers did the same thing in Young's second year before he ultimately found his footing.
Saleh responded with an unceremonious "no," and that was that. Ward did go on to have his best game of the season in Week 4's loss to the Ravens, but that still only amounted to one score, 222 yards, and a pick.
I'm not saying that the Titans should be ready to go ahead and can the guy, but would a second coach be fired with Ward under center before a change is made? I don't think so, especially not if Saleh keeps fielding solid draft picks and defensive improvements.
The further we progress into his second season, the more crucial Ward's own progression becomes. Tennessee can only wait and see for so much longer.

title: Titans Winners and Losers After First Quarter of 2026 NFL Season
full_text:
We're now essentially one quarter into the 2026 NFL season. Objectively, things could not be going any worse under Robert Saleh, at least as far as wins and losses go. The Tennessee Titans are 0-4, and look nearly identical to their despised franchise-reset state from last season.
Yet, there are things for Titans fans to hold out hope for. Between quick rookie developments and late arrivals, multiple players are starting to take leaps toward becoming reliable, even winning pieces for Tennessee.
On the flip side, there are a couple of assets heading in the opposite direction. Here are the biggest winners and losers from the Titans' first four games.
Anthony Hill Jr., the Titans' second-round rookie LB, is third in the NFL in total tackles with 42. He's stepped into a debatable LB room and turned it into one of Tennessee's defensive strengths when he's on the field - now, that's most of the time.
Hill has consistently topped the charts in our rookie power rankings. Before Week 4, Hill held the crown as the NFL's leading tackler. Mind you, he's four games into his professional career.
Say what you will about Saleh's job so far, but the coach clearly has a one-of-one mind for defensive talent and development. Hill is a peak example of that process, and goes down as a huge winner for the Titans so far.
Less excitingly, backup RB Tyjae Spears makes an unfortunate addition to the losers column through four contests.
With Tony Pollard in the final year of his contract and Spears entering this season fully healthy, 2026 appeared like the prime window for Spears to eventually take up lead-back duties. Up to this point, he's been on and off the field, and unreliable even in a secondary role.
Having been questionable with an ankle injury for two straight weeks now, Spears' impact has dwindled down to almost nothing despite playing through it. He's got just 15 carries for 65 yards this year.
In the receiving game, where Spears tends to thrive, just five receptions for 40 yards. Pollard being treated like a workhorse isn't working for the Titans, but Spears hasn't done enough to confidently pose himself as a replacement.
Alongside the aforementioned Hill, Carnell Tate has come on strong in his first NFL campaign. The rookie wide receiver is fresh off a breakout performance that only seems to signal more growth.
Tate went for 145 yards on nine receptions vs. the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4. He leads Tennessee in receptions (22), targets (32) and receiving yards (268). PFF has Tate with the second most contested catches at a 100% rate in the league, at 6/6.
The fourth overall pick has long arrived in an offense that is far from complete. If Cam Ward fully figures it out, Tate could find himself in superstar conversations sooner rather than later.
Speaking of Ward, the second-year signal caller finds himself on the negative side of this list. He's not had a bad season necessarily, but the standard is higher for him than anyone on this team.
Ward has thrown three touchdowns to two interceptions this season. His 63% completion rate thus far shows little improvement to last season, and worries about his footwork and decision-making continue to overshadow the wins.
PFF rankings see Ward in the league's bottom 10 in overall grade, passing yards, and passing scores. His best game came against the Ravens last week, and even that resulted in a loss that saw the Titans playing from behind the entire time.
As young, star-making pieces rise around him, the pressure for Ward to improve with them gets greater. The QB simply isn't there yet, and ringing alarm bells aren't far off if he doesn't find a way to succeed.
Finally, third-year T JC Latham has elevated into truly elite status on the offensive line. After a so-so first two seasons, the Alabama alumni's numbers are now an undeniable marker of his growth.
Latham has an astonishing 0% sack/QB hit rate this season. Saleh said prior to Week 4 that Latham is having a Pro-Bowl worthy season up to this point, and the T only helped his case vs. Baltimore. He might be the best protector on this Titans team right now.
With no sacks allowed through four games and one of the best island (one on one) win rates in the NFL, Latham deserves a spot as a winner here. Ward's life has been made a whole lot easier by Latham, and he's a piece that Tennessee must now prioritize keeping around in the long run.

title: The Titans’ Most Underrated Free-Agent Addition is Turning Heads Despite Tennessee's 0-4 Record
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans were incredibly active during NFL free agency in the spring, with one of their signings being edge rusher Jacob Martin.
Martin, a sixth-round pick in the 2018 NFL Draft by the Seattle Seahawks, has been a journeyman pass rusher for the entirety of his career. The Temple product has had stops with the Seahawks, obviously, the Houston Texans, the New York Jets, the Denver Broncos, the Indianapolis Colts, the Chicago Bears, the Washington Commanders, and now the Titans.
Outside of a three-year stint in Houston from 2019 to 2021, Martin hasn't been able to find a long-term home at the next level. However, he's off to a fantastic start in 2026 and is showing why Tennessee made the right decision inking him to a two-year deal in March.
Through four games, Martin has been one of Tennessee's most productive defenders. He has posted 1.5 sacks, 13 quarterback pressures , two defensive stops, and two tackles for loss so far, and is coming off a five-pressure game with half a sack against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4 . Martin also recorded seven quarterback pressures and a sack in the Week 2 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
Martin has been a bright spot on a Titans defense that has been inconsistent to kick off the year . But the unit hasn't gotten any help from an offense that's been dysfunctional and out of sorts on nearly every drive.
The Titans' addition of Jermaine Johnson was the premier acquisition for the team at edge rusher. However, Martin has slightly outplayed Johnson so far this season, tallying one more pressure and half a sack more, though Johnson has been better in the run game.
Regardless, Martin is making his presence felt on the defensive line, and it's integral that he keeps this level of play up. Tennessee's secondary hasn't been the most reliable, and the group could use a lot of help from the front seven in the pass-rushing department.
The Titans are eyeing their first win of the 2026 season at home against the Houston Texans in Week 5, and Martin is a player who will need to step up for Tennessee to finally break a losing streak that dates back to Week 17 of the 2025 season.

title: Titans Rookie Power Rankings: Nick Singleton Defines Week 4 With Disappointment
full_text:
With every passing week, our Titans rookie power rankings start to feel more important. The further this team falls into the pit, the more crucil the young talent on this roster become. Moving forward, some of these guys will be make or break pieces.
As usual, Week 4 resulted in a loss against the Baltimore Ravens. But one rookie had the biggest game of his young career, and all but one stood out in a positive way.
RG Fernando Carmona has been removed from this list until he returns from his ankle injury. Let's break this thing down.
This comes as no surprise. Carnell Tate just had his first signature game as a rookie, breaking out for 145 yards on nine receptions at Baltimore. The Titans may have fallen, but Tate's skyrocketing progression was a huge win on the day.
He could have had an even better showing too, if it wasn't for a handful of missed opportunities and the second-quarter fumble that went on to haunt Tennessee. Even so, he was the best player in the Titans' offense, and deserves the top spot on this list once again.
Tate's target share is increasing. He's getting extensive looks downfield, and making the most of them, for the most part. This is only the beginning for a draft investment that has already begun to prove his worth in Nashville.
Hill has probably become the most consistent rookie in Tennessee's 2026 class. The second-round rookie is third in the NFL in tackles (42), and had another promising turn in Week 4.
The LB's eight tackles were tied with fellow LB Cody Barton for the most on the team. Even when the plain ol' elite Ravens offense was progressing, Hill positioned himself correctly and made his presence known in passing lanes.
He's already leading the LB position in snap counts, and Hill is four games into his NFL career. The Titans got one, and he doesn't have to explode to do his job well on a weekly basis.
Faulk still can't find his way further up than this, but the EDGE has been sneakily improving on the defensive front in recent weeks.
His one tackle vs. the Ravens is deceiving; Faulk took more strides. The rookie's ability to play physically and outright move defenders out of his way bodes well for his development. Faulk's low snap count continues to limit his chances to really find his footing and make a difference.
When he's out there, however, Faulk is consistently making more plays. He gets a thumbs up this week, even being at third in our ranking.
Singleton unfortunately must go down as the most disappointing facet of Tennessee's rookie pool in Week 4. His debut against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2 was underwhelming, but positive noise from Robert Saleh suggested a second chance coming soon, no matter how small.
On three carries, Singleton generated just two yards. He was brought in to spell the consistenly ailed Tyjae Spears, although to no avail. Whether it's a matter of limited opportunity, rookie rust, or both, the first-year back just doesn't look ready yet.
Singleton needs more time waiting in the wings before he sees the field again. A disappointment for the time, for sure, but he's got plenty of time to get right in Brian Daboll's system going forward. A potential Tony Pollard trade would swing that door wide open.

title: Brian Daboll is Using Tony Pollard as Titans' Workhorse — Why That Plan Got Old Fast
full_text:
There's no denying the Tennessee Titans have talent, but muddled play-calling appears to be holding back a capable offense. After going 3-14 last season, fans and pundits expected more wins headed into the new season. Even the major sportsbooks, such as DraftKings, had Tennessee's win total betting line at 6.5 prior to Week 1.
Unfortunately, the Titans are off to a disastrous 0-4 start with a downward-spiraling offense.
In the offseason, Tennessee hired the defensive-minded Robert Saleh as the head coach and former NFL Coach of the Year winner Brian Daboll as the offensive coordinator. Daboll assumed offensive play calling.
The product on the field has been underwhelming despite the Titans defense having held opponents to only 20.8 points per game, which is the ninth best in the league . Tennessee's offense ranks in the bottom three in points, yards, and touchdowns and is yet to score more than 20 points in a game.
Daboll has proven to be a conservative playcaller, commanding the run roughly 42% of snaps, specifically veteran RB Tony Pollard. However, the Pollard-centric offense has been unsuccessful and needs a change.
Through four games no other Titan has received the ball more than Pollard, who has 54 rushing attempts and four receptions. Consequently, the heavy usage of Pollard has essentially nixed RB Tyjae Spears from significant playtime.
Spears only has 20 touches, nearly a third of the touches Pollard is getting despite averaging 5.25 yards per touch, which trumps Pollard's 3.95 yards per touch.
Now in his fourth season, Spears, a former third-round pick, has never been the starter in Tennessee. In his rookie season he played behind future Hall of Famer Derrick Henry, since he's played second to Pollard.
Daboll has used Spears primarily as a pass blocker, but he has shown himself to be a viable receiving back with five receptions for 40 yards. For comparison, Pollard has eight receptions for only 24 yards. Spears averages five more yards per reception than Pollard.
The strong preference for Pollard couldn't have been more evident than against the Ravens. Pollard was called on for a goal line punch for straight times; he was stuffed each time .
Daboll's horrendous call showed his lack of trust in QB Cam Ward and the other offensive talents. After Baltimore's goal line stand, the Titans were playing catch-up the remainder of the game until they ultimately fell 24-18, with their last score coming in the final two minutes.
Another dilemma in the backfield is rookie RB Nick Singleton.
Drafted in the 5th round, Singleton has only played a handful of snaps for the Titans. He only has seven carries across three games played for 12 yards. Up to this point in the season, Singleton has been relegated to a kick return specialist, and beyond that, his role in the offense is unknown. Pollard is a quality player, but it's safe to say he doesn't warrant 62 touches, especially with Spears outperforming him in average yards per touch.
Spears and Singleton have only combined 27 touches.
For perspective, Pollard has more rushing attempts than Christian McCaffrey and David Montgomery. McCaffrey has four touchdowns, Montgomery has two and Pollard only has one. With Pollard at the helm, the Titans have the sixth fewest rushing yards in the NFL. If Daboll doesn't trust his struggling second-year quarterback, why not lean on a talented backfield committee?
Pollard is in his age 29 season. Meanwhile, Spears and Singleton are 25 and 22, respectively. The Titans are decorated with young talent. 21-year-old WR Carnell Tate has blossomed with significant playing time. Spears or Singleton could be a breakout player for the Titans if given a fair chance.

title: The 1 Coaching Decision Robert Saleh Continues to Make That is Holding Titans Back
full_text:
All things considered, Robert Saleh can't be entirely blamed for the Tennessee Titans' shortcomings. We've noted time and time again that he inherited perhaps the worst rebuild in the NFL; it was always going to take more than a couple of games to undo what Brian Callahan did to this franchise.
He isn't without flaw, though. Saleh's game management has taken a few hits in the public arena already this season, but more than anything else, I'm confused by one personnel choice he's made for three straight weeks now.
Why is Cody Barton still playing over Cedric Gray? Against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4, Gray was on the field for just 28 (45.9%) of defensive snaps. Barton, on the other hand, notched 50 (82%). Not only was Cedric Gray better than Barton last season, but he's seemingly completely healthy right now.
Gray missed Week 1 due to an untimely UTV accident. He still nearly played vs. the Jets, before ultimately failing to clear concussion protocol. Since then, it's almost like one of the league's leading tacklers from last season disappeared from this roster.
To make matters worse, Barton is struggling in his wake. Even compared to rookie LB Anthony Hill Jr., Barton's role at MIKE looks contestable at best.
You'd think there's a reason for Saleh's insistence on Gray being held to a complimentary role, but such a reason hasn't been made clear. Gray is making plays in his limited time, exhibiting the same nose for the football that earned him a hefty share of snaps in the 2025 season.
According to Pro Football Reference, Gray was in play for 86.9% of Tennessee's defensive snaps.
Saleh praised Gray when asked about this discrepancy following Week 4's defeat, saying that the LB does "a good job in the run game and pass game." He ultimately threw a softball, pinning it on Barton/Hill being a good combination in the nickel defense.
The Titans' head coach also noted that as Tennessee leans into the dime defense, in which only one LB is on the field, snap counts at the position naturally fall. "Overall, percentage wise, it's going to be similar," Saleh finished, forecasting a similar situation moving forward.
Per PFF, Gray has a higher overall rating than Barton (68.8 to 66.5), and is only six tackles shy of the veteran (14 to 8) in spite of their massive snap differential. Barton simply doesn't fit the younger, more aggressive profile that the Titans' defense is quickly taking on.
Not only is this call a head-scratcher from Saleh, but it also appears pointless. The longer is takes to return Gray to the field more regularly, the more Saleh's own unit will suffer as a result.

title: Beyond The Numbers: A Deeper Look at Carnell Tate's Explosive Outing vs. Ravens
full_text:
Titans rookie WR Carnell Tate has really started to come along as of late. Over the last two weeks, the Ohio State alumni has been targeted a whopping 21 times, catching 15 of them for 203 receiving yards. The bulk of that came on Sunday in what many have labeled as the ‘ Carnell Tate breakout game .’
The former Buckeye recorded 145 yards on nine catches in Baltimore on Sunday. However, it was Tate’s nuanced understanding of Baltimore’s zone coverage and knowing how to exploit it on any given down that really caught my eye.
The Ravens were trying to take him away, but they simply couldn’t. Tate routinely exploited the coverage by attacking soft spots, finding holes, and giving QB Cam Ward an easy window to throw into.
That’s not to say he played a perfect game by any means. The rookie receiver left a lot of meat on the bone. Tate wasn’t able to reel in a couple of balls throughout the game that were at least catchable. He also had the backbreaking fumble at the end of the first half that negated what would’ve been a big gain.
Later in the contest, Tate ran a beautiful double move that essentially forced Ravens DB Kyle Hamilton to grab the rookie in order to slow him down, subsequently throwing off the timing of the deep route. The play ultimately resulted in defensive pass interference, but had they connected on that throw, we’d be talking close to 200 yards on the day.
Take a look at Tate's routes, as well as some equally eye-popping numbers:
Carnell Tate breakout game was fun 42.8% target share 6 catches of 10+ yds 3 catches of 20+ yds 1 catch of 30+ yds 21.5 PPR pts after 25.3 across first 3 games pic.twitter.com/0qP2HKArNv
To take the rookie’s performance a step further, Tate accounted for 48 percent of the team’s target share and 70.2 percent of the team’s air-yard share . The former top-five pick was also one of three receivers who had a first-read target share above 50 percent in Week 4 (Panthers WR Tet McMillan, Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb).
According to Pro Football Focus , Tate also recorded an absurd 4.39 yards per routes run (YPRR) on Sunday. YPRR takes into account the number of times a receiver runs a route as an eligible receiver compared to the amount of receiving yards he gains for a particular game.
Following this breakout performance, Tennessee’s rookie receiver is now just the fourth receiver under the age of 22 to record at least 145 yards in a game, joining Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase, Vikings WR Justin Jefferson, and Giants WR Malik Nabers as the only four to accomplish this feat.
It was also the most receiving yards by a Titans rookie receiver since A.J. Brown’s 153-yard performance against the Raiders back in 2019.
Another impressive stat: Tate currently ranks in the top 12 at his position in targets (ninth), receptions (eight), and receiving yards (12th), per PFF . Things could get very interesting for this Titans team if they start to connect on some of these missed opportunities that were there for the taking.
Unfortunately, the reality is, this is still a 0-4 squad. With that said, having someone like Tate develop into a bonafide number one wide receiver would be a game changer for this franchise, both in the immediate and long-term future. The guy is still 21 years old and has all the talent in the world. The likelihood is that he’s only gonna keep getting better with every passing week, month, and year.
If that’s the case, brighter days could be ahead for the Titans fanbase. They may just have to be a little patient to get there.
